37thread_local! {
38    /// Suppresses journal publication while a committed transaction applies
39    /// its already-staged mutations to the live pack/index state. The outer
40    /// transaction publishes the complete batch exactly once afterward.
41    static JOURNAL_SUPPRESSED: Cell<bool> = const { Cell::new(false) };
42    /// Set while a read-committed lookup falls back to the live index. That
43    /// fallback reads through `get_many`, which redirects to the overlay path
44    /// while a transaction is active, so without this flag the two would call
45    /// each other until the stack overflowed.
46    static READ_COMMITTED_FALLBACK: Cell<bool> = const { Cell::new(false) };
47}

49/// Callback that rewrites a node's child references given resolved child data,
50/// used to inline already-cached children in place of lazy hash pointers.
51pub type SwizzleFn = fn(&NodeData, &[NodeId], &[Option<Arc<NodeData>>]) -> NodeData;

53/// Lowercase hex rendering of a 32-byte digest, for error messages.
54fn hex32(digest: &Digest32) -> String {
55    use std::fmt::Write as _;
56    let mut out = String::with_capacity(64);
57    for byte in digest {
58        let _ = write!(out, "{byte:02x}");
59    }
60    out
61}

63/// Result of [`PackfileStorage::plan_collection_repack`] — what a real repack
64/// of this collection would do, computed exactly (same scan + reachability

80/// Which index-loading path a `PackfileStorage` open took.
81#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
82pub enum OpenPath {
83    /// A persisted index checkpoint validated against the current pack set's
84    /// fingerprint was loaded in place of a rescan.
85    Checkpoint,
86    /// No usable checkpoint: every pack's records were scanned and the
87    /// per-collection indexes rebuilt from scratch.
88    FullScan,
89}
90
91/// How strictly `PackfileStorage::checkpoint_scan_out` validates the live pack
92/// set against a persisted checkpoint.
93#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
94enum ReloadMode {
95    /// The live packs must match the checkpoint's fingerprint exactly, or a
96    /// delta log must bridge the checkpoint to them. Used by `open` and crash
97    /// recovery, where a mismatch means the checkpoint is stale and the caller
98    /// must rescan.
99    Strict,
100    /// Skip the exact-pack fingerprint gate and the delta-log replay; the
101    /// read-committed overlay is authoritative for the post-checkpoint suffix.
102    /// Used only by `reload_index_from_checkpoint`, where the writer is still
103    /// appending and its packs have already grown past the checkpoint (a strict
104    /// gate would fail the read closed).
105    JournalBound,
106}

108/// Where a checkpoint-path open sourced each collection's per-shard counts
109/// and home-shard assignment.
110#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
111pub enum BookkeepingSource {
112    /// Reconstructed from the fingerprint-gated `shard_collections.bin`
113    /// records — no slot walk across any collection index.
114    Sidecar,
115    /// Computed by walking every slot of every collection index.
116    SlotScan,
117}

119/// Wall-clock breakdown of one `PackfileStorage` open, by phase. Measured
120/// with a handful of `Instant::now()` deltas on the open path only, so
121/// recording these doesn't perturb the numbers they report.
122///
123/// The per-phase fields partition the synchronous open work; see the
124/// struct-level timing doc for what each phase covers. On the checkpoint
125/// path `full_scan` is zero; on the fallback path `checkpoint_decode` and
126/// `fingerprint` still reflect the attempt that failed validation (e.g. a
127/// missing or stale checkpoint) before the scan had to run.
128#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
129pub struct OpenTimings {
130    /// Total time spent opening the shard pool, including discovery, locking,
131    /// packfile recovery, and metadata restoration.
132    pub shard_open: std::time::Duration,
133    /// Directory and pack-file discovery.
134    pub shard_discovery: std::time::Duration,
135    /// Acquiring the writable pool lock.
136    pub writer_lock: std::time::Duration,
137    /// Cumulative packfile recovery/validation scan time in the shard pool.
138    pub packfile_recovery: std::time::Duration,
139    /// Number of packfiles passed through recovery/validation.
140    pub packfile_recovery_calls: u64,
141    /// Time spent opening packfiles and validating their headers.
142    pub packfile_open: std::time::Duration,
143    /// Number of packfiles successfully opened.
144    pub packfile_open_calls: u64,
145    /// Restoring pool metadata and persisted shard statistics.
146    pub metadata_restore: std::time::Duration,
147    /// Restoring pool.meta header and reading next pack ID.
148    pub pool_meta_restore: std::time::Duration,
149    /// Reading and restoring persisted snapshot counters from `shard_stats.bin`.
150    pub persisted_stats_restore: std::time::Duration,
151    /// Writing store.meta version marker via best-effort atomic write (fresh pool only; ZERO on existing pool).
152    pub store_meta_write: std::time::Duration,
153    /// Persisting pool.meta reservation and syncing file contents (fresh pool only; ZERO on existing pool).
154    pub pool_meta_persist: std::time::Duration,
155    /// Creating the initial packfile atomically, writing its header, syncing,
156    /// renaming, and performing the final directory sync (fresh pool only;
157    /// ZERO on existing pool).
158    pub initial_pack_create: std::time::Duration,
159    /// Unattributed time inside the `metadata_restore` span.
160    pub metadata_unattributed: std::time::Duration,
161    /// Shard-open time not covered by the named shard phases.
162    pub shard_open_unattributed: std::time::Duration,
163    /// Reading the collection-order and deleted-collections sidecars.
164    pub metadata_load: std::time::Duration,
165    /// Reading + decoding the persisted index checkpoint.
166    pub checkpoint_decode: std::time::Duration,
167    /// Recomputing the live `(pack_id, file_len)` set's fingerprint.
168    pub fingerprint: std::time::Duration,
169    /// Deserializing checkpoint index blobs into live collections (checkpoint
170    /// path) or building per-collection indexes from scanned records
171    /// (fallback path). On the checkpoint path this includes replaying any
172    /// fingerprint/generation-gated delta-log frames on top of the raw slots.
173    pub index_materialization: std::time::Duration,
174    /// Reading the delta log, validating its gates, and applying frames to
175    /// each affected collection (checkpoint path only; ZERO when there is no
176    /// committed log to replay).
177    pub delta_replay: std::time::Duration,
178    /// Grouping the replayed operations by collection and applying snapshot,
179    /// tombstone and generation gates, before any index is materialized
180    /// (checkpoint path only).
181    pub replay_prepare: std::time::Duration,
182    /// Seeding per-shard counts and home-shard assignment after the indexes are
183    /// materialized: the sidecar gate, or a slot walk (checkpoint path only).
184    pub bookkeeping: std::time::Duration,
185    /// Assembling the `PackfileStorage` from the loaded state, after the index
186    /// is built.
187    pub assemble: std::time::Duration,
188    /// Number of delta-log operations validated and applied during this open:
189    /// v3 slot frames, collection snapshots, and tombstones, or v2 frames
190    /// (checkpoint path only; zero when no committed log was replayed). A
191    /// deterministic replay-path signal, unlike the `delta_replay` duration,
192    /// which can round to zero on a fast machine.
193    pub delta_replay_operations: u64,
194    /// The full packfile scan + torn-tail recovery pass (fallback only).
195    pub full_scan: std::time::Duration,
196    /// Total synchronous wall time of the open.
197    pub total: std::time::Duration,
198    /// Which index-loading path was taken.
199    pub path: OpenPath,
200    /// Where per-shard counts and home-shard assignment came from (checkpoint
201    /// path only; the fallback path builds them from the scan).
202    pub bookkeeping_source: BookkeepingSource,
203}

240/// Where the time of one full index checkpoint went, phase by phase, so a
241/// slow rewrite (the delta-log rotation, a forced reclaim) can be attributed
242/// before anything is redesigned. Read through
243/// [`PackfileStorage::checkpoint_breakdown`].
244#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default)]
245pub struct CheckpointBreakdown {
246    /// The fsync of unsynced pack bytes done before any lock is taken.
247    pub pre_sync: std::time::Duration,
248    /// Waiting for every collection's put mutex and the creation lock.
249    pub lock_wait: std::time::Duration,
250    /// The pack flush and fsync under the locks (writers stalled).
251    pub locked_sync: std::time::Duration,
252    /// Fingerprint, snapshots, delta-epoch rotation and the coverage capture,
253    /// under the locks.
254    pub snapshot: std::time::Duration,
255    /// Serializing every collection's index into the checkpoint blobs.
256    pub serialize: std::time::Duration,
257    /// Writing the checkpoint, its fsync and rename.
258    pub write: std::time::Duration,
259    /// The directory fsync that makes the rename durable.
260    pub directory_sync: std::time::Duration,
261    /// Writing `journal.lsn`.
262    pub journal_lsn: std::time::Duration,
263    /// Reporting coverage and reclaiming the WAL (its rewrite and fsyncs).
264    pub reclaim: std::time::Duration,
265    /// Retiring the previous delta epoch.
266    pub retire: std::time::Duration,
267    /// The whole call.
268    pub total: std::time::Duration,
269    /// Size of the checkpoint file this call wrote, in bytes (0 if it could not
270    /// be read back).
271    pub checkpoint_bytes: u64,
272}
273
274impl CheckpointBreakdown {
275    /// Time in the call that belongs to no phase above: the final re-lock and
276    /// the bookkeeping around the phases. A large value means the attribution
277    /// is missing something.
278    #[must_use]
279    pub fn unaccounted(&self) -> std::time::Duration {
280        [
281            self.pre_sync,
282            self.lock_wait,
283            self.locked_sync,
284            self.snapshot,
285            self.serialize,
286            self.write,
287            self.directory_sync,
288            self.journal_lsn,
289            self.reclaim,
290            self.retire,
291        ]
292        .into_iter()
293        .fold(self.total, std::time::Duration::saturating_sub)
294    }
295}

297/// Wall-clock breakdown of one sync — the append-path `sync()` (dirty-scoped
298/// flush/fsync) or the full `sync_all` — by phase. The pack phases come from
299/// `ShardPool::last_sync_split` (which measures the flush and fsync legs
300/// separately) and the metadata phases from the sync method itself.
301#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
302pub struct SyncTimings {
303    /// Whether this barrier returned an error after collecting its partial timings.
304    pub failed: bool,
305    /// Writing buffered frames out to the pack files.
306    pub pack_flush: std::time::Duration,
307    /// fsync'ing the pack files.
308    pub pack_fsync: std::time::Duration,
309    /// Writing the shard→collection metadata sidecar.
310    pub sidecar: std::time::Duration,
311    /// Persisting the index checkpoint (complete rewrite) or appending the
312    /// incremental delta log instead (ZERO on the path not taken; the appended
313    /// case is measured when a dirty `sync()` can continue an existing log).
314    pub delta_log: std::time::Duration,
315    /// Persisting the index checkpoint.
316    pub checkpoint: std::time::Duration,
317    /// Coverage reporting and WAL reclaim performed by a coverage-step delta
318    /// batch (not by a checkpoint tail, whose phases are in
319    /// [`CheckpointBreakdown`]). This is the shared-segment rewrite and fsync
320    /// that shrinks the journal once every pool has reported.
321    pub reclaim: std::time::Duration,
322    /// Breakdown of [`Self::reclaim`]: deciding the shared-reclaim boundary
323    /// (directory lookup, or a scan when the directory could not be trusted).
324    pub reclaim_boundary: std::time::Duration,
325    /// Breakdown of [`Self::reclaim`]: reading and re-encoding the retained
326    /// suffix into the rebuilt segment.
327    pub reclaim_copy: std::time::Duration,
328    /// Breakdown of [`Self::reclaim`]: writing, fsyncing and renaming the
329    /// rebuilt segment into place. The likely disk cost.
330    pub reclaim_fsync: std::time::Duration,
331    /// Bytes the last reclaim rewrite moved and fsynced: the retained suffix.
332    /// This is what `reclaim_copy`/`reclaim_fsync` scale with.
333    pub reclaim_retained_bytes: u64,
334    /// The pool whose missing coverage stopped the last reclaim cut, so the
335    /// suffix could not be dropped sooner. None when an untagged frame stopped
336    /// it or the caller could not attribute it. Diagnostics only.
337    pub reclaim_blocked_by: Option<crate::layout::ShardType>,
338    /// Time spent in `remediate_lagging_pools`: in the non-background path this
339    /// force-checkpoints a pool holding the shared WAL back, and the caller
340    /// waits for it. Kept separate from [`Self::reclaim`] so a phase breakdown
341    /// can tell a coverage-step reclaim from a remediation checkpoint (whose
342    /// own journal wait would otherwise be miscounted as reclaim).
343    pub remediation: std::time::Duration,
344    /// Committing the pending write-ahead journal group (one sequential
345    /// fsync). Zero when no journal is configured.
346    pub wal: std::time::Duration,
347    /// Time spent waiting for the journal's single-writer mutex.
348    pub journal_lock_wait: std::time::Duration,
349    /// Time spent making the journal file durable.
350    pub journal_fsync: std::time::Duration,
351    /// Number of journal sync calls represented by this operation.
352    pub journal_sync_calls: u64,
353    /// Records appended to the journal by this operation.
354    pub journal_records: u64,
355    /// Whether this operation waited for the journal mutex.
356    pub journal_waiters: u64,
357    /// Whether this operation was already covered by another sync.
358    pub journal_coalesced: u64,
359    /// Number of journal sync callers active when this operation entered.
360    pub journal_in_flight: u64,
361    /// Time spent waiting for the shard pool's dirty-set lock in this barrier.
362    pub dirty_lock_wait: std::time::Duration,
363    /// Age of the oldest unpublished write when this barrier began.
364    pub pending_publish_age: std::time::Duration,
365    /// Total wall time of the `sync_all` call.
366    pub total: std::time::Duration,
367}

400impl SyncTimings {
401    /// Copy a coverage-step reclaim's phase breakdown into this barrier's
402    /// timings, so the `reclaim` total can be split into boundary, copy and
403    /// fsync. A no-op when no reclaim ran.
404    fn record_reclaim_phases(&mut self, reclaim: Option<&crate::journal::Reclaim>) {
405        if let Some(reclaim) = reclaim {
406            self.reclaim_boundary = reclaim.boundary;
407            self.reclaim_copy = reclaim.copy;
408            self.reclaim_fsync = reclaim.fsync;
409            self.reclaim_retained_bytes = reclaim.retained_bytes;
410            self.reclaim_blocked_by = reclaim.blocked_by;
411        }
412    }
413}

415/// Store-internal lifetime accumulator of per-phase sync wall time.
416///
417/// Each field is a running total in nanoseconds, added once per
418/// `sync()`/`sync_all` call in `count_sync_persistence`. This is the
419/// cumulative counterpart to the most-recent-only [`SyncTimings`] retained in
420/// `last_sync_timings`: without it, a run's scatter-vs-rewrite split can only
421/// be read off one (possibly atypical) barrier. [`Self::snapshot`] converts the
422/// atomics to a plain [`SyncTotalsSnapshot`] for [`RuntimeStats`].
423#[derive(Default)]
424struct SyncTotals {
425    /// Every sync that ran these accumulations (dirty or not).
426    calls: AtomicU64,
427    /// Sum of [`SyncTimings::total`].
428    total_ns: AtomicU64,
429    /// Sum of [`SyncTimings::pack_flush`].
430    pack_flush_ns: AtomicU64,
431    /// Sum of [`SyncTimings::pack_fsync`].
432    pack_fsync_ns: AtomicU64,
433    /// Sum of [`SyncTimings::sidecar`].
434    sidecar_ns: AtomicU64,
435    /// Sum of [`SyncTimings::delta_log`].
436    delta_log_ns: AtomicU64,
437    /// Sum of [`SyncTimings::checkpoint`].
438    checkpoint_ns: AtomicU64,
439    /// Sum of [`SyncTimings::wal`].
440    wal_ns: AtomicU64,
441    journal_lock_wait_ns: AtomicU64,
442    journal_fsync_ns: AtomicU64,
443    journal_sync_calls: AtomicU64,
444    journal_records: AtomicU64,
445    journal_waiters: AtomicU64,
446    journal_coalesced: AtomicU64,
447    max_journal_lock_wait_ns: AtomicU64,
448    max_journal_fsync_ns: AtomicU64,
449    dirty_lock_wait_ns: AtomicU64,
450    pending_publish_age_ns: AtomicU64,
451}
452
453impl SyncTotals {
454    fn add_duration(counter: &AtomicU64, duration: std::time::Duration) {
455        counter.fetch_add(
456            u64::try_from(duration.as_nanos()).unwrap_or(u64::MAX),
457            Ordering::Relaxed,
458        );
459    }
460
461    /// Fold one barrier's phase breakdown into the lifetime totals.
462    fn accumulate(&self, timings: &SyncTimings) {
463        self.calls.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
464        Self::add_duration(&self.total_ns, timings.total);
465        Self::add_duration(&self.pack_flush_ns, timings.pack_flush);
466        Self::add_duration(&self.pack_fsync_ns, timings.pack_fsync);
467        Self::add_duration(&self.sidecar_ns, timings.sidecar);
468        Self::add_duration(&self.delta_log_ns, timings.delta_log);
469        Self::add_duration(&self.checkpoint_ns, timings.checkpoint);
470        Self::add_duration(&self.wal_ns, timings.wal);
471        Self::add_duration(&self.journal_lock_wait_ns, timings.journal_lock_wait);
472        Self::add_duration(&self.journal_fsync_ns, timings.journal_fsync);
473        self.journal_sync_calls
474            .fetch_add(timings.journal_sync_calls, Ordering::Relaxed);
475        self.journal_records
476            .fetch_add(timings.journal_records, Ordering::Relaxed);
477        self.journal_waiters
478            .fetch_add(timings.journal_waiters, Ordering::Relaxed);
479        self.journal_coalesced
480            .fetch_add(timings.journal_coalesced, Ordering::Relaxed);
481        self.max_journal_lock_wait_ns.fetch_max(
482            u64::try_from(timings.journal_lock_wait.as_nanos()).unwrap_or(u64::MAX),
483            Ordering::Relaxed,
484        );
485        self.max_journal_fsync_ns.fetch_max(
486            u64::try_from(timings.journal_fsync.as_nanos()).unwrap_or(u64::MAX),
487            Ordering::Relaxed,
488        );
489        Self::add_duration(&self.dirty_lock_wait_ns, timings.dirty_lock_wait);
490        Self::add_duration(&self.pending_publish_age_ns, timings.pending_publish_age);
491    }
492
493    fn snapshot(&self) -> SyncTotalsSnapshot {
494        let duration =
495            |counter: &AtomicU64| std::time::Duration::from_nanos(counter.load(Ordering::Relaxed));
496        SyncTotalsSnapshot {
497            calls: self.calls.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
498            total: duration(&self.total_ns),
499            pack_flush: duration(&self.pack_flush_ns),
500            pack_fsync: duration(&self.pack_fsync_ns),
501            sidecar: duration(&self.sidecar_ns),
502            delta_log: duration(&self.delta_log_ns),
503            checkpoint: duration(&self.checkpoint_ns),
504            wal: duration(&self.wal_ns),
505            journal_lock_wait: duration(&self.journal_lock_wait_ns),
506            journal_fsync: duration(&self.journal_fsync_ns),
507            journal_sync_calls: self.journal_sync_calls.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
508            journal_records: self.journal_records.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
509            journal_waiters: self.journal_waiters.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
510            journal_coalesced: self.journal_coalesced.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
511            max_journal_lock_wait: duration(&self.max_journal_lock_wait_ns),
512            max_journal_fsync: duration(&self.max_journal_fsync_ns),
513            dirty_lock_wait: duration(&self.dirty_lock_wait_ns),
514            pending_publish_age: duration(&self.pending_publish_age_ns),
515        }
516    }
517
518    fn reset(&self) {
519        for counter in [
520            &self.calls,
521            &self.total_ns,
522            &self.pack_flush_ns,
523            &self.pack_fsync_ns,
524            &self.sidecar_ns,
525            &self.delta_log_ns,
526            &self.checkpoint_ns,
527            &self.wal_ns,
528            &self.journal_lock_wait_ns,
529            &self.journal_fsync_ns,
530            &self.journal_sync_calls,
531            &self.journal_records,
532            &self.journal_waiters,
533            &self.journal_coalesced,
534            &self.max_journal_lock_wait_ns,
535            &self.max_journal_fsync_ns,
536            &self.dirty_lock_wait_ns,
537            &self.pending_publish_age_ns,
538        ] {
539            counter.store(0, Ordering::Relaxed);
540        }
541    }
542}

592/// Fixed latency buckets used by sync diagnostics: `<1ms`, `<10ms`,
593/// `<100ms`, `<1s`, and `>=1s`.
594///
595/// Buckets are **non-cumulative**: `buckets[i]` counts only the observations
596/// that fell inside bucket `i`'s own range, so the total observation count is
597/// the sum of all five entries, not the last one.
598#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
599pub struct SyncLatencyHistogram {
600    /// Per-bucket observation counts, indexed to match the ranges above
601    /// (`buckets[0]` = `<1ms` … `buckets[4]` = `>=1s`). Non-cumulative.
602    pub buckets: [u64; 5],
603}
604
605impl SyncLatencyHistogram {
606    fn observe(&mut self, duration: std::time::Duration) {
607        let micros = duration.as_micros();
608        let bucket = if micros < 1_000 {
609            0
610        } else if micros < 10_000 {
611            1
612        } else if micros < 100_000 {
613            2
614        } else if micros < 1_000_000 {
615            3
616        } else {
617            4
618        };
619        self.buckets[bucket] = self.buckets[bucket].saturating_add(1);
620    }
621}

667/// Runtime sync diagnostics retained after the operation that produced them.
668#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
669#[non_exhaustive]
670pub struct SyncDiagnosticsSnapshot {
671    /// Non-cumulative [`SyncLatencyHistogram`] of journal fsync latencies
672    /// observed during the interval ending at the take. See
673    /// [`SyncLatencyHistogram::buckets`] for bucket membership.
674    pub fsync_latency: SyncLatencyHistogram,
675    /// Non-cumulative [`SyncLatencyHistogram`] of journal lock-wait latencies
676    /// observed during the interval ending at the take. See
677    /// [`SyncLatencyHistogram::buckets`] for bucket membership.
678    pub lock_wait_latency: SyncLatencyHistogram,
679    /// Maximum journal in-flight count observed during this snapshot.
680    /// Unlike the lifetime maxima in [`SyncTotalsSnapshot`], this value is
681    /// cleared by [`PackfileStorage::take_sync_diagnostics`].
682    pub peak_journal_in_flight: u64,
683    /// Maximum journal lock wait observed during this snapshot.
684    /// Unlike the lifetime maxima in [`SyncTotalsSnapshot`], this value is
685    /// cleared by [`PackfileStorage::take_sync_diagnostics`].
686    pub max_journal_lock_wait: std::time::Duration,
687    /// Maximum journal fsync duration observed during this snapshot.
688    /// Unlike the lifetime maxima in [`SyncTotalsSnapshot`], this value is
689    /// cleared by [`PackfileStorage::take_sync_diagnostics`].
690    pub max_journal_fsync: std::time::Duration,
691    /// The up-to-16 slowest sync samples observed during this snapshot,
692    /// ordered from slowest to fastest. This is interval-scoped and bounded,
693    /// not a lifetime history.
694    pub worst_syncs: Vec<SyncDiagnosticSample>,
695}

697#[derive(Default)]
698struct SyncDiagnostics {
699    fsync_latency: SyncLatencyHistogram,
700    lock_wait_latency: SyncLatencyHistogram,
701    peak_journal_in_flight: u64,
702    max_journal_lock_wait: std::time::Duration,
703    max_journal_fsync: std::time::Duration,
704    worst_syncs: Vec<SyncDiagnosticSample>,
705}
706
707impl SyncDiagnostics {
708    const WORST_LIMIT: usize = 16;
709
710    fn record(&mut self, sample: SyncDiagnosticSample) {
711        if sample.journal_path.is_some() {
712            if sample.journal_coalesced == 0 && !sample.journal_fsync.is_zero() {
713                self.fsync_latency.observe(sample.journal_fsync);
714            }
715            if sample.journal_coalesced == 0 {
716                self.lock_wait_latency.observe(sample.journal_lock_wait);
717            }
718            self.peak_journal_in_flight = self.peak_journal_in_flight.max(sample.journal_in_flight);
719            self.max_journal_lock_wait = self.max_journal_lock_wait.max(sample.journal_lock_wait);
720            self.max_journal_fsync = self.max_journal_fsync.max(sample.journal_fsync);
721        }
722        self.worst_syncs.push(sample);
723        self.worst_syncs
724            .sort_unstable_by_key(|sample| std::cmp::Reverse(sample.total));
725        self.worst_syncs.truncate(Self::WORST_LIMIT);
726    }
727
728    fn snapshot(&self) -> SyncDiagnosticsSnapshot {
729        SyncDiagnosticsSnapshot {
730            fsync_latency: self.fsync_latency,
731            lock_wait_latency: self.lock_wait_latency,
732            peak_journal_in_flight: self.peak_journal_in_flight,
733            max_journal_lock_wait: self.max_journal_lock_wait,
734            max_journal_fsync: self.max_journal_fsync,
735            worst_syncs: self.worst_syncs.clone(),
736        }
737    }
738
739    fn reset(&mut self) {
740        *self = Self::default();
741    }
742}

744/// Fixed latency buckets used by public operation diagnostics. Buckets are
745/// non-cumulative: `<50us`, `<100us`, `<250us`, `<1ms`, `<10ms`, and `>=10ms`.
746#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
747pub struct OperationLatency {
748    /// Number of timed operations.
749    pub calls: u64,
750    /// Sum of operation wall time.
751    pub total: std::time::Duration,
752    /// Largest observed operation wall time.
753    pub max: std::time::Duration,
754    /// Counts for `<50us`, `<100us`, `<250us`, `<1ms`, `<10ms`, and `>=10ms`.
755    pub buckets: [u64; 6],
756}
757
758#[derive(Default)]
759struct OperationLatencyTotals {
760    calls: AtomicU64,
761    total_ns: AtomicU64,
762    max_ns: AtomicU64,
763    buckets: [AtomicU64; 6],
764}
765
766impl OperationLatencyTotals {
767    fn observe(&self, duration: std::time::Duration) {
768        self.calls.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
769        self.total_ns.fetch_add(
770            u64::try_from(duration.as_nanos()).unwrap_or(u64::MAX),
771            Ordering::Relaxed,
772        );
773        self.max_ns.fetch_max(
774            u64::try_from(duration.as_nanos()).unwrap_or(u64::MAX),
775            Ordering::Relaxed,
776        );
777        let micros = duration.as_micros();
778        let bucket = if micros < 50 {
779            0
780        } else if micros < 100 {
781            1
782        } else if micros < 250 {
783            2
784        } else if micros < 1_000 {
785            3
786        } else if micros < 10_000 {
787            4
788        } else {
789            5
790        };
791        self.buckets[bucket].fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
792    }
793
794    fn snapshot(&self) -> OperationLatency {
795        OperationLatency {
796            calls: self.calls.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
797            total: std::time::Duration::from_nanos(self.total_ns.load(Ordering::Relaxed)),
798            max: std::time::Duration::from_nanos(self.max_ns.load(Ordering::Relaxed)),
799            buckets: std::array::from_fn(|index| self.buckets[index].load(Ordering::Relaxed)),
800        }
801    }
802
803    fn reset(&self) {
804        self.calls.store(0, Ordering::Relaxed);
805        self.total_ns.store(0, Ordering::Relaxed);
806        self.max_ns.store(0, Ordering::Relaxed);
807        for bucket in &self.buckets {
808            bucket.store(0, Ordering::Relaxed);
809        }
810    }
811}

813#[derive(Default)]
814struct OperationTimings {
815    get: OperationLatencyTotals,
816    get_many: OperationLatencyTotals,
817    get_many_with_refresh: OperationLatencyTotals,
818    put: OperationLatencyTotals,
819    put_many: OperationLatencyTotals,
820}

822impl OperationTimings {
823    fn reset(&self) {
824        self.get.reset();
825        self.get_many.reset();
826        self.get_many_with_refresh.reset();
827        self.put.reset();
828        self.put_many.reset();
829    }

832struct OperationTimer<'a> {
833    started: Option<std::time::Instant>,
834    totals: Option<&'a OperationLatencyTotals>,
835}

837impl<'a> OperationTimer<'a> {
838    fn disabled() -> Self {
839        Self {
840            started: None,
841            totals: None,
842        }
843    }
844
845    fn new(totals: &'a OperationLatencyTotals) -> Self {
846        Self {
847            started: Some(std::time::Instant::now()),

849        }

853impl Drop for OperationTimer<'_> {
854    fn drop(&mut self) {
855        if let (Some(totals), Some(started)) = (self.totals, self.started) {
856            totals.observe(started.elapsed());
857        }
858    }

861/// Bounds on a [`PackfileStorage::walk_ancestors`] call.
862///
863/// Without a cap, a walk whose `stop_at` set is never reached (e.g. the
864/// caller passed a stale or wrong boundary) silently degrades into "walk
865/// the entire history of this branch" — `max_nodes` is the safety valve
866/// for that case.
867#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default)]
868pub struct WalkLimits {
869    /// Stop discovering new ancestors once this many nodes have been
870    /// visited. `None` means unbounded (walk until `stop_at` or the
871    /// collection's true roots are reached).
872    pub max_nodes: Option<usize>,
873}

875/// Lazy, ancestor-first iterator over the result of
876/// [`PackfileStorage::walk_ancestors`].
877///
878/// Every node was already resolved (hash-verified, same as [`PackfileStorage::get`])
879/// against one frozen generation snapshot while [`PackfileStorage::walk_ancestors`]
880/// built the walk — this iterator just replays that in ancestor-first
881/// order. No further store access happens here, so a repack that runs
882/// after the walk was built can't cause a node to go missing partway
883/// through iteration.
884pub struct DagWalk {
885    order: std::vec::IntoIter<[u8; 16]>,
886    resolved: HashMap<[u8; 16], NodeData>,
887}
888
889impl Iterator for DagWalk {
890    type Item = Result<(NodeId, NodeData), StorageError>;
891
892    fn next(&mut self) -> Option<Self::Item> {
893        let hash = self.order.next()?;
894        let data = self
895            .resolved
896            .remove(&hash)
897            .expect("order only contains hashes this walk itself resolved");
898        Some(Ok((hash, data)))
899    }
900}

943/// Per-pack, per-collection on-disk bytes as `physical_layout` reports them
944/// (every appended frame, superseded ones included).
945fn disk_bytes_from_physical(
946    physical: &crate::packfile::layout::PhysicalLayout,
947) -> HashMap<u64, HashMap<[u8; 16], u64>> {
948    let mut bytes: HashMap<u64, HashMap<[u8; 16], u64>> = HashMap::new();
949    for (collection_id, layout) in &physical.collections {
950        for (pack_id, pack_bytes) in &layout.pack_bytes {
951            bytes
952                .entry(*pack_id)
953                .or_default()
954                .insert(*collection_id, *pack_bytes);
955        }
956    }
957    bytes
958}

960/// Magic bytes + version identifying the persisted shard→collection directory
961/// format (see `PackfileStorage::persist_shard_collections`).
962///
963/// Pre-release, no compatibility fallback: an unrecognized version is
964/// treated exactly like a missing/corrupt file (see
965/// `read_persisted_shard_collections`) — reset or let the next sync
966/// regenerate it, not a format this reader tries to still understand.
967/// This sidecar has changed shape three times already (adding insertion
968/// order, switching `slot` for `pack_id`, then v4 adding the
969/// pack-fingerprint gate); none of that carries forward, since nothing
970/// depends on reading a store from before the current format existed.
971const SHARD_ROOMS_MAGIC: &[u8; 4] = b"MSRM";
972/// v5 adds physical bytes to the reduced bookkeeping and pins it to the exact
973/// `(pack_id, file_len)` set by carrying the same `pack_fingerprint` as the
974/// index checkpoint.
975const SHARD_ROOMS_VERSION: u8 = 5;
976/// Header size: magic(4) + version(1) + `pack_fingerprint(8)` + `persisted_at(8)`.
977const SHARD_ROOMS_HEADER_LEN: usize = 4 + 1 + 8 + 8;
978/// One entry: `pack_id`(8) + `collection_id`(16) + count(8) + the
979/// collection's stable insertion ordinal(8).
980const SHARD_ROOMS_RECORD_LEN: usize = 8 + 16 + 8 + 8 + 8;
981
982/// The largest record offset `IndexEntry` can represent: its 32-bit offset
983/// field stores `offset + 1`, reserving the all-zeros encoding for the empty
984/// sentinel. Offsets beyond this can only come from legacy or externally
985/// created oversized packs — this engine's own writes rotate long before
986/// reaching it (`MAX_SHARD_BYTES` caps each shard's file size).
987const PACK_INDEX_OFFSET_LIMIT: u64 = crate::index::IndexEntry::MAX_OFFSET;
988
989/// Byte ceiling for the incremental index delta log. Once a session's
990/// accumulated frames exceed this, the next `sync()` stops appending and does
991/// a full checkpoint rewrite (which truncates the log), keeping replay cost
992/// and the log file bounded. Frames are 36 bytes each, so this is on the order
993/// of ~230k appends between full rewrites.
994const DELTA_LOG_CAP_BYTES: u64 = 256 * 1024 * 1024;
995
996/// What the disk records of a store's durable index state, read in one pass:
997/// the newest journal coverage the checkpoint and its delta log claim, and the
998/// fingerprint of the durable pack state they describe (0 if unknown).
999#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone, Copy)]
1000struct DurableIndexState {
1001    covered_lsn: u64,
1002    fingerprint: u64,
1003}
1004
1005/// A delta batch that does not fit under the delta-log cap.
1006#[derive(Debug)]
1007struct DeltaBatchTooLarge {
1008    batch_bytes: usize,
1009    log_bytes: u64,
1010    cap: u64,
1011}
1012
1013impl std::fmt::Display for DeltaBatchTooLarge {
1014    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
1015        write!(
1016            f,
1017            "the next delta batch of {} bytes does not fit: log {} bytes, cap {}",
1018            self.batch_bytes, self.log_bytes, self.cap
1019        )
1020    }
1021}
1022
1023impl std::error::Error for DeltaBatchTooLarge {}
1024
1025// The delta-log rotation length is three quarters of the cap, see
1026// `PackfileStorage::delta_log_rotate_bytes`. It cannot promise the next batch
1027// fits: a batch can carry whole-index snapshots, so a batch that does not is
1028// caught when it is built (`is_delta_batch_too_large`) and also rotates.
1029
1030/// Candidate offsets closer than this on the same shard count as one
1031/// sequential read run when measuring a `get_many` batch's locality.
1032/// `record_disk_len` is `frame_len + 8` and frames are at least
1033/// `FRAME_FIXED_LEN` bytes, so a gap this small means no more than one
1034/// minimum-size interleaved foreign frame sits between two candidate frames —
1035/// reading both is effectively a single sequential range. It is a shape
1036/// heuristic for the optimizer's "one read plan per shard" target, not exact
1037/// adjacency (that would require a per-candidate frame-length probe).
1038const READ_RUN_GAP_BYTES: u64 = 128;
1039
1040/// Largest on-disk size of a single frame: the 4-byte length prefix, a
1041/// [`packfile::MAX_RECORD_LEN`]-bounded body, and the 4-byte CRC. Used as the
1042/// per-candidate frame-length estimate when planning merged read extents: it
1043/// over-approximates so the plan never advises short of a frame's true end,
1044/// and it avoids a per-candidate length-prefix probe (which would fault in the
1045/// very cold page the plan exists to prefetch).
1046const MAX_FRAME_DISK_LEN: u64 = (packfile::MAX_RECORD_LEN + 8) as u64;
1047
1048/// Tuning for `get_many`'s merged read plan.
1049///
1050/// `get_many` probes the lossy index once per requested id, so a large batch
1051/// yields many candidate `(shard, offset)` locations scattered across a few
1052/// shards. Without a plan each candidate is read independently; on rotational
1053/// media the per-candidate seeks dominate. When enabled, candidates on the same
1054/// shard whose offsets are within [`Self::merge_gap_bytes`] of each other are
1055/// melded into one contiguous extent, and each extent is prefetched with
1056/// `madvise(MADV_WILLNEED)` before resolution — the kernel then reads it as one
1057/// sequential run while the existing per-candidate decode path still verifies
1058/// every requested hash (lossy-index false positives included).
1059///
1060/// # Measured behaviour (cold-cache, 1M records × 1 KiB, careful HDD vs SSD)
1061///
1062/// This plan is **rotational-media (HDD) only** and must not be enabled by
1063/// default anywhere:
1064///
1065/// - **Wins on HDD** when target spacing is roughly 700 KiB or more: 1.9-3×
1066///   faster than the `MADV_RANDOM` baseline, and 2.6-5× faster than
1067///   independent reads. The win comes from prefetching target neighborhoods,
1068///   not from reading through gaps — any gap from 0 to ~256 KiB performed about
1069///   equally.
1070/// - **Neutral on HDD** by ~174 KiB spacing (all policies ~1.0×): the batch is
1071///   dense enough that independent reads already touch most pages.
1072/// - **Loses on SSD** (0.6-0.85× vs `MADV_RANDOM`): there is no seek to avoid,
1073///   so reading through gaps is pure waste, and the plan reads far more bytes
1074///   than the readahead-suppressing alternative.
1075///
1076/// [`Self::random_advice`] — suppressing kernel readahead with `MADV_RANDOM`
1077/// and no planning at all — is the portable win: 4.5-6.5× on SSD, 1.4-3.4× on
1078/// sparse HDD, and neutral on dense HDD. Prefer it unless the workload is a
1079/// sparse batch on rotational media.
1080#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
1081pub struct ReadPlanPolicy {
1082    /// Candidate offsets at most this far apart (start to start, on the same
1083    /// shard) are melded into one prefetched extent. Reading through a gap can
1084    /// be cheaper than a seek, but a gap far larger than the target spacing
1085    /// makes the plan read through most of the file for no benefit — measured
1086    /// on a cold-cache HDD, every gap from 0 to ~256 KiB performed about
1087    /// equally, and a 2 MiB gap over-merged. [`ReadPlanPolicy::prefetch`] uses
1088    /// 64 KiB; `0` melds only adjacent offsets.
1089    pub merge_gap_bytes: u64,
1090    /// Hard ceiling on one merged extent. Bounds the bytes read through gaps
1091    /// and keeps a dense batch from collapsing into a single unbounded
1092    /// prefetch. `0` disables prefetching entirely.
1093    pub max_extent_bytes: u64,
1094    /// Batches with fewer candidate locations than this skip planning: a
1095    /// handful of reads gains nothing from a plan, and the grouping/sort is
1096    /// pure overhead.
1097    pub min_batch_candidates: usize,
1098    /// When set, advise each shard mapping `MADV_RANDOM` before reading, with
1099    /// no planning at all. A random-access hint suppresses the kernel's
1100    /// sequential readahead, so a scattered `get_many` reads only the pages
1101    /// it faults rather than having readahead amplify each one into a large
1102    /// block read.
1103    ///
1104    /// This is the **portable** win and the one to reach for first: measured
1105    /// at 4.5-6.5× faster than independent reads on SSD, 1.4-3.4× on sparse
1106    /// HDD, and neutral on dense HDD, with no device-specific tuning. Extent
1107    /// planning ([`Self::prefetch`]) only beats it on sparse rotational media.
1108    /// `false` on the presets that plan.
1109    ///
1110    /// # Warm and untested cases
1111    ///
1112    /// A warm-cache run showed no regression from suppression (random vs
1113    /// independent reads was 0.94-1.20× at 1-5 ms, i.e. within the spread), so
1114    /// the cold win does not reverse when data is resident. But only sparse
1115    /// *point* reads were tested: no warm dense case.
1116    ///
1117    /// # Persistent advice, and why this is not a default
1118    ///
1119    /// `madvise` is persistent mapping state, and repack/compaction read
1120    /// records through the *same* shard mmap this sets (`scan_full_adjacency`,
1121    /// `copy_record_to_shard`), so suppression can leak into them; nothing here
1122    /// resets it. A repack benchmark (fresh store per pass, 5 passes, 1M
1123    /// records) measured **no regression** — `REPACK_RANDOM_VS_PLAIN` = 0.998
1124    /// with fully overlapping ranges — but that store had **no edges**, so the
1125    /// mmap adjacency walk barely ran and the result mostly reflects
1126    /// `scan_packfile`, which uses its own file handle and is unaffected. The
1127    /// mmap walk path is therefore still unmeasured, and this null does not
1128    /// clear suppression for the default.
1129    ///
1130    /// Keep this opt-in. Making it safe by default needs the advice scoped to
1131    /// the point-read path — a separate mapping/fd for `get_many`, or an
1132    /// explicit concurrency-safe reset (`MADV_NORMAL`/`SEQUENTIAL`) before
1133    /// scan/compaction reads. Measurements are from one rotational HDD and one
1134    /// cheap SATA SSD; `NVMe` and other drives are untested.
1135    pub random_advice: bool,
1136}
1137
1138impl Default for ReadPlanPolicy {
1139    /// Disabled: the defaults change no behaviour, so nothing regresses on
1140    /// existing callers. The portable improvement is
1141    /// [`ReadPlanPolicy::random_advice`] (readahead suppression); extent
1142    /// planning ([`ReadPlanPolicy::prefetch`]) is rotational-media only. A
1143    /// store that wants either opts in explicitly.
1144    fn default() -> Self {
1145        Self::disabled()
1146    }
1147}
1148
1149impl ReadPlanPolicy {
1150    /// A plan that never prefetches: no extent is ever built.
1151    #[must_use]
1152    pub fn disabled() -> Self {
1153        Self {
1154            merge_gap_bytes: 0,
1155            max_extent_bytes: 0,
1156            min_batch_candidates: usize::MAX,
1157            random_advice: false,
1158        }
1159    }
1160
1161    /// No extent planning, but advise each shard `MADV_RANDOM` before reading
1162    /// so kernel readahead does not amplify a scattered batch into large
1163    /// sequential reads. The cheap baseline to compare a real plan against:
1164    /// if this alone captures the win, the planner earns nothing.
1165    #[must_use]
1166    pub fn random_advice() -> Self {
1167        Self {
1168            merge_gap_bytes: 0,
1169            max_extent_bytes: 0,
1170            min_batch_candidates: usize::MAX,
1171            random_advice: true,
1172        }
1173    }
1174
1175    /// A starting point for rotational (HDD) storage: meld candidates within
1176    /// 64 KiB, up to an 8 MiB extent, once a batch has at least 16 candidate
1177    /// locations. On a cold-cache HDD benchmark, any gap from 0 up to ~256 KiB
1178    /// performed about equally well, while the earlier 2 MiB guess over-merged
1179    /// and read through far more of the file than it saved in seeks. See the
1180    /// type docs for the measured HDD-only results and why readahead
1181    /// suppression ([`Self::random_advice`]) is the more portable win.
1182    #[must_use]
1183    pub fn prefetch() -> Self {
1184        Self {
1185            merge_gap_bytes: 64 * 1024,
1186            max_extent_bytes: 8 * 1024 * 1024,
1187            min_batch_candidates: 16,
1188            random_advice: false,
1189        }
1190    }
1191
1192    /// Whether a batch with `candidate_count` candidate locations should be
1193    /// planned.
1194    fn wants(&self, candidate_count: usize) -> bool {
1195        self.max_extent_bytes > 0 && candidate_count >= self.min_batch_candidates
1196    }
1197}
1198
1199/// One contiguous byte extent on a shard to prefetch as a unit.
1200#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
1201struct ReadExtent {
1202    /// Shard slot the extent lives on.
1203    slot: u16,
1204    /// Inclusive start offset (a candidate frame's length prefix).
1205    start: u64,
1206    /// Exclusive end offset.
1207    end: u64,
1208}
1209
1210/// Meld a shard's sorted candidate offsets into prefetch extents.
1211///
1212/// `per_shard` maps each touched shard slot to its candidate offsets, each
1213/// vector sorted ascending. A run starts at the first offset and absorbs the
1214/// next while the start-to-start distance stays within
1215/// [`ReadPlanPolicy::merge_gap_bytes`] and the resulting span stays within
1216/// [`ReadPlanPolicy::max_extent_bytes`]. A run's end is its last offset plus
1217/// [`MAX_FRAME_DISK_LEN`] (see that constant for why the frame length is
1218/// estimated rather than probed).
1219fn plan_read_extents(
1220    per_shard: &HashMap<u16, Vec<u64>>,
1221    policy: ReadPlanPolicy,
1222) -> Vec<ReadExtent> {
1223    let mut extents = Vec::new();
1224    // A single candidate's extent is always `MAX_FRAME_DISK_LEN` long, so a
1225    // cap below that would split every candidate onto its own extent. Floor it.
1226    let cap = policy.max_extent_bytes.max(MAX_FRAME_DISK_LEN);
1227    for (&slot, offsets) in per_shard {
1228        let Some(&first) = offsets.first() else {
1229            continue;
1230        };
1231        let mut run_start = first;
1232        let mut run_last = first;
1233        for &offset in &offsets[1..] {
1234            let gap_ok = offset.saturating_sub(run_last) <= policy.merge_gap_bytes;
1235            let span_ok = offset
1236                .saturating_add(MAX_FRAME_DISK_LEN)
1237                .saturating_sub(run_start)
1238                <= cap;
1239            if gap_ok && span_ok {
1240                run_last = offset;
1241            } else {
1242                extents.push(ReadExtent {
1243                    slot,
1244                    start: run_start,
1245                    end: run_last.saturating_add(MAX_FRAME_DISK_LEN),
1246                });
1247                run_start = offset;
1248                run_last = offset;
1249            }
1250        }
1251        extents.push(ReadExtent {
1252            slot,
1253            start: run_start,
1254            end: run_last.saturating_add(MAX_FRAME_DISK_LEN),
1255        });
1256    }
1257    // `per_shard` is a `HashMap`, so iteration (and therefore extent order)
1258    // would otherwise be nondeterministic across runs. Prefetch order does not
1259    // affect correctness, but a stable order keeps plans reproducible and
1260    // testable.
1261    extents.sort_unstable_by_key(|extent| (extent.slot, extent.start));
1262    extents
1263}
1264
1265/// Reject a record whose in-shard offset the 32-bit `IndexEntry` field cannot
1266/// represent, so the caller surfaces a `StorageError::Corrupt` instead of
1267/// silently dropping the record (or panicking in `IndexEntry::new`).
1268fn check_index_offset(slot: u16, hash: &[u8; 16], offset: u64) -> Result<(), StorageError> {
1269    if offset > PACK_INDEX_OFFSET_LIMIT {
1270        return Err(StorageError::Corrupt(format!(
1271            "shard {slot} holds record {hash:?} at offset {offset}, beyond the index offset limit {PACK_INDEX_OFFSET_LIMIT}"
1272        )));
1273    }
1274    Ok(())
1275}
1276
1277/// One persisted `(pack, collection)` bookkeeping record.
1278#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
1279pub struct PersistedShardRoom {
1280    /// Packfile identity.
1281    pub pack_id: u64,
1282    /// Collection identity.
1283    pub collection_id: [u8; 16],
1284    /// Number of records attributed to this collection in the pack.
1285    pub count: u64,
1286    /// Stable collection insertion order.
1287    pub insertion_order: u64,
1288    /// Physical bytes attributed to this collection.
1289    pub disk_bytes: u64,
1290}
1291
1292/// A decoded shard→collection directory: the pack set it was written
1293/// against, when it was written, and the per-(pack, collection) records.
1294#[derive(Clone)]
1295pub struct PersistedShardDirectory {
1296    /// The `pack_fingerprint` of the `(pack_id, file_len)` set the counts
1297    /// apply to. Only a directory whose fingerprint equals the index
1298    /// checkpoint's may serve open's per-shard bookkeeping without re-walking
1299    /// every slot — any other directory is stale (or corrupt) and must be
1300    /// ignored in favor of the slot walk.
1301    pub fingerprint: u64,
1302    /// Unix-seconds timestamp of when the directory was persisted.
1303    pub persisted_at: u64,
1304    /// One record per (pack, collection) the store contains.
1305    pub records: Vec<PersistedShardRoom>,
1306}
1307
1308/// Decode the small inspection sidecar. This is deliberately shared by all
1309/// read-only CLI summary helpers so they agree on validation and format
1310/// compatibility.
1311#[must_use]
1312pub fn read_persisted_shard_collections(
1313    base_dir: &std::path::Path,
1314) -> Option<PersistedShardDirectory> {
1315    let buf = fs::read(base_dir.join("shard_collections.bin")).ok()?;
1316    if buf.len() < SHARD_ROOMS_HEADER_LEN
1317        || &buf[0..4] != SHARD_ROOMS_MAGIC
1318        || buf[4] != SHARD_ROOMS_VERSION
1319    {
1320        return None;
1321    }
1322    let body = &buf[SHARD_ROOMS_HEADER_LEN..];
1323    if body.len().checked_rem(SHARD_ROOMS_RECORD_LEN) != Some(0) {
1324        return None;
1325    }
1326    let fingerprint = u64::from_le_bytes(buf[5..13].try_into().ok()?);
1327    let persisted_at = u64::from_le_bytes(buf[13..21].try_into().ok()?);
1328    let records = body
1329        .chunks_exact(SHARD_ROOMS_RECORD_LEN)
1330        .map(|chunk| {
1331            let pack_id = u64::from_le_bytes(chunk[0..8].try_into().ok()?);
1332            let mut collection_id = [0u8; 16];
1333            collection_id.copy_from_slice(&chunk[8..24]);
1334            let count = u64::from_le_bytes(chunk[24..32].try_into().ok()?);
1335            let insertion_order = u64::from_le_bytes(chunk[32..40].try_into().ok()?);
1336            let disk_bytes = u64::from_le_bytes(chunk[40..48].try_into().ok()?);
1337            Some(PersistedShardRoom {
1338                pack_id,
1339                collection_id,
1340                count,
1341                insertion_order,
1342                disk_bytes,
1343            })
1344        })
1345        .collect::<Option<Vec<_>>>()?;
1346    Some(PersistedShardDirectory {
1347        fingerprint,
1348        persisted_at,
1349        records,
1350    })
1351}
1352
1353/// The durable insertion order supplied by the inspection directory.
1354fn persisted_collection_order(base_dir: &std::path::Path) -> Option<Vec<[u8; 16]>> {
1355    let records = read_persisted_shard_collections(base_dir)?.records;
1356    let mut orders: HashMap<[u8; 16], u64> = HashMap::new();
1357    for record in records {
1358        let order = record.insertion_order;
1359        orders
1360            .entry(record.collection_id)
1361            .and_modify(|current| *current = (*current).min(order))
1362            .or_insert(order);
1363    }
1364    let mut collections: Vec<([u8; 16], u64)> = orders.into_iter().collect();
1365    collections.sort_unstable_by_key(|(collection_id, order)| (*order, *collection_id));
1366    Some(
1367        collections
1368            .into_iter()
1369            .map(|(collection_id, _)| collection_id)
1370            .collect(),
1371    )
1372}
1373
1374/// Disambiguates concurrent `persist_shard_collections` tmp filenames within
1375/// this process, paired with the process id for uniqueness across
1376/// processes — same rationale as `shard::STATS_TMP_COUNTER`.
1377static SHARD_ROOMS_TMP_COUNTER: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);
1378
1379/// Immutable snapshot of a collection's in-memory state.
1380///
1381/// Index and cache are bundled so readers see a consistent triple
1382/// via a single `ArcSwap::load()` — no three-lock coordination.
1383///
1384/// `generation` is the collection index's structural generation: it
1385/// increments on every capacity-changing or shape-changing rebuild (growth,
1386/// repack, refresh) and is preserved across plain COW writes. The delta log
1387/// stamps every frame with the generation it was recorded under, so a log
1388/// never replay-applies frames for a pre-resize table onto a resized one.
1389#[derive(Clone)]
1390struct RoomGeneration {
1391    index: LossyIndex,
1392    cache: Arc<NodeCache>,
1393    generation: u64,
1394}
1395
1396/// Where a just-appended record lives: its shard slot, byte offset, and on-disk
1397/// length.
1398#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
1399struct RecordLocator {
1400    slot: u16,
1401    offset: u64,
1402    len: u64,
1403}
1404
1405struct PutManyProgress {
1406    generation: u64,
1407    owned_index: Option<LossyIndex>,
1408    structural_change: bool,
1409    index_needs_rebuild: bool,
1410    /// Redo inputs for the entries inserted so far: `(id, slot, offset, record_len)`.
1411    pending_deltas: Vec<(NodeId, u16, u64, u64)>,
1412    pending_shard_collections: Vec<(u64, u64)>,
1413    pending_shard_collection_counts: Vec<u64>,
1414    invalidate_delta: bool,
1415    undo_log: Vec<EntryUndo>,
1416}
