1418/// Index tables that must advance together when a reader reloads a checkpoint.
1419/// Individual table guards are mapped from this shared lock, so a reload's
1420/// replacement is indivisible with respect to every table lookup.
1421struct IndexTables {
1422    collections: HashMap<[u8; 16], ArcSwap<RoomGeneration>>,
1423    collection_order: Vec<[u8; 16]>,
1424    shard_collections: HashMap<u64, HashMap<[u8; 16], u64>>,
1425    collection_shards: HashMap<[u8; 16], HashSet<u64>>,
1426    collection_disk_bytes: HashMap<u64, HashMap<[u8; 16], u64>>,
1427}
1428
1429/// Session state for the incremental index delta log (`index.delta`).
1430///
1431/// A fresh checkpoint rewrite re-bases this structure. Between rewrites, live
1432/// index mutations are coalesced per collection as v3 slot updates, whole-index
1433/// snapshots, or deletions, then appended by the next `sync()`.
1434#[derive(Clone, Default)]
1435struct DeltaLogState {
1436    /// Fingerprint of the checkpoint this session continues. `None` when the
1437    /// store opened via a full rescan and hasn't rewritten a checkpoint yet —
1438    /// every such open forces the next dirty sync to a full rewrite.
1439    base_fingerprint: Option<u64>,
1440    /// Generation of each collection at the last checkpoint or snapshot.
1441    base_generations: HashMap<[u8; 16], u64>,
1442    /// Stable order keys preserved across deletes and snapshots.
1443    base_order: HashMap<[u8; 16], u64>,
1444    /// Monotonic order key allocated to the next newly created collection.
1445    next_order_key: u64,
1446    /// Per-collection operations pending for the next v3 append. Snapshot and
1447    /// deletion entries subsume earlier slot updates for their collection.
1448    pending: HashMap<[u8; 16], PendingDelta>,
1449    /// Bytes already committed to the on-disk log (upper bound that a fresh
1450    /// header may still need to be written). Resets to zero on rewrite.
1451    log_bytes: u64,
1452    /// Wire version of the active on-disk epoch. A v2 epoch is read for
1453    /// compatibility but is rebased to v3 before any further writes.
1454    log_version: u8,
1455    /// The `pack_id`s of the packs the checkpoint of this epoch recorded in its
1456    /// pack table. Every slot a delta operation of this epoch names resolves
1457    /// through that table, so only while every live pack is in it can a reader
1458    /// apply the log; a pack created since forces a full checkpoint instead of a
1459    /// delta coverage batch.
1460    base_pack_ids: HashSet<u64>,
1461    /// Bytes of the on-disk log an fsync has covered. Ordinary delta batches are
1462    /// not fsynced (the log is rebuildable acceleration), so without this a
1463    /// coverage batch, which must be durable, would pay for every batch written
1464    /// since the epoch began in one fsync.
1465    log_synced_bytes: u64,
1466    /// The highest redo `delta_seq` assigned so far in this pool. It resumes above
1467    /// the checkpoint's base sequence at open and is written into the next
1468    /// checkpoint as its base, so the ordering key survives reopen and rotation.
1469    delta_seq_high: u64,
1470}
1471
1472#[derive(Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
1473enum PendingDelta {
1474    /// Logical redo records for the collection, in the order they were recorded
1475    /// (each carries its `delta_seq`).
1476    Redo(Vec<RedoRecord>),
1477    Snapshot,
1478    Delete {
1479        generation: u64,
1480    },
1481}
1482
1483struct V3PendingBatch {
1484    operations: Vec<DeltaOperation>,
1485    generation_updates: Vec<([u8; 16], u64)>,
1486    order_updates: Vec<([u8; 16], u64)>,
1487    next_order_key: u64,
1488}
1489
1490/// Written-but-unsynced pack bytes at which a sync with a journal enabled also
1491/// fsyncs the dirty packs. With a journal, a sync only has to fsync the WAL, so
1492/// pack data would otherwise pile up unsynced until the next checkpoint and be
1493/// flushed all at once there, under the collection locks. Fsyncing it in slices
1494/// as it accumulates keeps that burst small. Zero disables it.
1495pub const DEFAULT_PACK_FSYNC_BUDGET_BYTES: u64 = 8 << 20;
1496
1497/// Unsynced delta-log bytes at which an ordinary delta batch also fsyncs the
1498/// log. A coverage batch must be durable, and its fsync covers everything
1499/// written to the log before it, so leaving the backlog to it would make the
1500/// batch that lets the journal be reclaimed pay for the whole epoch at once.
1501/// Zero disables it.
1502pub const DEFAULT_DELTA_FSYNC_BUDGET_BYTES: u64 = 1 << 20;
1503
1504/// A content-addressed packfile storage engine backed by a global shard pool.
1505///
1506/// All collections share a small pool of shard files (~4, each ~2GB), keeping
1507/// file descriptor usage constant regardless of collection count.
1508///
1509/// Per-collection state (index + cache) is bundled in an immutable
1510/// `RoomGeneration` and swapped atomically via `ArcSwap`:
1511///
1512/// - **Reads**: `load_full()` once, see a consistent snapshot.
1513/// - **Writes**: build new generation under put lock, swap atomically.
1514/// - **Delete**: drop the generation — cache disappears with it.
1515///
1516/// # Timing instrumentation
1517///
1518/// Every open records a wall-clock breakdown of its phases (and which
1519/// index-loading path it took) into [`OpenTimings`], surfaced via
1520/// [`PackfileStorage::open_timings`]; every `sync_all` records a per-phase
1521/// breakdown into [`SyncTimings`], surfaced via
1522/// [`PackfileStorage::sync_timings`]. These exist to decide whether startup
1523/// is dominated by deserialization (justifying mmap-ready persisted
1524/// indexes) or by validation I/O, and whether sync is dominated by the
1525/// checkpoint rewrite — before either format change is built. The cost is a
1526/// handful of `Instant::now()` deltas on the open/sync paths only, never
1527/// per record.
1528///
1529/// The phases measured:
1530/// - **shard directory discovery/open**: directory scan plus each pack
1531///   file's open and (for the writer) writer-lock take.
1532/// - **metadata load**: the collection-order and deleted-collections
1533///   sidecars.
1534/// - **checkpoint decode**: reading + decoding the persisted index
1535///   checkpoint from disk.
1536/// - **fingerprint**: recomputing the live set of `(pack_id, file_len)`
1537///   tuples and hashing them for validation against the checkpoint.
1538/// - **index materialization**: deserializing checkpoint index blobs, or
1539///   (on the fallback path) building per-collection indexes from a scan.
1540/// - **full scan**: the fallback path's packfile scan + torn-tail recovery
1541///   (zero on the checkpoint path).
1542pub struct PackfileStorage {
1543    shards: ShardPool,
1544    /// Collection indexes and their cross-table bookkeeping, replaced as one
1545    /// snapshot when a read-only worker reloads a checkpoint.
1546    index_tables: RwLock<IndexTables>,
1547    pinned: PinnedNodes,
1548    base_dir: PathBuf,
1549    swizzle: Option<SwizzleFn>,
1550    put_locks: parking_lot::Mutex<HashMap<[u8; 16], Arc<parking_lot::Mutex<()>>>>,
1551    /// Per-collection gates for read-miss refreshes. A reader that observes
1552    /// an index miss waits for an in-flight refresh of the same collection
1553    /// instead of starting another full scan.
1554    refresh_locks: parking_lot::Mutex<HashMap<[u8; 16], Arc<parking_lot::Mutex<()>>>>,
1555    /// Pack fingerprint observed at the last read-miss refresh per collection.
1556    /// A subsequent miss with the same fingerprint skips the expensive rebuild.
1557    last_refresh_fingerprint: parking_lot::Mutex<HashMap<[u8; 16], u64>>,
1558    /// Durable pool fingerprint observed when this handle was opened. This is
1559    /// the baseline for collections that did not yet exist at open time.
1560    initial_durable_fingerprint: u64,
1561    /// Serializes the *publication* of a brand-new collection against a
1562    /// checkpoint rewrite (see `persist_index_checkpoint`). Creates take this
1563    /// lock shared for the whole put; the checkpoint holds it exclusive for
1564    /// the fingerprint→snapshot window, so a record whose bytes land on disk
1565    /// mid-rewrite can never be fingerprinted without its collection being
1566    /// snapshotted in the same checkpoint. Existing-collection puts never
1567    /// touch it (their `put_mutex` already gates them), so the shrink-latency
1568    /// property the epoch-handoff window exists to protect is untouched.
1569    collection_creation: parking_lot::RwLock<()>,
1570    /// In-memory cache of the `deleted.collections` file, seeded once at
1571    /// `open()` from disk. Guards both the set and the read-modify-write of
1572    /// the backing file, so a plain membership check (the common case: most
1573    /// collections were never deleted) never touches disk. Collection locks
1574    /// protect a collection's lifecycle, but distinct collections may be
1575    /// recreated or deleted concurrently, hence the separate lock here.
1576    deleted_collections: parking_lot::Mutex<HashSet<[u8; 16]>>,
1577    live_roots: RwLock<HashMap<[u8; 16], Vec<NodeId>>>,
1578    repack_threshold_entries: AtomicU64,
1579    cache_capacity: usize,
1580    /// Per-instance index config: seed from the pool's `pool.meta`, floor
1581    /// and load factor from defaults (or future tuning).
1582    index_config: crate::index::IndexConfig,
1583    /// Merged-read-plan tuning for `get_many` (see [`ReadPlanPolicy`]).
1584    /// Read once per batch; settable at runtime via
1585    /// [`Self::set_read_plan_policy`].
1586    read_plan: parking_lot::RwLock<ReadPlanPolicy>,
1587    /// Total number of `repack_collection_reachable` calls across all collections.
1588    repack_count: AtomicU64,
1589    /// Total records kept (rewritten into the new generation) across all repacks.
1590    repack_kept_total: AtomicU64,
1591    /// Total records dropped (found unreachable) across all repacks.
1592    repack_dropped_total: AtomicU64,
1593    /// Per-collection repack counts, so a hot collection's churn is visible individually.
1594    repack_counts_by_collection: RwLock<HashMap<[u8; 16], u64>>,
1595    /// Per-collection incremental repack state. Each entry tracks the byte
1596    /// offset up to which each shard has been scanned for this collection and
1597    /// the deduplicated hash → (`slot`, offset) map from the last repack.
1598    /// On the next repack, only bytes after these offsets are scanned and
1599    /// merged into the existing map — turning O(n²) full rescan into
1600    /// O(n) total work across all repack calls.
1601    repack_incremental: RwLock<HashMap<[u8; 16], RepackIncrementalState>>,
1602    /// Persisted directory: which collections have live records in each shard,
1603    /// and how many. Maintained incrementally (a plain `put` just
1604    /// increments one counter; a full index rebuild/repack/initial scan
1605    /// replaces one collection's contribution wholesale via
1606    /// `LossyIndex::slot_counts`) rather than ever re-derived by
1607    /// scanning a shard file, which is what made `collections_referencing_shard`
1608    /// and a `collections`-style listing expensive before this existed.
1609    /// Reverse index of `shard_collections`: which shards a given collection currently
1610    /// contributes a nonzero count to. Lets a collection's full-index-rebuild
1611    /// path (`replace_collection_shard_counts`) clear exactly the shard entries
1612    /// it used to occupy without scanning every shard in `shard_collections`.
1613    /// Wall-clock instant of the last `maybe_persist_shard_collections` flush,
1614    /// used to rate-limit that timer-driven path.
1615    last_shard_collections_flush: RwLock<Option<std::time::Instant>>,
1616    /// Wall-clock breakdown of the most recent `open` — which index-loading
1617    /// path was taken and how long each phase took — set at construction.
1618    last_open_timings: parking_lot::Mutex<Option<OpenTimings>>,
1619    /// Wall-clock breakdown of the most recent `sync_all`, by phase.
1620    last_sync_timings: parking_lot::Mutex<Option<SyncTimings>>,
1621    /// Test-only: a smaller delta-log cap (0 = the real one), so a batch that
1622    /// does not fit can be produced without writing a 256 MiB log.
1623    #[cfg(test)]
1624    delta_log_cap_override: AtomicU64,
1625    /// Phase breakdown of the most recent full index checkpoint.
1626    last_checkpoint_breakdown: parking_lot::Mutex<Option<CheckpointBreakdown>>,
1627    /// Lifetime per-phase sync totals, accumulated once per sync in
1628    /// `count_sync_persistence`, so the scatter-vs-rewrite split can be read
1629    /// across a whole run instead of only the most recent barrier (which
1630    /// `last_sync_timings` alone cannot answer).
1631    sync_totals: SyncTotals,
1632    /// Rolling sync diagnostics retained for post-run inspection. This is
1633    /// deliberately bounded and never participates in durability decisions.
1634    sync_diagnostics: parking_lot::Mutex<SyncDiagnostics>,
1635    /// Number and time spent publishing mutations to the optional journal.
1636    publish_calls: AtomicU64,
1637    publish_time_ns: AtomicU64,
1638    pending_publish_since: parking_lot::Mutex<Option<std::time::Instant>>,
1639    publish_generation: AtomicU64,
1640    /// Minimum wall-clock interval between full checkpoint rewrites needed
1641    /// because no usable delta base exists or a v3 append failed. Zero disables this half of the
1642    /// rewrite budget. See [`Self::set_checkpoint_rewrite_budget`].
1643    checkpoint_rewrite_min_interval_ns: AtomicU64,
1644    /// Written-but-unsynced pack bytes at which a journal-mode sync also fsyncs
1645    /// the dirty packs (0 disables). See [`Self::set_pack_fsync_budget`].
1646    pack_fsync_budget_bytes: AtomicU64,
1647    /// Unsynced delta-log bytes at which a delta batch also fsyncs the log
1648    /// (0 disables). See [`DEFAULT_DELTA_FSYNC_BUDGET_BYTES`].
1649    delta_fsync_budget_bytes: AtomicU64,
1650    /// Maximum `put_bytes + put_many_bytes` accumulated since the last full
1651    /// checkpoint rewrite before one is forced even inside the time interval.
1652    /// Zero disables this half of the budget.
1653    checkpoint_rewrite_max_bytes: AtomicU64,
1654    /// Instant of the last full checkpoint rewrite this session — the time
1655    /// half of the rewrite budget.
1656    last_checkpoint_rewrite_at: parking_lot::Mutex<Option<std::time::Instant>>,
1657    /// `put_bytes + put_many_bytes` sampled at the last full checkpoint
1658    /// rewrite — the size half of the rewrite budget.
1659    checkpoint_bytes_at_last_rewrite: AtomicU64,
1660    /// Syncs that skipped a structurally-needed full checkpoint rewrite
1661    /// because the configured time/size budget still had headroom. The
1662    /// on-disk checkpoint stays stale by design; the next open then falls
1663    /// back to a rescan because the pack fingerprint advanced past it.
1664    checkpoint_skips: AtomicU64,
1665    /// Gates the logical read-path counters (`get`/`get_many` below). Off by
1666    /// default so a store doing no reads-of-record pays one relaxed load per
1667    /// logical read at most, and the write/batch/sync counters are the only
1668    /// always-on instrumentation (each is a single batch-granular `fetch_add`
1669    /// on a write-locked or per-call path, never per-record on the hot read
1670    /// path). See [`Self::set_stats_enabled`].
1671    stats_enabled: AtomicBool,
1672    /// Opt-in wall-clock latency accounting for the public storage operations.
1673    /// The timer is created only while `stats_enabled` is true so normal
1674    /// deployments pay no `Instant` cost for this diagnostic.
1675    operation_timings: OperationTimings,
1676    /// Whether [`Self::get_many_with_refresh`] may rescan a collection when
1677    /// the caller's in-memory snapshot misses. On by default. A single-writer
1678    /// store sets this `false`: its in-memory index is authoritative for every
1679    /// key it has written -- the lossy index only yields false-positive
1680    /// candidate collisions, never false negatives -- so a negative lookup is
1681    /// a true miss and refreshing can only spend a durable-fingerprint probe
1682    /// -- and, after each checkpoint, a full rescan -- to rediscover nothing.
1683    /// Multi-process readers leave it on to observe records the writer process
1684    /// appends.
1685    refresh_on_miss: AtomicBool,
1686    /// Number of times this class of store was assembled in this process — 1
1687    /// for a fresh open. Not reset by `reset_stats` (it counts stores, not work).
1688    open_count: AtomicU64,
1689
1690    // Logical read-path counters. Only incremented while `stats_enabled` is
1691    // true; otherwise the read path touches none of these.
1692    /// Logical `get` calls (including cache hits and any collection's absence).
1693    get_calls: AtomicU64,
1694    /// Logical `get` calls that resolved to no record (unknown collection,
1695    /// empty index probe, or unresolved candidate).
1696    get_misses: AtomicU64,
1697    /// Logical `get_many` calls.
1698    get_many_calls: AtomicU64,
1699    /// Records requested across `get_many` calls.
1700    get_many_records: AtomicU64,
1701    /// `get_many` results that resolved to no record.
1702    get_many_misses: AtomicU64,
1703    /// Read-miss refreshes that actually rescanned a collection.
1704    miss_refreshes: AtomicU64,
1705    /// Read-miss refreshes skipped because another refresh was recent.
1706    miss_refresh_skips: AtomicU64,
1707    /// Missing keys recovered by a read-miss refresh.
1708    miss_refresh_recovered: AtomicU64,
1709    /// IDs submitted in the retry request after a refresh. Proves that only
1710    /// missing keys are retried: `miss_refresh_retry_ids == count(missing)`.
1711    miss_refresh_retry_ids: AtomicU64,
1712    /// Fingerprint read errors after refresh — used to rate-limit warnings
1713    /// and expose diagnostics.
1714    miss_refresh_fp_errors: AtomicU64,
1715    /// Candidate locations yielded by the lossy index.
1716    index_candidates: AtomicU64,
1717    /// Candidate locations actually read from packfiles.
1718    candidate_reads: AtomicU64,
1719    /// Candidate records rejected after full-hash verification.
1720    candidate_hash_mismatches: AtomicU64,
1721    /// Unique shards touched across `get_many` batches.
1722    get_many_shards_touched: AtomicU64,
1723    /// On-disk frame bytes touched by candidate-record reads (a prefix read
1724    /// per frame; gated on stats, and only covers the candidate-resolve path,
1725    /// not refresh rescan). This sums on-disk *frame lengths* — a logical
1726    /// extent estimate: an mmap read can pull in whole pages, readahead
1727    /// ranges, and merged extents, so this must not be read as a physical
1728    /// disk-byte count. The honest `disk-extent` complement to
1729    /// `candidate_reads`: `candidate_frame_bytes / candidate_reads` is the
1730    /// average compressed frame the cold lookups drag in.
1731    candidate_frame_bytes: AtomicU64,
1732    /// Offset runs a `get_many` batch collapses its candidate reads into.
1733    /// Offsets within [`READ_RUN_GAP_BYTES`] of the previous candidate on the
1734    /// same shard count as one sequential run; the frontier batch's "one read
1735    /// plan per shard" target shows up here as runs ≈ shards, not ≈
1736    /// candidates.
1737    read_many_runs: AtomicU64,
1738    /// Plan fan-in of a `get_many` batch: per shard, `last_offset −
1739    /// first_offset` summed across touched shards (byte-extent the batch
1740    /// scatters over, even if it only touches sparse frames). Drives the
1741    /// scattered-read signal independent of candidate count.
1742    read_many_span_bytes: AtomicU64,
1743    /// Merged read extents prefetched with `madvise(MADV_WILLNEED)` across
1744    /// `get_many` batches. This is the physical plan the batch executed, as
1745    /// opposed to the [`READ_RUN_GAP_BYTES`] logical shape in
1746    /// [`Self::read_many_runs`].
1747    read_plan_extents: AtomicU64,
1748    /// Bytes covered by prefetched read extents (sum of extent lengths, not
1749    /// physical disk bytes — `madvise` is a hint the kernel may partially or
1750    /// fully ignore).
1751    read_plan_prefetch_bytes: AtomicU64,
1752    /// Planned extents that were not prefetched — offset beyond the current
1753    /// mapping (typically a buffered-but-unflushed frame), missing mapping, or
1754    /// a failed `madvise`. A persistently nonzero value means the plan is
1755    /// silently degrading to no prefetch for those extents.
1756    read_plan_skipped_extents: AtomicU64,
1757
1758    // Always-on write-path counters (per-record `fetch_add` only on the
1759    // single-record `put`, whose hot cost is dominated by the write itself).
1760    /// Single-record `put` attempts.
1761    put_calls: AtomicU64,
1762    /// Bytes accepted by single-record `put` attempts.
1763    put_bytes: AtomicU64,
1764    /// `put_many` calls (batches).
1765    put_many_calls: AtomicU64,
1766    /// Records written across `put_many` calls.
1767    put_many_records: AtomicU64,
1768    /// Bytes written across `put_many` calls.
1769    put_many_bytes: AtomicU64,
1770    /// `put_many` calls that started on the owned, no-clone fast path.
1771    put_many_fast_path_calls: AtomicU64,
1772    /// `put_many` calls that had to materialize an owned index up front
1773    /// (mmap-backed first write, or a brand-new collection).
1774    put_many_clone_path_calls: AtomicU64,
1775    /// Cumulative nanoseconds spent materializing or growing an owned index in
1776    /// `put_many` (batch-granular; drives the steady-append scaler's
1777    /// resume-from-checkpoint cost).
1778    index_clone_time_ns: AtomicU64,
1779    /// Index grow/rebuild events in `put_many` (each requests a v3 snapshot).
1780    index_grow_count: AtomicU64,
1781    /// Fallback `rebuild_index` calls (full pack scan).
1782    index_rebuild_count: AtomicU64,
1783    /// `invalidate_delta_log` calls — structural changes represented by a
1784    /// whole-collection snapshot in the v3 log.
1785    delta_invalidations: AtomicU64,
1786    /// `sync`/`sync_all` calls.
1787    sync_calls: AtomicU64,
1788    /// Syncs that rewrote the index checkpoint in full.
1789    checkpoint_writes: AtomicU64,
1790    /// Background checkpoint tails started (one per detached checkpoint).
1791    checkpoint_tails_started: AtomicU64,
1792    /// Syncs that ran with a tail already in flight and appended to it rather
1793    /// than starting another checkpoint.
1794    syncs_with_tail_in_flight: AtomicU64,
1795    /// Syncs that waited for an in-flight tail (emergency zone or rotation).
1796    syncs_waited_for_tail: AtomicU64,
1797    /// Syncs that appended the incremental delta log instead.
1798    delta_appends: AtomicU64,
1799    /// Writes of the shard→collection inspection sidecar
1800    /// (`shard_collections.bin`). Counts every temp-write+rename, whichever
1801    /// caller triggered it.
1802    sidecar_writes: AtomicU64,
1803    /// Whether any collection data changed since the last `index.checkpoint`
1804    /// write. Set by every generation swap (`put`/`put_many`/`repack`/`refresh`);
1805    /// cleared only by a successful [`Self::persist_index_checkpoint`], so a
1806    /// failed write is retried on the next sync. Lets `sync()`/`sync_all()`
1807    /// skip rewriting the checkpoint when nothing has changed since the last
1808    /// one — a steady-state writer that syncs between writes pays no checkpoint
1809    /// cost, while a crash left a stale checkpoint is still always resolved by
1810    /// the fingerprint → rescan fallback.
1811    index_checkpoint_dirty: AtomicBool,
1812    /// The shard→collection sidecar is known missing or invalid and must be
1813    /// regenerated even though no index is dirty (see
1814    /// `RoomScanOutput::sidecar_missing`). Distinct from
1815    /// `shard_collections_stale`: that flag only says ordinary writes have
1816    /// advanced the in-memory bookkeeping past the on-disk copy, which is
1817    /// deferred to the next persistence anchor.
1818    shard_collections_dirty: AtomicBool,
1819    /// A completed sync barrier advanced the in-memory shard→collection
1820    /// bookkeeping past the on-disk sidecar by deferring its write. Set only on
1821    /// the delta-append and budget-deferred-checkpoint paths, never by the raw
1822    /// mutation helpers: bookkeeping changed by a write that was never synced
1823    /// already invalidates the checkpoint fast path, so the next open
1824    /// full-scans and has no use for a sidecar. The sidecar is rebuildable
1825    /// acceleration metadata, so this only schedules a flush at the next
1826    /// anchor: a checkpoint rewrite, a repack, or shutdown.
1827    shard_collections_stale: AtomicBool,
1828    /// A missing sidecar was observed, but its physical byte metrics could not
1829    /// be rebuilt. Keep retrying rather than publishing misleading zeros.
1830    shard_collections_recovery_failed: AtomicBool,
1831    /// A sidecar persist failure has already been logged; cleared on success so
1832    /// a persistent failure logs once per streak, not once per sync.
1833    shard_collections_failure_logged: AtomicBool,
1834    /// Test-only: runs after the recovery scan and before its totals are
1835    /// swapped in, so a test can hold recovery inside that window.
1836    #[cfg(test)]
1837    recovery_pause_hook: parking_lot::Mutex<Option<Arc<dyn Fn() + Send + Sync>>>,
1838    /// Session state for the incremental index delta log: the base checkpoint
1839    /// fingerprint + generations the log continues, and the frames accumulated
1840    /// since the last persist. See [`DeltaLogState`].
1841    delta_state: parking_lot::Mutex<DeltaLogState>,
1842    /// Serializes checkpoint/delta persistence calls while allowing the
1843    /// delta-state mutex to be released during whole-index snapshot encoding.
1844    index_persist_lock: parking_lot::Mutex<()>,
1845    /// Optional write-ahead journal coordinator. When present, every mutation
1846    /// is published to it and `sync` commits a single durable group, so the
1847    /// per-shard pack fsyncs and the index checkpoint can be deferred without
1848    /// risking acknowledged data (see [`Self::enable_journal`]).
1849    journal: parking_lot::Mutex<Option<Arc<JournalCoordinator>>>,
1850    /// Pool tag this store publishes under on a shared journal, as a
1851    /// [`crate::journal::pool_tag`] code (`0` = untagged/per-pool). Set by
1852    /// [`Self::enable_shared_journal`]; read on the publish and replay hot
1853    /// paths, so it is a plain atomic rather than behind the journal mutex.
1854    journal_pool: std::sync::atomic::AtomicU8,
1855    /// Committed groups recovered when the journal was opened, retained for
1856    /// [`Self::replay_journal`] to re-apply after a reopen.
1857    journal_recovery: parking_lot::Mutex<Vec<crate::journal::CommittedGroup>>,
1858    /// Set while [`Self::replay_journal`] re-applies recovered mutations, so
1859    /// those writes are not re-published to the journal.
1860    replaying: AtomicBool,
1861    /// Optional read-only journal overlay backing [`Self::get_read_committed`].
1862    /// Enabled on a read-only store so a worker can observe committed-but-
1863    /// unflushed journal groups that the durable fingerprint gate deliberately
1864    /// hides. See [`Self::enable_read_journal`].
1865    read_journal: parking_lot::Mutex<Option<ReadJournal>>,
1866    /// Number of in-process transactions whose published groups are still
1867    /// being materialized. While non-zero, ordinary reads consult the journal
1868    /// overlay before the live index.
1869    transaction_overlay_users: AtomicU64,
1870    /// The transaction overlay while no transaction uses it. It is kept out of
1871    /// `read_journal` so read-committed reads on the writer skip the journal
1872    /// refresh, and kept at all so the next activation resumes its scan
1873    /// position instead of rescanning the segment.
1874    #[cfg(feature = "multi-reader")]
1875    parked_transaction_overlay: parking_lot::Mutex<Option<ReadJournal>>,
1876    /// Serializes overlay activation and deactivation, so the overlay moves
1877    /// between `read_journal` and the parking slot exactly once per 0 <-> 1
1878    /// transition of `transaction_overlay_users`.
1879    #[cfg(feature = "multi-reader")]
1880    transaction_overlay_lifecycle: parking_lot::Mutex<()>,
1881    /// Test-only total of segment bytes the transaction overlay has scanned,
1882    /// across activations, whether the overlay was retained or rebuilt.
1883    #[cfg(all(test, feature = "multi-reader"))]
1884    transaction_overlay_scanned: AtomicU64,
1885    /// Journal LSN covered by the durable index this handle actually loaded.
1886    ///
1887    /// Read once at open, when the index is built from the on-disk checkpoint
1888    /// (or a full scan). It is the *only* coverage the overlay may prune
1889    /// through: a fresher `journal.lsn` written by a concurrent checkpoint does
1890    /// not mean this handle's in-memory index contains those records. Advancing
1891    /// this pair requires loading the corresponding checkpoint, not a live
1892    /// packfile rescan. See [`Self::get_read_committed`].
1893    // Only read back by the (feature-gated) read-committed overlay; a
1894    // non-`multi-reader` build still writes it once at open so the two
1895    // build configurations share one open path, but never reads it back.
1896    #[cfg_attr(not(feature = "multi-reader"), allow(dead_code))]
1897    read_covered_lsn: AtomicU64,
1898    /// The journal LSN this pool's packs are known to durably cover, so a reopen
1899    /// need not replay at or below it. Read from disk once at open
1900    /// ([`Self::read_journal_lsn`]) and advanced by whatever makes more of the
1901    /// journal safe to drop: a checkpoint's `journal.lsn` write, or a coverage
1902    /// batch appended to the delta log. It only ever moves forward.
1903    ///
1904    /// Shared (`Arc`) because a checkpoint tail on its own thread advances it
1905    /// after the image is durable and cannot borrow the store; the cost is one
1906    /// small allocation per pool.
1907    durable_coverage: Arc<AtomicU64>,
1908    /// The checkpoint tail running on its own thread, if one is (see
1909    /// [`CheckpointTail`]). At most one at a time; joined before a synchronous
1910    /// checkpoint, at close, and when the WAL nears its cap.
1911    checkpoint_worker: parking_lot::Mutex<Option<CheckpointWorker>>,
1912    /// Whether a sync that needs a full checkpoint hands its tail to a worker
1913    /// thread instead of running it inline.
1914    background_checkpoint: AtomicBool,
1915    /// Test-only: a hold and a failure the next checkpoint tail takes with it.
1916    #[cfg(test)]
1917    checkpoint_tail_hook: parking_lot::Mutex<Option<TailHook>>,
1918    /// Successful checkpoint-bound index reloads triggered by the
1919    /// read-committed overlay, because a writer's reclaim outran the coverage
1920    /// this handle's index incorporated. A WAL-cell failure on the reload path
1921    /// is visible here instead of looking like an ordinary miss. See
1922    /// [`Self::refresh_read_journal`].
1923    read_reloads: AtomicU64,
1924    /// Reload attempts that could not load a checkpoint matching the current
1925    /// packs, so the read-committed overlay failed closed.
1926    read_reload_failures: AtomicU64,
1927}
1928
1929/// Per-collection state for incremental repack.
1930#[derive(Clone)]
1931struct RepackIncrementalState {
1932    /// Per-shard byte offset: next scan starts here (file length at end
1933    /// of last scan). Shards not in this map haven't been scanned yet.
1934    // A slot can be retired and reused for a different pack.  Keep the
1935    // pack_id beside the cursor so an offset from the old incarnation is
1936    // never applied to the replacement file.
1937    scan_offsets: HashMap<u16, (u64, u64)>,
1938    /// The deduplicated hash → (`slot`, offset) map from the last repack.
1939    /// The next repack merges newly-scanned entries into this map.
1940    live_map: HashMap<[u8; 16], (u16, u64)>,
1941    /// Cached edge lists for every node that survived the last repack.
1942    /// Lets the BFS and full-scan adjacency walks skip re-reading disk for
1943    /// nodes that were already seen — turning O(total) disk reads per repack
1944    /// call into O(delta) reads for only nodes added since the last repack.
1945    adjacency: HashMap<[u8; 16], Vec<[u8; 16]>>,
1946    /// The live-roots snapshot from the last repack. Used to identify which
1947    /// roots are genuinely new so the incremental BFS can seed only those,
1948    /// rather than re-walking the entire reachable set from scratch.
1949    prev_roots: Vec<[u8; 16]>,
1950}
1951
1952const DEFAULT_REPACK_THRESHOLD_ENTRIES: u64 = 2048;
1953const DEFAULT_CACHE_CAPACITY: usize = 100_000;
1954
1955/// Minimum `LossyIndex` capacity for a brand-new collection's first
1956/// insert (`put` and `put_many`), in slots (8 bytes each).
1957///
1958/// Not the index's own 16-slot hard floor: at the ~75% load factor
1959/// `grow()` targets, 16 slots admits only ~12 entries before the next
1960/// insert forces a grow -- and every `grow()` invalidates the delta log
1961/// (see its doc comment), forcing the next sync to do a full checkpoint
1962/// rewrite instead of a cheap delta append. A workload that lands entries
1963/// one at a time into a new collection (e.g. events arriving
1964/// individually) would trade checkpoint bloat for far more frequent full
1965/// rewrites. 64 slots (512 B) covers a "handful of records" collection
1966/// without ever growing, while remaining ~64x smaller than the old flat
1967/// 4096-slot (32 KiB) floor this replaced.
1968const NEW_COLLECTION_INDEX_FLOOR: usize = 64;
1969
1970impl PackfileStorage {
1971    fn refresh_lock(&self, collection_id: &[u8; 16]) -> Arc<parking_lot::Mutex<()>> {
1972        let mut locks = self.refresh_locks.lock();
1973        locks
1974            .entry(*collection_id)
1975            .or_insert_with(|| Arc::new(parking_lot::Mutex::new(())))
1976            .clone()
1977    }
1978
1979    fn post_refresh_fingerprint(&self) -> Option<u64> {
1980        match crate::index::checkpoint::read_durable_fingerprint(&self.base_dir) {
1981            Ok(Some(fp)) => Some(fp.fingerprint),
1982            Ok(None) => Some(0),
1983            Err(error) => {
1984                let previous = self.miss_refresh_fp_errors.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
1985                let count = previous.saturating_add(1);
1986                let periodic = count
1987                    .checked_rem(100)
1988                    .is_some_and(|remainder| remainder == 0);
1989                if previous == 0 || periodic {
1990                    eprintln!(
1991                        "warning: unable to observe post-refresh fingerprint (count={count}): {error}"
1992                    );
1993                }
1994                None
1995            }
1996        }
1997    }
1998
1999    fn refresh_and_retry(
2000        &self,
2001        collection_id: &[u8; 16],
2002        ids: &[NodeId],
2003        missing: Vec<usize>,
2004        results: &mut [Option<NodeData>],
2005    ) -> Result<(), StorageError> {
2006        self.refresh_collection(collection_id)?;
2007        // Reread the fingerprint after refresh to handle a concurrent sync.
2008        if let Some(fp) = self.post_refresh_fingerprint() {
2009            self.last_refresh_fingerprint
2010                .lock()
2011                .insert(*collection_id, fp);
2012        }
2013        self.miss_refreshes.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
2014
2015        let retry_ids: Vec<NodeId> = missing.iter().map(|&index| ids[index]).collect();
2016        let retry_count = u64::try_from(retry_ids.len()).unwrap_or(u64::MAX);
2017        self.miss_refresh_retry_ids
2018            .fetch_add(retry_count, Ordering::Relaxed);
2019        let retry = self.get_many(collection_id, &retry_ids)?;
2020        let mut recovered = 0u64;
2021        for (index, value) in missing.into_iter().zip(retry) {
2022            if value.is_some() {
2023                recovered = recovered.saturating_add(1);
2024                results[index] = value;
2025            }
2026        }
2027        self.miss_refresh_recovered
2028            .fetch_add(recovered, Ordering::Relaxed);
2029        Ok(())
2030    }
2031
2032    /// Open a packfile storage with default settings.
2033    ///
2034    /// # Errors
2035    /// Returns `io::Error` if the base directory cannot be created or read.
2036    pub fn open(base_dir: PathBuf) -> Result<Self, std::io::Error> {
2037        Self::open_with_options(
2038            base_dir,
2039            DEFAULT_CACHE_CAPACITY,
2040            None,
2041            true,
2042            None,
2043            true,
2044            packfile::ChecksumPolicy::Full,
2045        )
2046    }
2047
2048    /// Open a packfile storage with explicit compression and checksum
2049    /// policies — the advanced durability/performance entry point. See

2214    /// Open a read-only observer with the read-committed journal overlay
2215    /// enabled, in one call.
2216    #[cfg(feature = "multi-reader")]
2217    ///
2218    /// This is the intended constructor for an authoritative read-only worker
2219    /// handle. The durable read APIs ([`StorageEngine::get_many`],
2220    /// [`Self::get_many_with_refresh`]) deliberately hide a writer's
2221    /// unflushed and not-yet-checkpointed mutations, so a worker that must
2222    /// observe another process's committed writes has to read through
2223    /// [`Self::get_read_committed`] — and that only consults an overlay once
2224    /// [`Self::enable_read_journal`] has attached a writer's segment. Pairing
2225    /// the two here makes this the only supported way to obtain such a handle,
2226    /// so a caller cannot open one that silently falls back to the durable
2227    /// API.
2228    ///
2229    /// `wal_path` is the writer's journal segment. See
2230    /// [`Self::enable_read_journal`] for the read-only safety contract and
2231    /// [`Self::open_read_only`] for the writer-coexistence contract.
2232    ///
2233    /// # Errors
2234    /// Returns [`StorageError`] if the store cannot be opened read-only (same
2235    /// as [`Self::open_read_only`]), or if the segment is unreadable, a
2236    /// committed group fails validation, or a coverage gap cannot be resolved
2237    /// by reloading the checkpoint (same as [`Self::enable_read_journal`]).
2238    pub fn open_read_committed(
2239        base_dir: PathBuf,
2240        wal_path: impl AsRef<Path>,
2241    ) -> Result<Self, StorageError> {
2242        let store = Self::open_read_only(base_dir)?;
2243        store.enable_read_journal(wal_path)?;
2244        Ok(store)
2245    }
2246
2247    /// Open a read-only worker on one pool of a **shared** WAL.
2248    ///
2249    /// Identical to [`Self::open_read_committed`] except the overlay applies
2250    /// only frames tagged with `pool`, so a worker reading the state pool does
2251    /// not observe event-DAG or edges mutations that share the same
2252    /// segment. `wal_path` is the database root's shared `wal.bin`, not a
2253    /// per-pool segment.
2254    ///
2255    /// # Errors
2256    /// Same as [`Self::open_read_committed`].
2257    #[cfg(feature = "multi-reader")]
2258    pub fn open_read_committed_shared(
2259        base_dir: PathBuf,
2260        wal_path: impl AsRef<Path>,
2261        pool: crate::layout::ShardType,
2262    ) -> Result<Self, StorageError> {
2263        let store = Self::open_read_only(base_dir)?;
2264        store.enable_read_journal_shared(wal_path, pool)?;
2265        Ok(store)
2266    }

2306
2307    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
2308    #[allow(clippy::too_many_lines)]
2309    fn open_with_options(
2310        base_dir: PathBuf,
2311        cache_capacity: usize,
2312        swizzle: Option<SwizzleFn>,
2313        writable: bool,
2314        max_shard_bytes: Option<u64>,
2315        compress: bool,
2316        checksum_policy: packfile::ChecksumPolicy,
2317    ) -> Result<Self, std::io::Error> {
2318        fs::create_dir_all(&base_dir)?;
2319
2320        let started = std::time::Instant::now();
2321        let mut timings = OpenTimings::default();
2322
2323        let shard_open_started = std::time::Instant::now();
2324        let shards = if writable {
2325            match max_shard_bytes {
2326                // Custom rotation thresholds are only used by benchmarks/
2327                // tests today, none of which also need to disable
2328                // compression, so this combination just keeps the default.
2329                Some(max_shard_bytes) => ShardPool::open_with_policies(
2330                    base_dir.clone(),
2331                    compress,
2332                    checksum_policy,
2333                    Some(max_shard_bytes),
2334                )?,
2335                None => ShardPool::open_with_policies(
2336                    base_dir.clone(),
2337                    compress,
2338                    checksum_policy,
2339                    None,
2340                )?,
2341            }
2342        } else {
2343            ShardPool::open_read_only_with_policies(base_dir.clone(), checksum_policy)?
2344        };
2345        let shard_open_time = shard_open_started.elapsed();
2346        timings.shard_open = shard_open_time;
2347        let index_config = crate::index::IndexConfig {
2348            seed: shards.bucket_seed(),
2349            ..Default::default()
2350        };
2351        if let Some(shard_timings) = shards.open_timings() {
2352            timings.shard_open = shard_timings.total;
2353            timings.shard_discovery = shard_timings.discovery;
2354            timings.writer_lock = shard_timings.writer_lock;
2355            timings.packfile_recovery = shard_timings.packfile_recovery;
2356            timings.packfile_recovery_calls = shard_timings.packfile_recovery_calls;
2357            timings.packfile_open = shard_timings.packfile_open;
2358            timings.packfile_open_calls = shard_timings.packfile_open_calls;
2359            timings.metadata_restore = shard_timings.metadata_restore;
2360            timings.pool_meta_restore = shard_timings.pool_meta_restore;
2361            timings.persisted_stats_restore = shard_timings.persisted_stats_restore;
2362            timings.store_meta_write = shard_timings.store_meta_write;
2363            timings.pool_meta_persist = shard_timings.pool_meta_persist;
2364            timings.initial_pack_create = shard_timings.initial_pack_create;
2365            timings.metadata_unattributed = shard_timings.metadata_unattributed;
2366            timings.shard_open_unattributed = shard_timings.unattributed;
2367        }
2368
2369        // Phase 1: accumulate all records per collection across every shard so
2370        // the index can be sized once for the true total.
2371        let mut collection_entries: HashMap<[u8; 16], Vec<ShardRecord>> = HashMap::new();
2372        let metadata_started = std::time::Instant::now();
2373        // Seed logical insertion order before scanning. A newly written collection
2374        // cannot appear in the sidecar until the next flush, so append it at
2375        // first physical sight below. Legacy v1 sidecars yield no order and
2376        // therefore use the same first-seen fallback for every collection.
2377        let mut collection_order = persisted_collection_order(&base_dir).unwrap_or_default();
2378        let mut known_collections: HashSet<[u8; 16]> = collection_order.iter().copied().collect();
2379
2380        // Collect open shard info (slot, pack_id, path, length) before the scan
2381        // loop so we don't hold the shards read-lock across the I/O-heavy scan.
2382        // The lengths feed the checkpoint fingerprint (see `index::checkpoint`).
2383        let open_shards: Vec<(u16, u64, PathBuf, u64)> = shards
2384            .all_shards()
2385            .into_iter()
2386            .map(|(id, shard)| (id, shard.pack_id, shard.path.clone(), shard.file_len()))
2387            .collect();
2388
2389        // A checkpoint from the previous session's last sync lets us skip the
2390        // rescan and index rebuild entirely. It is only trusted when every
2391        // pack on disk still matches the fingerprint it was written against.
2392        let deleted_collections = Self::load_deleted_collections(&base_dir);
2393        // Capture the journal coverage *before* loading the index, so the bound
2394        // can never be newer than the index this handle builds. A writer writes
2395        // `journal.lsn` only after its covering checkpoint, so reading it first
2396        // always yields a bound <= the coverage of the checkpoint/scan below.
2397        let durable_state = Self::durable_index_state(&base_dir);
2398        let read_covered = Self::journal_lsn_with(&base_dir, durable_state.covered_lsn);
2399        timings.metadata_load = metadata_started.elapsed();
2400        if let Some((scan_out, collection_order, delta_state, checkpoint_covered)) =
2401            Self::checkpoint_scan_out(
2402                &base_dir,
2403                cache_capacity,
2404                &shards,
2405                &open_shards,
2406                &deleted_collections,
2407                writable,
2408                ReloadMode::Strict,
2409                index_config,
2410                &mut timings,
2411            )
2412        {
2413            timings.path = OpenPath::Checkpoint;
2414            let assemble_started = std::time::Instant::now();
2415            let store = Self::assemble(
2416                shards,
2417                scan_out,
2418                collection_order,
2419                deleted_collections,
2420                base_dir,
2421                swizzle,
2422                cache_capacity,
2423                delta_state,
2424                checkpoint_covered,
2425                read_covered,
2426                durable_state.fingerprint,
2427            );
2428            timings.assemble = assemble_started.elapsed();
2429            timings.total = started.elapsed();
2430            *store.last_open_timings.lock() = Some(timings);
2431            return Ok(store);
2432        }
2433        timings.path = OpenPath::FullScan;
2434        // The checkpoint/log gates rejected the persisted index state; never
2435        // carry forward a stale log into the rescanned session — a writable
2436        // open can delete it outright (read-only opens leave the file alone
2437        // but will re-rescan, since the damaged bases can never trust it).
2438        if writable {
2439            Self::sweep_orphan_delta_logs(&base_dir, None);
2440        }
2441
2442        let scan_started = std::time::Instant::now();
2443        for (slot, shard_pack_id, path, _file_len) in open_shards {
2444            // A read-only open must never touch the file at all — the
2445            // truncating recovery scan below is only safe when we're the
2446            // sole writer (guaranteed by the writer lock); a read-only
2447            // opener can run concurrently with an active writer (no lock
2448            // taken at all — see ShardPool::open_read_only), so it must
2449            // use the non-mutating scan_packfile, which just stops
2450            // cleanly at a torn tail (indistinguishable from a writer's
2451            // in-flight append) instead of truncating it away.
2452            let entries = if writable {
2453                // Recovery can safely truncate only a torn final frame. Any
2454                // other failure (CRC mismatch, invalid framing, permissions)
2455                // means this pack cannot be indexed faithfully; fail open
2456                // rather than publish a store that silently omitted it.
2457                packfile::scan_and_recover_packfile(&path).map_err(|error| {
2458                    std::io::Error::new(
2459                        error.kind(),
2460                        format!("recovery scan failed for pack {}: {error}", path.display()),
2461                    )
2462                })?
2463            } else {
2464                // Read-only mode must not truncate a possibly in-flight tail,
2465                // but it also cannot safely omit a shard.  Publishing a
2466                // partial index after an I/O or corruption failure makes real
2467                // records look deleted.  Surface the error and let the caller
2468                // retry after the writer has finished or repair the pack.
2469                packfile::scan_packfile(&path).map_err(|error| {
2470                    std::io::Error::new(
2471                        error.kind(),
2472                        format!(
2473                            "read-only scan failed for shard {slot:02x} ({}): {error}",
2474                            path.display()
2475                        ),
2476                    )
2477                })?
2478            };
2479            for (collection_id, hash, offset) in entries {
2480                if known_collections.insert(collection_id) {
2481                    collection_order.push(collection_id);
2482                }
2483                collection_entries.entry(collection_id).or_default().push((
2484                    slot,
2485                    hash,
2486                    offset,
2487                    shard_pack_id,
2488                ));
2489            }
2490        }
2491        collection_order.retain(|collection_id| collection_entries.contains_key(collection_id));
2492        timings.full_scan = scan_started.elapsed();
2493
2494        let mut scan_out = RoomScanOutput::default();
2495
2496        // Phase 2: build per-collection indexes sized to the true total.
2497        let materialization_started = std::time::Instant::now();
2498        for collection_id in &collection_order {
2499            if deleted_collections.contains(collection_id) {
2500                continue;
2501            }
2502            Self::init_collection_from_scan(
2503                collection_id,
2504                &collection_entries[collection_id],
2505                &shards,
2506                cache_capacity,
2507                index_config,
2508                &mut scan_out,
2509            )?;
2510        }
2511        timings.index_materialization = materialization_started.elapsed();
2512
2513        let store = Self::assemble(
2514            shards,
2515            scan_out,
2516            collection_order,
2517            deleted_collections,
2518            base_dir,
2519            swizzle,
2520            cache_capacity,
2521            // A full rescan re-cooks every index from scratch, so no delta log
2522            // can continue anything the checkpoint recorded; force the next
2523            // dirty sync into a full checkpoint rewrite that re-bases the log.
2524            DeltaLogState::default(),
2525            read_covered,
2526            read_covered,
2527            durable_state.fingerprint,
2528        );
2529        // A writer that had to rescan has no checkpoint describing this pack
2530        // set. Mark it dirty so the next sync persists one; otherwise a store
2531        // opened and synced without further writes (e.g. after an aborted
2532        // import) would rescan every packfile on every open forever.
2533        if writable {
2534            store.index_checkpoint_dirty.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
2535        }
2536        timings.total = started.elapsed();
2537        *store.last_open_timings.lock() = Some(timings);
2538        Ok(store)
2539    }
2540
2541    /// Builds one collection's index, cache, and shard-directory contribution
2542    /// from its scanned records, and inserts all three into `out` — the
2543    /// per-collection body of `open_with_options`'s phase 2, factored out to
2544    /// keep that function under the line-count lint rather than
2545    /// suppressing it.
2546    fn init_collection_from_scan(
2547        collection_id: &[u8; 16],
2548        records: &[ShardRecord],
2549        shards: &ShardPool,
2550        cache_capacity: usize,
2551        index_config: crate::index::IndexConfig,
2552        out: &mut RoomScanOutput,
2553    ) -> Result<(), StorageError> {
2554        // Seed each collection's home shard from the scan: the shard of its
2555        // last-scanned record is a best-effort proxy for "most recent"
2556        // (shards are scanned in ascending ID order, and IDs generally
2557        // increase over time via rotation) — not exact chronology across
2558        // shards, but enough to keep a resumed collection's writes landing near
2559        // its existing data instead of restarting at whatever the pool's
2560        // active shard happens to be.
2561        if let Some(&(last_slot, _, _, _)) = records.last() {
2562            shards.set_collection_home(collection_id, last_slot);
2563        }
2564        let index = LossyIndex::with_config(
2565            records
2566                .len()
2567                .saturating_mul(2)
2568                .max(NEW_COLLECTION_INDEX_FLOOR),
2569            index_config,
2570        );
2571        for (slot, hash, offset, _pack_id) in records {
2572            check_index_offset(*slot, hash, *offset)?;
2573            let _ = index.insert(hash, *slot, *offset);
2574        }
2575        for (slot, _hash, offset, pack_id) in records {
2576            let shard = shards
2577                .get_shard(*slot)
2578                .ok_or_else(|| StorageError::Corrupt(format!("missing shard slot {slot}")))?;
2579            let bytes = ShardPool::record_disk_len_at(&shard, *offset)?;
2580            let total = out
2581                .collection_disk_bytes
2582                .entry(*pack_id)
2583                .or_default()
2584                .entry(*collection_id)
2585                .or_default();
2586            *total = total.saturating_add(bytes);
2587        }
2588        let counts = index.slot_counts();
2589
2590        // Build slot→pack_id lookup from the records for this collection.
2591        let slot_to_pack_id: HashMap<u16, u64> = records
2592            .iter()
2593            .map(|(slot, _, _, pack_id)| (*slot, *pack_id))
2594            .collect();
2595
2596        for (&slot, &count) in &counts {
2597            let pack_id = slot_to_pack_id
2598                .get(&slot)
2599                .copied()
2600                .unwrap_or(u64::from(slot));
2601            out.shard_collections
2602                .entry(pack_id)
2603                .or_default()
2604                .insert(*collection_id, count);
2605            out.collection_shards
2606                .entry(*collection_id)
2607                .or_default()
2608                .insert(pack_id);
2609        }
2610        out.collections.insert(
2611            *collection_id,
2612            ArcSwap::from_pointee(RoomGeneration {
2613                index,
2614                cache: Arc::new(NodeCache::new(cache_capacity)),
2615                generation: 1,
2616            }),
2617        );
2618        Ok(())
2619    }
2620
2621    /// Assemble a fully constructed store from the per-collection state both
2622    /// the rescan path and the checkpoint fast path produce, so the two share
2623    /// one field-for-field constructor.
2624    #[allow(
2625        clippy::too_many_arguments,
2626        clippy::too_many_lines,
2627        reason = "one field-for-field constructor shared by both open paths"
2628    )]
2629    fn assemble(
2630        shards: ShardPool,
2631        scan_out: RoomScanOutput,
2632        collection_order: Vec<[u8; 16]>,
2633        deleted_collections: HashSet<[u8; 16]>,
2634        base_dir: PathBuf,
2635        swizzle: Option<SwizzleFn>,
2636        cache_capacity: usize,
2637        delta_state: DeltaLogState,
2638        read_covered: u64,
2639        durable_coverage: u64,
2640        initial_durable_fp: u64,
2641    ) -> Self {
2642        let index_config = crate::index::IndexConfig {
2643            seed: shards.bucket_seed(),
2644            ..Default::default()
2645        };
2646        // Seed the per-collection refresh fingerprint from the persisted
2647        // checkpoint/delta state so the first miss for each collection can
2648        // skip refresh when nothing durable changed.
2649        let initial_fingerprints: HashMap<[u8; 16], u64> = collection_order
2650            .iter()
2651            .map(|&cid| (cid, initial_durable_fp))
2652            .collect();
2653        // The checkpoint coverage this open's index corresponds to, captured
2654        // before the index was loaded. Bound to the loaded index, never
2655        // re-read from disk by the overlay.
2656        let read_covered_lsn = AtomicU64::new(read_covered);
2657        Self {
2658            shards,
2659            index_tables: RwLock::new(IndexTables {
2660                collections: scan_out.collections,
2661                collection_order,
2662                shard_collections: scan_out.shard_collections,
2663                collection_shards: scan_out.collection_shards,
2664                collection_disk_bytes: scan_out.collection_disk_bytes,
2665            }),
2666            pinned: PinnedNodes::new(),
2667            base_dir,
2668            swizzle,
2669            put_locks: parking_lot::Mutex::new(HashMap::new()),
2670            refresh_locks: parking_lot::Mutex::new(HashMap::new()),
2671            last_refresh_fingerprint: parking_lot::Mutex::new(initial_fingerprints),
2672            initial_durable_fingerprint: initial_durable_fp,
2673            collection_creation: parking_lot::RwLock::new(()),
2674            deleted_collections: parking_lot::Mutex::new(deleted_collections),
2675            live_roots: RwLock::new(HashMap::new()),
2676            repack_threshold_entries: AtomicU64::new(DEFAULT_REPACK_THRESHOLD_ENTRIES),
2677            cache_capacity,
2678            index_config,
2679            read_plan: RwLock::new(ReadPlanPolicy::default()),
2680            repack_count: AtomicU64::new(0),
2681            repack_kept_total: AtomicU64::new(0),
2682            repack_dropped_total: AtomicU64::new(0),
2683            repack_counts_by_collection: RwLock::new(HashMap::new()),
