2777
2778    /// Path of this store's persisted-index checkpoint.
2779    fn index_checkpoint_path(base_dir: &std::path::Path) -> PathBuf {
2780        base_dir.join(crate::index::checkpoint::INDEX_CHECKPOINT_FILE)
2781    }
2782
2783    /// Path of one *epoch* of this store's incremental index delta log.
2784    ///
2785    /// Named by the checkpoint fingerprint it continues (`index.delta.<hex
2786    /// fingerprint>`) rather than a single fixed name: the epoch-handoff
2787    /// protocol (see `persist_index_checkpoint`) needs the about-to-be-retired
2788    /// epoch (D0, continuing the old checkpoint) and the freshly rotated one
2789    /// (D1, continuing the new one) to coexist on disk as distinct files
2790    /// while the new checkpoint is serialized and fsynced unlocked. Naming by
2791    /// fingerprint also *is* the reopen gate: a loader only ever looks at the
2792    /// epoch whose name matches the checkpoint's own `pack_fingerprint`, so
2793    /// a leftover D0 (crash before retirement) or an orphaned D1 (crash
2794    /// before the checkpoint that would have validated it) are both
2795    /// automatically ignored without any extra bookkeeping.
2796    fn delta_path(base_dir: &std::path::Path, fingerprint: u64) -> PathBuf {
2797        base_dir.join(format!("{INDEX_DELTA_FILE}.{fingerprint:016x}"))
2798    }
2799
2800    /// Path of the sidecar recording the journal LSN the on-disk index
2801    /// checkpoint covers. Written only when a journal is enabled; its contents
2802    /// bound [`Self::replay_journal`] to the post-checkpoint suffix.
2803    fn journal_lsn_path(base_dir: &std::path::Path) -> PathBuf {
2804        base_dir.join("journal.lsn")
2805    }
2806
2807    /// The journal LSN this pool's durable state covers (0 when none is
2808    /// recorded): the newest of the `journal.lsn` a checkpoint wrote, the
2809    /// coverage the checkpoint's own header records, and what a committed batch
2810    /// of the delta log that continues the current checkpoint claims.
2811    ///
2812    /// A missing, torn or corrupt record of either kind claims nothing, so the
2813    /// result can only be lower than the truth, which makes recovery replay
2814    /// more, never less. It reads the disk (and scans the delta log), so a
2815    /// writer uses [`Self::durable_coverage`] instead.
2816    #[must_use]
2817    pub fn read_journal_lsn(base_dir: &std::path::Path) -> u64 {
2818        Self::journal_lsn_with(base_dir, Self::durable_index_state(base_dir).covered_lsn)
2819    }
2820
2821    /// `read_journal_lsn` given the coverage a checkpoint and its delta log
2822    /// already yielded, so an open that also needs the log's fingerprint scans
2823    /// the log once.
2824    fn journal_lsn_with(base_dir: &std::path::Path, checkpoint_and_delta: u64) -> u64 {
2825        let recorded = fs::read(Self::journal_lsn_path(base_dir))
2826            .ok()
2827            .and_then(|bytes| bytes.get(..8).map(<[u8; 8]>::try_from))
2828            .and_then(Result::ok)
2829            .map_or(0, u64::from_le_bytes);
2830        recorded.max(checkpoint_and_delta)
2831    }
2832
2833    /// What the disk records of the durable index state, in one pass over the
2834    /// checkpoint and its delta log: the coverage the checkpoint records or a
2835    /// committed batch of the log continuing it claims (whichever is newer; 0
2836    /// when there is neither), and the fingerprint of the durable pack state
2837    /// (0 when unknown). The log only counts if it names that checkpoint's
2838    /// fingerprint; a stale epoch left by a crash is inert.
2839    ///
2840    /// Reading the checkpoint's own record matters: a new checkpoint retires
2841    /// the delta epoch that held the newest claim, and `journal.lsn` is written
2842    /// only after the checkpoint is durable, so for a moment the checkpoint's
2843    /// header is the only place that coverage is written down.
2844    fn durable_index_state(base_dir: &std::path::Path) -> DurableIndexState {
2845        let Ok(Some(summary)) = crate::index::checkpoint::read_checkpoint_summary(
2846            &Self::index_checkpoint_path(base_dir),
2847        ) else {
2848            return DurableIndexState::default();
2849        };
2850        // One pass over the delta log yields both what it claims and where it
2851        // ends; the log is only trusted if it names this checkpoint.
2852        let tail =
2853            delta::read_delta_tail_fingerprint(&Self::delta_path(base_dir, summary.fingerprint));
2854        let (log_coverage, fingerprint) = match tail {
2855            Ok(Some(tail)) if tail.base_fingerprint == summary.fingerprint => {
2856                (tail.coverage.unwrap_or(0), tail.tail_fingerprint)
2857            }
2858            Ok(Some(_) | None) => (0, summary.fingerprint),
2859            Err(_) => (0, 0),
2860        };
2861        DurableIndexState {
2862            covered_lsn: summary.covered_lsn.max(log_coverage),
2863            fingerprint,
2864        }
2865    }
2866
2867    /// The journal LSN this pool's packs are known to durably cover, held in
2868    /// memory. What [`Self::read_journal_lsn`] said at open, moved forward by
2869    /// every checkpoint and coverage batch this handle wrote since.
2870    #[must_use]
2871    pub fn durable_coverage(&self) -> u64 {
2872        self.durable_coverage.load(Ordering::Acquire)
2873    }
2874
2875    /// Remove every on-disk delta-log epoch file except `keep` (pass `None`
2876    /// to remove all of them, e.g. after a full rescan with no checkpoint to
2877    /// continue). Best-effort and silent on failure — an orphaned epoch file
2878    /// left behind is always safe: it is either identical to the kept one
2879    /// (redundant) or has a fingerprint that can never match the current
2880    /// checkpoint again (inert). Also opportunistically removes the single
2881    /// fixed-name log from before epoch-named logs existed; it is never read
2882    /// by this version, so leaving it around would just be clutter.
2883    fn sweep_orphan_delta_logs(base_dir: &std::path::Path, keep: Option<&std::path::Path>) {
2884        let _ = fs::remove_file(base_dir.join(INDEX_DELTA_FILE));
2885        let Ok(read_dir) = fs::read_dir(base_dir) else {
2886            return;
2887        };
2888        let prefix = format!("{INDEX_DELTA_FILE}.");
2889        for entry in read_dir.flatten() {
2890            let path = entry.path();
2891            if keep.is_some_and(|keep| keep == path) {
2892                continue;
2893            }
2894            let Some(name) = path.file_name().and_then(|n| n.to_str()) else {
2895                continue;
2896            };
2897            if name.starts_with(&prefix) {
2898                let _ = fs::remove_file(&path);
2899            }
2900        }
2901    }
2902
2903    /// Attempt to recover the per-shard/collection bookkeeping from the
2904    /// inspection sidecar, gated on the checkpoint's own pack fingerprint.
2905    ///
2906    /// Returns `BookkeepingSource::Sidecar` plus the slotted counts (for home
2907    /// shard selection) and pack-keyed entries (for the shard directory) only
2908    /// when the sidecar is gated to this exact pack set and describes every
2909    /// non-deleted collection completely — per-pack counts must sum to the
2910    /// checkpoint's own slot count. Stale, corrupt, or absent sidecars (or
2911    /// one referencing packs that aren't live open shards) fall through to
2912    /// `BookkeepingSource::SlotScan` with empty maps: correctness never
2913    /// depends on the sidecar, it only accelerates.
2914    #[allow(clippy::type_complexity)]
2915    fn gated_sidecar_bookkeeping(
2916        base_dir: &std::path::Path,
2917        local_fingerprint: u64,
2918        current_len: &HashMap<[u8; 16], u32>,
2919        open_shards: &[(u16, u64, PathBuf, u64)],
2920        deleted_collections: &HashSet<[u8; 16]>,
2921    ) -> (BookkeepingSource, HashMap<[u8; 16], HashMap<u16, u64>>) {
2922        let mut counts: HashMap<[u8; 16], HashMap<u16, u64>> = HashMap::new();
2923        let Some(directory) = read_persisted_shard_collections(base_dir) else {
2924            return (BookkeepingSource::SlotScan, counts);
2925        };
2926        if directory.fingerprint != local_fingerprint {
2927            return (BookkeepingSource::SlotScan, counts);
2928        }
2929        let pack_to_slot: HashMap<u64, u16> = open_shards
2930            .iter()
2931            .map(|(slot, pack_id, _, _)| (*pack_id, *slot))
2932            .collect();
2933        for record in &directory.records {
2934            if deleted_collections.contains(&record.collection_id) {
2935                continue;
2936            }
2937            let Some(slot) = pack_to_slot.get(&record.pack_id) else {
2938                return (BookkeepingSource::SlotScan, counts);
2939            };
2940            counts
2941                .entry(record.collection_id)
2942                .or_default()
2943                .insert(*slot, record.count);
2944        }
2945        for (collection_id, len) in current_len {
2946            if deleted_collections.contains(collection_id) {
2947                continue;
2948            }
2949            let Some(slot_counts) = counts.get(collection_id) else {
2950                return (BookkeepingSource::SlotScan, counts);
2951            };
2952            if slot_counts.values().copied().sum::<u64>() != u64::from(*len) {
2953                return (BookkeepingSource::SlotScan, counts);
2954            }
2955        }
2956        (BookkeepingSource::Sidecar, counts)
2957    }
2958
2959    /// Whether every pending redo set names a record that is really at its
2960    /// locator: the frame there belongs to the same collection and carries the
2961    /// same full hash. Any mismatch, or a frame that cannot be read, fails the
2962    /// whole log closed to the caller's rescan.
2963    fn redo_locators_verified(
2964        shards: &ShardPool,
2965        sets: &HashMap<[u8; 16], Vec<RedoRecord>>,
2966        pack_lookup: &HashMap<u64, (u16, u64)>,
2967    ) -> bool {
2968        sets.values().flatten().all(|record| {
2969            let RedoOp::Set {
2970                full_hash,
2971                pack_id,
2972                offset,
2973                ..
2974            } = record.op
2975            else {
2976                return false;
2977            };
2978            let Some(shard) = pack_lookup
2979                .get(&pack_id)
2980                .and_then(|(slot, _)| shards.get_shard(*slot))
2981            else {
2982                return false;
2983            };
2984            matches!(
2985                shards.record_identity_at(&shard, offset),
2986                Ok((collection, hash)) if collection == record.collection_id && hash == full_hash
2987            )
2988        })
2989    }
2990
2991    /// Apply logical redo sets, in `delta_seq` order, to a loaded index whose
2992    /// slots are already this process's. The index is pre-sized once for the whole
2993    /// batch and grown from its persisted identity tables when a growth boundary
2994    /// is reached; if it cannot grow (incomplete tables), the whole replay fails
2995    /// closed to the caller's rescan. Locators are checked for extent by the
2996    /// caller; identity is confirmed lazily by reads, which compare the record's
2997    /// hash.
2998    fn apply_redo_sets(
2999        index: LossyIndex,
3000        records: &[RedoRecord],
3001        pack_lookup: &HashMap<u64, (u16, u64)>,
3002    ) -> Option<LossyIndex> {
3003        let mut index = if index.is_mmap_backed() {
3004            index.clone()
3005        } else {
3006            index
3007        };
3008        let target =
3009            LossyIndex::capacity_for_entries(index.len().saturating_add(records.len()), 0)?;
3010        while usize::try_from(index.capacity()).ok()? < target {
3011            index = index.grow()?;
3012        }
3013        for record in records {
3014            let RedoOp::Set {
3015                full_hash,
3016                pack_id,
3017                offset,
3018                ..
3019            } = record.op
3020            else {
3021                return None;
3022            };
3023            let (slot, _) = *pack_lookup.get(&pack_id)?;
3024            if index.insert(&full_hash, slot, offset).is_err() {
3025                index = index.grow()?;
3026                index.insert(&full_hash, slot, offset).ok()?;
3027            }
3028        }
3029        Some(index)
3030    }
3031
3032    /// Fast-path index loading for `open_with_options`: build the
3033    /// per-collection state directly from the persisted-index checkpoint
3034    /// instead of rescanning every packfile.
3035    ///
3036    /// Returns `None` — falling through to the full rescan — for a missing,
3037    /// malformed, or stale checkpoint, one that doesn't describe the pack set
3038    /// currently on disk, or a delta log that can't be replayed onto the
3039    /// checkpoint. The fast path deliberately skips the torn-tail recovery
3040    /// scan, which is safe: a fingerprint match means the packs are the exact
3041    /// state the previous session's last sync fsynced, so there can be no torn
3042    /// tail to recover.
3043    ///
3044    /// On success, also returns the fresh [`DeltaLogState`] for the session: the
3045    /// delta log's base fingerprint (the checkpoint's) and each collection's
3046    /// checkpoint generation. A malformed or semantically inconsistent log
3047    /// makes this function return `None`, selecting the full rescan path.
3048    ///
3049    /// `reload_mode` selects the caller's stance (see [`ReloadMode`]).
3050    /// `ReloadMode::JournalBound` is for the read-committed overlay's reload
3051    /// (see `reload_index_from_checkpoint`): the caller is a read-only worker
3052    /// advancing its index/coverage pair to a writer's checkpoint, not a
3053    /// session opening the store. In that mode the exact-pack fingerprint gate
3054    /// and the delta-log replay are skipped. A writer that is still appending
3055    /// has already grown the live packs past the checkpoint, and the delta log
3056    /// may not yet cover that growth, so the gate would reject the checkpoint
3057    /// and fail the read closed — the failure mode that otherwise looks like a
3058    /// persistent miss. The overlay is authoritative for the post-checkpoint
3059    /// suffix, so the durable index only needs the checkpoint's base, and its
3060    /// coverage binds to exactly that base. The checkpoint itself must still be
3061    /// valid; only the "packs match exactly / log bridges to live" checks are
3062    /// dropped.
3063    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
3064    #[allow(clippy::too_many_lines)]
3065    fn checkpoint_scan_out(
3066        base_dir: &std::path::Path,
3067        cache_capacity: usize,
3068        shards: &ShardPool,
3069        open_shards: &[(u16, u64, PathBuf, u64)],
3070        deleted_collections: &HashSet<[u8; 16]>,
3071        writable: bool,
3072        reload_mode: ReloadMode,
3073        index_config: crate::index::IndexConfig,
3074        timings: &mut OpenTimings,
3075    ) -> Option<(RoomScanOutput, Vec<[u8; 16]>, DeltaLogState, u64)> {
3076        let decode_started = std::time::Instant::now();
3077        let checkpoint =
3078            crate::index::checkpoint::read_checkpoint(&Self::index_checkpoint_path(base_dir));
3079        timings.checkpoint_decode = decode_started.elapsed();
3080        let checkpoint = checkpoint?;
3081        let covered_lsn = checkpoint.covered_lsn;
3082        let fingerprint_started = std::time::Instant::now();
3083        let packs: Vec<(u64, u64)> = open_shards
3084            .iter()
3085            .map(|(_, pack_id, _, file_len)| (*pack_id, *file_len))
3086            .collect();
3087        let local_fingerprint = crate::index::checkpoint::pack_fingerprint(&packs);
3088        timings.fingerprint = fingerprint_started.elapsed();
3089
3090        // Generations at the checkpoint, per collection — used both to seed the
3091        // new session's `DeltaLogState` and to gate whether any delta frames may be
3092        // applied (a frame's stamp must equal the checkpoint generation it
3093        // claims to continue, which also rules out the never-recorded ancestors
3094        // of collections created or structurally changed since the checkpoint).
3095        let ckpt_generations: HashMap<[u8; 16], u64> = checkpoint
3096            .collections
3097            .iter()
3098            .map(|loaded| (loaded.collection_id, loaded.generation))
3099            .collect();
3100
3101        let delta_path = Self::delta_path(base_dir, checkpoint.fingerprint);
3102        // Only the epoch named for this exact checkpoint can ever be trusted
3103        // (see `delta_path`); anything else on disk — a stale predecessor
3104        // epoch left by a crash between checkpoint rename and retirement, or
3105        // an orphaned successor epoch from a rewrite that never completed —
3106        // is inert by construction, but sweep it now on a writable open so
3107        // it doesn't accumulate across sessions.
3108        if writable {
3109            Self::sweep_orphan_delta_logs(base_dir, Some(&delta_path));
3110        }
3111        // A delta log can only continue a checkpoint whose packs have advanced
3112        // (every append accompanies a flush that grows a pack, changing the
3113        // fingerprint). When the packs still match the checkpoint exactly,
3114        // any leftover log is stale — likely a crashed full rewrite that had
3115        // already committed the new checkpoint but not yet deleted its
3116        // predecessor log. Never replayed; removed on a writable open.
3117        // A read-journal reload deliberately skips the exact-pack gate and the
3118        // delta replay (see this function's doc): the overlay supplies the
3119        // committed suffix, and requiring the live pack set to match would fail
3120        // the read closed while a writer is still appending.
3121        let replay_needed =
3122            reload_mode == ReloadMode::Strict && local_fingerprint != checkpoint.fingerprint;
3123        if !replay_needed && writable {
3124            let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&delta_path);
3125        }
3126        // The new session continues whatever log is genuinely on disk — its
3127        // committed byte length must be inherited, not zeroed: a later append
3128        // decides whether to write a fresh base header from `log_bytes == 0`,
3129        // and re-headering an existing log would corrupt the batch framing the
3130        // next reader depends on. Zero only when the open removed the file.
3131        let mut log_bytes_on_disk = 0u64;
3132
3133        // Gate the log (case B only): it must start at this checkpoint and end
3134        // at the exact pack set now on disk, and every committed frame must
3135        // target a checkpointed collection at its recorded checkpoint
3136        // generation. Any failure rejects the log wholesale and falls through
3137        // to the rescan — never a partial replay.
3138        let mut replay_frames: Vec<DeltaFrame> = Vec::new();
3139        let mut replay_operations = Vec::new();
3140        // The journal coverage the applied part of the delta log claims. A
3141        // coverage batch lets the journal be reclaimed past the checkpoint's own
3142        // coverage, so the index built here is only complete up to the claim if
3143        // the operations the claim describes were applied.
3144        let mut log_coverage: Option<u64> = None;
3145        // A checkpoint with no surviving delta log is a valid base for the
3146        // current v3 writer. Only an actual v2 log needs a one-time rebase.
3147        let mut replay_log_version = 3;
3148        if replay_needed {
3149            let delta_started = std::time::Instant::now();
3150            if let Some(log) = delta::read_delta_log_v3(&delta_path) {
3151                if log.base_fingerprint != checkpoint.fingerprint
3152                    || log.tail_fingerprint != local_fingerprint
3153                {
3154                    timings.delta_replay = delta_started.elapsed();
3155                    if writable {
3156                        let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&delta_path);
3157                    }
3158                    return None;
3159                }
3160                log_bytes_on_disk = log.file_len;
3161                log_coverage = log.coverage;
3162                replay_operations = log.operations;
3163                replay_log_version = 3;
3164            } else {
3165                let log = delta::read_delta_log(&delta_path);
3166                let trusted = log.as_ref().is_some_and(|log| {
3167                    log.base_fingerprint == checkpoint.fingerprint
3168                        && log.tail_fingerprint == local_fingerprint
3169                        && log.frames.iter().all(|frame| {
3170                            !deleted_collections.contains(&frame.collection_id)
3171                                && ckpt_generations.get(&frame.collection_id)
3172                                    == Some(&frame.generation)
3173                        })
3174                });
3175                if trusted {
3176                    let trusted_log = log.expect("trusted implies a decoded v2 log");
3177                    log_bytes_on_disk = trusted_log.file_len;
3178                    replay_frames = trusted_log.frames;
3179                    replay_log_version = 2;
3180                } else {
3181                    timings.delta_replay = delta_started.elapsed();
3182                    if writable {
3183                        let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&delta_path);
3184                    }
3185                    return None;
3186                }
3187            }
3188            timings.delta_replay = delta_started.elapsed();
3189            // Reachable only after a log validated against both fingerprints,
3190            // so a nonzero count means operations were actually replayed.
3191            timings.delta_replay_operations = u64::try_from(replay_operations.len())
3192                .unwrap_or(u64::MAX)
3193                .saturating_add(u64::try_from(replay_frames.len()).unwrap_or(u64::MAX));
3194        } else if reload_mode == ReloadMode::JournalBound {
3195            // A read-journal reload skips the exact-pack gate (the writer keeps
3196            // appending), but it must still see the index changes a coverage
3197            // batch describes, or a reclaim past the checkpoint's coverage would
3198            // leave records that are in neither the index nor the journal. Take
3199            // the delta operations up to the last coverage claim. Every one of
3200            // them was written after the packs they name were durable, and the
3201            // writer only appends coverage while every live pack is in this
3202            // checkpoint's pack table, so their slots translate below; if one
3203            // does not, the load fails closed like any other bad slot.
3204            let delta_started = std::time::Instant::now();
3205            if let Some(mut log) = delta::read_delta_log_v3(&delta_path) {
3206                if log.base_fingerprint == checkpoint.fingerprint && log.coverage_prefix_ops > 0 {
3207                    log.operations.truncate(log.coverage_prefix_ops);
3208                    log_coverage = log.coverage;
3209                    replay_operations = log.operations;
3210                    timings.delta_replay_operations =
3211                        u64::try_from(replay_operations.len()).unwrap_or(u64::MAX);
3212                }
3213            }
3214            timings.delta_replay = delta_started.elapsed();
3215        }
3216
3217        let prepare_started = std::time::Instant::now();
3218        // Group the (gated) frames by target collection once, so the
3219        // materialization loop below applies each collection's frames by hash
3220        // lookup rather than re-scanning the whole frame list per collection.
3221        let mut frames_by_collection: HashMap<[u8; 16], Vec<DeltaFrame>> = HashMap::new();
3222        for frame in &replay_frames {
3223            frames_by_collection
3224                .entry(frame.collection_id)
3225                .or_default()
3226                .push(*frame);
3227        }
3228
3229        let mut live_generations: HashMap<[u8; 16], u64> = ckpt_generations
3230            .iter()
3231            .filter(|(collection_id, _)| !deleted_collections.contains(*collection_id))
3232            .map(|(collection_id, generation)| (*collection_id, *generation))
3233            .collect();
3234        let mut live_order: HashMap<[u8; 16], u64> = checkpoint
3235            .collections
3236            .iter()
3237            .filter(|loaded| !deleted_collections.contains(&loaded.collection_id))
3238            .enumerate()
3239            .map(|(order, loaded)| {
3240                (
3241                    loaded.collection_id,
3242                    u64::try_from(order).unwrap_or(u64::MAX),
3243                )
3244            })
3245            .collect();
3246        let mut snapshot_indexes: HashMap<[u8; 16], (u64, LossyIndex)> = HashMap::new();
3247        let mut v3_tombstones = HashSet::new();
3248        // Logical redo: every pack this log may name, by its stable id, with its
3249        // current length. The log's tail fingerprint pins those lengths, so a
3250        // record whose extent lies outside its pack is corruption.
3251        let pack_lookup: HashMap<u64, (u16, u64)> = open_shards
3252            .iter()
3253            .map(|(slot, pack_id, _, file_len)| (*pack_id, (*slot, *file_len)))
3254            .collect();
3255        let mut redo_by_collection: HashMap<[u8; 16], Vec<RedoRecord>> = HashMap::new();
3256        let mut last_delta_seq = checkpoint.base_delta_seq;
3257        let reject_log = || {
3258            if writable {
3259                let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&delta_path);
3260            }
3261        };
3262        for operation in replay_operations {
3263            match operation {
3264                DeltaOperation::Redo(record) => {
3265                    // Strictly increasing above the checkpoint's base sequence.
3266                    if record.delta_seq <= last_delta_seq {
3267                        reject_log();
3268                        return None;
3269                    }
3270                    last_delta_seq = record.delta_seq;
3271                    if deleted_collections.contains(&record.collection_id) {
3272                        continue;
3273                    }
3274                    let RedoOp::Set {
3275                        pack_id,
3276                        offset,
3277                        record_len,
3278                        ..
3279                    } = record.op
3280                    else {
3281                        reject_log();
3282                        return None;
3283                    };
3284                    let extent_ok = pack_lookup.get(&pack_id).is_some_and(|(_, pack_len)| {
3285                        offset
3286                            .checked_add(u64::from(record_len))
3287                            .is_some_and(|end| end <= *pack_len)
3288                    });
3289                    if live_generations.get(&record.collection_id) != Some(&record.base_generation)
3290                        || !extent_ok
3291                    {
3292                        reject_log();
3293                        return None;
3294                    }
3295                    redo_by_collection
3296                        .entry(record.collection_id)
3297                        .or_default()
3298                        .push(record);
3299                }
3300                DeltaOperation::Incremental(frame) => {
3301                    if deleted_collections.contains(&frame.collection_id) {
3302                        continue;
3303                    }
3304                    if live_generations.get(&frame.collection_id) != Some(&frame.generation) {
3305                        if writable {
3306                            let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&delta_path);
3307                        }
3308                        return None;
3309                    }
3310                    if let Some((_, index)) = snapshot_indexes.get(&frame.collection_id) {
3311                        if index.replay_frames(std::slice::from_ref(&frame)).is_err() {
3312                            if writable {
3313                                let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&delta_path);
3314                            }
3315                            return None;
3316                        }
3317                    } else {
3318                        frames_by_collection
3319                            .entry(frame.collection_id)
3320                            .or_default()
3321                            .push(frame);
3322                    }
3323                }
3324                DeltaOperation::CollectionSnapshot {
3325                    collection_id,
3326                    generation,
3327                    order_key,
3328                    index_blob,
3329                } => {
3330                    if deleted_collections.contains(&collection_id) {
3331                        continue;
3332                    }
3333                    let Some(capacity_bytes) = index_blob.get(..8) else {
3334                        if writable {
3335                            let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&delta_path);
3336                        }
3337                        return None;
3338                    };
3339                    let capacity =
3340                        usize::try_from(u64::from_le_bytes(capacity_bytes.try_into().ok()?))
3341                            .ok()?;
3342                    let expected_blob_len = capacity.checked_mul(24)?.checked_add(8)?;
3343                    if expected_blob_len != index_blob.len() {
3344                        if writable {
3345                            let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&delta_path);
3346                        }
3347                        return None;
3348                    }
3349                    let Ok(index) = LossyIndex::deserialize_with_config(&index_blob, index_config)
3350                    else {
3351                        if writable {
3352                            let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&delta_path);
3353                        }
3354                        return None;
3355                    };
3356                    frames_by_collection.remove(&collection_id);
3357                    redo_by_collection.remove(&collection_id);
3358                    snapshot_indexes.insert(collection_id, (generation, index));
3359                    live_generations.insert(collection_id, generation);
3360                    live_order.insert(collection_id, order_key);
3361                    v3_tombstones.remove(&collection_id);
3362                }
3363                DeltaOperation::CollectionTombstone {
3364                    collection_id,
3365                    generation,
3366                } => {
3367                    if deleted_collections.contains(&collection_id) {
3368                        continue;
3369                    }
3370                    if live_generations.get(&collection_id) != Some(&generation) {
3371                        if writable {
3372                            let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&delta_path);
3373                        }
3374                        return None;
3375                    }
3376                    live_generations.remove(&collection_id);
3377                    live_order.remove(&collection_id);
3378                    frames_by_collection.remove(&collection_id);
3379                    redo_by_collection.remove(&collection_id);
3380                    snapshot_indexes.remove(&collection_id);
3381                    v3_tombstones.insert(collection_id);
3382                }
3383                // A coverage claim changes no index state; it is read
3384                // separately (see `durable_coverage_from_disk`).
3385                DeltaOperation::Coverage { .. } => {}
3386            }
3387        }
3388
3389        // Every redo record's locator must lead to the record it names. A locator
3390        // that is in bounds but wrong would otherwise be installed, and the key
3391        // would read as missing (the read compares the frame's hash and skips a
3392        // mismatch). Offsets ascend within a pack in log order, since each set
3393        // names a freshly appended record, so this is a sequential pass over
3394        // pages the pack recovery has just read.
3395        if !Self::redo_locators_verified(shards, &redo_by_collection, &pack_lookup) {
3396            reject_log();
3397            return None;
3398        }
3399
3400        let slot_to_pack_id: HashMap<u16, u64> = open_shards
3401            .iter()
3402            .map(|(slot, pack_id, _, _)| (*slot, *pack_id))
3403            .collect();
3404
3405        // Translate every slot this checkpoint's index entries (and any
3406        // delta frame continuing it) encode — the writer's own local slot at
3407        // checkpoint-write time — to this reader's own local slot for the
3408        // same pack_id. Slot numbers are a process-local handle, not a
3409        // stable identity: a fresh reader's `discover_shards` reassigns
3410        // slots by first-free-in-pack_id-order, which does not reproduce
3411        // the writer's numbering once any shard has ever been retired (see
3412        // `CHECKPOINT_VERSION`'s v6 doc comment). A checkpoint_slot with no
3413        // entry here (its pack_id isn't among this reader's currently-open
3414        // packs) is left unmapped; any index entry that actually needs it
3415        // makes `remap_slots` fail closed below, forcing a full rescan
3416        // rather than serving an unresolvable slot.
3417        let pack_id_to_local_slot: HashMap<u64, u16> = open_shards
3418            .iter()
3419            .map(|(slot, pack_id, _, _)| (*pack_id, *slot))
3420            .collect();
3421        let slot_remap: HashMap<u16, u16> = checkpoint
3422            .pack_table
3423            .iter()
3424            .filter_map(|&(checkpoint_slot, pack_id)| {
3425                pack_id_to_local_slot
3426                    .get(&pack_id)
3427                    .map(|&local_slot| (checkpoint_slot, local_slot))
3428            })
3429            .collect();
3430
3431        // The inspection sidecar is the same reduced per-(pack, collection)
3432        // bookkeeping the loop below would recover by walking every slot of
3433        // every collection index. Accept it only when it is gated to the pack
3434        // set now on disk and describes every non-deleted collection completely
3435        // (see `gated_sidecar_bookkeeping`); any mismatch falls through to the
3436        // faithful slot walk, because the sidecar is an acceleration and
3437        // correctness never depends on it.
3438        //
3439        // Gating needs each collection's post-replay length (the checkpoint
3440        // occupancy plus whatever fresh-slot writes the replayed frames add),
3441        // so the sidecar check runs after materialization below.
3442        let mut scan_out = RoomScanOutput::default();
3443        let mut collection_order = Vec::with_capacity(checkpoint.collections.len());
3444        let mut current_len: HashMap<[u8; 16], u32> =
3445            HashMap::with_capacity(checkpoint.collections.len());
3446        timings.replay_prepare = prepare_started.elapsed();
3447        let materialization_started = std::time::Instant::now();
3448        for loaded in &checkpoint.collections {
3449            if deleted_collections.contains(&loaded.collection_id)
3450                || v3_tombstones.contains(&loaded.collection_id)
3451            {
3452                // The checkpoint may predate the deletion marker; the
3453                // logical-delete set is authoritative.
3454                continue;
3455            }
3456            // The checkpoint reader has already validated this range. Keep it
3457            // mmap-backed through the read-only fast path; the first writer
3458            // copy-on-writes it into the normal atomic slot array.
3459            let (mut index, generation) = if let Some((generation, index)) =
3460                snapshot_indexes.remove(&loaded.collection_id)
3461            {
3462                (index, generation)
3463            } else {
3464                let mmap_index = if loaded.has_homes_tails {
3465                    LossyIndex::from_mmap_slots_with_homes_tails(
3466                        Arc::clone(&checkpoint.mmap),
3467                        loaded.slots_offset,
3468                        loaded.homes_offset,
3469                        loaded.tails_offset,
3470                        loaded.capacity,
3471                        loaded.slot_count,
3472                        index_config,
3473                    )
3474                } else {
3475                    LossyIndex::from_mmap_slots_with_config(
3476                        Arc::clone(&checkpoint.mmap),
3477                        loaded.slots_offset,
3478                        loaded.capacity,
3479                        loaded.slot_count,
3480                        index_config,
3481                    )
3482                };
3483                let index = if let Some(frames) = frames_by_collection.get(&loaded.collection_id) {
3484                    let owned = mmap_index.clone();
3485                    if owned.replay_frames(frames).is_err() {
3486                        if writable {
3487                            let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&delta_path);
3488                        }
3489                        return None;
3490                    }
3491                    owned
3492                } else {
3493                    mmap_index
3494                };
3495                (index, loaded.generation)
3496            };
3497            if !index.remap_slots(&slot_remap) {
3498                return None;
3499            }
3500            let index = match redo_by_collection.remove(&loaded.collection_id) {
3501                Some(records) => Self::apply_redo_sets(index, &records, &pack_lookup)?,
3502                None => index,
3503            };
3504            current_len.insert(loaded.collection_id, u32::try_from(index.len()).ok()?);
3505            scan_out.collections.insert(
3506                loaded.collection_id,
3507                ArcSwap::from_pointee(RoomGeneration {
3508                    index,
3509                    cache: Arc::new(NodeCache::new(cache_capacity)),
3510                    generation,
3511                }),
3512            );
3513            collection_order.push(loaded.collection_id);
3514        }
3515        for (collection_id, (generation, mut index)) in snapshot_indexes {
3516            if deleted_collections.contains(&collection_id) {
3517                continue;
3518            }
3519            if !index.remap_slots(&slot_remap) {
3520                return None;
3521            }
3522            let index = match redo_by_collection.remove(&collection_id) {
3523                Some(records) => Self::apply_redo_sets(index, &records, &pack_lookup)?,
3524                None => index,
3525            };
3526            current_len.insert(collection_id, u32::try_from(index.len()).ok()?);
3527            scan_out.collections.insert(
3528                collection_id,
3529                ArcSwap::from_pointee(RoomGeneration {
3530                    index,
3531                    cache: Arc::new(NodeCache::new(cache_capacity)),
3532                    generation,
3533                }),
3534            );
3535            collection_order.push(collection_id);
3536        }
3537        if replay_log_version == 3 {
3538            collection_order
3539                .sort_unstable_by_key(|id| (live_order.get(id).copied().unwrap_or(u64::MAX), *id));
3540        }
3541        timings.index_materialization = materialization_started.elapsed();
3542        let bookkeeping_started = std::time::Instant::now();
3543
3544        let mut all_deleted_collections = deleted_collections.clone();
3545        all_deleted_collections.extend(v3_tombstones.iter().copied());
3546        let (bookkeeping_source, sidecar_counts) = Self::gated_sidecar_bookkeeping(
3547            base_dir,
3548            local_fingerprint,
3549            &current_len,
3550            open_shards,
3551            &all_deleted_collections,
3552        );
3553        timings.bookkeeping_source = bookkeeping_source;
3554        if bookkeeping_source == BookkeepingSource::Sidecar {
3555            if let Some(directory) = read_persisted_shard_collections(base_dir) {
3556                for record in directory.records {
3557                    let total = scan_out
3558                        .collection_disk_bytes
3559                        .entry(record.pack_id)
3560                        .or_default()
3561                        .entry(record.collection_id)
3562                        .or_default();
3563                    *total = total.saturating_add(record.disk_bytes);
3564                }
3565            }
3566        } else if writable {
3567            // No valid sidecar to seed the physical byte totals from. Rebuild
3568            // them exactly (every appended frame, as `physical_layout`
3569            // counts) rather than persisting zeros, and make the next sync
3570            // rewrite the sidecar. This is a recovery path, so one pack scan
3571            // is acceptable.
3572            scan_out.sidecar_missing = true;
3573            scan_out.sidecar_recovery_failed = true;
3574            if let Ok(physical) = crate::packfile::layout::physical_layout(base_dir) {
3575                scan_out.collection_disk_bytes = disk_bytes_from_physical(&physical);
3576                scan_out.sidecar_recovery_failed = false;
3577            }
3578        }
3579
3580        // Bookkeeping (home-shard seeding + shard directory) from the sidecar
3581        // where that passed its gates, otherwise a slot walk of the — possibly
3582        // replayed — live indexes.
3583        let counts_lookup: HashMap<[u8; 16], HashMap<u16, u64>> = match bookkeeping_source {
3584            BookkeepingSource::Sidecar => sidecar_counts,
3585            BookkeepingSource::SlotScan => {
3586                let mut out = HashMap::with_capacity(collection_order.len());
3587                for collection_id in &collection_order {
3588                    if let Some(gen) = scan_out.collections.get(collection_id) {
3589                        out.insert(*collection_id, gen.load().index.slot_counts());
3590                    }
3591                }
3592                out
3593            }
3594        };
3595        for collection_id in &collection_order {
3596            let counts = &counts_lookup[collection_id];
3597            // Seed the home shard from the highest shard a slot references —
3598            // the nearest proxy for the scan path's "shard of the last
3599            // record", since slots were appended in shard-id order.
3600            if let Some(&home_shard) = counts.keys().max() {
3601                shards.set_collection_home(collection_id, home_shard);
3602            }
3603            for (&slot, &count) in counts {
3604                let pack_id = slot_to_pack_id
3605                    .get(&slot)
3606                    .copied()
3607                    .unwrap_or(u64::from(slot));
3608                scan_out
3609                    .shard_collections
3610                    .entry(pack_id)
3611                    .or_default()
3612                    .insert(*collection_id, count);
3613                scan_out
3614                    .collection_shards
3615                    .entry(*collection_id)
3616                    .or_default()
3617                    .insert(pack_id);
3618            }
3619        }
3620        // `SlotScan` derives counts straight from the live indexes; the
3621        // sidecar's `counts` are consumed above either way.
3622
3623        timings.bookkeeping = bookkeeping_started.elapsed();
3624
3625        let delta_state = DeltaLogState {
3626            base_fingerprint: Some(checkpoint.fingerprint),
3627            base_generations: live_generations,
3628            next_order_key: live_order
3629                .values()
3630                .copied()
3631                .max()
3632                .map_or(0, |last| last.saturating_add(1)),
3633            base_order: live_order,
3634            log_bytes: log_bytes_on_disk,
3635            // What was on disk at open is treated as durable; only what this
3636            // session appends is owed an fsync.
3637            log_synced_bytes: log_bytes_on_disk,
3638            delta_seq_high: last_delta_seq,
3639            log_version: replay_log_version,
3640            base_pack_ids: checkpoint
3641                .pack_table
3642                .iter()
3643                .map(|&(_, pack_id)| pack_id)
3644                .collect(),
3645            ..DeltaLogState::default()
3646        };
3647
3648        // The index holds the checkpoint plus the operations of the log that were
3649        // applied, so it covers whatever those describe as well.
3650        let covered_lsn = covered_lsn.max(log_coverage.unwrap_or(0));
3651        Some((scan_out, collection_order, delta_state, covered_lsn))
3652    }
3653
3654    fn generation(&self, collection_id: &[u8; 16]) -> Option<arc_swap::Guard<Arc<RoomGeneration>>> {
3655        self.collections_read()
3656            .get(collection_id)
3657            .map(arc_swap::ArcSwapAny::load)
3658    }
3659
3660    fn collections_read(
3661        &self,
3662    ) -> parking_lot::MappedRwLockReadGuard<'_, HashMap<[u8; 16], ArcSwap<RoomGeneration>>> {
3663        parking_lot::RwLockReadGuard::map(self.index_tables.read(), |tables| &tables.collections)
3664    }
3665
3666    fn collections_write(
3667        &self,
3668    ) -> parking_lot::MappedRwLockWriteGuard<'_, HashMap<[u8; 16], ArcSwap<RoomGeneration>>> {
3669        parking_lot::RwLockWriteGuard::map(self.index_tables.write(), |tables| {
3670            &mut tables.collections
3671        })
3672    }
3673
3674    fn shard_collections_read(
3675        &self,
3676    ) -> parking_lot::MappedRwLockReadGuard<'_, HashMap<u64, HashMap<[u8; 16], u64>>> {
3677        parking_lot::RwLockReadGuard::map(self.index_tables.read(), |tables| {
3678            &tables.shard_collections
3679        })
3680    }
3681
3682    /// Collection IDs currently known to this engine, sorted for deterministic output.
3683    pub fn collection_ids(&self) -> Vec<[u8; 16]> {
3684        let mut ids: Vec<[u8; 16]> = self.collections_read().keys().copied().collect();
3685        ids.sort_unstable();
3686        ids
3687    }
3688
3689    /// Collection IDs whose live indexes currently reference records in
3690    /// `slot`. A collection repacked away from the slot is excluded even if
3691    /// its old bytes remain in the append-only pack. Order is unspecified.
3692    ///
3693    /// # Errors
3694    /// Returns [`StorageError::Io`] with `NotFound` if `slot` does not
3695    /// correspond to an open shard.
3696    pub fn collections_referencing_shard(&self, slot: u16) -> Result<Vec<[u8; 16]>, StorageError> {
3697        let shard = self.shards.get_shard(slot).ok_or_else(|| {
3698            StorageError::Io(std::io::Error::new(
3699                std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound,
3700                format!("no open shard with id {slot}"),
3701            ))
3702        })?;
3703        // O(1) against the incrementally-maintained shard→collection directory
3704        // instead of scanning the shard file — this used to be the
3705        // dominant cost of shard retirement/evacuation-style operations
3706        // on a large shard.
3707        Ok(self
3708            .shard_collections_read()
3709            .get(&shard.pack_id)
3710            .map(|collections| collections.keys().copied().collect())
3711            .unwrap_or_default())
3712    }
3713
3714    /// Repack every collection that still references `slot`.
3715    ///
3716    /// A shard only ever retires once *every* collection referencing it has
3717    /// repacked past its data there (see `retire_empty_shards`) — there's
3718    /// no per-shard compaction primitive, since reachability (what's
3719    /// live vs. garbage) is inherently a per-collection concept, not a shard
3720    /// one. This is the targeted way to reclaim one specific shard: find
3721    /// every collection still pinning it live and repack each of them, instead
3722    /// of waiting for each collection to independently cross its own repack
3723    /// threshold. Live records get moved to whatever's currently that
3724    /// collection's home shard (`ShardPool::collection_home`) — not necessarily the
3725    /// pool's single "main" shard, since homes are per-collection, not global.
3726    ///
3727    /// Returns `(collection_id, kept, dropped)` for each collection repacked, in the
3728    /// order `collections_referencing_shard` returned them. Does not itself
3729    /// guarantee the shard retires — a collection with `set_live_roots` never
3730    /// called preserves everything (nothing is provably garbage) and its
3731    /// repack is a no-op for this purpose.
3732    ///
3733    /// # Errors
3734    /// Returns `StorageError` if any collection's repack fails; already-repacked
3735    /// collections in this call are not rolled back.
3736    pub fn repack_shard(
3737        &self,
3738        slot: u16,
3739        extract_edges: impl Fn(&[u8; 16], &[u8]) -> Vec<[u8; 16]>,
3740    ) -> Result<Vec<([u8; 16], usize, usize)>, StorageError> {
3741        let collections = self.collections_referencing_shard(slot)?;
3742        let mut results = Vec::with_capacity(collections.len());
3743        for collection_id in collections {
3744            let (kept, dropped) = self
3745                .repack_collection_reachable(&collection_id, |hash, data| {
3746                    extract_edges(hash, data)
3747                })?;
3748            results.push((collection_id, kept, dropped));
3749        }
3750        Ok(results)
3751    }
3752
3753    /// A collection's `(entry count, memory usage in bytes, index capacity)`,
3754    /// if the collection exists. `entry count / capacity` is the index's
3755    /// load factor.
3756    pub fn collection_index_info(&self, collection_id: &[u8; 16]) -> Option<(usize, usize, u32)> {
3757        self.collections_read().get(collection_id).map(|gen| {
3758            let g = gen.load();
3759            (g.index.len(), g.index.memory_usage(), g.index.capacity())
3760        })
3761    }
3762
3763    /// `(collection_id, entry count, memory usage in bytes, index capacity)`
3764    /// for every known collection, sorted by collection ID, in a single pass
3765    /// over the collection map.
3766    pub fn collection_summaries(&self) -> Vec<CollectionSummary> {
3767        let tables = self.index_tables.read();
3768        tables
3769            .collection_order
3770            .iter()
3771            .filter_map(|id| {
3772                tables.collections.get(id).map(|gen| {
3773                    let g = gen.load();
3774                    (
3775                        *id,
3776                        g.index.len(),
3777                        g.index.memory_usage(),
3778                        g.index.capacity(),
3779                    )
3780                })
3781            })
3782            .collect()
3783    }

3820    /// Returns `true` if a collection's index has reached the configured repack
3821    /// threshold.
3822    ///
3823    /// Repacking is entirely caller-driven — nothing in this engine polls
3824    /// this on its own. A background GC worker is expected to call this
3825    /// periodically and issue `repack_collection_reachable` itself; nothing in
3826    /// `mtxdb` currently does so.
3827    #[must_use]
3828    pub fn needs_repack(&self, collection_id: &[u8; 16]) -> bool {
3829        let count = self
3830            .collection_index_info(collection_id)
3831            .map_or(0, |(len, _, _)| len as u64);
3832        count
3833            >= self
3834                .repack_threshold_entries
3835                .load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed)
3836    }

3868    fn scan_collection_records(
3869        &self,
3870        collection_id: &[u8; 16],
3871    ) -> Result<Vec<ScannedShard>, StorageError> {
3872        let mut scanned: Vec<ScannedShard> = Vec::new();
3873        for (slot, shard) in self.shards.all_shards() {
3874            match packfile::scan_packfile(&shard.path) {
3875                Ok(entries) => {
3876                    let collection_entries: Vec<([u8; 16], u64)> = entries
3877                        .into_iter()
3878                        .filter(|(rid, _, _)| rid == collection_id)
3879                        .map(|(_, hash, offset)| (hash, offset))
3880                        .collect();
3881                    if !collection_entries.is_empty() {
3882                        scanned.push((slot, collection_entries));
3883                    }
3884                }
3885                Err(e) => {
3886                    return Err(StorageError::Io(e));
3887                }
3888            }
3889        }
3890        Ok(scanned)
3891    }
3892
3893    /// Scan every open shard once and build deduplicated record maps for the
3894    /// requested collections. This is the batch counterpart to `scan_collection_records`:
3895    /// a shard-compaction preflight must not reread the same packfile once per
3896    /// collection in its closure.
3897    fn scan_collection_record_maps(
3898        &self,
3899        collection_ids: &[[u8; 16]],
3900    ) -> Result<HashMap<[u8; 16], RepackRecordMap>, StorageError> {
3901        let wanted: HashSet<[u8; 16]> = collection_ids.iter().copied().collect();
3902        let mut maps: HashMap<[u8; 16], RepackRecordMap> = wanted
3903            .iter()
3904            .copied()
3905            .map(|collection_id| (collection_id, HashMap::new()))
3906            .collect();
3907        for (slot, shard) in self.shards.all_shards() {
3908            for (collection_id, hash, offset) in packfile::scan_packfile(&shard.path)? {
3909                if wanted.contains(&collection_id) {
3910                    maps.entry(collection_id)
3911                        .or_default()
3912                        .insert(hash, (slot, offset));
3913                }
3914            }
3915        }
3916        Ok(maps)
3917    }
3918
3919    fn build_index(
3920        offsets: &[([u8; 16], u16, u64)],
3921        index_config: crate::index::IndexConfig,
3922    ) -> Result<LossyIndex, StorageError> {
3923        let index = LossyIndex::with_config(
3924            offsets
3925                .len()
3926                .saturating_mul(2)
3927                .max(NEW_COLLECTION_INDEX_FLOOR),
3928            index_config,
3929        );
3930        for (hash, slot, offset) in offsets {
3931            check_index_offset(*slot, hash, *offset)?;
3932            let _ = index.insert(hash, *slot, *offset);
3933        }
3934        Ok(index)
3935    }
3936
3937    /// Convert a slot-keyed `slot_counts` from `LossyIndex` to a pack_id-keyed
3938    /// `HashMap<u64, u64>` for use with `replace_collection_shard_counts`.
3939    fn slot_counts_to_pack_id_counts(&self, counts: &HashMap<u16, u64>) -> HashMap<u64, u64> {
3940        let shards = self.shards.all_shards();
3941        let slot_to_pack_id: HashMap<u16, u64> = shards
3942            .iter()
3943            .map(|(slot, shard)| (*slot, shard.pack_id))
3944            .collect();
3945        counts
3946            .iter()
3947            .map(|(&slot, &count)| {
3948                let pack_id = slot_to_pack_id
3949                    .get(&slot)
3950                    .copied()
3951                    .unwrap_or(u64::from(slot));
3952                (pack_id, count)
3953            })
3954            .collect()
3955    }
