3957    fn deleted_collections_path(base_dir: &std::path::Path) -> PathBuf {
3958        base_dir.join("deleted.collections")
3959    }
3960
3961    fn load_deleted_collections(base_dir: &std::path::Path) -> HashSet<[u8; 16]> {
3962        let path = Self::deleted_collections_path(base_dir);
3963        let Ok(bytes) = fs::read(&path) else {
3964            return HashSet::new();
3965        };
3966        bytes
3967            .chunks_exact(16)
3968            .map(|chunk| {
3969                let mut id = [0u8; 16];
3970                id.copy_from_slice(chunk);
3971                id
3972            })
3973            .collect()
3974    }
3975
3976    fn persist_deleted_collection(&self, collection_id: &[u8; 16]) -> Result<(), StorageError> {
3977        let path = Self::deleted_collections_path(&self.base_dir);
3978        let mut set = self.deleted_collections.lock();
3979        set.insert(*collection_id);
3980        let bytes: Vec<u8> = set.iter().flat_map(|id| id.iter().copied()).collect();
3981        fs::write(&path, &bytes).map_err(StorageError::Io)?;
3982        Ok(())
3983    }
3984
3985    /// Fast path for `store_generation`'s new-collection case: most
3986    /// collections were never deleted, so check the in-memory cache before
3987    /// paying for a lock + no-op write. Avoids re-reading `deleted.collections`
3988    /// from disk on every first write to a new collection — previously this
3989    /// reloaded the whole file from disk unconditionally, which under a cold
3990    /// page cache turned a batch of first-writes across many collections into
3991    /// one serialized disk read per collection.
3992    fn is_deleted_collection(&self, collection_id: &[u8; 16]) -> bool {
3993        self.deleted_collections.lock().contains(collection_id)
3994    }
3995
3996    fn clear_deleted_collection(&self, collection_id: &[u8; 16]) -> Result<(), StorageError> {
3997        let path = Self::deleted_collections_path(&self.base_dir);
3998        let mut set = self.deleted_collections.lock();
3999        if set.remove(collection_id) {
4000            let bytes: Vec<u8> = set.iter().flat_map(|id| id.iter().copied()).collect();
4001            fs::write(&path, &bytes).map_err(StorageError::Io)?;
4002        }
4003        Ok(())
4004    }
4005
4006    /// Records one new record landing in `slot` for `collection_id` — the
4007    /// cheap, O(1) path for a plain `put` that only appends, never moves
4008    /// or drops anything. Kept separate from
4009    /// [`Self::replace_collection_shard_counts`], which pays for a full
4010    /// per-shard recount and is reserved for the cases that actually
4011    /// change a collection's existing distribution (an index rebuild or a
4012    /// repack), so a normal write never regresses to O(collection size).
4013    fn record_new_shard_collection(&self, pack_id: u64, collection_id: &[u8; 16], disk_bytes: u64) {
4014        let mut tables = self.index_tables.write();
4015        let count = tables
4016            .shard_collections
4017            .entry(pack_id)
4018            .or_default()
4019            .entry(*collection_id)
4020            .or_insert(0);
4021        *count = count.saturating_add(1);
4022        tables
4023            .collection_shards
4024            .entry(*collection_id)
4025            .or_default()
4026            .insert(pack_id);
4027        let bytes = tables
4028            .collection_disk_bytes
4029            .entry(pack_id)
4030            .or_default()
4031            .entry(*collection_id)
4032            .or_default();
4033        *bytes = bytes.saturating_add(disk_bytes);
4034    }
4035
4036    fn record_put_many_shard_collections(
4037        &self,
4038        collection_id: &[u8; 16],
4039        count_packs: &[u64],
4040        byte_packs: &[(u64, u64)],
4041    ) {
4042        let mut tables = self.index_tables.write();
4043        for &pack_id in count_packs {
4044            let count = tables
4045                .shard_collections
4046                .entry(pack_id)
4047                .or_default()
4048                .entry(*collection_id)
4049                .or_insert(0);
4050            *count = count.saturating_add(1);
4051            tables
4052                .collection_shards
4053                .entry(*collection_id)
4054                .or_default()
4055                .insert(pack_id);
4056        }
4057        for &(pack_id, disk_bytes) in byte_packs {
4058            let bytes = tables
4059                .collection_disk_bytes
4060                .entry(pack_id)
4061                .or_default()
4062                .entry(*collection_id)
4063                .or_default();
4064            *bytes = bytes.saturating_add(disk_bytes);
4065        }
4066    }
4067
4068    fn record_disk_bytes(&self, pack_id: u64, collection_id: &[u8; 16], disk_bytes: u64) {
4069        let mut tables = self.index_tables.write();
4070        let bytes = tables
4071            .collection_disk_bytes
4072            .entry(pack_id)
4073            .or_default()
4074            .entry(*collection_id)
4075            .or_default();
4076        *bytes = bytes.saturating_add(disk_bytes);
4077    }
4078
4079    fn replace_collection_disk_bytes(
4080        &self,
4081        collection_id: &[u8; 16],
4082        bytes_by_pack: &HashMap<u64, u64>,
4083    ) {
4084        let mut tables = self.index_tables.write();
4085        for collections in tables.collection_disk_bytes.values_mut() {
4086            collections.remove(collection_id);
4087        }
4088        for (&pack_id, &disk_bytes) in bytes_by_pack {
4089            tables
4090                .collection_disk_bytes
4091                .entry(pack_id)
4092                .or_default()
4093                .insert(*collection_id, disk_bytes);
4094        }
4095        tables
4096            .collection_disk_bytes
4097            .retain(|_, collections| !collections.is_empty());
4098    }
4099
4100    /// Replaces `collection_id`'s entire contribution to `shard_collections` with
4101    /// `counts` (typically `LossyIndex::slot_counts()` converted to `pack_id` keys)
4102    /// — clears it out of any shard it no longer occupies and installs the fresh
4103    /// per-shard counts. Used wherever a collection's index is replaced wholesale
4104    /// rather than incrementally appended to, since only then can its distribution
4105    /// across shards actually change.
4106    fn replace_collection_shard_counts(
4107        &self,
4108        collection_id: &[u8; 16],
4109        counts: &HashMap<u64, u64>,
4110    ) {
4111        let mut tables = self.index_tables.write();
4112        let old_shards = tables
4113            .collection_shards
4114            .insert(*collection_id, counts.keys().copied().collect());
4115        if let Some(old_shards) = old_shards {
4116            for pack_id in &old_shards {
4117                if !counts.contains_key(pack_id) {
4118                    if let Some(m) = tables.shard_collections.get_mut(pack_id) {
4119                        m.remove(collection_id);
4120                        if m.is_empty() {
4121                            tables.shard_collections.remove(pack_id);
4122                        }
4123                    }
4124                }
4125            }
4126        }
4127        for (&pack_id, &count) in counts {
4128            tables
4129                .shard_collections
4130                .entry(pack_id)
4131                .or_default()
4132                .insert(*collection_id, count);
4133        }
4134    }
4135
4136    /// Removes `collection_id` from `shard_collections`/`collection_shards` entirely —
4137    /// used on collection deletion, where nothing of the collection survives in any
4138    /// shard.
4139    fn remove_collection_shard_counts(&self, collection_id: &[u8; 16]) {
4140        let mut tables = self.index_tables.write();
4141        let Some(old_shards) = tables.collection_shards.remove(collection_id) else {
4142            return;
4143        };
4144        for pack_id in old_shards {
4145            if let Some(m) = tables.shard_collections.get_mut(&pack_id) {
4146                m.remove(collection_id);
4147                if m.is_empty() {
4148                    tables.shard_collections.remove(&pack_id);
4149                }
4150            }
4151        }
4152    }
4153
4154    /// Path to the persisted shard→collection directory for a base directory.
4155    fn shard_collections_path(base_dir: &std::path::Path) -> PathBuf {
4156        base_dir.join("shard_collections.bin")
4157    }
4158
4159    /// Persist the current `shard_collections` directory to disk: which collections
4160    /// have live records in each shard, and how many. Read by
4161    /// [`Self::collection_directory_from_disk`] — a free function a separate,
4162    /// short-lived process (a `collections`-style CLI listing) can call without
4163    /// opening a full `PackfileStorage` (which would otherwise mean
4164    /// scanning and index-building every shard just to answer "what collections
4165    /// exist and how big are they").
4166    ///
4167    /// Writes to a temp file and renames into place, same crash-safety
4168    /// pattern as `ShardPool::persist_stats`.
4169    ///
4170    /// The header pins the directory to the `pack_fingerprint` of the
4171    /// current committed pack set. Only the caller writing right after
4172    /// flush+fsync (the index-checkpoint rewrite) is guaranteed to produce a
4173    /// fingerprint matching the checkpoint's, which is what lets open rebuild
4174    /// per-shard counts from these records instead of walking every slot; any
4175    /// other write leaves a directory that open either accepts (pack set
4176    /// unchanged) or safely falls back from.
4177    ///
4178    /// # Errors
4179    /// Returns `StorageError` on write or rename failure.
4180    pub fn persist_shard_collections(&self) -> Result<(), StorageError> {
4181        if self
4182            .shard_collections_recovery_failed
4183            .load(Ordering::Acquire)
4184        {
4185            // The open-time recovery scan failed, so the byte totals are not
4186            // trustworthy. Retry it now; until it succeeds nothing is written,
4187            // so zero-byte fallbacks are never published.
4188            //
4189            // The scan and the swap of the in-memory totals must not interleave
4190            // with an append: a frame written after the scan would be missing
4191            // from the totals while the persisted fingerprint already covers
4192            // it, and nothing would ever correct that. So hold every
4193            // collection's put mutex (the same sorted-lock pattern the
4194            // checkpoint writer uses; no caller holds one when it persists)
4195            // across the flush, the scan, and the swap. This only runs on the
4196            // rare recovery path, so briefly stalling writers is acceptable.
4197            // Take the creation lock first, then read the collection set: a
4198            // collection created earlier is in the set, and none can appear
4199            // while it is held. Sort so every mutex is acquired in one global
4200            // order, whatever else locks several collections at once.
4201            let create_guard = self.collection_creation.write();
4202            let mut collection_ids: Vec<[u8; 16]> =
4203                self.collections_read().keys().copied().collect();
4204            collection_ids.sort_unstable();
4205            collection_ids.dedup();
4206            let lock_arcs: Vec<_> = collection_ids.iter().map(|id| self.put_mutex(id)).collect();
4207            let guards: Vec<_> = lock_arcs.iter().map(|arc| arc.lock()).collect();
4208            self.shards.flush_all().map_err(StorageError::Io)?;
4209            let physical = crate::packfile::layout::physical_layout(&self.base_dir)
4210                .map_err(StorageError::Io)?;
4211            #[cfg(test)]
4212            {
4213                let hook = self.recovery_pause_hook.lock().clone();
4214                if let Some(hook) = hook {
4215                    hook();
4216                }
4217            }
4218            self.index_tables.write().collection_disk_bytes = disk_bytes_from_physical(&physical);
4219            drop(guards);
4220            drop(create_guard);
4221            self.shard_collections_recovery_failed
4222                .store(false, Ordering::Release);
4223        }
4224        let mut buf = Vec::new();
4225        buf.extend_from_slice(SHARD_ROOMS_MAGIC);
4226        buf.push(SHARD_ROOMS_VERSION);
4227        let packs: Vec<(u64, u64)> = self
4228            .shards
4229            .all_shards()
4230            .into_iter()
4231            .map(|(_, shard)| (shard.pack_id, shard.file_len()))
4232            .collect();
4233        let fingerprint = crate::index::checkpoint::pack_fingerprint(&packs);
4234        buf.extend_from_slice(&fingerprint.to_le_bytes());
4235        let persisted_at = std::time::SystemTime::now()
4236            .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
4237            .map_or(0, |d| d.as_secs());
4238        buf.extend_from_slice(&persisted_at.to_le_bytes());
4239        let records = {
4240            let tables = self.index_tables.read();
4241            let collection_order: HashMap<[u8; 16], u64> = tables
4242                .collection_order
4243                .iter()
4244                .enumerate()
4245                .map(|(index, collection_id)| {
4246                    u64::try_from(index)
4247                        .map(|index| (*collection_id, index))
4248                        .map_err(|_| {
4249                            StorageError::Io(std::io::Error::other("collection order exceeds u64"))
4250                        })
4251                })
4252                .collect::<Result<_, _>>()?;
4253            let mut records = Vec::new();
4254            for (pack_id, collections) in &tables.shard_collections {
4255                for (collection_id, count) in collections {
4256                    let order = collection_order
4257                        .get(collection_id)
4258                        .copied()
4259                        .unwrap_or(u64::MAX);
4260                    let disk_bytes = tables
4261                        .collection_disk_bytes
4262                        .get(pack_id)
4263                        .and_then(|collections| collections.get(collection_id))
4264                        .copied()
4265                        .unwrap_or(0);
4266                    records.push((*pack_id, *collection_id, *count, order, disk_bytes));
4267                }
4268            }
4269            records
4270        };
4271        for (pack_id, collection_id, count, order, disk_bytes) in records {
4272            buf.extend_from_slice(&pack_id.to_le_bytes());
4273            buf.extend_from_slice(&collection_id);
4274            buf.extend_from_slice(&count.to_le_bytes());
4275            buf.extend_from_slice(&order.to_le_bytes());
4276            buf.extend_from_slice(&disk_bytes.to_le_bytes());
4277        }
4278
4279        let unique = SHARD_ROOMS_TMP_COUNTER.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
4280        let tmp_path = Self::shard_collections_path(&self.base_dir)
4281            .with_extension(format!("bin.tmp.{}.{unique}", std::process::id()));
4282        let final_path = Self::shard_collections_path(&self.base_dir);
4283        let write_result = (|| -> std::io::Result<()> {
4284            let mut tmp = fs::File::create(&tmp_path)?;
4285            std::io::Write::write_all(&mut tmp, &buf)?;
4286            // See the matching comment in `checkpoint::write_checkpoint`:
4287            // this tmp file is renamed away immediately below and never
4288            // reopened by this name, so only its data need survive —
4289            // `sync_data` (fdatasync) skips the timestamp-only metadata
4290            // flush `sync_all` (fsync) would also perform.
4291            tmp.sync_data()
4292        })();
4293        if let Err(e) = write_result {
4294            let _ = fs::remove_file(&tmp_path);
4295            return Err(StorageError::Io(e));
4296        }
4297        fs::rename(&tmp_path, &final_path).map_err(StorageError::Io)?;
4298        // Counted only after the rename succeeds, so the metric reflects
4299        // completed sidecar writes, not attempts (no containing-directory
4300        // fsync is issued, so "completed" stops short of claiming power-loss
4301        // durability for the directory entry itself).
4302        self.sidecar_writes.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
4303        self.shard_collections_dirty.store(false, Ordering::Relaxed);
4304        self.shard_collections_stale.store(false, Ordering::Relaxed);
4305        Ok(())
4306    }
4307
4308    /// True when a completed sync barrier deferred the `shard_collections.bin`
4309    /// write to the next anchor (checkpoint rewrite, repack, or clean
4310    /// shutdown). Writes that have not been synced are not reported here: they
4311    /// invalidate the checkpoint fast path, so the next open full-scans and
4312    /// never consults the sidecar.
4313    pub fn is_shard_collections_stale(&self) -> bool {
4314        self.shard_collections_stale.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
4315    }
4316
4317    /// Best-effort wrapper around [`Self::persist_shard_collections`] — logs and
4318    /// swallows a failure rather than turning it into a hard error, same
4319    /// contract as `ShardPool`'s stats persistence: this is observability
4320    /// data, not something worth failing an otherwise-successful sync
4321    /// over.
4322    fn persist_shard_collections_best_effort(&self) {
4323        match self.persist_shard_collections() {
4324            Ok(()) => self
4325                .shard_collections_failure_logged
4326                .store(false, Ordering::Relaxed),
4327            Err(e) => {
4328                // A persistent failure would otherwise log on every sync.
4329                if !self
4330                    .shard_collections_failure_logged
4331                    .swap(true, Ordering::Relaxed)
4332                {
4333                    eprintln!("mtxdb: failed to persist shard→collection directory: {e}");
4334                }
4335            }
4336        }
4337    }
4338
4339    /// Replace this collection's pending slot deltas with a whole-index v3
4340    /// snapshot after a structural change (capacity growth, rebuild, repack,
4341    /// refresh, or collection creation). The counter records collection-level
4342    /// snapshot promotions; it no longer means a store-wide checkpoint rewrite.
4343    fn invalidate_delta_log(&self, collection_id: &[u8; 16]) {
4344        self.delta_invalidations.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
4345        self.delta_state
4346            .lock()
4347            .pending
4348            .insert(*collection_id, PendingDelta::Snapshot);
4349    }
4350
4351    fn mark_v3_collection_deleted(&self, collection_id: &[u8; 16]) {
4352        let mut state = self.delta_state.lock();
4353        // The tombstone validates against the generation visible to replay
4354        // immediately before this operation, which may be an earlier
4355        // checkpoint/snapshot generation rather than the just-deleted live
4356        // generation (for example, if growth and deletion happened in one
4357        // unsynced interval).
4358        let generation = state
4359            .base_generations
4360            .get(collection_id)
4361            .copied()
4362            .unwrap_or(0);
4363        state
4364            .pending
4365            .insert(*collection_id, PendingDelta::Delete { generation });
4366    }
4367
4368    /// Record a successful index insertion as a logical redo record, if the delta
4369    /// log can legitimately continue through it.
4370    ///
4371    /// The record names the change by content identity (`hash`) and its
4372    /// locator (`pack_id`, `offset`, `record_len`), not by table position, and
4373    /// takes its `delta_seq` from this pool's counter under the delta-state lock,
4374    /// so sequence order is append order across collections. Recording stops
4375    /// once a snapshot or tombstone supersedes the collection's pending updates.
4376    /// A generation mismatch, or a locator a record cannot represent, promotes
4377    /// the collection to a snapshot instead.
4378    fn record_redo(
4379        &self,
4380        collection_id: &[u8; 16],
4381        generation: u64,
4382        hash: &[u8; 16],
4383        slot: u16,
4384        offset: u64,
4385        record_len: u64,
4386    ) {
4387        // A slot with no open shard has no stable pack id to name. Falling back
4388        // to the slot number would name a different pack that happens to carry
4389        // that number, so such a record is not representable: the collection is
4390        // snapshotted instead.
4391        let pack_id = self.shards.get_shard(slot).map(|shard| shard.pack_id);
4392        let record_len = u32::try_from(record_len).unwrap_or(0);
4393        let representable =
4394            pack_id.is_some() && record_len != 0 && offset <= crate::index::IndexEntry::MAX_OFFSET;
4395        let pack_id = pack_id.unwrap_or(0);
4396        let mut state = self.delta_state.lock();
4397        let base_generation_matches =
4398            state.base_generations.get(collection_id) == Some(&generation);
4399        if !representable || !base_generation_matches {
4400            // Replaces pending records too: the snapshot taken at sync time
4401            // includes them.
4402            if !matches!(
4403                state.pending.get(collection_id),
4404                Some(PendingDelta::Delete { .. })
4405            ) {
4406                state.pending.insert(*collection_id, PendingDelta::Snapshot);
4407            }
4408            return;
4409        }
4410        if matches!(
4411            state.pending.get(collection_id),
4412            Some(PendingDelta::Snapshot | PendingDelta::Delete { .. })
4413        ) {
4414            return;
4415        }
4416        state.delta_seq_high = state.delta_seq_high.saturating_add(1);
4417        let record = RedoRecord {
4418            collection_id: *collection_id,
4419            op: RedoOp::Set {
4420                full_hash: *hash,
4421                pack_id,
4422                offset,
4423                record_len,
4424            },
4425            delta_seq: state.delta_seq_high,
4426            base_generation: generation,
4427        };
4428        match state.pending.entry(*collection_id) {
4429            std::collections::hash_map::Entry::Vacant(entry) => {
4430                entry.insert(PendingDelta::Redo(vec![record]));
4431            }
4432            std::collections::hash_map::Entry::Occupied(mut entry) => {
4433                if let PendingDelta::Redo(records) = entry.get_mut() {
4434                    records.push(record);
4435                }
4436            }
4437        }
4438    }
4439
4440    /// Snapshot every collection's live generation for a checkpoint, encoded as
4441    /// `(collection_id, generation, room)`. Callers hold all collection put
4442    /// mutexes, so the snapshot is a consistent point in the index.
4443    fn checkpoint_snapshots(&self) -> Vec<([u8; 16], u64, Arc<RoomGeneration>)> {
4444        let tables = self.index_tables.read();
4445        tables
4446            .collection_order
4447            .iter()
4448            .filter_map(|collection_id| {
4449                tables.collections.get(collection_id).map(|g| {
4450                    let generation = arc_swap::ArcSwapAny::load_full(g);
4451                    (*collection_id, generation.generation, generation)
4452                })
4453            })
4454            .collect()
4455    }
4456
4457    /// The journal LSN this store's checkpoint covers: its own pool's committed
4458    /// watermark on a shared segment (one group can interleave other pools'
4459    /// frames), or the global committed LSN for a per-pool segment. `None` when
4460    /// no journal is enabled.
4461    ///
4462    /// The value is floored by the durable coverage already recorded beside the
4463    /// checkpoint. A pool whose frames have all been reclaimed has no committed
4464    /// group left to derive a watermark from, so the fresh coordinator reports
4465    /// zero for it; writing that zero would erase the durable coverage and make
4466    /// the next replay start from a stale bound. Coverage only ever advances.
4467    fn checkpoint_covered_lsn(&self) -> Option<u64> {
4468        self.journal().map(|journal| {
4469            #[cfg(feature = "multi-reader")]
4470            let committed = match pool_from_tag(self.journal_pool.load(Ordering::Acquire)) {
4471                Some(pool) => journal.committed_lsn_for_pool(pool),
4472                None => journal.committed_lsn(),
4473            };
4474            #[cfg(not(feature = "multi-reader"))]
4475            let committed = journal.committed_lsn();
4476            // The shared-WAL coverage batch and the full checkpoint both run
4477            // `sync_all` after capturing this and before recording it, so a
4478            // frame at or below `committed` that has been applied is covered.
4479            // `a_power_cut_image_never_loses_a_record_a_claim_covered` checks
4480            // it for autocommit writes and shared-WAL transactions, on records
4481            // made durable by a full sync of both pools (an inflated claim
4482            // fails it). A pool synced alone while another stays silent, and
4483            // per-pool coordinators, are not exercised. `max` only keeps the
4484            // value from moving backwards.
4485            committed.max(self.durable_coverage())
4486        })
4487    }
4488
4489    /// Persist the full per-collection index state to `index.checkpoint`, so
4490    /// the next open can load it instead of rescanning every packfile.
4491    ///
4492    /// Called after every sync barrier — packfile data first, checkpoint
4493    /// second. A crash in between leaves a fingerprint mismatch that the next
4494    /// open resolves with a rescan; a crash after leaves a valid checkpoint.
4495    ///
4496    /// The rewrite hands off the delta log across two epochs: the session
4497    /// keeps appending to the log that continues the *old* checkpoint (D0)
4498    /// right up to the rotation below, after which every `put` is recorded
4499    /// against a fresh epoch (D1) named for the new checkpoint's fingerprint.
4500    /// D0's file is untouched through the rotation and retired only once the
4501    /// new checkpoint (C1) is durably renamed, so a crash at any point pairs
4502    /// the loader with whichever log legitimately continues the checkpoint on
4503    /// disk: before C1's rename C0 + D0 is authoritative, after it C1 + D1.
4504    /// The log's fingerprint-based name is itself the safety gate — a stale
4505    /// predecessor (D0) or an orphaned successor (D1) can never match the
4506    /// checkpoint a reopen loads (see [`Self::delta_path`]).
4507    ///
4508    /// Cheap no-op when no collection data has changed since the last write
4509    /// (`index_checkpoint_dirty` cleared on success), so a writer that syncs
4510    /// repeatedly without writes doesn't rewrite the acceleration file. The
4511    /// flag is cleared only when nothing after this rewrite's snapshot is
4512    /// left unpersisted (see the lock re-acquisition below), so a transient
4513    /// failure or a racing write defers rather than drops the update.
4514    fn persist_index_checkpoint(&self) -> Result<(), StorageError> {
4515        // A synchronous checkpoint never overlaps a worker's.
4516        self.finish_checkpoint_worker(true);
4517        let Some(captured) = self.capture_checkpoint()? else {
4518            return Ok(());
4519        };
4520        let CapturedCheckpoint { tail, breakdown } = captured;
4521        match tail.run() {
4522            Ok(done) => {
4523                self.record_checkpoint(breakdown, &done);
4524                Ok(())
4525            }
4526            Err(error) => {
4527                self.abandon_checkpoint();
4528                Err(error)
4529            }
4530        }
4531    }
4532
4533    /// The part of a checkpoint that needs the locks: everything up to the
4534    /// point where the image bytes and the delta-epoch rotation are captured.
4535    /// After it returns the returned tail owns everything it needs, so it can
4536    /// run on any thread. `None` when nothing is dirty.
4537    fn capture_checkpoint(&self) -> Result<Option<CapturedCheckpoint>, StorageError> {
4538        let started = std::time::Instant::now();
4539        let mut breakdown = CheckpointBreakdown::default();
4540        if !self.index_checkpoint_dirty.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
4541            return Ok(None);
4542        }
4543        // With a journal, this checkpoint must make the packs durable before it
4544        // records coverage, and it does so below with every collection locked,
4545        // which stalls every writer for as long as the fsync takes. Do the bulk
4546        // of that here first, with no lock held: the fsync under the locks then
4547        // only covers what was written since.
4548        if self.journal().is_some() {
4549            self.shards.sync_dirty()?;
4550        }
4551        breakdown.pre_sync = started.elapsed();
4552        let lock_started = std::time::Instant::now();
4553        // Epoch-handoff protocol: hold every collection's put_mutex only
4554        // across the snapshot + epoch rotation below (same sorted-lock
4555        // pattern as `retire_empty_shards_after_batch`), then release it
4556        // before the comparatively slow serialize + fsync + rename. This is
4557        // safe — where releasing right after the fingerprint snapshot alone
4558        // was *not* (see git history on this function) — because rotation
4559        // switches every future `put`'s delta frames onto a fresh epoch
4560        // (named for the fingerprint captured here) before the locks drop,
4561        // rather than leaving them targeting an epoch that's about to be
4562        // silently discarded:
4563        //
4564        //   - Every put after this point is recorded, if at all, against the
4565        //     *new* epoch (D1), never the old one (D0) — `rotate_delta_epoch`
4566        //     runs inside the same locked section as the fingerprint/index
4567        //     snapshot, so there is no window where a put's frame could still
4568        //     land on D0 after D0's corresponding checkpoint state has
4569        //     already been captured for D1's own checkpoint.
4570        //   - D0's on-disk file is left completely untouched by the rotation
4571        //     — only retired (deleted) after the new checkpoint (C1) is
4572        //     durably renamed, below. So a crash before C1 exists leaves the
4573        //     old checkpoint (C0) still correctly paired with D0.
4574        //   - D1 is only ever trusted by a reopen if it names the exact
4575        //     fingerprint of the checkpoint that reopen loads (see
4576        //     `delta_path`) — so a crash after rotation but before C1 is
4577        //     durable leaves D1 orphaned (no checkpoint names its
4578        //     fingerprint) and correctly ignored; the reopen uses C0 + D0.
4579        //
4580        // `RoomGeneration` is immutable once published (COW, swapped
4581        // atomically), so an owned `Arc` clone taken under the lock is as
4582        // good a snapshot as the live one for serialization purposes.
4583        let mut collection_ids: Vec<[u8; 16]> = self.collections_read().keys().copied().collect();
4584        collection_ids.sort_unstable();
4585        // The guards borrow these `Arc`s, so the handles must outlive the
4586        // guards; this vector is also re-used for the end-of-function
4587        // dirty-check re-lock so late-added collections stay pinned too.
4588        let mut lock_arcs: Vec<_> = collection_ids.iter().map(|id| self.put_mutex(id)).collect();
4589
4590        // Exclude new-collection publication from the fingerprint→snapshot
4591        // window. A put *to* an existing collection is already gated by that
4592        // collection's `put_mutex`, but a put that is about to *create* a
4593        // collection holds no mutex this function acquired, so its record
4594        // frame could be Eager-flushed into a pack between our `flush_all` and
4595        // our fingerprint read — the fingerprint would then name a record
4596        // whose collection never made it into the snapshot, and a reopen that
4597        // trusts C1 would silently drop it. Publishing puts hold this lock
4598        // shared across the entire put; acquiring it exclusive here (before
4599        // the fingerprint, held through the rotation) means no such put can
4600        // interleave its flush with our capture: it either finished
4601        // beforehand (its collection is in the snapshot) or runs entirely
4602        // afterwards (its bytes land post-fingerprint, and the fingerprint
4603        // mismatch on reopen routes to the full rescan).
4604        let create_guard = self.collection_creation.write();
4605        // A collection created between the initial scan above and this lock
4606        // wasn't in the locked set and must be now — otherwise a put to one
4607        // serially dispatched by the engine could still squeeze under the
4608        // fingerprint while its publication was snapshotted.
4609        let ids_now: Vec<[u8; 16]> = self.collections_read().keys().copied().collect();
4610        for id in ids_now.iter().filter(|id| !collection_ids.contains(id)) {
4611            lock_arcs.push(self.put_mutex(id));
4612        }
4613        // Now build the lock guards: the arcs must outlive them (collected
4614        // in `lock_arcs` above and reused below for the dirty-check).
4615        let guards: Vec<_> = lock_arcs.iter().map(|arc| arc.lock()).collect();
4616        breakdown.lock_wait = lock_started.elapsed();
4617        let locked_started = std::time::Instant::now();
4618
4619        // Commit any buffered frames first: the fingerprint below pins each
4620        // shard to its committed on-disk length, and the serialized index
4621        // offsets must be readable against exactly that length on the next
4622        // open. Writing the checkpoint while records are still buffered
4623        // would persist virtual offsets the fingerprint can't describe.
4624        //
4625        // With a journal enabled the checkpoint is also the point at which the
4626        // packfiles themselves must become durable — the WAL only covers the
4627        // post-checkpoint suffix — so fsync every shard here, not just flush.
4628        if self.journal().is_some() {
4629            self.shards.sync_all()?;
4630        } else {
4631            self.shards.flush_all()?;
4632        }
4633        breakdown.locked_sync = locked_started.elapsed();
4634        let snapshot_started = std::time::Instant::now();
4635        let live_shards = self.shards.all_shards();
4636        let packs: Vec<(u64, u64)> = live_shards
4637            .iter()
4638            .map(|(_, shard)| (shard.pack_id, shard.file_len()))
4639            .collect();
4640        let fingerprint = crate::index::checkpoint::pack_fingerprint(&packs);
4641        // Every pack live right now, keyed by this writer's own local slot —
4642        // lets a reader translate this checkpoint's slot-encoded index
4643        // entries to its own local slot for the same pack_id, rather than
4644        // trusting the writer's raw slot number (see CHECKPOINT_VERSION's
4645        // doc comment on the v6 bump for why that's unsafe after a
4646        // retirement).
4647        let pack_table: Vec<(u16, u64)> = live_shards
4648            .iter()
4649            .map(|(slot, shard)| (*slot, shard.pack_id))
4650            .collect();
4651
4652        let snapshots = self.checkpoint_snapshots();
4653        let serialize_started = std::time::Instant::now();
4654
4655        // Rotate the delta epoch while still locked: `old_base_fingerprint`
4656        // (D0's name, if any) is retired below only after `fingerprint`'s
4657        // checkpoint (C1) is durable; every collection's writers already
4658        // target the new epoch (D1) by the time the locks drop next.
4659        let old_base_fingerprint = self.rotate_delta_epoch(fingerprint, &snapshots);
4660        // Every put mutex is held, so no redo record is in flight: the sequence
4661        // reached so far is exactly what this checkpoint incorporates.
4662        let base_delta_seq = self.delta_state.lock().delta_seq_high;
4663        self.delta_state.lock().base_pack_ids =
4664            pack_table.iter().map(|&(_, pack_id)| pack_id).collect();
4665        // Every collection's put mutex is held here, so no `put` is mid-flight
4666        // and every mutation published so far has completed its index update.
4667        // The recorded LSN must be *committed*, not merely published: a
4668        // concurrent put can publish above the last WAL commit, and LSNs above
4669        // `committed_lsn` are discarded and reused after a crash. Recording one
4670        // as covered would make a reopen skip a future mutation that reuses
4671        // that LSN (the journal scan only knows the committed prefix). The
4672        // committed LSN is conservative -- the fsynced packs above may cover
4673        // more -- and replaying that suffix again is idempotent.
4674        //
4675        // On a shared segment the global committed LSN can include other pools'
4676        // frames, which this checkpoint does not materialize. Record this
4677        // pool's own committed watermark instead, so its coverage and the
4678        // reclaim floor both describe only frames this index holds.
4679        let wal_lsn = self.checkpoint_covered_lsn();
4680        // The image is captured here, under the locks, as bytes: the tail never
4681        // reads the live table. Pending frames were cleared by the rotation and
4682        // no put is mid-flight, so clearing the flag now loses nothing; a put
4683        // after the locks drop sets it again, and a failed tail sets it back.
4684        let blobs = Self::serialize_snapshots(&snapshots);
4685        breakdown.serialize = serialize_started.elapsed();
4686        self.index_checkpoint_dirty.store(false, Ordering::Relaxed);
4687        drop(guards);
4688        breakdown.snapshot = snapshot_started
4689            .elapsed()
4690            .saturating_sub(breakdown.serialize);
4691        // A collection published after this point lands after `fingerprint`
4692        // (its frames change a pack length), so a reopen that trusts C1 either
4693        // finds its frames in the new epoch or fails the tail-fingerprint gate
4694        // and rescans; it can never be silently omitted, because the image was
4695        // captured with publication excluded. The creation lock therefore drops
4696        // with the put mutexes rather than riding out the tail: every in-flight
4697        // sync appends to the new epoch through `append_index_delta_v3`, which
4698        // also takes this lock, so holding it across the tail would stall every
4699        // sync for the tail's duration and defeat the background checkpoint.
4700        drop(create_guard);
4701        let tail = CheckpointTail {
4702            base_dir: self.base_dir.clone(),
4703            fingerprint,
4704            covered_lsn: wal_lsn,
4705            base_delta_seq,
4706            blobs,
4707            pack_table,
4708            old_base_fingerprint,
4709            journal: self.journal(),
4710            pool_tag: self.journal_pool.load(Ordering::Acquire),
4711            durable_coverage: Arc::clone(&self.durable_coverage),
4712            #[cfg(test)]
4713            hook: self.checkpoint_tail_hook.lock().take(),
4714        };
4715        breakdown.total = started.elapsed();
4716        Ok(Some(CapturedCheckpoint { tail, breakdown }))
4717    }
4718
4719    /// Serialize snapshots and write their checkpoint, for the test mirrors of
4720    /// the production capture and [`CheckpointTail::run`].
4721    #[cfg(test)]
4722    fn write_checkpoint_snapshot(
4723        path: &Path,
4724        fingerprint: u64,
4725        covered_lsn: u64,
4726        base_delta_seq: u64,
4727        snapshots: &[([u8; 16], u64, Arc<RoomGeneration>)],
4728        pack_table: &[(u16, u64)],
4729    ) -> std::io::Result<std::time::Duration> {
4730        let serialize_started = std::time::Instant::now();
4731        let entries: Vec<([u8; 16], u64, Vec<u8>)> = snapshots
4732            .iter()
4733            .map(|(collection_id, generation, room)| {
4734                (*collection_id, *generation, room.index.serialize())
4735            })
4736            .collect();
4737        let blobs: Vec<([u8; 16], u64, &[u8])> = entries
4738            .iter()
4739            .map(|(collection_id, generation, blob)| (*collection_id, *generation, blob.as_slice()))
4740            .collect();
4741        let serialized = serialize_started.elapsed();
4742        crate::index::checkpoint::write_checkpoint(
4743            path,
4744            fingerprint,
4745            covered_lsn,
4746            base_delta_seq,
4747            &blobs,
4748            pack_table,
4749        )?;
4750        Ok(serialized)
4751    }
4752
4753    /// Serialize every snapshot's index into an owned checkpoint blob.
4754    fn serialize_snapshots(
4755        snapshots: &[([u8; 16], u64, Arc<RoomGeneration>)],
4756    ) -> Vec<([u8; 16], u64, Vec<u8>)> {
4757        snapshots
4758            .iter()
4759            .map(|(collection_id, generation, room)| {
4760                (*collection_id, *generation, room.index.serialize())
4761            })
4762            .collect()
4763    }
4764
4765    /// Fold a finished tail into the capture's breakdown and publish it.
4766    fn record_checkpoint(&self, mut breakdown: CheckpointBreakdown, done: &CheckpointBreakdown) {
4767        breakdown.write = done.write;
4768        breakdown.directory_sync = done.directory_sync;
4769        breakdown.journal_lsn = done.journal_lsn;
4770        breakdown.reclaim = done.reclaim;
4771        breakdown.retire = done.retire;
4772        breakdown.checkpoint_bytes = done.checkpoint_bytes;
4773        // The capture's own time plus the tail's, not the time until somebody
4774        // collected the worker.
4775        breakdown.total = breakdown.total.saturating_add(done.total);
4776        *self.last_checkpoint_breakdown.lock() = Some(breakdown);
4777    }
4778
4779    /// A checkpoint whose tail failed did not become durable: the old
4780    /// checkpoint and its log still pair, but the epoch this session rotated onto
4781    /// names an image that does not exist. Forget it so the next sync rewrites
4782    /// the checkpoint rather than appending to an orphaned log.
4783    fn abandon_checkpoint(&self) {
4784        self.delta_state.lock().base_fingerprint = None;
4785        self.index_checkpoint_dirty.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
4786    }
4787
4788    /// Collect the background checkpoint tail. Returns whether none is left
4789    /// running. With `wait` it blocks until the tail ends; without, it only
4790    /// collects one that already has. A failed or panicked tail is reported and
4791    /// abandoned, and the old checkpoint and log stay valid.
4792    fn finish_checkpoint_worker(&self, wait: bool) -> bool {
4793        let mut slot = self.checkpoint_worker.lock();
4794        let Some(worker) = slot.take() else {
4795            return true;
4796        };
4797        if !wait && !worker.handle.is_finished() {
4798            *slot = Some(worker);
4799            return false;
4800        }
4801        drop(slot);
4802        match worker.handle.join() {
4803            Ok(Ok(done)) => self.record_checkpoint(worker.breakdown, &done),
4804            Ok(Err(error)) => {
4805                eprintln!("mtxdb: background checkpoint failed: {error}");
4806                self.abandon_checkpoint();
4807            }
4808            Err(_) => {
4809                eprintln!("mtxdb: background checkpoint panicked");
4810                self.abandon_checkpoint();
4811            }
4812        }
4813        true
4814    }
4815
4816    /// Collect a finished checkpoint tail before a sync decides what to do.
4817    /// Returns `true` when none is still running.
4818    ///
4819    /// A tail still running holds the WAL: no coverage may be claimed and
4820    /// nothing reclaimed until its image is durable, and a second checkpoint
4821    /// must not start. It is waited for only when the WAL nears its cap or the
4822    /// delta log its rotation point (reclaim is never suppressed indefinitely).
4823    /// Otherwise this sync's operations go to the new epoch's log and the sync
4824    /// is done, which is why `false` means the caller returns.
4825    fn settle_checkpoint_worker(&self) -> bool {
4826        let must_wait = self
4827            .journal()
4828            .is_some_and(|journal| journal.in_emergency_zone())
4829            || self.delta_state.lock().log_bytes >= self.delta_log_rotate_bytes();
4830        let had_tail = self.checkpoint_worker.lock().is_some();
4831        if self.finish_checkpoint_worker(must_wait) {
4832            return true;
4833        }
4834        if had_tail {
4835            self.syncs_with_tail_in_flight
4836                .fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
4837            if must_wait {
4838                self.syncs_waited_for_tail.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
4839            }
4840        }
4841        if self.index_checkpoint_dirty.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
4842            && !self.delta_state.lock().pending.is_empty()
4843        {
4844            match self.append_index_delta() {
4845                Ok(()) => self.shard_collections_stale.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed),
4846                Err(error) => {
4847                    eprintln!("mtxdb: delta append during a checkpoint failed: {error}");
4848                }
4849            }
4850        }
4851        false
4852    }
4853
4854    /// Test-only: hold the next background checkpoint tail until the returned
4855    /// sender is used or dropped; with `fail` the tail then errors instead of
4856    /// installing.
4857    #[cfg(test)]
4858    pub(crate) fn hold_next_checkpoint_tail(&self, fail: bool) -> std::sync::mpsc::Sender<()> {
4859        let (release, gate) = std::sync::mpsc::channel();
4860        *self.checkpoint_tail_hook.lock() = Some(TailHook { gate, fail });
4861        release
4862    }

4864    /// Whether a checkpoint tail is running on its worker thread.
4865    #[must_use]
4866    pub fn checkpoint_in_flight(&self) -> bool {
4867        self.checkpoint_worker.lock().is_some()
4868    }
4869
4870    /// Block until any background checkpoint has finished.
4871    pub fn wait_for_checkpoint(&self) {
4872        self.finish_checkpoint_worker(true);
4873    }
4874
4875    /// Let a sync that needs a full checkpoint hand its tail (write, fsync,
4876    /// install, coverage, reclaim, retire) to a worker thread. Off by default.
4877    pub fn set_background_checkpoint(&self, enabled: bool) {
4878        self.background_checkpoint.store(enabled, Ordering::Relaxed);
4879    }
4880
4881    /// Full checkpoint for a sync: capture under the locks, then run the tail on
4882    /// a worker when enabled, inline otherwise. Logs and swallows a failure like
4883    /// [`Self::persist_index_checkpoint_best_effort`].
4884    fn persist_index_checkpoint_for_sync(&self) {
4885        if !self.background_checkpoint.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
4886            self.persist_index_checkpoint_best_effort();
4887            return;
4888        }
4889        if let Err(error) = self.start_checkpoint_worker() {
4890            eprintln!("mtxdb: failed to persist index checkpoint: {error}");
4891        }
4892    }
4893
4894    /// Capture a checkpoint under the locks and hand its tail to a worker
4895    /// thread, returning once the capture is done. A failed spawn abandons the
4896    /// capture (the next sync rewrites the checkpoint).
4897    fn start_checkpoint_worker(&self) -> Result<(), StorageError> {
4898        let Some(CapturedCheckpoint { tail, breakdown }) = self.capture_checkpoint()? else {
4899            return Ok(());
4900        };
4901        let spawned = std::thread::Builder::new()
4902            .name("mtxdb-checkpoint".into())
4903            .spawn(move || tail.run());
4904        match spawned {
4905            Ok(handle) => {
4906                self.checkpoint_tails_started
4907                    .fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
4908                *self.checkpoint_worker.lock() = Some(CheckpointWorker { handle, breakdown });
4909                Ok(())
4910            }
4911            Err(error) => {
4912                self.abandon_checkpoint();
4913                Err(StorageError::Io(error))
4914            }
4915        }
4916    }
4917
4918    /// Switch the live delta-log state onto a fresh epoch named for
4919    /// `fingerprint`, the checkpoint about to be written. Must be called
4920    /// while every collection's `put_mutex` is held (see
4921    /// `persist_index_checkpoint`), so every `put` from here on is recorded,
4922    /// if at all, against the new epoch — never the one this call is
4923    /// replacing. Returns the *previous* base fingerprint (the epoch to
4924    /// retire once the new checkpoint is durable), or `None` if this session
4925    /// had no prior epoch (opened via a full rescan).
4926    fn rotate_delta_epoch(
4927        &self,
4928        fingerprint: u64,
4929        snapshots: &[([u8; 16], u64, Arc<RoomGeneration>)],
4930    ) -> Option<u64> {
4931        let mut state = self.delta_state.lock();
4932        let old_base_fingerprint = state.base_fingerprint;
4933        state.base_fingerprint = Some(fingerprint);
4934        state.base_generations = snapshots
4935            .iter()
4936            .map(|(collection_id, generation, _)| (*collection_id, *generation))
4937            .collect();
4938        state.base_order = snapshots
4939            .iter()
4940            .enumerate()
4941            .map(|(order, (collection_id, _, _))| {
4942                (*collection_id, u64::try_from(order).unwrap_or(u64::MAX))
4943            })
4944            .collect();
4945        state.next_order_key = u64::try_from(snapshots.len()).unwrap_or(u64::MAX);
4946        state.pending.clear();
4947        state.log_bytes = 0;
4948        state.log_synced_bytes = 0;
4949        state.log_version = 3;
4950        old_base_fingerprint
4951    }
4952
4953    /// Test-only: a byte-for-byte mirror of `persist_index_checkpoint`,
4954    /// except it sleeps for `delay` right after releasing the locks (in
4955    /// place of, not in addition to, the production function's body — this
4956    /// is never called from non-test code and the production function is
4957    /// untouched). Lets a test make the unlocked window arbitrarily long
4958    /// without depending on a dataset large enough to make a real
4959    /// serialize+fsync slow relative to test-machine noise. See
4960    /// `test_put_does_not_block_on_slow_checkpoint_rewrite`.
4961    #[cfg(test)]
4962    fn test_persist_index_checkpoint_with_delay(
4963        &self,
4964        delay: std::time::Duration,
4965        entered_unlocked_window: &AtomicBool,
4966    ) -> Result<(), StorageError> {
4967        if !self.index_checkpoint_dirty.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
4968            entered_unlocked_window.store(true, Ordering::Release);
4969            return Ok(());
4970        }
4971        let mut collection_ids: Vec<[u8; 16]> = self.collections_read().keys().copied().collect();
4972        collection_ids.sort_unstable();
4973        let mut lock_arcs: Vec<_> = collection_ids.iter().map(|id| self.put_mutex(id)).collect();
4974        let create_guard = self.collection_creation.write();
4975        let ids_now: Vec<[u8; 16]> = self.collections_read().keys().copied().collect();
4976        for id in ids_now.iter().filter(|id| !collection_ids.contains(id)) {
4977            lock_arcs.push(self.put_mutex(id));
4978        }
4979        let guards: Vec<_> = lock_arcs.iter().map(|arc| arc.lock()).collect();
4980        self.shards.flush_all()?;
4981        let fingerprint = self.current_pack_fingerprint();
4982        let snapshots = self.checkpoint_snapshots();
4983        let old_base_fingerprint = self.rotate_delta_epoch(fingerprint, &snapshots);
4984        let covered_lsn = self.checkpoint_covered_lsn().unwrap_or(0);
4985        drop(guards);
4986        drop(create_guard);
4987
4988        // The test waits on this: it now *knows* the rewrite is sleeping in
4989        // its unlocked window rather than guessing via a fixed sleep, so a
4990        // put issued from here provably overlaps the delay.
4991        entered_unlocked_window.store(true, Ordering::Release);
4992
4993        std::thread::sleep(delay);
4994
4995        let pack_table: Vec<(u16, u64)> = self
4996            .shards
4997            .all_shards()
4998            .iter()
4999            .map(|(slot, shard)| (*slot, shard.pack_id))
5000            .collect();
5001        Self::write_checkpoint_snapshot(
5002            &Self::index_checkpoint_path(&self.base_dir),
5003            fingerprint,
5004            covered_lsn,
5005            self.delta_state.lock().delta_seq_high,
5006            &snapshots,
5007            &pack_table,
5008        )
5009        .map_err(StorageError::Io)?;
5010        let _ = crate::shard::sync_directory(&self.base_dir);
5011        self.retire_delta_epoch(old_base_fingerprint);
5012        let guards = lock_arcs.iter().map(|m| m.lock()).collect::<Vec<_>>();
5013        let has_unfinished_work = {
5014            let state = self.delta_state.lock();
5015            !state.pending.is_empty()
5016        };
5017        if !has_unfinished_work {
5018            self.index_checkpoint_dirty.store(false, Ordering::Relaxed);
5019        }
5020        drop(guards);
5021        self.persist_shard_collections_best_effort();
5022        Ok(())
5023    }
5024
5025    /// Test-only: turn a copy of this pool's directory into the disk a power
5026    /// cut would leave, by cutting every pack back to the length an fsync has
5027    /// covered. Bytes written but not yet fsynced are what a crash may lose;
5028    /// bytes still buffered in memory are not in the copy at all.
5029    #[cfg(all(test, feature = "multi-reader"))]
5030    pub(crate) fn test_cut_packs_to_synced(&self, image_dir: &Path) {
5031        for (_, shard) in self.shards.all_shards() {
5032            let name = shard.path.file_name().expect("a pack has a file name");
5033            let file = fs::OpenOptions::new()
5034                .write(true)
5035                .open(image_dir.join(name))
5036                .expect("the image holds every pack");
5037            file.set_len(shard.synced_len().min(shard.file_len()))
5038                .expect("cut the pack");
5039        }
5040    }

5042    /// Test-only: perform exactly the locked prefix of
5043    /// `persist_index_checkpoint` (flush, fingerprint, index snapshot, epoch
5044    /// rotation) and then stop, *never* writing or renaming a checkpoint.
5045    /// Simulates a crash between the D0→D1 rotation and C1's rename — the
5046    /// window where D1 exists only in memory and no on-disk checkpoint names
5047    /// its fingerprint yet.
5048    #[cfg(test)]
5049    fn test_rotate_epoch_without_checkpoint(&self) -> (u64, Option<u64>) {
5050        let mut collection_ids: Vec<[u8; 16]> = self.collections_read().keys().copied().collect();
5051        collection_ids.sort_unstable();
5052        let mutexes: Vec<_> = collection_ids.iter().map(|id| self.put_mutex(id)).collect();
5053        let _guards: Vec<_> = mutexes.iter().map(|m| m.lock()).collect();
5054        self.shards.flush_all().unwrap();
5055        let fingerprint = self.current_pack_fingerprint();
5056        let snapshots = self.checkpoint_snapshots();
5057        let old_base_fingerprint = self.rotate_delta_epoch(fingerprint, &snapshots);
5058        (fingerprint, old_base_fingerprint)
5059    }

5061    /// Test-only: perform everything `persist_index_checkpoint` does up
5062    /// through the checkpoint rename and its directory fsync, but stop
5063    /// *before* `retire_delta_epoch`. Simulates a crash between C1 becoming
5064    /// durable and D0's retirement — the window where both C1+D1 (current)
5065    /// and C0's now-stale D0 (orphaned) exist on disk simultaneously.
5066    #[cfg(test)]
5067    fn test_write_checkpoint_without_retire(&self) -> Result<(u64, Option<u64>), StorageError> {
5068        let mut collection_ids: Vec<[u8; 16]> = self.collections_read().keys().copied().collect();
5069        collection_ids.sort_unstable();
5070        let mutexes: Vec<_> = collection_ids.iter().map(|id| self.put_mutex(id)).collect();
5071        let guards: Vec<_> = mutexes.iter().map(|m| m.lock()).collect();
5072        self.shards.flush_all()?;
5073        let fingerprint = self.current_pack_fingerprint();
5074        let snapshots = self.checkpoint_snapshots();
5075        let old_base_fingerprint = self.rotate_delta_epoch(fingerprint, &snapshots);
5076        let covered_lsn = self.checkpoint_covered_lsn().unwrap_or(0);

5079            .shards
5080            .all_shards()
5081            .iter()
5082            .map(|(slot, shard)| (*slot, shard.pack_id))
5083            .collect();
5084        Self::write_checkpoint_snapshot(
5085            &Self::index_checkpoint_path(&self.base_dir),
5086            fingerprint,
5087            covered_lsn,
5088            self.delta_state.lock().delta_seq_high,
5089            &snapshots,

5091        )
5092        .map_err(StorageError::Io)?;

5101    /// simply names a fingerprint no future checkpoint will ever carry again.
5102    #[cfg(test)]

5104        retire_delta_epoch_file(&self.base_dir, old_base_fingerprint);
