5107    /// Append the pending delta operations and clear the dirty flag. The
5108    /// on-disk log, if any, is
5109    /// continued; otherwise a fresh header pins `base_fingerprint` (the
5110    /// checkpoint the frames extend) for the reopen replay gate.
5111    fn append_index_delta(&self) -> Result<(), StorageError> {
5112        self.append_index_delta_v3(false).map(|_| ())
5113    }
5114
5115    /// The delta-log cap, the bytes still free under it for a batch, and the
5116    /// length of a batch before any operation is added to it.
5117    fn delta_batch_budget(&self, state: &DeltaLogState, with_coverage: bool) -> (u64, u64, usize) {
5118        let cap = self.delta_log_cap();
5119        let header = if state.log_bytes == 0 {
5120            DELTA_LOG_HEADER_LEN as u64
5121        } else {
5122            0
5123        };
5124        let budget = cap.saturating_sub(state.log_bytes).saturating_sub(header);
5125        let mut projected = delta::v3_empty_batch_len();
5126        if with_coverage {
5127            projected = projected.saturating_add(delta::v3_coverage_frame_len());
5128        }
5129        (cap, budget, projected)
5130    }
5131
5132    fn build_v3_pending_batch(
5133        &self,
5134        state: &DeltaLogState,
5135        with_coverage: bool,
5136    ) -> Result<V3PendingBatch, StorageError> {
5137        // The batch's length is known from its parts without building them, so
5138        // one that cannot fit under the delta-log cap is refused before a
5139        // whole-index snapshot is serialized just to be thrown away.
5140        let (cap, budget, mut projected) = self.delta_batch_budget(state, with_coverage);
5141        let too_large = |projected: usize| {
5142            StorageError::Io(std::io::Error::other(DeltaBatchTooLarge {
5143                batch_bytes: projected,
5144                log_bytes: state.log_bytes,
5145                cap,
5146            }))
5147        };
5148        let collections = self.collections_read();
5149        let mut operations = Vec::new();
5150        let mut redo: Vec<RedoRecord> = Vec::new();
5151        let mut pending_ids: Vec<_> = state.pending.keys().copied().collect();
5152        pending_ids.sort_unstable();
5153        let mut generation_updates = Vec::new();
5154        let mut order_updates = Vec::new();
5155        let mut next_order_key = state.next_order_key;
5156        for collection_id in pending_ids {
5157            let pending = state
5158                .pending
5159                .get(&collection_id)
5160                .expect("pending id exists");
5161            match pending {
5162                PendingDelta::Redo(records) => {
5163                    let Some(base_generation) = state.base_generations.get(&collection_id) else {
5164                        return Err(StorageError::Io(std::io::Error::other(
5165                            "redo records target a collection without a base",
5166                        )));
5167                    };
5168                    if records
5169                        .iter()
5170                        .any(|record| record.base_generation != *base_generation)
5171                    {
5172                        return Err(StorageError::Io(std::io::Error::other(
5173                            "a redo record's generation differs from its base",
5174                        )));
5175                    }
5176                    projected = projected
5177                        .saturating_add(records.len().saturating_mul(delta::v3_redo_frame_len()));
5178                    redo.extend(records.iter().copied());
5179                }
5180                PendingDelta::Snapshot => {
5181                    if let Some(room) = collections.get(&collection_id) {
5182                        let generation = arc_swap::ArcSwapAny::load_full(room);
5183                        let frame_len =
5184                            delta::v3_snapshot_frame_len(generation.index.serialized_len())
5185                                .ok_or_else(|| {
5186                                    StorageError::Io(std::io::Error::other(
5187                                        "v3 batch size overflow",
5188                                    ))
5189                                })?;
5190                        projected = projected.saturating_add(frame_len);
5191                        if u64::try_from(projected).unwrap_or(u64::MAX) > budget {
5192                            return Err(too_large(projected));
5193                        }
5194                        let order_key =
5195                            if let Some(order_key) = state.base_order.get(&collection_id) {
5196                                *order_key
5197                            } else {
5198                                let order_key = next_order_key;
5199                                next_order_key = next_order_key.saturating_add(1);
5200                                order_key
5201                            };
5202                        operations.push(DeltaOperation::CollectionSnapshot {
5203                            collection_id,
5204                            generation: generation.generation,
5205                            order_key,
5206                            index_blob: generation.index.serialize(),
5207                        });
5208                        generation_updates.push((collection_id, generation.generation));
5209                        order_updates.push((collection_id, order_key));
5210                    } else if let Some(&generation) = state.base_generations.get(&collection_id) {
5211                        projected = projected.saturating_add(delta::v3_tombstone_frame_len());
5212                        operations.push(DeltaOperation::CollectionTombstone {
5213                            collection_id,
5214                            generation,
5215                        });
5216                        generation_updates.push((collection_id, 0));
5217                    }
5218                }
5219                PendingDelta::Delete { generation } => {
5220                    if state.base_generations.contains_key(&collection_id) {
5221                        projected = projected.saturating_add(delta::v3_tombstone_frame_len());
5222                        operations.push(DeltaOperation::CollectionTombstone {
5223                            collection_id,
5224                            generation: *generation,
5225                        });
5226                        generation_updates.push((collection_id, 0));
5227                    }
5228                }
5229            }
5230        }
5231        // Serialized in `delta_seq` order, whatever the collection order, so a
5232        // reader that validates strict monotonicity sees the append order.
5233        redo.sort_unstable_by_key(|record| record.delta_seq);
5234        operations.extend(redo.into_iter().map(DeltaOperation::Redo));
5235        Ok(V3PendingBatch {
5236            operations,
5237            generation_updates,
5238            order_updates,
5239            next_order_key,
5240        })
5241    }
5242
5243    fn write_v3_delta_batch(
5244        &self,
5245        state: &mut DeltaLogState,
5246        base_fingerprint: u64,
5247        operations: &[DeltaOperation],
5248        tail_fingerprint: u64,
5249        durable: bool,
5250    ) -> Result<(), StorageError> {
5251        let path = Self::delta_path(&self.base_dir, base_fingerprint);
5252        let on_disk_len = fs::metadata(&path)
5253            .map_or_else(
5254                |error| {
5255                    if error.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound {
5256                        Ok(0)
5257                    } else {
5258                        Err(error)
5259                    }
5260                },
5261                |metadata| Ok(metadata.len()),
5262            )
5263            .map_err(StorageError::Io)?;
5264        if on_disk_len < state.log_bytes {
5265            return Err(StorageError::Io(std::io::Error::other(
5266                "v3 delta log shrank below its sealed frontier",
5267            )));
5268        }
5269        if on_disk_len > state.log_bytes {
5270            fs::OpenOptions::new()
5271                .write(true)
5272                .open(&path)
5273                .and_then(|file| file.set_len(state.log_bytes))
5274                .map_err(StorageError::Io)?;
5275        }
5276        let write_header = state.log_bytes == 0;
5277        let batch_bytes = delta::v3_batch_len(operations)
5278            .ok_or_else(|| StorageError::Io(std::io::Error::other("v3 batch size overflow")))?;
5279        let next_len = state
5280            .log_bytes
5281            .saturating_add(u64::try_from(batch_bytes).unwrap_or(u64::MAX))
5282            .saturating_add(if write_header {
5283                DELTA_LOG_HEADER_LEN as u64
5284            } else {
5285                0
5286            });
5287        let cap = self.delta_log_cap();
5288        if next_len > cap {
5289            return Err(StorageError::Io(std::io::Error::other(
5290                DeltaBatchTooLarge {
5291                    batch_bytes,
5292                    log_bytes: state.log_bytes,
5293                    cap,
5294                },
5295            )));
5296        }
5297        let bytes_written = delta::append_v3_batch_with_durability(
5298            &path,
5299            write_header,
5300            base_fingerprint,
5301            operations,
5302            tail_fingerprint,
5303            durable,
5304        )
5305        .map_err(StorageError::Io)?;
5306        state.log_bytes = state
5307            .log_bytes
5308            .saturating_add(u64::try_from(bytes_written).unwrap_or(u64::MAX));
5309        if durable {
5310            state.log_synced_bytes = state.log_bytes;
5311        } else {
5312            // Pay for the log's durability in slices as it grows. Best effort:
5313            // the log is acceleration, and a coverage batch fsyncs it again.
5314            let budget = self.delta_fsync_budget_bytes.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
5315            if budget != 0 && state.log_bytes.saturating_sub(state.log_synced_bytes) >= budget {
5316                match fs::OpenOptions::new()
5317                    .write(true)
5318                    .open(&path)
5319                    .and_then(|file| file.sync_data())
5320                {
5321                    Ok(()) => state.log_synced_bytes = state.log_bytes,
5322                    Err(error) => eprintln!("mtxdb: delta log fsync failed: {error}"),
5323                }
5324            }
5325        }
5326        Ok(())
5327    }
5328
5329    /// Append v3 operations. Collection locks pin every live index
5330    /// and the collection-creation lock prevents an unrepresented collection
5331    /// from appearing between pack flush and snapshot capture.
5332    ///
5333    /// With `with_coverage` the batch also carries a claim that the packs
5334    /// durably cover this pool's journal frames through the returned LSN, so
5335    /// the journal can be reclaimed without a full checkpoint. The ordering that
5336    /// makes the claim true: with every collection locked (so no put is
5337    /// mid-flight and everything published for this pool has been applied) the
5338    /// LSN is captured and every pack is fsynced, and only then is the batch,
5339    /// claim last, appended and fsynced. A crash before the batch is durable
5340    /// leaves no claim; a torn batch fails its CRC and claims nothing.
5341    fn append_index_delta_v3(&self, with_coverage: bool) -> Result<Option<u64>, StorageError> {
5342        if with_coverage {
5343            // Make the bulk of the pack bytes durable before any lock is taken;
5344            // the fsync under the locks below then only covers what was written
5345            // since.
5346            self.shards.sync_dirty()?;
5347        }
5348        let create_guard = self.collection_creation.write();
5349        let mut ids: Vec<[u8; 16]> = self.collections_read().keys().copied().collect();
5350        {
5351            let state = self.delta_state.lock();
5352            ids.extend(state.pending.keys().copied());
5353        }
5354        ids.sort_unstable();
5355        ids.dedup();
5356        let lock_arcs: Vec<_> = ids.iter().map(|id| self.put_mutex(id)).collect();
5357        let guards: Vec<_> = lock_arcs.iter().map(|lock| lock.lock()).collect();
5358
5359        // A put may have completed after the caller's initial dirty flush but
5360        // before these locks were acquired. Flush again while the snapshot set
5361        // is stable so the tail fingerprint covers every serialized slot.
5362        self.shards.flush_all()?;
5363        let covered = if with_coverage {
5364            let covered = self.checkpoint_covered_lsn();
5365            // Everything up to `covered` is applied and flushed; make it durable
5366            // before claiming it. `sync_all`, not `sync_dirty`: a claim must not
5367            // rest on a dirty bit some other syncer cleared.
5368            self.shards.sync_all()?;
5369            covered
5370        } else {
5371            None
5372        };
5373        let tail_fingerprint = self.current_pack_fingerprint();
5374
5375        // Copy the small state-machine metadata, then release its mutex while
5376        // serializing whole-index snapshots. Collection put locks and the
5377        // creation lock keep this snapshot stable; the persistence lock keeps
5378        // another sync from advancing the on-disk frontier concurrently.
5379        let snapshot_state = self.delta_state.lock().clone();
5380        let Some(base_fingerprint) = snapshot_state.base_fingerprint else {
5381            return Err(StorageError::Io(std::io::Error::other(
5382                "v3 delta append with no base fingerprint",
5383            )));
5384        };
5385        if snapshot_state.log_version != 3 {
5386            return Err(StorageError::Io(std::io::Error::other(
5387                "v3 delta append without a clean v3 checkpoint base",
5388            )));
5389        }
5390        if snapshot_state.pending.is_empty() && covered.is_none() {
5391            return Err(StorageError::Io(std::io::Error::other(
5392                "v3 delta append with no pending operations",
5393            )));
5394        }
5395
5396        let batch = self.build_v3_pending_batch(&snapshot_state, with_coverage)?;
5397        let V3PendingBatch {
5398            mut operations,
5399            generation_updates,
5400            order_updates,
5401            next_order_key,
5402        } = batch;
5403
5404        let mut state = self.delta_state.lock();
5405        if state.pending != snapshot_state.pending
5406            || state.base_fingerprint != snapshot_state.base_fingerprint
5407            || state.log_bytes != snapshot_state.log_bytes
5408            || state.log_version != snapshot_state.log_version
5409        {
5410            return Err(StorageError::Io(std::io::Error::other(
5411                "v3 delta state changed while snapshot batch was prepared",
5412            )));
5413        }
5414        // The claim is the batch's last operation, so a reader that applies the
5415        // operations up to it holds exactly the index the claim describes.
5416        if let Some(covered_lsn) = covered {
5417            operations.push(DeltaOperation::Coverage { covered_lsn });
5418        }
5419        self.write_v3_delta_batch(
5420            &mut state,
5421            base_fingerprint,
5422            &operations,
5423            tail_fingerprint,
5424            covered.is_some(),
5425        )?;
5426        for (collection_id, generation) in generation_updates {
5427            if generation == 0 {
5428                state.base_generations.remove(&collection_id);
5429                state.base_order.remove(&collection_id);
5430            } else {
5431                state.base_generations.insert(collection_id, generation);
5432            }
5433        }
5434        for (collection_id, order_key) in order_updates {
5435            state.base_order.insert(collection_id, order_key);
5436        }
5437        state.next_order_key = state.next_order_key.max(next_order_key);
5438        state.pending.clear();
5439        self.index_checkpoint_dirty.store(false, Ordering::Relaxed);
5440        drop(state);
5441        drop(guards);
5442        drop(create_guard);
5443        if let Some(covered_lsn) = covered {
5444            // The batch is durable, so the claim is too.
5445            self.durable_coverage
5446                .fetch_max(covered_lsn, Ordering::AcqRel);
5447        }
5448        Ok(covered)
5449    }
5450
5451    /// Best-effort wrapper around [`Self::persist_index_checkpoint`] — logs
5452    /// and swallows a failure rather than turning it into a hard error. The
5453    /// checkpoint is an acceleration structure; packfiles remain
5454    /// authoritative, so a failed persist only costs the next open a rescan.
5455    fn persist_index_checkpoint_best_effort(&self) {
5456        if let Err(e) = self.persist_index_checkpoint() {
5457            eprintln!("mtxdb: failed to persist index checkpoint: {e}");
5458        }
5459    }
5460
5461    /// Reads a persisted shard→collection directory directly off disk, with no
5462    /// `ShardPool`/`PackfileStorage` construction at all — the fast path
5463    /// for a `collections`-style CLI listing. Returns each collection's total record
5464    /// count summed across every shard it appears in, in insertion order.
5465    ///
5466    /// Best-effort: a missing, truncated, or corrupt file just yields an
5467    /// empty result rather than an error — the caller decides whether to
5468    /// fall back to a full scan (e.g. because this store predates the
5469    /// feature, or a writer hasn't flushed it yet).
5470    #[must_use]
5471    pub fn collection_directory_from_disk(base_dir: &std::path::Path) -> Vec<([u8; 16], u64)> {
5472        let Some(records) = read_persisted_shard_collections(base_dir).map(|d| d.records) else {
5473            return Vec::new();
5474        };
5475        let mut totals: HashMap<[u8; 16], (u64, u64)> = HashMap::new();
5476        for record in records {
5477            let entry = totals
5478                .entry(record.collection_id)
5479                .or_insert((0, record.insertion_order));
5480            entry.0 = entry.0.saturating_add(record.count);
5481            entry.1 = entry.1.min(record.insertion_order);
5482        }
5483        let mut result: Vec<([u8; 16], u64, u64)> = totals
5484            .into_iter()
5485            .map(|(collection_id, (count, order))| (collection_id, count, order))
5486            .collect();
5487        result.sort_unstable_by_key(|(collection_id, _, order)| (*order, *collection_id));
5488
5489        result
5490            .into_iter()
5491            .map(|(collection_id, count, _)| (collection_id, count))
5492            .collect()
5493    }
5494
5495    /// Reads collection summaries from the persisted shard→collection directory without
5496    /// opening packfiles. The node count and index-RAM figure match the
5497    /// index rebuilt by [`Self::open`], provided the sidecar is current.
5498    ///
5499    /// Returns `None` when the directory has not been persisted yet or is
5500    /// malformed.
5501    #[must_use]
5502    pub fn collection_summaries_from_disk(
5503        base_dir: &std::path::Path,
5504    ) -> Option<Vec<CollectionSummary>> {
5505        Self::collection_directory_persisted_at(base_dir)?;
5506        Self::collection_directory_from_disk(base_dir)
5507            .into_iter()
5508            .map(|(collection_id, nodes)| {
5509                let nodes = usize::try_from(nodes).ok()?;
5510                // A live collection always starts at `NEW_COLLECTION_INDEX_FLOOR`
5511                // (64), not `LossyIndex::new`'s own generic 16-slot floor — use
5512                // the same starting point here or a small collection's
5513                // capacity/memory estimate undershoots its real index.
5514                let capacity = u32::try_from(LossyIndex::capacity_for_entries(
5515                    nodes,
5516                    NEW_COLLECTION_INDEX_FLOOR,
5517                )?)
5518                .ok()?;
5519                Some((
5520                    collection_id,
5521                    nodes,
5522                    LossyIndex::memory_usage_for_entries(nodes, NEW_COLLECTION_INDEX_FLOOR)?,
5523                    capacity,
5524                ))
5525            })
5526            .collect()
5527    }
5528
5529    /// Current live shard `pack_id`s per collection from the persisted shard→collection
5530    /// directory, without opening packfiles or rebuilding collection indexes.
5531    ///
5532    /// Returns `None` when the directory has not been persisted yet or is
5533    /// malformed.
5534    #[must_use]
5535    pub fn collection_shards_from_disk(
5536        base_dir: &std::path::Path,
5537    ) -> Option<HashMap<[u8; 16], Vec<u64>>> {
5538        let records = read_persisted_shard_collections(base_dir)?.records;
5539        let mut shards: HashMap<[u8; 16], Vec<u64>> = HashMap::new();
5540        for record in records {
5541            // A zero count means this (pack, collection) pair has no live
5542            // records anymore (e.g. the collection was deleted): the sidecar
5543            // still carries the entry, but reporting it here would give
5544            // callers like the CLI's "found in -t <other>" hint a false
5545            // positive pointing at a shard that no longer holds the data.
5546            if record.count == 0 {
5547                continue;
5548            }
5549            shards
5550                .entry(record.collection_id)
5551                .or_default()
5552                .push(record.pack_id);
5553        }
5554        for collection_shards in shards.values_mut() {
5555            collection_shards.sort_unstable();
5556            collection_shards.dedup();
5557        }
5558        Some(shards)
5559    }
5560
5561    /// Current physical bytes per collection from the persisted directory.
5562    /// Values include superseded frames and are `None` for stores whose
5563    /// sidecar predates persisted physical metrics.
5564    #[must_use]
5565    pub fn collection_disk_bytes_from_disk(
5566        base_dir: &std::path::Path,
5567    ) -> Option<HashMap<[u8; 16], u64>> {
5568        let records = read_persisted_shard_collections(base_dir)?.records;
5569        let mut bytes = HashMap::new();
5570        for record in records {
5571            let total = bytes.entry(record.collection_id).or_insert(0_u64);
5572            *total = total.saturating_add(record.disk_bytes);
5573        }
5574        Some(bytes)
5575    }

5577    /// Current live-node count per shard from the persisted shard→collection
5578    /// directory, without opening packfiles or rebuilding collection indexes.
5579    ///
5580    /// Returns `None` when the directory has not been persisted yet or is
5581    /// malformed. Callers that need an authoritative fresh count can then
5582    /// explicitly open the store and rebuild its indexes instead.
5583    #[must_use]
5584    pub fn shard_node_counts_from_disk(base_dir: &std::path::Path) -> Option<HashMap<u64, u64>> {
5585        let records = read_persisted_shard_collections(base_dir)?.records;
5586        let mut totals = HashMap::new();
5587        for record in records {
5588            let total = totals.entry(record.pack_id).or_insert(0_u64);
5589            *total = total.saturating_add(record.count);
5590        }
5591        Some(totals)
5592    }

5594    /// Current number of collections with live nodes per shard from the persisted
5595    /// shard→collection directory, without opening packfiles or rebuilding collection
5596    /// indexes.
5597    ///
5598    /// Returns `None` when the directory has not been persisted yet or is
5599    /// malformed.
5600    #[must_use]
5601    pub fn shard_collection_counts_from_disk(
5602        base_dir: &std::path::Path,
5603    ) -> Option<HashMap<u64, u64>> {

5605        let mut totals = HashMap::new();
5606        for record in records {

5608            *count = count.saturating_add(1);

5613    /// Unix-seconds timestamp of the persisted shard→collection directory, if
5614    /// one exists — lets a reader (e.g. a `collections` CLI listing) label how
5615    /// stale the counts it's showing are, the same way
5616    /// `ShardPool::stats_persisted_at` does for shard IO stats.
5617    #[must_use]
5618    pub fn collection_directory_persisted_at(base_dir: &std::path::Path) -> Option<u64> {
5619        read_persisted_shard_collections(base_dir).map(|d| d.persisted_at)
5620    }
5621
5622    /// Pin one `Arc<Shard>` per distinct shard id, keeping each shard's file
5623    /// handle (and thus its `Drop`-triggered deletion, see `Shard::drop`)
5624    /// alive for as long as the returned map is held — even if a later
5625    /// write in the same operation triggers `ShardPool::rotate` and retires
5626    /// that shard id's pool slot.
5627    ///
5628    /// This matters specifically for a scan-then-rewrite repack: without
5629    /// it, re-querying `ShardPool::get_shard` on every loop iteration can
5630    /// observe a shard that a *rotation triggered by the same repack's own
5631    /// writes* just retired-and-recreated at the same path, turning a
5632    /// stale-but-valid offset into a read into unrelated, freshly-written
5633    /// bytes.
5634    fn pin_shards(&self, slots: impl Iterator<Item = u16>) -> HashMap<u16, Arc<Shard>> {
5635        let unique: HashSet<u16> = slots.collect();
5636        unique
5637            .into_iter()
5638            .filter_map(|id| self.shards.get_shard(id).map(|shard| (id, shard)))
5639            .collect()
5640    }
5641
5642    /// Whether `loaded` still refers to the collection's current generation.
5643    ///
5644    /// The read paths use this to detect a repack that swapped the generation
5645    /// (and so may have retired the shards `loaded`'s index points at) between
5646    /// an index lookup and pinning those shards. A stable generation means the
5647    /// pin happened before any retirement.
5648    fn same_generation(
5649        current: Option<&arc_swap::Guard<Arc<RoomGeneration>>>,
5650        loaded: &arc_swap::Guard<Arc<RoomGeneration>>,
5651    ) -> bool {
5652        current.is_some_and(|current| Arc::ptr_eq(&**current, &**loaded))
5653    }
5654
5655    /// Copy a record from an old (pinned) shard to the active shard.
5656    /// Returns the new `(hash, slot, offset)` or None if `old_slot`
5657    /// isn't in `pinned`.
5658    fn copy_record_to_shard(
5659        &self,
5660        collection_id: &[u8; 16],
5661        pinned: &HashMap<u16, Arc<Shard>>,
5662        old_slot: u16,
5663        old_offset: u64,
5664    ) -> Result<Option<RepackCopiedRecord>, StorageError> {
5665        let Some(old_shard) = pinned.get(&old_slot) else {
5666            return Ok(None);
5667        };
5668        let record = self.read_at(old_shard, old_offset, true)?;
5669        let (new_slot, new_offset, disk_bytes) = self.shards.put_record_with_len(&Record {
5670            collection_id: *collection_id,
5671            hash: record.hash,
5672            data: record.data,
5673            metadata: record.metadata,
5674        })?;
5675        Ok(Some((record.hash, new_slot, new_offset, disk_bytes)))
5676    }
5677    fn swap_generation(
5678        &self,
5679        collection_id: &[u8; 16],
5680        index: LossyIndex,
5681    ) -> Result<(), StorageError> {
5682        let cache = self.generation(collection_id).map(|g| g.cache.clone());
5683        self.store_generation(collection_id, index, cache, true)
5684    }
5685
5686    /// Store a new generation for a collection, reusing the existing cache if present.
5687    ///
5688    /// If the collection is new (not yet in the `collections` map), it is added to
5689    /// `collection_order` so that [`Self::collection_summaries`] will include it, and
5690    /// any prior tombstone in `deleted.collections` is cleared so the collection
5691    /// survives a restart.
5692    ///
5693    /// `bump_generation` marks a shape change (capacity growth, rebuild,
5694    /// repack, refresh) rather than a plain copy-on-write update. Shape changes
5695    /// and new collections are represented by whole-index snapshots in v3.
5696    fn store_generation(
5697        &self,
5698        collection_id: &[u8; 16],
5699        index: LossyIndex,
5700        cache: Option<Arc<NodeCache>>,
5701        bump_generation: bool,
5702    ) -> Result<(), StorageError> {
5703        let cache = cache.unwrap_or_else(|| Arc::new(NodeCache::new(self.cache_capacity)));
5704        let is_new = self.collections_read().get(collection_id).is_none();
5705        let structural = bump_generation || is_new;
5706        if structural {
5707            self.invalidate_delta_log(collection_id);
5708        }
5709        let generation = self.generation(collection_id).map_or(1, |gen| {
5710            gen.generation.saturating_add(u64::from(bump_generation))
5711        });
5712        let new_gen = Arc::new(RoomGeneration {
5713            index,
5714            cache,
5715            generation,
5716        });
5717
5718        // Clear a prior deletion marker before publishing the recreated
5719        // generation. A failure must fail the write: otherwise it appears to
5720        // succeed but disappears on the next startup scan.
5721        if is_new {
5722            if self.is_deleted_collection(collection_id) {
5723                self.clear_deleted_collection(collection_id)?;
5724            }
5725            let mut tables = self.index_tables.write();
5726            tables
5727                .collections
5728                .entry(*collection_id)
5729                .or_insert_with(|| {
5730                    ArcSwap::from_pointee(RoomGeneration {
5731                        index: LossyIndex::new(0),
5732                        cache: Arc::new(NodeCache::new(self.cache_capacity)),
5733                        generation: 1,
5734                    })
5735                })
5736                .store(new_gen);
5737            if !tables.collection_order.contains(collection_id) {
5738                tables.collection_order.push(*collection_id);
5739            }
5740        } else {
5741            // Fast path: just update the ArcSwap using a read lock on the map.
5742            // This avoids a global write lock on every single put() call.
5743            let read_guard = self.collections_read();
5744            if let Some(arc_swap) = read_guard.get(collection_id) {
5745                arc_swap.store(new_gen);
5746            } else {
5747                // Fallback in case of a race condition with a deletion
5748                drop(read_guard);
5749                self.collections_write()
5750                    .entry(*collection_id)
5751                    .or_insert_with(|| {
5752                        ArcSwap::from_pointee(RoomGeneration {
5753                            index: LossyIndex::new(0),
5754                            cache: Arc::new(NodeCache::new(self.cache_capacity)),
5755                            generation: 1,
5756                        })
5757                    })
5758                    .store(new_gen);
5759            }
5760        }
5761        self.index_checkpoint_dirty.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
5762        Ok(())
5763    }
5764    /// Forces a re-scan of a collection's shards from disk and atomically swaps in the new index.
5765    /// This is designed for multi-worker environments to pull in external appends on demand.
5766    ///
5767    /// # Errors
5768    /// Returns `StorageError` if reading or parsing the underlying shards fails.
5769    pub fn refresh_collection(&self, collection_id: &[u8; 16]) -> Result<(), StorageError> {
5770        let collection_arc = self.put_mutex(collection_id);
5771        let _collection_guard = collection_arc.lock();
5772        // A refresh that publishes a *newly discovered* collection must be
5773        // excluded from a concurrent checkpoint's fingerprint→snapshot
5774        // window, exactly like a new-collection `put`/`put_many` (see the
5775        // comment on `put`). Otherwise its `rebuild_index` flush could land
5776        // the refreshed records in a pack covered by the checkpoint's
5777        // fingerprint while the collection itself is absent from the
5778        // snapshot, and a reopen trusting that checkpoint would lose them.
5779        let _create_guard = if self.generation(collection_id).is_none() {
5780            Some(self.collection_creation.read())
5781        } else {
5782            None
5783        };
5784        self.shards.discover_shards()?;
5785        let new_index = self.rebuild_index(collection_id)?;
5786        let existing_cache = self.generation(collection_id).map(|g| g.cache.clone());
5787        self.store_generation(collection_id, new_index, existing_cache, true)
5788    }
5789
5790    fn rebuild_index(&self, collection_id: &[u8; 16]) -> Result<LossyIndex, StorageError> {
5791        // Full-fallback path: a batch that exhausted growth re-scans the
5792        // packfiles. Tracked so a heavy rebuild is visible in `stats()`.
5793        self.index_rebuild_count.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
5794        // `scan_collection_records` traverses packfiles; any buffered frames
5795        // (this collection's or any other's) are invisible to it, so a fresh
5796        // flush guarantees the rebuilt index reflects every record that has
5797        // actually been put. Callers only reach this path while holding the
5798        // collection's put mutex, so nothing new can buffer for this
5799        // collection between the flush and the scan.
5800        self.shards.flush_all()?;
5801        let scanned = self.scan_collection_records(collection_id)?;
5802        let total: usize = scanned.iter().map(|(_, e)| e.len()).sum();
5803        let index = LossyIndex::with_config(
5804            total.saturating_mul(2).max(NEW_COLLECTION_INDEX_FLOOR),
5805            self.index_config,
5806        );
5807        for (slot, entries) in scanned {
5808            for (hash, offset) in entries {
5809                // `IndexEntry` can only represent offsets up to
5810                // `PACK_INDEX_OFFSET_LIMIT`. Offsets a legacy or externally
5811                // created oversized shard can no longer fit are rejected
5812                // rather than silently skipped: writes are already capped at
5813                // `MAX_SHARD_BYTES`, so a record beyond the limit means the
5814                // shard did not come from this engine, and silently indexing
5815                // around it would make its data unreachable while reporting a
5816                // successful rebuild.
5817                check_index_offset(slot, &hash, offset)?;
5818                let _ = index.insert(&hash, slot, offset);
5819            }
5820        }
5821        Ok(index)
5822    }
5823
5824    /// Rehash a checkpoint-derived index without rescanning unrelated packs.
5825    ///
5826    /// A compact checkpoint keeps the packed `(shard, offset)` slots but not
5827    /// the 64-bit home hashes needed by [`LossyIndex::grow`].  Each occupied
5828    /// slot still names an authoritative frame whose fixed metadata prefix
5829    /// contains the full hash, so recover those identities and rehash only
5830    /// this collection's entries.  A missing shard, malformed frame, or a
5831    /// frame from another collection fails closed to the caller's existing
5832    /// whole-collection scan fallback.
5833    fn grow_checkpoint_index(
5834        &self,
5835        collection_id: &[u8; 16],
5836        index: &LossyIndex,
5837    ) -> Result<Option<LossyIndex>, StorageError> {
5838        index.grow_by_recovering_hashes(|slot, offset, slot_tag| {
5839            let shard = self.shards.get_shard(slot).ok_or_else(|| {
5840                StorageError::Corrupt(format!("checkpoint index refers to missing shard {slot}"))
5841            })?;
5842            let (found_collection, hash) = self.shards.record_identity_at(&shard, offset)?;
5843            if &found_collection != collection_id {
5844                return Err(StorageError::Corrupt(format!(
5845                    "checkpoint index offset {offset} in shard {slot} belongs to another collection"
5846                )));
5847            }
5848            if index.tag_for_hash(&hash) != slot_tag {
5849                return Err(StorageError::Corrupt(format!(
5850                    "checkpoint index tag does not match frame at offset {offset} in shard {slot}"
5851                )));
5852            }
5853            Ok(hash)
5854        })
5855    }
5856
5857    /// Insert with exact identity checks for checkpoint-derived slots.
5858    ///
5859    /// A compact checkpoint retains a slot's tag and location but not the
5860    /// remaining hash bits. On the rare same-tag probe, recover that frame's
5861    /// metadata, hydrate the in-memory slot, and retry. Active indexes carry
5862    /// their identities already, so their ordinary inserts take no I/O path.
5863    fn insert_index(
5864        &self,
5865        collection_id: &[u8; 16],
5866        index: &LossyIndex,
5867        hash: &NodeId,
5868        slot: u16,
5869        offset: u64,
5870    ) -> Result<Result<(u32, u64, bool), InsertError>, StorageError> {
5871        Ok(self
5872            .insert_index_undoable(collection_id, index, hash, slot, offset)?
5873            .map(|(bucket, slot, undo)| (bucket, slot, undo.was_empty())))
5874    }
5875
5876    /// Like [`Self::insert_index`], but also returns the [`EntryUndo`]
5877    /// needed to reverse this one write, for callers mutating a still-live
5878    /// (not cloned) index across a multi-record batch.
5879    fn insert_index_undoable(
5880        &self,
5881        collection_id: &[u8; 16],
5882        index: &LossyIndex,
5883        hash: &NodeId,
5884        slot: u16,
5885        offset: u64,
5886    ) -> Result<Result<(u32, u64, EntryUndo), InsertError>, StorageError> {
5887        loop {
5888            match index.insert_undoable(hash, slot, offset) {
5889                Ok(written) => return Ok(Ok(written)),
5890                Err(InsertError::TableFull) => return Ok(Err(InsertError::TableFull)),
5891                Err(InsertError::NeedsIdentity {
5892                    bucket,
5893                    slot,
5894                    offset,
5895                }) => {
5896                    let shard = self.shards.get_shard(slot).ok_or_else(|| {
5897                        StorageError::Corrupt(format!(
5898                            "index refers to missing shard {slot} while resolving a tag collision"
5899                        ))
5900                    })?;
5901                    let (found_collection, found_hash) =
5902                        self.shards.record_identity_at(&shard, offset)?;
5903                    if &found_collection != collection_id
5904                        || !index.hydrate_slot_identity(bucket, &found_hash)
5905                    {
5906                        return Err(StorageError::Corrupt(format!(
5907                            "index tag candidate at offset {offset} in shard {slot} is inconsistent"
5908                        )));
5909                    }
5910                }
5911            }
5912        }
5913    }
5914
5915    /// Fetch a node and return it as a `NodeRef` with swizzled children.
5916    ///
5917    /// # Errors
5918    /// Returns `StorageError` on I/O failure or CRC mismatch.
5919    pub fn get_swizzled(
5920        &self,
5921        collection_id: &[u8; 16],
5922        id: &NodeId,
5923        extract_children: impl Fn(&NodeData) -> Vec<NodeId>,
5924    ) -> Result<Option<NodeRef>, StorageError> {
5925        let Some(data) = self.get(collection_id, id)? else {
5926            return Ok(None);
5927        };
5928
5929        if let Some(swizzle_fn) = self.swizzle {
5930            let children = extract_children(&data);
5931            if !children.is_empty() {
5932                let cached = if let Some(gen) = self.generation(collection_id) {
5933                    gen.cache.resolve_hashes(&children)
5934                } else {
5935                    vec![None; children.len()]
5936                };
5937                let swizzled = swizzle_fn(&data, &children, &cached);
5938                if let Some(gen) = self.generation(collection_id) {
5939                    gen.cache.insert(*id, Arc::new(swizzled.clone()));
5940                }
5941                return Ok(Some(NodeRef::Resolved(*id, Arc::new(swizzled))));
5942            }
5943        }
5944
5945        Ok(Some(NodeRef::Resolved(*id, Arc::new(data))))
5946    }
5947
5948    /// Resolve `id` against `candidates` through `pinned` shard handles.
5949    ///
5950    /// Holding the pinned `Arc<Shard>`s for the whole read keeps each shard's
5951    /// file handle alive, so a concurrent repack that swaps the generation and
5952    /// retires those shard ids cannot turn a live record into a miss while the
5953    /// lookup is in flight. See [`Self::pin_shards`].
5954    fn resolve_from_pinned(
5955        &self,
5956        id: &NodeId,
5957        candidates: &[(u16, u64)],
5958        pinned: &HashMap<u16, Arc<Shard>>,
5959        track: bool,
5960    ) -> Result<Option<NodeData>, StorageError> {
5961        let mut last_err: Option<StorageError> = None;
5962        for &(slot, offset) in candidates {
5963            let Some(shard) = pinned.get(&slot) else {
5964                continue;
5965            };
5966
5967            if track {
5968                self.candidate_reads.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
5969                if let Ok(len) = Self::record_disk_len_at(shard.as_ref(), offset) {
5970                    self.candidate_frame_bytes.fetch_add(len, Ordering::Relaxed);
5971                }
5972            }
5973
5974            match self.read_at(
5975                shard,
5976                offset,
5977                self.shards.checksum_policy().verifies_reads(),
5978            ) {
5979                Ok(record) => {
5980                    if record.hash != *id {
5981                        if track {
5982                            self.candidate_hash_mismatches
5983                                .fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
5984                        }
5985                        continue;
5986                    }
5987
5988                    let data = NodeData {
5989                        bytes: record.data,
5990                        children: Vec::new(),
5991                    };
5992                    // A raw mmap-backed `Bytes` is already cheap to retain
5993                    // in the caller. Do not turn every cold lookup into an
5994                    // LRU write (hash probe, lock, and eviction bookkeeping).
5995                    // The cache remains populated by writes and swizzling,
5996                    // where it stores work that cannot be recovered by a
5997                    // simple mmap range.
5998                    return Ok(Some(data));
5999                }
6000                Err(e) => {
6001                    last_err = Some(e);
6002                }
6003            }
6004        }
6005
6006        if let Some(err) = last_err {
6007            return Err(err);
6008        }
6009        Ok(None)
6010    }
6011
6012    // repack_collection_rewrite and repack_collection_topo were retired: both scanned
6013    // for records without deduplicating physical duplicates (each prior
6014    // repack's rewritten copies included), giving an exponential blowup on
6015    // repeated calls against a growing collection, and both re-fetched
6016    // Arc<Shard> per loop iteration rather than pinning shards for the
6017    // call's duration — vulnerable to the rotation race documented on
6018    // `pin_shards`. `repack_collection_reachable`'s no-live-roots fallback
6019    // subsumes both: same topological ordering, correct dedup via
6020    // `hash_to_shard_offset`, and pinned shards throughout.
6021
6022    /// BFS outward from `roots` over `extract_edges`, reading only records
6023    /// actually reached. Returns the sorted, deduplicated live hash set and
6024    /// the adjacency discovered along the way.
6025    fn bfs_live_set(
6026        pool: &ShardPool,
6027        roots: &[[u8; 16]],
6028        hash_to_shard_offset: &HashMap<[u8; 16], (u16, u64)>,
6029        pinned: &HashMap<u16, Arc<Shard>>,
6030        extract_edges: &impl Fn(&[u8; 16], &[u8]) -> Vec<[u8; 16]>,
6031    ) -> Result<AdjacencyResult, StorageError> {
6032        let mut visited: HashSet<[u8; 16]> = HashSet::new();
6033        let mut queue: VecDeque<[u8; 16]> = VecDeque::new();
6034        let mut adjacency: HashMap<[u8; 16], Vec<[u8; 16]>> = HashMap::new();
6035
6036        for root in roots {
6037            if hash_to_shard_offset.contains_key(root) && visited.insert(*root) {
6038                queue.push_back(*root);
6039            }
6040        }
6041
6042        while let Some(hash) = queue.pop_front() {
6043            let Some(&(slot, offset)) = hash_to_shard_offset.get(&hash) else {
6044                continue;
6045            };
6046            let Some(old_shard) = pinned.get(&slot) else {
6047                continue;
6048            };
6049            let record = pool.read_at(old_shard, offset, true)?;
6050            let edges = extract_edges(&hash, &record.data);
6051            for edge in &edges {
6052                if hash_to_shard_offset.contains_key(edge) && visited.insert(*edge) {
6053                    queue.push_back(*edge);
6054                }
6055            }
6056            adjacency.insert(hash, edges);
6057        }
6058
6059        let mut live_hashes: Vec<[u8; 16]> = visited.into_iter().collect();
6060        live_hashes.sort_unstable();
6061        Ok((live_hashes, adjacency))
6062    }
6063
6064    /// BFS backward (toward ancestors) from `frontier` over `extract_edges`,
6065    /// stopping expansion (and excluding from the result) anything in
6066    /// `stop_at`. Unlike [`Self::bfs_live_set`]/[`Self::bfs_bounded`]'s
6067    /// repack-side sibling, this resolves each node through `gen`'s index
6068    /// — a single frozen generation snapshot taken once before the walk
6069    /// starts — one hash lookup at a time, rather than pre-scanning every
6070    /// shard for the whole collection up front. Cost is proportional to the
6071    /// number of nodes actually walked, not collection size.
6072    ///
6073    /// Pinning `gen` for the whole walk (instead of re-resolving through
6074    /// `self.get()` per node against whatever generation happens to be
6075    /// live at call time) is also what makes this concurrency-safe: a
6076    /// repack that runs mid-walk and GCs a hash this walk already needs
6077    /// swaps in a *new* generation rather than mutating this one, so a
6078    /// node this walk has already committed to visiting can't vanish out
6079    /// from under it and get silently skipped.
6080    ///
6081    /// Returns the resolved `NodeData` for each visited node alongside the
6082    /// adjacency, so the caller has everything it needs without a second
6083    /// per-node fetch.
6084    ///
6085    /// This is an **ancestor walk with stop markers**, not a "span between
6086    /// two frontiers": a branch whose history never crosses any `stop_at`
6087    /// node is walked all the way back to the collection's true roots, not
6088    /// truncated at some implied boundary. A real from/to span would need
6089    /// `ancestors(frontier) ∩ descendants(stop_at)`, which requires
6090    /// reverse adjacency this call doesn't have — out of scope here.
6091    ///
6092    /// `limits.max_nodes`, if set, caps how many nodes this walk will visit
6093    /// before giving up on expanding further (existing queued nodes still
6094    /// finish resolving their own edges into `adjacency`, but no new nodes
6095    /// are enqueued past the cap) — the safety valve for exactly the
6096    /// runaway case above, where `stop_at` never gets hit.
6097    fn bfs_ancestors(
6098        &self,
6099        gen: &Arc<RoomGeneration>,
6100        frontier: &[[u8; 16]],
6101        stop_at: &[[u8; 16]],
6102        extract_edges: &impl Fn(&[u8; 16], &[u8]) -> Vec<[u8; 16]>,
6103        limits: WalkLimits,
6104    ) -> Result<(AdjacencyResult, HashMap<[u8; 16], NodeData>), StorageError> {
6105        let boundary: HashSet<[u8; 16]> = stop_at.iter().copied().collect();
6106        let mut visited: HashSet<[u8; 16]> = HashSet::new();
6107        let mut queue: VecDeque<[u8; 16]> = VecDeque::new();
6108        let mut adjacency: HashMap<[u8; 16], Vec<[u8; 16]>> = HashMap::new();
6109        let mut resolved: HashMap<[u8; 16], NodeData> = HashMap::new();
6110        let at_cap =
6111            |visited: &HashSet<[u8; 16]>| limits.max_nodes.is_some_and(|max| visited.len() >= max);
6112
6113        // Pin every shard this snapshot's index references before resolving
6114        // anything. The walk reads against a frozen generation, but a
6115        // concurrent repack can still retire the shard ids that generation's
6116        // index points at; without pinning, a node resolved after the swap
6117        // would miss even though it is still live. See `pin_shards`.
6118        let pinned = self.pin_shards(
6119            gen.index
6120                .referenced_slot_ids()
6121                .into_iter()
6122                .enumerate()
6123                .filter(|&(_, referenced)| referenced)
6124                .map(|(slot, _)| u16::try_from(slot).expect("shard slot fits u16")),
6125        );
6126
6127        for root in frontier {
6128            if !boundary.contains(root) && !at_cap(&visited) && visited.insert(*root) {
6129                queue.push_back(*root);
6130            }
6131        }
6132
6133        while let Some(hash) = queue.pop_front() {
6134            let Some(data) = self.resolve_pinned(gen, &pinned, &hash)? else {
6135                // Not actually present under this generation — nothing to
6136                // expand from and nothing to yield.
6137                continue;
6138            };
6139            let edges = extract_edges(&hash, &data.bytes);
6140            for edge in &edges {
6141                if !boundary.contains(edge) && !at_cap(&visited) && visited.insert(*edge) {
6142                    queue.push_back(*edge);
6143                }
6144            }
6145            adjacency.insert(hash, edges);
6146            resolved.insert(hash, data);
6147        }
6148
6149        // live_hashes tracks only nodes actually resolved, not everything
6150        // `visited` touched — a hash that turned out absent under `gen`
6151        // was marked visited to prevent re-queueing, but never belongs in
6152        // the CSR or the output.
6153        let mut live_hashes: Vec<[u8; 16]> = resolved.keys().copied().collect();
6154        live_hashes.sort_unstable();
6155        Ok(((live_hashes, adjacency), resolved))
6156    }
6157
6158    /// Resolves `id` within a specific, already-loaded generation snapshot
6159    /// rather than whatever generation happens to be live when called —
6160    /// the building block [`Self::bfs_ancestors`] uses to keep an entire
6161    /// walk consistent against one point-in-time view of the collection.
6162    ///
6163    /// `pinned` must hold every shard the snapshot's index references (see
6164    /// [`Self::pin_shards`]), so a repack that swaps in a new generation and
6165    /// retires those shards partway through the walk cannot make a later node
6166    /// miss.
6167    fn resolve_pinned(
6168        &self,
6169        gen: &Arc<RoomGeneration>,
6170        pinned: &HashMap<u16, Arc<Shard>>,
6171        id: &NodeId,
6172    ) -> Result<Option<NodeData>, StorageError> {
6173        if let Some(data) = gen.cache.get(id) {
6174            return Ok(Some((*data).clone()));
6175        }
6176        let track = self.stats_enabled.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
6177        let candidates: Vec<(u16, u64)> = gen.index.lookup_all(id).collect();
6178        if track {
6179            self.index_candidates
6180                .fetch_add(candidates.len() as u64, Ordering::Relaxed);
6181        }
6182        self.resolve_from_pinned(id, &candidates, pinned, track)
6183    }
6184
6185    /// Read every record's edges, with no reachability filtering.
6186    /// Used when a collection has no configured live roots, so nothing is known
6187    /// to be garbage. Iterates `hash_to_shard_offset` directly rather
6188    /// than the raw scan output, so it works for both full and incremental
6189    /// repack (where the map was built by merging new entries into a
6190    /// previous state rather than scanning every packfile from byte zero).
6191    fn scan_full_adjacency(
6192        pool: &ShardPool,
6193        hash_to_shard_offset: &HashMap<[u8; 16], (u16, u64)>,
6194        pinned: &HashMap<u16, Arc<Shard>>,
6195        extract_edges: &impl Fn(&[u8; 16], &[u8]) -> Vec<[u8; 16]>,
6196    ) -> Result<AdjacencyResult, StorageError> {
6197        let mut all_hashes: Vec<[u8; 16]> = hash_to_shard_offset.keys().copied().collect();
6198        all_hashes.sort_unstable();
6199        let mut adjacency: HashMap<[u8; 16], Vec<[u8; 16]>> = HashMap::new();
6200        for (hash, &(slot, offset)) in hash_to_shard_offset {
6201            if let Some(shard) = pinned.get(&slot) {
6202                let record = pool.read_at(shard, offset, true)?;
6203                let edges = extract_edges(hash, &record.data);
6204                adjacency.insert(*hash, edges);
6205            }
6206        }
6207        Ok((all_hashes, adjacency))
6208    }
6209
6210    /// Rewrite a collection's records in topological order, optionally performing
6211    /// garbage collection — this is the engine's one repack entry point.
6212    ///
6213    /// If live roots are configured for this collection (see
6214    /// [`Self::set_live_roots`]), traverses outward from them via
6215    /// `extract_edges` and drops anything not reached: only reachable
6216    /// records are read from disk during the traversal, so unreachable
6217    /// data is never even fetched, not just excluded from the output.
6218    ///
6219    /// If no live roots are configured (`set_live_roots` was never called,
6220    /// or was called with an empty list), nothing is known to be garbage,
6221    /// so every scanned record is preserved, still deduplicated and
6222    /// rewritten in topological order — rather than risk deleting live
6223    /// data on the assumption that "no roots" means "nothing is live".
6224    ///
6225    /// All shards this call will read from are pinned (held via an
6226    /// `Arc<Shard>` for the whole call) before any writes happen, so a
6227    /// rotation triggered by this call's own writes can never retire a
6228    /// shard this
6229    /// call still needs to read stale data from.
6230    ///
6231    /// Returns `(kept, dropped)`: the number of records written to the new
6232    /// generation, and the number of scanned records found unreachable and
6233    /// discarded.
6234    ///
6235    /// # Errors
6236    /// Returns `StorageError` on I/O or corruption.
6237    /// Builds this repack's deduped `hash → (slot, offset)` map,
6238    /// incrementally where possible, and returns the previous
6239    /// [`RepackIncrementalState`] (moved out, not cloned) so the caller can
6240    /// reuse its `adjacency` cache when deciding which nodes need fresh disk
6241    /// reads.
6242    ///
6243    /// On the incremental path the previous `live_map` is extended in-place
6244    /// with only the newly-appended entries from each shard (O(delta) scan
6245    /// work per repack call rather than O(total)). On the cold-start path
6246    /// (first repack for this collection) every shard is scanned from byte
6247    /// zero.
6248    ///
6249    /// Returns `(hash_to_shard_offset, Some(prev))` on the incremental path
6250    /// and `(hash_to_shard_offset, None)` on the cold-start path. The caller
6251    /// must pass `prev` to the adjacency helpers to unlock the incremental
6252    /// BFS optimisation; when it is `None` the caller uses the full-scan
6253    /// adjacency helpers instead.
6254    ///
6255    /// # Errors
6256    /// Returns `StorageError` on I/O failure scanning a shard.
6257    fn repack_scan_incremental(
6258        &self,
6259        collection_id: &[u8; 16],
6260    ) -> Result<RepackScanResult, StorageError> {
6261        // Check for existing state under a read lock, then move it out under a
6262        // write lock if present — O(1) ownership transfer, no clone.
6263        let has_prev = self.repack_incremental.read().contains_key(collection_id);
6264        if has_prev {
6265            let prev = self
6266                .repack_incremental
6267                .write()
6268                .remove(collection_id)
6269                .expect("entry was present under read lock and collection mutex is held");
6270
6271            let shards = self.shards.all_shards();
6272            let current_pack_ids: HashMap<u16, u64> = shards
6273                .iter()
6274                .map(|(slot, shard)| (*slot, shard.pack_id))
6275                .collect();
6276            // Slot IDs are recyclable.  A cursor (and every entry in the
6277            // carried live_map) is meaningful only for the pack incarnation
6278            // that produced it.  On any replacement or disappearance, start
6279            // over rather than mixing old offsets with the new pack.
6280            let pack_changed = prev
6281                .scan_offsets
6282                .iter()
6283                .any(|(slot, (pack_id, _))| current_pack_ids.get(slot) != Some(pack_id));
6284            if pack_changed {
6285                let scanned = self.scan_collection_records(collection_id)?;
6286                let mut map = HashMap::new();
6287                for (slot, entries) in scanned {
6288                    for (hash, offset) in entries {
6289                        map.insert(hash, (slot, offset));
6290                    }
6291                }
6292                return Ok((map, None));
6293            }
6294
6295            // Scan only bytes appended since the last repack, merging into
6296            // the stolen live_map in-place — O(delta) work, not O(total).
6297            let mut map = prev.live_map.clone();
6298            for (slot, shard) in shards {
6299                let start = prev
6300                    .scan_offsets
6301                    .get(&slot)
6302                    .filter(|(pack_id, _)| *pack_id == shard.pack_id)
6303                    .map_or(0, |(_, offset)| *offset);
6304                let entries =
6305                    packfile::scan_packfile_from(&shard.path, start).map_err(StorageError::Io)?;
6306                for (rid, hash, offset) in entries {
6307                    if rid == *collection_id {
6308                        map.insert(hash, (slot, offset));
6309                    }
6310                }
6311            }
6312            Ok((map, Some(prev)))
6313        } else {
6314            // First repack: full scan of every shard.
6315            let scanned = self.scan_collection_records(collection_id)?;
6316            let mut map = HashMap::new();
6317            for (slot, entries) in &scanned {
6318                for (hash, offset) in entries {
6319                    map.insert(*hash, (*slot, *offset));
6320                }
6321            }
6322            Ok((map, None))
6323        }
6324    }
6325
6326    /// Incremental BFS reachability walk.
6327    ///
6328    /// Uses the adjacency cache from `prev` to avoid re-reading disk for nodes
6329    /// that were already known-live after the last repack. Only newly-added
6330    /// nodes (those absent from `prev.adjacency`) require a disk read.
6331    ///
6332    /// **Root-removal invariant (critical):** This function must NOT be called
6333    /// when the current root set is a strict subset of `prev.prev_roots` (i.e.
6334    /// any root was removed since the last repack). In that case nodes
6335    /// exclusively reachable through the removed root would remain in the live
6336    /// set indefinitely, because `visited` in `prev.adjacency` only grows —
6337    /// nothing in this incremental path forces a re-check of reachability.
6338    /// The caller ([`Self::repack_collection_reachable`]) detects root removal
6339    /// and falls back to [`Self::bfs_live_set`] (cold-start, full BFS) for
6340    /// that repack, then saves a fresh cursor so subsequent repacks can be
6341    /// incremental again.
6342    ///
6343    /// **Memory:** `prev.adjacency` holds `O(live_nodes` × `avg_fanout`) hashes
6344    /// (≈ `live_nodes × avg_fanout × 16` bytes) in RAM per collection. This
6345    /// is the cost of eliminating the O(live) disk reads per repack call —
6346    /// callers should be aware for large collections.
6347    fn bfs_live_set_incremental(
6348        pool: &ShardPool,
6349        roots: &[[u8; 16]],
6350        hash_to_shard_offset: &HashMap<[u8; 16], (u16, u64)>,
6351        prev: &RepackIncrementalState,
6352        pinned: &HashMap<u16, Arc<Shard>>,
6353        extract_edges: &impl Fn(&[u8; 16], &[u8]) -> Vec<[u8; 16]>,
6354    ) -> Result<AdjacencyResult, StorageError> {
6355        // Seed with roots that are not already in the cached live set.
6356        // Anything in prev.adjacency was reachable last time and — given no
6357        // root was removed — is still reachable now; no need to re-expand it.
6358        let mut visited: HashSet<[u8; 16]> = prev.adjacency.keys().copied().collect();
6359        let mut queue: VecDeque<[u8; 16]> = VecDeque::new();
6360        // Retain the cached edges for already-live nodes.  Initialising these
6361        // entries with empty vectors loses prior edges when they are not put
6362        // back on the queue during an incremental rooted repack.
6363        let mut adjacency = prev.adjacency.clone();
6364
6365        for root in roots {
6366            if hash_to_shard_offset.contains_key(root) && visited.insert(*root) {
6367                queue.push_back(*root);
6368            }
6369        }
6370
6371        while let Some(hash) = queue.pop_front() {
6372            // Fast path: edge list already cached — no disk read needed.
6373            if let Some(edges) = prev.adjacency.get(&hash) {
6374                for edge in edges {
6375                    if hash_to_shard_offset.contains_key(edge) && visited.insert(*edge) {
6376                        queue.push_back(*edge);
6377                    }
6378                }
6379                adjacency.insert(hash, edges.clone());
6380                continue;
6381            }
6382
6383            // Slow path: new node, must read from disk.
6384            let Some(&(slot, offset)) = hash_to_shard_offset.get(&hash) else {
6385                continue;
6386            };
6387            let Some(old_shard) = pinned.get(&slot) else {
6388                continue;
6389            };
6390            let record = pool.read_at(old_shard, offset, true)?;
6391            let edges = extract_edges(&hash, &record.data);
6392            for edge in &edges {
6393                if hash_to_shard_offset.contains_key(edge) && visited.insert(*edge) {
6394                    queue.push_back(*edge);
6395                }
6396            }
6397            adjacency.insert(hash, edges);
6398        }
6399
6400        // Restrict adjacency to the actual visited set — entries inherited
6401        // from prev that are no longer in hash_to_shard_offset (e.g. they
6402        // were in a shard that was later dropped) must not survive.
6403        adjacency.retain(|h, _| visited.contains(h) && hash_to_shard_offset.contains_key(h));
6404
6405        let mut live_hashes: Vec<[u8; 16]> = visited
6406            .into_iter()
6407            .filter(|h| hash_to_shard_offset.contains_key(h))
6408            .collect();
6409        live_hashes.sort_unstable();
6410        Ok((live_hashes, adjacency))
6411    }
6412
6413    /// Incremental full-adjacency scan (no-roots / preserve-everything path).
6414    ///
6415    /// For each hash in `hash_to_shard_offset`, reuses the cached edge list
6416    /// from `prev.adjacency` when available — avoiding a disk read for any
6417    /// node that survived the last repack. Only genuinely new hashes (not in
6418    /// the cache) require a disk read.
6419    ///
6420    /// All hashes in `hash_to_shard_offset` are live (no GC in this path),
6421    /// so the result is always the full map.
6422    ///
6423    /// **Memory:** same as [`Self::bfs_live_set_incremental`] — see that doc.
6424    fn scan_full_adjacency_incremental(
6425        pool: &ShardPool,
6426        hash_to_shard_offset: &HashMap<[u8; 16], (u16, u64)>,
6427        prev: &RepackIncrementalState,
6428        pinned: &HashMap<u16, Arc<Shard>>,
6429        extract_edges: &impl Fn(&[u8; 16], &[u8]) -> Vec<[u8; 16]>,
6430    ) -> Result<AdjacencyResult, StorageError> {
6431        let mut all_hashes: Vec<[u8; 16]> = hash_to_shard_offset.keys().copied().collect();
6432        all_hashes.sort_unstable();
6433        let mut adjacency: HashMap<[u8; 16], Vec<[u8; 16]>> =
6434            HashMap::with_capacity(hash_to_shard_offset.len());
6435
6436        for (hash, &(slot, offset)) in hash_to_shard_offset {
6437            // Fast path: node was live last time, edge list is cached.
6438            if let Some(edges) = prev.adjacency.get(hash) {
6439                adjacency.insert(*hash, edges.clone());
6440                continue;
6441            }
6442            // Slow path: new node, must read from disk.
6443            if let Some(shard) = pinned.get(&slot) {
6444                let record = pool.read_at(shard, offset, true)?;
6445                let edges = extract_edges(hash, &record.data);
6446                adjacency.insert(*hash, edges);
6447            }
6448        }
6449        Ok((all_hashes, adjacency))
6450    }
6451
6452    /// Saves the cursor state a future call to [`Self::repack_scan_incremental`]
6453    /// needs: each shard's current byte length (the next repack's scan start
6454    /// point), the deduped live map restricted to hashes that survived into
6455    /// `new_offsets`, the adjacency cache for those survivors (so the next
6456    /// repack's BFS/scan can skip re-reading disk for already-seen nodes), and
6457    /// the roots snapshot (so the next repack can detect whether any root was
6458    /// removed and fall back to a full BFS sweep if so).
6459    ///
6460    /// Anything this repack dropped must not resurface via the carried-forward
6461    /// `live_map` or adjacency cache next time.
6462    fn repack_save_incremental_state(
6463        &self,
6464        collection_id: &[u8; 16],
6465        new_offsets: &[([u8; 16], u16, u64)],
6466        adjacency: HashMap<[u8; 16], Vec<[u8; 16]>>,
6467        current_roots: &[[u8; 16]],
6468    ) {
6469        let surviving: HashSet<[u8; 16]> = new_offsets.iter().map(|&(h, _, _)| h).collect();
6470
6471        let mut scan_offsets = HashMap::new();
6472        for (slot, shard) in self.shards.all_shards() {
6473            scan_offsets.insert(slot, (shard.pack_id, shard.file_len()));
6474        }
6475        let next_live_map: HashMap<[u8; 16], (u16, u64)> = new_offsets
6476            .iter()
6477            .map(|&(hash, slot, offset)| (hash, (slot, offset)))
6478            .collect();
6479        // Evict dropped nodes from the adjacency cache so they can't
6480        // re-enter the live set on a future incremental BFS pass.
6481        let next_adjacency: HashMap<[u8; 16], Vec<[u8; 16]>> = adjacency
6482            .into_iter()
6483            .filter(|(h, _)| surviving.contains(h))
6484            .collect();
6485        self.repack_incremental.write().insert(
6486            *collection_id,
6487            RepackIncrementalState {
6488                scan_offsets,
6489                live_map: next_live_map,
6490                adjacency: next_adjacency,
6491                prev_roots: current_roots.to_vec(),
6492            },
6493        );
6494    }
6495
6496    /// Non-mutating preview of what [`Self::repack_collection_reachable`] would
6497    /// do for `collection_id`: runs the exact same scan + reachability
6498    /// computation (so kept/dropped counts are exact, not estimates), but
6499    /// performs no writes, no index swap, and no incremental-repack
6500    /// cursor update. Used to preview a repack's effect before committing
6501    /// to it — e.g. a shard-compaction preflight that needs "how many
6502    /// bytes would survive, and which shards do they currently live in"
6503    /// without actually rewriting anything.
6504    ///
6505    /// # Errors
6506    /// Returns `StorageError` on I/O or corruption.
6507    pub fn plan_collection_repack(
6508        &self,
6509        collection_id: &[u8; 16],
6510        extract_edges: impl Fn(&[u8; 16], &[u8]) -> Vec<[u8; 16]>,
6511    ) -> Result<RepackPlan, StorageError> {
6512        // `repack_scan_incremental` moves the cursor out to avoid cloning on
6513        // real repacks.  A plan must leave that state untouched, and must not
6514        // race a real repack while temporarily doing so.
6515        let collection_arc = self.put_mutex(collection_id);
6516        let _collection_guard = collection_arc.lock();
6517        // Make buffered frames visible to the packfile scan so the plan
6518        // reflects records that have actually been put (not yet flushed).
6519        self.shards.flush_all()?;
6520        let saved_state = self.repack_incremental.read().get(collection_id).cloned();
6521        let result = self
6522            .repack_scan_incremental(collection_id)
6523            .and_then(|(map, _)| {
6524                self.plan_collection_repack_from_map(collection_id, &map, &extract_edges)
6525            });
6526        let mut states = self.repack_incremental.write();
6527        if let Some(state) = saved_state {
6528            states.insert(*collection_id, state);
6529        } else {
6530            states.remove(collection_id);
6531        }
6532        result
6533    }
6534
6535    fn plan_collection_repack_from_map(
6536        &self,
6537        collection_id: &[u8; 16],
6538        hash_to_shard_offset: &RepackRecordMap,
6539        extract_edges: &impl Fn(&[u8; 16], &[u8]) -> Vec<[u8; 16]>,
6540    ) -> Result<RepackPlan, StorageError> {
6541        let pinned = self.pin_shards(hash_to_shard_offset.values().map(|&(id, _)| id));
6542
6543        let roots = self.live_roots.read().get(collection_id).cloned();
6544        let (live_hashes, _adjacency) = match roots {
6545            Some(roots) if !roots.is_empty() => Self::bfs_live_set(
6546                &self.shards,
6547                &roots,
6548                hash_to_shard_offset,
6549                &pinned,
6550                &extract_edges,
6551            )?,
6552            _ => Self::scan_full_adjacency(
6553                &self.shards,
6554                hash_to_shard_offset,
6555                &pinned,
6556                &extract_edges,
6557            )?,
6558        };
6559        let dropped = hash_to_shard_offset.len().saturating_sub(live_hashes.len());
6560
6561        let live_set: HashSet<[u8; 16]> = live_hashes.iter().copied().collect();
6562        let mut kept_bytes: u64 = 0;
6563        let mut dropped_bytes: u64 = 0;
6564        let mut shards_touched: HashSet<u16> = HashSet::new();
6565        for (hash, &(slot, offset)) in hash_to_shard_offset {
6566            if let Some(shard) = pinned.get(&slot) {
6567                // Actual on-disk bytes, not the uncompressed upper bound —
6568                // a repack preflight should report what will really be
6569                // reclaimed/kept, which is smaller than plaintext size for
6570                // any frame that compressed.
6571                if let Ok(bytes) = Self::record_disk_len_at(shard, offset) {
6572                    if live_set.contains(hash) {
6573                        shards_touched.insert(slot);
6574                        kept_bytes = kept_bytes.saturating_add(bytes);
6575                    } else {
6576                        dropped_bytes = dropped_bytes.saturating_add(bytes);
6577                    }
6578                }
6579            }
6580        }
6581
6582        let mut shards_touched: Vec<u16> = shards_touched.into_iter().collect();
6583        shards_touched.sort_unstable();
6584        Ok(RepackPlan {
6585            kept: live_hashes.len(),
6586            dropped,
6587            kept_bytes,
6588            dropped_bytes,
6589            shards_touched,
6590        })
6591    }
6592
6593    /// Plan several collection repacks from one physical scan of their shard
6594    /// closure. Unlike repeatedly calling [`Self::plan_collection_repack`], this
6595    /// is O(bytes scanned) rather than O(collections × bytes scanned).
6596    ///
6597    /// # Errors
6598    /// Returns `StorageError` on I/O or corruption while scanning or
6599    /// resolving a requested collection's records.
6600    pub fn plan_collections_repack(
6601        &self,
6602        collection_ids: &[[u8; 16]],
6603        extract_edges: impl Fn(&[u8; 16], &[u8]) -> Vec<[u8; 16]>,
6604    ) -> Result<Vec<RepackPlan>, StorageError> {
6605        // Planning reads packfiles directly; flush first so buffered records
6606        // are part of the plan.
6607        self.shards.flush_all()?;
6608        let maps = self.scan_collection_record_maps(collection_ids)?;
6609        collection_ids
6610            .iter()
6611            .map(|collection_id| {
6612                let map = maps.get(collection_id).ok_or_else(|| {
6613                    StorageError::Corrupt("repack batch scan lost requested collection".to_owned())
6614                })?;
6615                self.plan_collection_repack_from_map(collection_id, map, &extract_edges)
6616            })
6617            .collect()
6618    }
6619
6620    /// Finds every collection and shard transitively reachable from
6621    /// `start_shard` via the collection↔shard reference relation: collections
6622    /// referencing this shard, the other shards those collections reference,
6623    /// the collections referencing *those* shards, and so on until nothing new
6624    /// is found. In practice this converges immediately in almost every
6625    /// case — a collection typically has a live footprint on only one or two
6626    /// shards (sticky home routing) — but the closure has to be computed
6627    /// rather than assumed, since a collection-scoped repack can't correctly
6628    /// judge liveness by looking at only one shard's slice of that collection's
6629    /// data (see [`Self::collections_referencing_shard`]'s doc).
6630    ///
6631    /// This is the basis for a shard-compaction preflight: you can't
6632    /// truthfully say "this touches N collections across K shards" without
6633    /// first finding the full closure, not just the one shard the
6634    /// operation was originally pointed at.
6635    ///
6636    /// # Errors
6637    /// Returns `StorageError` if `start_shard` isn't an open shard.
6638    pub fn repack_closure(
6639        &self,
6640        start_shard: u16,
6641    ) -> Result<(Vec<[u8; 16]>, Vec<u16>), StorageError> {
6642        let mut collections: HashSet<[u8; 16]> = HashSet::new();
6643        let mut shards: HashSet<u16> = HashSet::new();
6644        let mut shard_queue = vec![start_shard];
6645        let mut collection_queue: Vec<[u8; 16]> = Vec::new();
6646
6647        loop {
6648            if let Some(slot) = shard_queue.pop() {
6649                if shards.insert(slot) {
6650                    for collection_id in self.collections_referencing_shard(slot)? {
6651                        if collections.insert(collection_id) {
6652                            collection_queue.push(collection_id);
6653                        }
6654                    }
6655                }
6656            } else if let Some(collection_id) = collection_queue.pop() {
6657                for slot in self.collection_referenced_shards(&collection_id) {
6658                    if !shards.contains(&slot) {
6659                        shard_queue.push(slot);
6660                    }
6661                }
6662            } else {
6663                break;
6664            }
6665        }
6666
6667        let mut collections: Vec<[u8; 16]> = collections.into_iter().collect();
6668        collections.sort_unstable();
6669        let mut shards: Vec<u16> = shards.into_iter().collect();
6670        shards.sort_unstable();
6671        Ok((collections, shards))
6672    }
6673
6674    /// Every shard id `collection_id`'s current index has at least one live
6675    /// entry pointing into. Empty if the collection doesn't exist.
6676    #[must_use]
6677    pub fn collection_referenced_shards(&self, collection_id: &[u8; 16]) -> Vec<u16> {
6678        let Some(gen) = self.generation(collection_id) else {
6679            return Vec::new();
6680        };
6681        gen.index
6682            .referenced_slot_ids()
6683            .iter()
6684            .enumerate()
6685            .filter_map(|(i, &referenced)| referenced.then(|| u16::try_from(i).ok()).flatten())
6686            .collect()
6687    }
6688
6689    /// Like `collection_referenced_shards`, but returns the `pack_id`
6690    /// for each shard rather than the runtime slot index.
6691    pub fn collection_referenced_pack_ids(&self, collection_id: &[u8; 16]) -> Vec<u64> {
6692        self.collection_referenced_shards(collection_id)
6693            .iter()
6694            .filter_map(|&slot| self.shards.get_shard(slot).map(|s| s.pack_id))
6695            .collect()
6696    }
6697
6698    /// Current indexed-node count for every shard.
6699    ///
6700    /// Unlike a physical packfile scan, these counts include only index
6701    /// entries that are presently live and resolve through a collection's current
6702    /// generation. Rewritten or superseded append entries are excluded.
6703    #[must_use]
6704    pub fn shard_node_counts(&self) -> HashMap<u64, u64> {
6705        self.index_tables
6706            .read()
6707            .shard_collections
6708            .iter()
6709            .map(|(&slot, collections)| {
6710                let count = collections
6711                    .values()
6712                    .copied()
6713                    .fold(0u64, u64::saturating_add);
6714                (slot, count)
6715            })
6716            .collect()
6717    }
6718
6719    /// # Errors
6720    /// Returns `StorageError` on I/O or corruption.
6721    ///
6722    /// # Panics
6723    /// Panics if any hash in the CSR exceeds `u32::MAX` local ID space.
6724    // Four dispatch arms (roots/no-roots × incremental/cold-start) plus root-removal
6725    // detection make this function long; splitting it would just move the complexity
6726    // without reducing it.
6727    #[allow(clippy::too_many_lines)]
6728    pub fn repack_collection_reachable(
6729        &self,
6730        collection_id: &[u8; 16],
6731        extract_edges: impl Fn(&[u8; 16], &[u8]) -> Vec<[u8; 16]>,
6732    ) -> Result<(usize, usize), StorageError> {
6733        let collection_arc = self.put_mutex(collection_id);
6734        let collection_guard = collection_arc.lock();
6735
