8448
8449    fn delete_collection(&self, collection_id: &[u8; 16]) -> Result<(), StorageError> {
8450        // Acquire the collection's put mutex to serialize with any in-flight put,
8451        // preventing a concurrent put from resurrecting the collection after we
8452        // remove it from the generation map.
8453        let collection_arc = self.put_mutex(collection_id);
8454        let _collection_guard = collection_arc.lock();
8455
8456        self.collections_write().remove(collection_id);
8457        self.live_roots.write().remove(collection_id);
8458        // A deletion changes the collection directory the same way a refill
8459        // does, so any pending delta frames are no longer replayable against
8460        // the checkpoint they were recorded against.
8461        self.delta_invalidations.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
8462        self.mark_v3_collection_deleted(collection_id);
8463        self.index_checkpoint_dirty.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
8464        // Keep lock entries for the storage lifetime. Removing an entry while
8465        // a caller still owns its Arc permits a later put to obtain a second
8466        // mutex and bypass this deletion's serialization.
8467        self.remove_collection_shard_counts(collection_id);
8468        self.persist_deleted_collection(collection_id)?;
8469        self.publish_mutation(|| JournalMutation::DeleteCollection {
8470            collection_id: *collection_id,
8471        })?;
8472        Ok(())
8473    }
8474
8475    fn sync(&self) -> Result<(), StorageError> {
8476        let started = std::time::Instant::now();
8477        let mut timings = SyncTimings::default();
8478        let pending_generation = self.mark_sync_pending_age(&mut timings);
8479        let result = self
8480            .sync_durability(true, &mut timings)
8481            .map(|()| self.persist_index_checkpoint_or_delta(&mut timings));
8482        timings.failed = result.is_err();
8483        self.finish_sync_pending_age(pending_generation);
8484        // Remediation runs after the journal barrier and is part of what the
8485        // caller waited for: a sync that unblocks a stalled shared WAL pays the
8486        // capture (or, without background checkpoints, the whole checkpoint).
8487        if result.is_ok() {
8488            let remediation_started = std::time::Instant::now();
8489            self.remediate_lagging_pools();
8490            timings.remediation = remediation_started.elapsed();
8491        }
8492        timings.total = started.elapsed();
8493        self.record_sync_diagnostics(&timings);
8494        if result.is_ok() {
8495            self.count_sync_persistence(&timings);
8496        }
8497        *self.last_sync_timings.lock() = Some(timings);
8498        result
8499    }
8500
8501    fn refresh_collection(&self, collection_id: &[u8; 16]) -> Result<(), StorageError> {
8502        Self::refresh_collection(self, collection_id)
8503    }
8504}
8505
8506impl PackfileStorage {
8507    /// Check collection existence using the historical boolean API.
8508    ///
8509    /// Call [`Self::try_collection_exists`] when storage errors must be
8510    /// distinguished from a missing collection.
8511    #[must_use]
8512    pub fn collection_exists(&self, collection_id: &[u8; 16]) -> bool {
8513        self.try_collection_exists(collection_id).unwrap_or(false)
8514    }
8515
8516    /// Check collection existence without hiding overlay/read failures.
8517    ///
8518    /// The trait's historical boolean API is retained for compatibility and
8519    /// fails closed on errors. New callers that need to distinguish absence
8520    /// from storage failure should use this method.
8521    ///
8522    /// # Errors
8523    /// Returns a storage or journal-overlay error when the authoritative
8524    /// read-committed lookup cannot be completed.
8525    pub fn try_collection_exists(&self, collection_id: &[u8; 16]) -> Result<bool, StorageError> {
8526        if self.transaction_overlay_users.load(Ordering::Acquire) != 0 {
8527            return self
8528                .get_read_committed(
8529                    collection_id,
8530                    std::slice::from_ref(&COLLECTION_METADATA_RECORD_ID),
8531                )
8532                .map(|values| values.first().is_some_and(Option::is_some));
8533        }
8534        Ok(self.generation(collection_id).is_some())
8535    }
8536
8537    /// Return collection length at read-committed visibility.
8538    ///
8539    /// Overlay puts replace durable values with the same node ID and add to
8540    /// the durable count only for new IDs. A committed collection delete
8541    /// hides the durable generation until replacement puts are applied.
8542    ///
8543    /// # Errors
8544    /// Returns a storage or journal-overlay error when the authoritative
8545    /// read-committed view cannot be refreshed.
8546    pub fn try_collection_len(
8547        &self,
8548        collection_id: &[u8; 16],
8549    ) -> Result<Option<usize>, StorageError> {
8550        if self.transaction_overlay_users.load(Ordering::Acquire) == 0 {
8551            return Ok(self
8552                .generation(collection_id)
8553                .map(|generation| generation.index.len()));
8554        }
8555
8556        let overlay_guard = self.refresh_read_journal()?;
8557        let Some(overlay) = overlay_guard.as_ref() else {
8558            return Ok(self
8559                .generation(collection_id)
8560                .map(|generation| generation.index.len()));
8561        };
8562        let puts = overlay.puts.get(collection_id);
8563        let deleted = overlay.delete_lsn.contains_key(collection_id);
8564        let generation = self.generation(collection_id);
8565        let durable_len = generation
8566            .as_ref()
8567            .map_or(0, |generation| generation.index.len());
8568
8569        if deleted {
8570            return Ok(puts
8571                .filter(|puts| !puts.is_empty())
8572                .map(std::collections::HashMap::len));
8573        }
8574
8575        let Some(puts) = puts else {
8576            return Ok(generation.map(|_| durable_len));
8577        };
8578        let additions = puts
8579            .keys()
8580            .filter(|node_id| {
8581                generation.as_ref().map_or(true, |generation| {
8582                    generation.index.lookup_all(node_id).next().is_none()
8583                })
8584            })
8585            .count();
8586        let length = durable_len.saturating_add(additions);
8587        Ok(if generation.is_some() || !puts.is_empty() {
8588            Some(length)
8589        } else {
8590            None
8591        })
8592    }
8593
8594    /// Hint the kernel to read each planned extent as one sequential run.
8595    ///
8596    /// Reads go through the shard's mmap, so the physical coalescing is a
8597    /// `madvise(MADV_WILLNEED)` over the merged range rather than a `pread`
8598    /// into a buffer: the existing zero-copy decode path is unchanged, and the
8599    /// kernel is free to queue the readahead asynchronously while resolution
8600    /// proceeds. Best-effort: an extent that cannot be advised (missing
8601    /// mapping, offset beyond the current mapping, or a failed `madvise`) is
8602    /// counted in `read_plan_skipped_extents` rather than silently dropped.
8603    #[cfg(unix)]
8604    fn prefetch_extents(
8605        &self,
8606        extents: &[ReadExtent],
8607        pinned: &HashMap<u16, Arc<Shard>>,
8608        track: bool,
8609    ) {
8610        for extent in extents {
8611            match Self::prefetch_extent(extent, pinned) {
8612                Some(len) => {
8613                    if track {
8614                        self.read_plan_extents.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
8615                        self.read_plan_prefetch_bytes
8616                            .fetch_add(len, Ordering::Relaxed);
8617                    }
8618                }
8619                None => {
8620                    if track {
8621                        self.read_plan_skipped_extents
8622                            .fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
8623                    }
8624                }
8625            }
8626        }
8627    }
8628
8629    /// Advise every pinned shard mapping `MADV_RANDOM` before a scattered
8630    /// batch read, so the kernel does not let readahead amplify each fault
8631    /// into a large sequential block read. This is the no-plan alternative to
8632    /// [`Self::prefetch_extents`]: it does not merge or prefetch anything, it
8633    /// only stops readahead from over-reading beyond the pages actually
8634    /// touched. A shard whose mapping is absent or whose `madvise` fails is
8635    /// simply left alone — the read still works, just with default advice.
8636    #[cfg(unix)]
8637    fn advise_random(pinned: &HashMap<u16, Arc<Shard>>) {
8638        for shard in pinned.values() {
8639            if let Ok(guard) = shard.mmap() {
8640                if let Some(mapping) = guard.as_ref() {
8641                    let _ = mapping.advise(memmap2::Advice::Random);
8642                }
8643            }
8644        }
8645    }
8646
8647    /// Non-Unix builds have no `madvise`; readahead advice is a no-op.
8648    #[cfg(not(unix))]
8649    fn advise_random(_pinned: &HashMap<u16, Arc<Shard>>) {}
8650
8651    /// `madvise(MADV_WILLNEED)` one extent, returning its byte length on
8652    /// success and `None` if it could not be advised.
8653    ///
8654    /// `advise_range` requires the offset and length to lie within the mapping;
8655    /// clamp rather than error, since a virtual (buffered-but-unflushed) offset
8656    /// is legitimately beyond the current mapping and simply cannot be
8657    /// prefetched until the shard flushes.
8658    #[cfg(unix)]
8659    fn prefetch_extent(extent: &ReadExtent, pinned: &HashMap<u16, Arc<Shard>>) -> Option<u64> {
8660        let shard = pinned.get(&extent.slot)?;
8661        let guard = shard.mmap().ok()?;
8662        let mapping = guard.as_ref()?;
8663        let start = usize::try_from(extent.start).ok()?;
8664        let end = usize::try_from(extent.end)
8665            .unwrap_or(usize::MAX)
8666            .min(mapping.len());
8667        if start >= end {
8668            return None;
8669        }
8670        let len = end.saturating_sub(start);
8671        mapping
8672            .advise_range(memmap2::Advice::WillNeed, start, len)
8673            .ok()?;
8674        Some(u64::try_from(len).unwrap_or(u64::MAX))
8675    }
8676
8677    /// Non-Unix builds have no `madvise`; every planned extent is skipped.
8678    #[cfg(not(unix))]
8679    fn prefetch_extents(
8680        &self,
8681        extents: &[ReadExtent],
8682        _pinned: &HashMap<u16, Arc<Shard>>,
8683        track: bool,
8684    ) {
8685        if track {
8686            self.read_plan_skipped_extents
8687                .fetch_add(extents.len() as u64, Ordering::Relaxed);
8688        }
8689    }
8690
8691    /// Persist the pre-batch generation after a batch failed after physical
8692    /// appends. The append-only frames remain as unreachable bytes, but the
8693    /// checkpoint's matching pack fingerprint makes that exclusion durable
8694    /// across a crash before the caller can run a later sync.
8695    fn persist_failed_batch_boundary(&self, error: StorageError) -> StorageError {
8696        let _persist_guard = self.index_persist_lock.lock();
8697        self.index_checkpoint_dirty.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
8698        match self
8699            .shards
8700            .sync_dirty()
8701            .map_err(StorageError::Io)
8702            .and_then(|()| self.persist_index_checkpoint())
8703        {
8704            Ok(()) => error,
8705            Err(boundary_error) => boundary_error,
8706        }
8707    }
8708
8709    /// Sync all open shards to disk (full pool, not just dirty).
8710    ///
8711    /// A full checkpoint rewrite also persists the shard→collection directory
8712    /// as a side effect — the rewrite is an anchor at which this observability
8713    /// sidecar is re-pinned to the same pack fingerprint the checkpoint just
8714    /// became. A delta-only barrier defers it; see
8715    /// `persist_index_checkpoint_or_delta` for the deferral policy.
8716    ///
8717    /// # Errors
8718    /// Returns `StorageError` on I/O failure.
8719    pub fn sync_all(&self) -> Result<(), StorageError> {
8720        let started = std::time::Instant::now();
8721        let mut timings = SyncTimings::default();
8722        let pending_generation = self.mark_sync_pending_age(&mut timings);
8723        let result = self
8724            .sync_durability(false, &mut timings)
8725            .map(|()| self.persist_index_checkpoint_or_delta(&mut timings));
8726        timings.failed = result.is_err();
8727        self.finish_sync_pending_age(pending_generation);
8728        if result.is_ok() {
8729            let remediation_started = std::time::Instant::now();
8730            self.remediate_lagging_pools();
8731            timings.remediation = remediation_started.elapsed();
8732        }
8733        timings.total = started.elapsed();
8734        self.record_sync_diagnostics(&timings);
8735        if result.is_ok() {
8736            self.count_sync_persistence(&timings);
8737        }
8738        *self.last_sync_timings.lock() = Some(timings);
8739        result
8740    }
8741
8742    /// Rewrite the on-disk index checkpoint now, bypassing the delta-append
8743    /// fast path a normal sync takes whenever the delta log can continue.
8744    ///
8745    /// [`Self::sync_all`] appends a delta and does not advance the checkpoint's
8746    /// covered LSN, so the read-committed reader-reload path is reached only
8747    /// when a full checkpoint runs — a delta-log cap rollover, or this call.
8748    /// Tests and benchmarks use this to exercise that path deterministically;
8749    /// production callers normally rely on `sync_all`.
8750    ///
8751    /// This hook is for reload-path testing, not a production durability
8752    /// barrier. It fsyncs dirty shard frames before taking `index_persist_lock`
8753    /// (so the fsync never runs under the lock a concurrent sync holds across
8754    /// its own checkpoint — the same order as the normal sync path,
8755    /// `sync_durability` before `persist_index_checkpoint_or_delta`). A
8756    /// concurrent put can still append between that fsync and the snapshot
8757    /// `persist_index_checkpoint` takes under its collection locks.
8758    ///
8759    /// In the no-journal path, concurrent writes may be flushed but not fsynced
8760    /// before the checkpoint snapshot, and the fingerprint gate is not
8761    /// guaranteed to reject the result (a torn write that preserves the
8762    /// recorded length can still match), so do not treat this call as a
8763    /// durability boundary. With a journal enabled, `persist_index_checkpoint`
8764    /// fsyncs the shards under its collection locks and the journal remains
8765    /// authoritative. Marking the index dirty first makes the rewrite run even
8766    /// immediately after a delta sync; the flag stays set if the fsync fails,
8767    /// so a later call retries rather than dropping it.
8768    ///
8769    /// Intentionally public so the standalone `mtxdb-benches` crate can reach
8770    /// it; a cargo feature-gated benchmark API would give stronger separation,
8771    /// at the cost of a feature that crate would have to enable.
8772    ///
8773    /// # Errors
8774    /// Propagates any shard-fsync or checkpoint-write failure.
8775    pub fn force_index_checkpoint(&self) -> Result<(), StorageError> {
8776        self.index_checkpoint_dirty.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
8777        self.shards.sync_dirty().map_err(StorageError::Io)?;
8778        let _persist_guard = self.index_persist_lock.lock();
8779        self.persist_index_checkpoint()
8780    }
8781
8782    /// Checkpoint to unblock WAL reclaim, detaching the tail when the
8783    /// background checkpoint is enabled.
8784    ///
8785    /// [`Self::force_index_checkpoint`] always joins and runs inline, so a
8786    /// shared-WAL remediation that forced it would pay the whole checkpoint on
8787    /// the syncing thread — exactly what the background path exists to avoid.
8788    /// This captures under the locks and spawns the tail, returning once the
8789    /// capture is done; the tail reports coverage when its image is durable.
8790    /// Falls back to the synchronous path when backgrounding is off or a
8791    /// capture cannot start.
8792    ///
8793    /// # Errors
8794    /// Propagates any shard-fsync failure from the synchronous fallback.
8795    pub fn force_index_checkpoint_detached(&self) -> Result<(), StorageError> {
8796        if !self.background_checkpoint.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
8797            return self.force_index_checkpoint();
8798        }
8799        self.shards.sync_dirty().map_err(StorageError::Io)?;
8800        // Serialize with this pool's own syncs, and never start a second tail:
8801        // it would rotate the epoch again and race the first on the checkpoint
8802        // file. A tail already running is what remediation wanted; its coverage
8803        // lands when its image is durable, and a sync near the WAL cap waits for
8804        // it. Only mark the index dirty when a checkpoint really starts, or the
8805        // next sync would rewrite an image nothing needs.
8806        let _persist_guard = self.index_persist_lock.lock();
8807        if !self.finish_checkpoint_worker(false) {
8808            return Ok(());
8809        }
8810        self.index_checkpoint_dirty.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
8811        self.start_checkpoint_worker()
8812    }
8813
8814    /// Bound how often a structurally-needed full checkpoint rewrite may run.
8815    ///
8816    /// Both budgets are unlimited at zero, and the pair is *disabled* when both
8817    /// are zero (the default). A rewrite is deferred only while both
8818    /// configured budgets still have headroom; exhausting either forces it.
8819    ///
8820    /// Deferring is safe for durability: packfiles stay authoritative and are
8821    /// still synced first, so this only costs the next open a rescan — the
8822    /// stale on-disk checkpoint (and the delta log, whose tail no longer matches
8823    /// the advanced packs) is rejected by the fingerprint gates. It is the
8824    /// write-neutral fallback when no checkpoint base exists, a legacy v2 log
8825    /// needs rebasing, or a v3 append fails (for example, when its byte cap is
8826    /// exceeded); see `delta_state_needs_full_rewrite` and `checkpoint_skips`.
8827    pub fn set_checkpoint_rewrite_budget(&self, min_interval: std::time::Duration, max_bytes: u64) {
8828        self.checkpoint_rewrite_min_interval_ns.store(
8829            u64::try_from(min_interval.as_nanos()).unwrap_or(u64::MAX),
8830            Ordering::Relaxed,
8831        );
8832        self.checkpoint_rewrite_max_bytes
8833            .store(max_bytes, Ordering::Relaxed);
8834    }
8835
8836    /// Set how many written-but-unsynced pack bytes make a journal-mode sync also
8837    /// fsync the dirty packs; zero disables it and leaves pack fsyncs to the
8838    /// checkpoint. This only schedules fsyncs earlier: coverage still comes from
8839    /// the checkpoint's own fsync of every shard, so it never claims pack data
8840    /// the packs have not made durable.
8841    pub fn set_pack_fsync_budget(&self, bytes: u64) {
8842        self.pack_fsync_budget_bytes.store(bytes, Ordering::Relaxed);
8843    }
8844
8845    /// Set how many unsynced delta-log bytes make a delta batch also fsync the
8846    /// log; zero disables it. Like the pack budget it only schedules an fsync
8847    /// earlier, so a later coverage batch, which is always fsynced, pays for
8848    /// less.
8849    pub fn set_delta_fsync_budget(&self, bytes: u64) {
8850        self.delta_fsync_budget_bytes
8851            .store(bytes, Ordering::Relaxed);
8852    }
8853
8854    /// Route durability through a write-ahead journal at `path`.
8855    ///
8856    /// After this, every mutation (`put`/`put_many`/`delete_collection`) is
8857    /// published to the journal with a monotonic LSN, and `sync` durably
8858    /// commits the pending group as one sequential fsync. Packfile shard
8859    /// fsyncs and the index checkpoint then become acceleration-only: a crash
8860    /// that loses them replays the journal instead of rescanning every pack.
8861    ///
8862    /// This is opt-in and off by default (the store's historical behavior —
8863    /// packfiles are the sync point — is unchanged until it is called).
8864    ///
8865    /// # Errors
8866    /// Returns `StorageError` if the journal segment cannot be opened or its
8867    /// committed prefix cannot be validated.
8868    pub fn enable_journal(&self, path: impl AsRef<std::path::Path>) -> Result<(), StorageError> {
8869        self.reject_per_pool_journal_in_root()?;
8870        let (journal, scan) = Journal::open(path).map_err(StorageError::Io)?;
8871        self.journal_recovery.lock().clone_from(&scan.groups);
8872        *self.journal.lock() = Some(Arc::new(JournalCoordinator::new(journal, &scan)));
8873        Ok(())
8874    }
8875
8876    /// Fail closed when a path-based per-pool journal would be attached to a
8877    /// store that lives inside a database root.
8878    ///
8879    /// Every root is driven by one root-level pool-tagged segment through one
8880    /// coordinator. Letting a caller hand such a pool a private per-pool
8881    /// `wal.bin` would split the durability fence and silently diverge from the
8882    /// root's WAL. A standalone store outside any root keeps the per-pool
8883    /// journal path.
8884    fn reject_per_pool_journal_in_root(&self) -> Result<(), StorageError> {
8885        match crate::layout::enclosing_root(&self.base_dir)? {
8886            Some(root) => Err(StorageError::Internal(format!(
8887                "{} is inside database root {}; attach it to the root coordinator \
8888                 with PackfileStorage::enable_shared_journal instead of a per-pool journal",
8889                self.base_dir.display(),
8890                root.display()
8891            ))),
8892            None => Ok(()),
8893        }
8894    }
8895
8896    /// Route durability through a journal whose group sequence is drawn from a
8897    /// shared, cross-pool counter.
8898    ///
8899    /// Identical to [`Self::enable_journal`] except the coordinator orders its
8900    /// groups by `sequence`, so several pools' segments share one global order
8901    /// (see [`JournalCoordinator::with_shared_sequence`]). The caller
8902    /// initializes `sequence` above the maximum recovered
8903    /// [`Journal::next_sequence`] across the participating segments.
8904    ///
8905    /// # Errors
8906    /// Same as [`Self::enable_journal`].
8907    #[cfg(feature = "multi-reader")]
8908    pub fn enable_journal_with_sequence(
8909        &self,
8910        path: impl AsRef<std::path::Path>,
8911        sequence: Arc<AtomicU64>,
8912    ) -> Result<(), StorageError> {
8913        self.reject_per_pool_journal_in_root()?;
8914        let (journal, scan) = Journal::open(path).map_err(StorageError::Io)?;
8915        self.journal_recovery.lock().clone_from(&scan.groups);
8916        *self.journal.lock() = Some(Arc::new(JournalCoordinator::with_shared_sequence(
8917            journal, &scan, sequence,
8918        )));
8919        Ok(())
8920    }
8921
8922    /// Attach this store to a shared, multi-pool journal coordinator.
8923    ///
8924    /// Every mutation this store publishes is tagged with `pool`, so recovery
8925    /// routes it back to this pool. Because all pools share one coordinator
8926    /// (and therefore one segment), any one pool's `sync`/`sync_all` fences
8927    /// every pool's pending mutations in a single group and a single fsync —
8928    /// instead of each pool paying its own WAL fsync.
8929    ///
8930    /// The coordinator must be built from a pool-tagged segment (see
8931    /// [`Journal::open_shared`]) and the caller must hold the root writer lock
8932    /// ([`crate::journal::SharedWalLock`]). This is opt-in; a store that never
8933    /// calls it keeps the legacy per-pool journal path unchanged.
8934    ///
8935    /// The store's existing durable coverage (the `journal.lsn` written beside
8936    /// its last checkpoint) is reported to the coordinator on attach. Without
8937    /// it, a pool whose frames were reclaimed before a restart has no coverage
8938    /// in the freshly recovered segment, and reclaim could advance past frames
8939    /// this store has not materialized (or block on a pool that is in fact
8940    /// already covered).
8941    ///
8942    /// # Errors
8943    /// Returns `InvalidInput` if a journal is already enabled on this store.
8944    #[cfg(feature = "multi-reader")]
8945    pub fn enable_shared_journal(
8946        &self,
8947        journal: Arc<JournalCoordinator>,
8948        pool: crate::layout::ShardType,
8949    ) -> Result<(), StorageError> {
8950        let mut slot = self.journal.lock();
8951        if slot.is_some() {
8952            return Err(StorageError::Internal(
8953                "a journal is already enabled on this store".into(),
8954            ));
8955        }
8956        self.journal_recovery
8957            .lock()
8958            .clone_from(&journal.recovered_groups());
8959        self.journal_pool.store(pool_tag(pool), Ordering::Release);
8960        journal.report_pool_coverage(pool, self.durable_coverage());
8961        *slot = Some(journal);
8962        Ok(())
8963    }
8964
8965    /// Re-apply the recovered journal's post-checkpoint mutations after a
8966    /// reopen, then dirty the index so the next sync checkpoints them.
8967    ///
8968    /// Only entries with `lsn >` the sidecar's covered LSN are re-applied, so a
8969    /// checkpoint bounds the work. Re-applying a mutation that was already
8970    /// durable in a packfile (because its shard fsync happened to survive) is
8971    /// idempotent on the append-only store: it writes a duplicate frame and
8972    /// repoints the index, and a later repack drops the dead copy.
8973    ///
8974    /// Returns the number of mutations re-applied. No-op (0) when no journal is
8975    /// enabled or nothing is uncovered.
8976    ///
8977    /// # Errors
8978    /// Propagates any write failure from re-applying a mutation.
8979    pub fn replay_journal(&self) -> Result<u64, StorageError> {
8980        if self.journal().is_none() {
8981            return Ok(0);
8982        }
8983        let covered = self.durable_coverage();
8984        let groups = self.journal_recovery.lock().clone();
8985        self.replaying.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
8986        let result = (|| -> Result<u64, StorageError> {
8987            let mut replayed = 0u64;
8988            // On a shared journal, replay only this pool's frames; the other
8989            // pools' mutations are replayed by their own stores.
8990            let pool = pool_from_tag(self.journal_pool.load(Ordering::Acquire));
8991            for group in &groups {
8992                for entry in &group.entries {
8993                    if entry.lsn <= covered {
8994                        continue;
8995                    }
8996                    if pool.is_some_and(|pool| entry.pool != Some(pool)) {
8997                        continue;
8998                    }
8999                    match &entry.mutation {
9000                        JournalMutation::Put {
9001                            collection_id,
9002                            node_id,
9003                            payload,
9004                        } => {
9005                            let data = NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from(payload.clone()));
9006                            self.put(collection_id, node_id, &data)?;
9007                        }
9008                        JournalMutation::DeleteCollection { collection_id } => {
9009                            self.delete_collection(collection_id)?;
9010                        }
9011                    }
9012                    replayed = replayed.saturating_add(1);
9013                }
9014            }
9015            Ok(replayed)
9016        })();
9017        self.replaying.store(false, Ordering::SeqCst);
9018        let replayed = result?;
9019        if replayed > 0 {
9020            self.index_checkpoint_dirty.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
9021        }
9022        Ok(replayed)
9023    }
9024
9025    /// The journal coordinator, if [`Self::enable_journal`] was called.
9026    #[must_use]
9027    pub fn journal(&self) -> Option<Arc<JournalCoordinator>> {
9028        self.journal.lock().clone()
9029    }
9030
9031    /// Start a bounded background WAL group committer on this store's journal.
9032    ///
9033    /// Additive and opt-in: without it the store keeps the historical blocking
9034    /// [`StorageEngine::sync`] behavior. The committer fsyncs the pending WAL
9035    /// group at most once per [`GroupCommitConfig::interval`], coalescing every
9036    /// mutation published in that window into one group, and flushes early once
9037    /// [`GroupCommitConfig::max_pending`] records are outstanding. It commits
9038    /// the journal only; packfile checkpointing and segment reclaim remain the
9039    /// explicit `sync`/`sync_all` path. No-op when no journal is enabled.
9040    ///
9041    /// # Errors
9042    /// Returns a storage error if the committer thread cannot be spawned.
9043    pub fn start_background_commit(&self, config: GroupCommitConfig) -> Result<(), StorageError> {
9044        match self.journal() {
9045            Some(journal) => journal
9046                .start_background_committer(config)
9047                .map_err(StorageError::Io),
9048            None => Ok(()),
9049        }
9050    }
9051
9052    /// Stop the background committer (if any), join it, and flush the final
9053    /// pending WAL group so a quiet stream's last write is durable before this
9054    /// returns. No-op when no journal is enabled.
9055    ///
9056    /// # Errors
9057    /// Returns a storage error if the final flush fails.
9058    pub fn stop_background_commit(&self) -> Result<(), StorageError> {
9059        match self.journal() {
9060            Some(journal) => journal
9061                .stop_background_committer()
9062                .map_err(StorageError::Io),
9063            None => Ok(()),
9064        }
9065    }
9066
9067    /// Register a non-blocking durability request through `target_lsn`,
9068    /// returning `None` when no journal is enabled.
9069    #[must_use]
9070    pub fn request_durable(&self, target_lsn: u64) -> Option<DurabilityToken> {
9071        self.journal()
9072            .map(|journal| journal.request_durable(target_lsn))
9073    }
9074
9075    /// Block until the group covering `token` is durable. No-op when no journal
9076    /// is enabled. Pair with [`Self::request_durable`].
9077    ///
9078    /// # Errors
9079    /// Returns a storage error if the target was never published, the journal
9080    /// is poisoned, the background committer failed, or the commit fails.
9081    pub fn wait_durable(&self, token: DurabilityToken) -> Result<(), StorageError> {
9082        match self.journal() {
9083            Some(journal) => journal
9084                .wait_durable(token)
9085                .map(|_| ())
9086                .map_err(StorageError::Io),
9087            None => Ok(()),
9088        }
9089    }
9090
9091    /// Perform one bounded WAL group commit over everything published so far.
9092    /// No-op when no journal is enabled.
9093    ///
9094    /// # Errors
9095    /// Returns a storage error if appending or fsyncing the group fails.
9096    pub fn flush_durable(&self) -> Result<(), StorageError> {
9097        match self.journal() {
9098            Some(journal) => journal
9099                .flush_durable()
9100                .map(|_| ())
9101                .map_err(StorageError::Io),
9102            None => Ok(()),
9103        }
9104    }
9105
9106    /// Whether ordinary reads must go through the transaction overlay: a
9107    /// transaction is using it, and this read is not the overlay path's own
9108    /// fallback to the live index.
9109    fn overlay_reads_active(&self) -> bool {
9110        self.transaction_overlay_users.load(Ordering::Acquire) != 0
9111            && !READ_COMMITTED_FALLBACK.with(Cell::get)
9112    }
9113
9114    /// Enable the in-process read overlay for a published transaction that is
9115    /// still being materialized. The overlay is shared with the existing
9116    /// read-committed implementation, but ordinary reads consult it only
9117    /// while at least one transaction is in this state.
9118    #[cfg(feature = "multi-reader")]
9119    pub(crate) fn activate_transaction_overlay(
9120        &self,
9121        wal_path: &Path,
9122        pool: crate::layout::ShardType,
9123    ) -> Result<(), StorageError> {
9124        let _lifecycle = self.transaction_overlay_lifecycle.lock();
9125        let previous = self
9126            .transaction_overlay_users
9127            .fetch_add(1, Ordering::AcqRel);
9128        if previous == 0 {
9129            if let Err(error) = self.enable_transaction_read_journal(wal_path, pool) {
9130                self.transaction_overlay_users
9131                    .fetch_sub(1, Ordering::AcqRel);
9132                return Err(error);
9133            }
9134        }
9135        Ok(())
9136    }
9137
9138    /// Whether a journal overlay is installed on the read path.
9139    #[cfg(all(test, feature = "multi-reader"))]
9140    pub(crate) fn read_journal_installed(&self) -> bool {
9141        self.read_journal.lock().is_some()
9142    }
9143
9144    /// Total segment bytes the retained transaction overlay has scanned.
9145    #[cfg(all(test, feature = "multi-reader"))]
9146    pub(crate) fn transaction_overlay_scanned_bytes(&self) -> u64 {
9147        self.transaction_overlay_scanned.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
9148    }
9149
9150    /// Stop consulting the in-process transaction overlay after all staged
9151    /// mutations have been materialized or the transaction was abandoned
9152    /// before journal publication.
9153    #[cfg(feature = "multi-reader")]
9154    pub(crate) fn deactivate_transaction_overlay(&self) {
9155        let _lifecycle = self.transaction_overlay_lifecycle.lock();
9156        let mut users = self.transaction_overlay_users.load(Ordering::Acquire);
9157        loop {
9158            let next = users
9159                .checked_sub(1)
9160                .expect("transaction overlay deactivated too often");
9161            match self.transaction_overlay_users.compare_exchange_weak(
9162                users,
9163                next,
9164                Ordering::AcqRel,
9165                Ordering::Acquire,
9166            ) {
9167                Ok(_) => break,
9168                Err(current) => users = current,
9169            }
9170        }
9171        if users == 1 {
9172            self.park_transaction_overlay();
9173        }
9174    }
9175
9176    /// Publish one mutation to the journal, if enabled. Returns the assigned
9177    /// LSN, or `None` when no journal is configured.
9178    ///
9179    /// `mutation` is a closure so its payload (a full record copy) is only
9180    /// built when a journal is actually configured.
9181    fn publish_mutation(
9182        &self,
9183        mutation: impl FnOnce() -> JournalMutation,
9184    ) -> Result<Option<u64>, StorageError> {
9185        let started = std::time::Instant::now();
9186        if JOURNAL_SUPPRESSED.with(Cell::get) {
9187            return Ok(None);
9188        }
9189        let Some(journal) = self.journal() else {
9190            self.record_published_mutation(started);
9191            return Ok(None);
9192        };
9193        // Replayed mutations are already durable in the journal; never
9194        // re-publish them.
9195        if self.replaying.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
9196            return Ok(None);
9197        }
9198        // The live index is already updated synchronously on the write path.
9199        // Append this autocommit mutation as its own complete, visible group;
9200        // durability remains separate so the background committer can batch
9201        // several such groups into one fsync. On a shared journal, tag the
9202        // frame with this store's pool so recovery can route it.
9203        #[cfg(feature = "multi-reader")]
9204        let result = match pool_from_tag(self.journal_pool.load(Ordering::Acquire)) {
9205            Some(pool) => journal
9206                .publish_group_tagged(pool, &[mutation()])
9207                .map(|receipt| receipt.last_lsn),
9208            None => journal
9209                .publish_group(&[mutation()])
9210                .map(|receipt| receipt.last_lsn),
9211        }
9212        .map(Some)
9213        .map_err(StorageError::Io);
9214        #[cfg(not(feature = "multi-reader"))]
9215        let result = journal
9216            .publish_group(&[mutation()])
9217            .map(|receipt| receipt.last_lsn)
9218            .map(Some)
9219            .map_err(StorageError::Io);
9220        if result.is_ok() {
9221            self.record_published_mutation(started);
9222        }
9223        result
9224    }
9225
9226    /// Apply a mutation staged by a database transaction without publishing
9227    /// it to the legacy per-write journal queue. The transaction coordinator
9228    /// publishes the complete batch after every pool has applied successfully.
9229    #[cfg(feature = "multi-reader")]
9230    pub(crate) fn apply_transaction_mutation(
9231        &self,
9232        mutation: &JournalMutation,
9233    ) -> Result<(), StorageError> {
9234        JOURNAL_SUPPRESSED.with(|suppressed| {
9235            let previous = suppressed.replace(true);
9236            let result = match mutation {
9237                JournalMutation::Put {
9238                    collection_id,
9239                    node_id,
9240                    payload,
9241                } => self.put(
9242                    collection_id,
9243                    node_id,
9244                    &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from(payload.clone())),
9245                ),
9246                JournalMutation::DeleteCollection { collection_id } => {
9247                    self.delete_collection(collection_id)
9248                }
9249            };
9250            suppressed.set(previous);
9251            result
9252        })
9253    }
9254
9255    fn record_published_mutation(&self, started: std::time::Instant) {
9256        self.publish_calls.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
9257        self.publish_time_ns.fetch_add(
9258            u64::try_from(started.elapsed().as_nanos()).unwrap_or(u64::MAX),
9259            Ordering::Relaxed,
9260        );
9261        let mut pending = self.pending_publish_since.lock();
9262        if pending.is_none() {
9263            *pending = Some(std::time::Instant::now());
9264        }
9265        self.publish_generation.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Release);
9266    }
9267
9268    /// Advance one barrier's durability boundary.
9269    ///
9270    /// With a journal enabled, that boundary is the pending WAL group: flush
9271    /// buffered frames to the page cache, then commit the group as one
9272    /// sequential fsync. Packfile shard fsyncs and the index checkpoint are
9273    /// then acceleration-only and recovered from the journal on reopen.
9274    /// Without a journal, behaves as before (fsync the dirty shards, or every
9275    /// shard for `sync_all`).
9276    fn sync_durability(
9277        &self,
9278        dirty_only: bool,
9279        timings: &mut SyncTimings,
9280    ) -> Result<(), StorageError> {
9281        let dirty_lock_before = self.shards.dirty_lock_wait();
9282        if let Some(journal) = self.journal() {
9283            let flush_started = std::time::Instant::now();
9284            self.shards.flush_all()?;
9285            timings.pack_flush = flush_started.elapsed();
9286            let target = journal.capture_sync_target();
9287            let wal_started = std::time::Instant::now();
9288            let (_, journal_timings) = journal
9289                .sync_through_timed(target)
9290                .map_err(StorageError::Io)?;
9291            timings.wal = wal_started.elapsed();
9292            timings.journal_lock_wait = journal_timings.journal_lock_wait;
9293            timings.journal_fsync = journal_timings.journal_fsync;
9294            timings.journal_sync_calls = 1;
9295            timings.journal_records = journal_timings.journal_records;
9296            timings.journal_waiters = u64::from(journal_timings.journal_waiter);
9297            timings.journal_coalesced = u64::from(journal_timings.journal_coalesced);
9298            timings.journal_in_flight = journal_timings.journal_in_flight;
9299            // The WAL is durable, so the packs are only owed for the checkpoint.
9300            // Pay that in slices, outside every collection lock, once enough has
9301            // accumulated, instead of all at once at the checkpoint.
9302            let budget = self.pack_fsync_budget_bytes.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
9303            if budget != 0 && self.shards.unsynced_bytes() >= budget {
9304                self.shards.sync_dirty()?;
9305                if let Some((_, fsync)) = self.shards.last_sync_split() {
9306                    timings.pack_fsync = fsync;
9307                }
9308            }
9309        } else if dirty_only {
9310            self.shards.sync_dirty()?;
9311            if let Some((flush, fsync)) = self.shards.last_sync_split() {
9312                timings.pack_flush = flush;
9313                timings.pack_fsync = fsync;
9314            }
9315        } else {
9316            self.shards.sync_all()?;
9317            if let Some((flush, fsync)) = self.shards.last_sync_split() {
9318                timings.pack_flush = flush;
9319                timings.pack_fsync = fsync;
9320            }
9321        }
9322        timings.dirty_lock_wait = self
9323            .shards
9324            .dirty_lock_wait()
9325            .saturating_sub(dirty_lock_before);
9326        Ok(())
9327    }
9328
9329    /// Batch-granular sync accounting: every sync counts once, and the
9330    /// checkpoint-vs-delta discriminator comes from which phase
9331    /// `persist_index_checkpoint_or_delta` actually ran (a non-dirty sync runs
9332    /// neither). `sync` (dirty-scoped) and `sync_all` both funnel through here,
9333    /// so this is also the single point that folds each barrier's phase
9334    /// breakdown into the lifetime `sync_totals`.
9335    fn count_sync_persistence(&self, timings: &SyncTimings) {
9336        self.sync_calls.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
9337        self.sync_totals.accumulate(timings);
9338        if !timings.checkpoint.is_zero() {
9339            self.checkpoint_writes.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
9340        } else if !timings.delta_log.is_zero() {
9341            self.delta_appends.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
9342        }
9343    }
9344
9345    fn record_sync_diagnostics(&self, timings: &SyncTimings) {
9346        let journal_path = self
9347            .journal()
9348            .map(|journal| journal.path().display().to_string());
9349        let timestamp_ms = std::time::SystemTime::now()
9350            .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
9351            .map_or(0, |duration| duration.as_millis());
9352        self.sync_diagnostics.lock().record(SyncDiagnosticSample {
9353            timestamp_ms,
9354            process_id: std::process::id(),
9355            journal_path,
9356            total: timings.total,
9357            failed: timings.failed,
9358            pack_flush: timings.pack_flush,
9359            pack_fsync: timings.pack_fsync,
9360            sidecar: timings.sidecar,
9361            delta_log: timings.delta_log,
9362            checkpoint: timings.checkpoint,
9363            dirty_lock_wait: timings.dirty_lock_wait,
9364            pending_publish_age: timings.pending_publish_age,
9365            wal: timings.wal,
9366            journal_lock_wait: timings.journal_lock_wait,
9367            journal_fsync: timings.journal_fsync,
9368            journal_records: timings.journal_records,
9369            journal_in_flight: timings.journal_in_flight,
9370            journal_waiters: timings.journal_waiters,
9371            journal_coalesced: timings.journal_coalesced,
9372        });
9373    }
9374
9375    fn mark_sync_pending_age(&self, timings: &mut SyncTimings) -> u64 {
9376        let generation = self.publish_generation.load(Ordering::Acquire);
9377        if let Some(since) = *self.pending_publish_since.lock() {
9378            timings.pending_publish_age = since.elapsed();
9379        }
9380        generation
9381    }
9382
9383    fn finish_sync_pending_age(&self, generation: u64) {
9384        if self.publish_generation.load(Ordering::Acquire) == generation {
9385            *self.pending_publish_since.lock() = None;
9386        }
9387    }
9388    /// `put_bytes + put_many_bytes` written since the last full checkpoint
9389    /// rewrite — the size dimension of the rewrite budget.
9390    fn written_bytes_since_last_rewrite(&self) -> u64 {
9391        self.put_bytes
9392            .load(Ordering::Relaxed)
9393            .saturating_add(self.put_many_bytes.load(Ordering::Relaxed))
9394            .saturating_sub(
9395                self.checkpoint_bytes_at_last_rewrite
9396                    .load(Ordering::Relaxed),
9397            )
9398    }
9399
9400    /// Whether a structurally-needed full checkpoint rewrite should be deferred
9401    /// under the configured time/size budget.
9402    ///
9403    /// Both budgets are unlimited at zero. A zero/zero budget (the default)
9404    /// never defers, preserving the historical behavior of rewriting on every
9405    /// invalidated dirty barrier. With one budget configured, deferral is gated
9406    /// on that one alone; with both, a rewrite runs as soon as either headroom
9407    /// runs out.
9408    fn should_defer_checkpoint_rewrite(&self) -> bool {
9409        let interval = std::time::Duration::from_nanos(
9410            self.checkpoint_rewrite_min_interval_ns
9411                .load(Ordering::Relaxed),
9412        );
9413        let max_bytes = self.checkpoint_rewrite_max_bytes.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
9414        if interval.is_zero() && max_bytes == 0 {
9415            return false;
9416        }
9417        let time_headroom = interval.is_zero()
9418            || self
9419                .last_checkpoint_rewrite_at
9420                .lock()
9421                .as_ref()
9422                .is_some_and(|last| last.elapsed() < interval);
9423        let size_headroom = max_bytes == 0 || self.written_bytes_since_last_rewrite() < max_bytes;
9424        time_headroom && size_headroom
9425    }
9426
9427    /// Record that a full checkpoint rewrite just completed, resetting both
9428    /// budget baselines to now and the current write counter.
9429    fn note_checkpoint_rewrite(&self) {
9430        *self.last_checkpoint_rewrite_at.lock() = Some(std::time::Instant::now());
9431        self.checkpoint_bytes_at_last_rewrite.store(
9432            self.put_bytes
9433                .load(Ordering::Relaxed)
9434                .saturating_add(self.put_many_bytes.load(Ordering::Relaxed)),
9435            Ordering::Relaxed,
9436        );
9437    }
9438
9439    /// Whether pending state needs a full checkpoint rather than a v3 delta
9440    /// append. Missing bases, legacy v2 epochs, or no pending operations need
9441    /// a checkpoint; oversized v3 batches fall back from the append helper.
9442    fn delta_state_needs_full_rewrite(&self) -> bool {
9443        let state = self.delta_state.lock();
9444        state.base_fingerprint.is_none() || state.log_version != 3 || state.pending.is_empty()
9445    }
9446
9447    /// Tell the journal this pool's packs durably cover its frames through
9448    /// `lsn`, and reclaim what that lets go of. Best-effort: a failed
9449    /// compaction costs disk, never correctness (the coverage is already
9450    /// durable).
9451    fn report_coverage_and_reclaim(&self, lsn: u64) -> Option<crate::journal::Reclaim> {
9452        let journal = self.journal()?;
9453        report_coverage_and_reclaim_via(&journal, self.journal_pool.load(Ordering::Acquire), lsn)
9454    }
9455
9456    /// After a sync (no lock held): if a shared-WAL reclaim is stalled in the
9457    /// emergency zone, make the pools holding it back checkpoint. Which pools,
9458    /// and how, is decided by the coordinator and whoever owns the pools.
9459    fn remediate_lagging_pools(&self) {
9460        #[cfg(feature = "multi-reader")]
9461        if let Some(journal) = self.journal() {
9462            journal.remediate_blockers(pool_from_tag(self.journal_pool.load(Ordering::Acquire)));
9463        }
9464        #[cfg(not(feature = "multi-reader"))]
9465        let _ = self;
9466    }
9467
9468    /// Whether this sync must take a full checkpoint so the journal can be
9469    /// reclaimed: the segment is large, and this pool has journal frames its
9470    /// last checkpoint does not yet cover. A pool with nothing new to cover
9471    /// gains nothing from a rewrite and never holds the segment back, since its
9472    /// earlier coverage is already reported.
9473    fn journal_needs_reclaim_checkpoint(&self) -> bool {
9474        let Some(journal) = self.journal() else {
9475            return false;
9476        };
9477        #[cfg(feature = "multi-reader")]
9478        let this_pool = pool_from_tag(self.journal_pool.load(Ordering::Acquire));
9479        #[cfg(not(feature = "multi-reader"))]
9480        let this_pool = None;
9481        if !journal.should_force_reclaim_checkpoint(this_pool) {
9482            return false;
9483        }
9484        #[cfg(feature = "multi-reader")]
9485        if let Some(pool) = pool_from_tag(self.journal_pool.load(Ordering::Acquire)) {
9486            return journal.committed_lsn_for_pool(pool) > self.durable_coverage();
9487        }
9488        true
9489    }
9490
9491    /// Whether a delta log continues the checkpoint this session is based on, so
9492    /// a batch can be appended to it (pending operations or not).
9493    fn delta_base_is_usable(&self) -> bool {
9494        let state = self.delta_state.lock();
9495        state.base_fingerprint.is_some() && state.log_version == 3
9496    }
9497
9498    /// The delta-log size limit: the real cap, or a test's smaller one.
9499    fn delta_log_cap(&self) -> u64 {
9500        #[cfg(test)]
9501        {
9502            let limit = self.delta_log_cap_override.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
9503            if limit != 0 {
9504                return limit;
9505            }
9506        }
9507        let _ = self;
9508        DELTA_LOG_CAP_BYTES
9509    }
9510
9511    /// Log length at which a sync rewrites the checkpoint instead of appending:
9512    /// three quarters of [`Self::delta_log_cap`].
9513    fn delta_log_rotate_bytes(&self) -> u64 {
9514        self.delta_log_cap().saturating_div(4).saturating_mul(3)
9515    }
9516
9517    /// The details of `error` if it is a delta batch that does not fit under the
9518    /// cap. That is a planned rotation, not a failure: the batch may carry
9519    /// whole-index snapshots, so it is refused by its projected length.
9520    fn delta_batch_too_large(error: &StorageError) -> Option<&DeltaBatchTooLarge> {
9521        match error {
9522            StorageError::Io(io) => io
9523                .get_ref()
9524                .and_then(|inner| inner.downcast_ref::<DeltaBatchTooLarge>()),
9525            _ => None,
9526        }
9527    }
9528
9529    /// Whether every live pack is one the base checkpoint's pack table names,
9530    /// so every slot a delta operation of this epoch carries resolves through
9531    /// that table for any reader. A pack created since forces a full
9532    /// checkpoint, which records the new table.
9533    fn packs_match_checkpoint_table(&self) -> bool {
9534        let state = self.delta_state.lock();
9535        !state.base_pack_ids.is_empty()
9536            && self
9537                .shards
9538                .all_shards()
9539                .iter()
9540                .all(|(_, shard)| state.base_pack_ids.contains(&shard.pack_id))
9541    }
9542
9543    /// Persist the dirty index state for a sync barrier — a delta append when
9544    /// the log can be continued, otherwise a full checkpoint rewrite — and
9545    /// record which path ran in `timings`. No-op when nothing is dirty.
9546    ///
9547    /// The shard→collection inspection sidecar is deferred away from the
9548    /// per-event durable barrier: a delta append and a deferred checkpoint
9549    /// rewrite only set `shard_collections_stale`, leaving the on-disk copy
9550    /// (and its pack fingerprint) behind the live pack set. That is safe
9551    /// because the sidecar is rebuildable acceleration metadata — the next open
9552    /// fails its fingerprint gate and falls back to the slot walk — so the hot
9553    /// barrier never pays its `sync_data` + rename. The sidecar is re-pinned
9554    /// only at anchors: a successful full checkpoint rewrite (to the same pack
9555    /// fingerprint the checkpoint just became), a repack, or shutdown (`Drop`).
9556    /// A known missing/invalid sidecar (`shard_collections_dirty`) is still
9557    /// regenerated even on an otherwise clean barrier, because that is a rare
9558    /// recovery path rather than a steady-state write.
9559    fn persist_index_checkpoint_or_delta(&self, timings: &mut SyncTimings) {
9560        let _persist_guard = self.index_persist_lock.lock();
9561        if !self.settle_checkpoint_worker() {
9562            return;
9563        }
9564        // A delta append does not advance the journal coverage, so on its own it
9565        // never lets the segment shrink and the journal would fill to its hard
9566        // limit. Once the segment is large, a pool with journal frames its
9567        // checkpoint does not yet cover takes the full checkpoint (which records
9568        // coverage and reclaims), even if its index is clean; a shared segment is
9569        // only reclaimed once every such pool has reported.
9570        let journal_needs_reclaim = self.journal_needs_reclaim_checkpoint();
9571        if journal_needs_reclaim {
9572            self.index_checkpoint_dirty.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
9573        }
9574        if !self.index_checkpoint_dirty.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
9575            // Nothing to checkpoint, but a sidecar lost while the checkpoint
9576            // survived still has to be regenerated. A sidecar that is merely
9577            // stale from deferred writes is left for the next anchor.
9578            if self.shard_collections_dirty.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
9579                let sidecar_started = std::time::Instant::now();
9580                self.persist_shard_collections_best_effort();
9581                timings.sidecar = sidecar_started.elapsed();
9582            }
9583            return;
9584        }
9585        // Only a full checkpoint rewrite re-pins the sidecar to the pack
9586        // fingerprint the checkpoint just became. Every other dirty path
9587        // records staleness instead and writes nothing.
9588        let mut sidecar_anchor = false;
9589        // When the journal must be reclaimed and a delta log can continue the
9590        // checkpoint, record the coverage in a delta batch instead of rewriting
9591        // the whole index: the packs are made durable, then the batch carrying
9592        // the claim is, and only then is the journal reclaimed.
9593        let mut coverage_batch_written = false;
9594        let log_bytes = self.delta_state.lock().log_bytes;
9595        let rotating = log_bytes >= self.delta_log_rotate_bytes();
9596        if rotating {
9597            eprintln!(
9598                "mtxdb: delta log is at {log_bytes} of {} bytes, rewriting the checkpoint \
9599                 before it reaches the cap",
9600                self.delta_log_cap()
9601            );
9602        }
9603        if journal_needs_reclaim
9604            && !rotating
9605            && self.delta_base_is_usable()
9606            && self.packs_match_checkpoint_table()
9607        {
9608            let delta_started = std::time::Instant::now();
9609            match self.append_index_delta_v3(true) {
9610                Ok(Some(covered)) => {
9611                    timings.delta_log = delta_started.elapsed();
9612                    let reclaim_started = std::time::Instant::now();
9613                    let reclaim = self.report_coverage_and_reclaim(covered);
9614                    timings.reclaim = reclaim_started.elapsed();
9615                    timings.record_reclaim_phases(reclaim.as_ref());
9616                    coverage_batch_written = true;
9617                }
9618                Ok(None) => {}
9619                Err(error) if Self::delta_batch_too_large(&error).is_some() => {
9620                    if let Some(detail) = Self::delta_batch_too_large(&error) {
9621                        eprintln!(
9622                            "mtxdb: rotating the delta log: {detail}; rewriting the checkpoint"
9623                        );
9624                    }
9625                }
9626                Err(error) => {
9627                    eprintln!("mtxdb: delta coverage batch failed, rewriting checkpoint: {error}");
9628                }
9629            }
9630        }
9631        if coverage_batch_written {
9632            // Like any delta append: the sidecar is merely stale, unless it is
9633            // known missing.
9634            if self.shard_collections_dirty.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
9635                sidecar_anchor = true;
9636            } else {
9637                self.shard_collections_stale.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
9638            }
9639        } else if journal_needs_reclaim || rotating || self.delta_state_needs_full_rewrite() {
9640            // A deferral budget postpones acceleration rewrites; it must not
9641            // postpone the one that lets the journal be reclaimed, or the segment
9642            // fills and commits fail, nor the one that keeps the delta log under
9643            // its cap.
9644            if !journal_needs_reclaim && !rotating && self.should_defer_checkpoint_rewrite() {
9645                // Write-neutral stopgap: the caller already synced the
9646                // packfiles, so skipping the acceleration rewrite costs only
9647                // the next open a rescan — the stale on-disk checkpoint no
9648                // longer matches the advanced pack fingerprint, and the delta
9649                // log's tail does not either, so the opener rejects both. Leave
9650                // `index_checkpoint_dirty` set so a later barrier past the
9651                // budget still rewrites.
9652                self.checkpoint_skips.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
9653                self.shard_collections_stale.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
9654                return;
9655            }
9656            let checkpoint_started = std::time::Instant::now();
9657            self.persist_index_checkpoint_for_sync();
9658            self.note_checkpoint_rewrite();
9659            timings.checkpoint = checkpoint_started.elapsed();
9660            sidecar_anchor = true;
9661        } else {
9662            let delta_started = std::time::Instant::now();
9663            if let Err(error) = self.append_index_delta() {
9664                // An append failure took the frames with it, so the pending state
9665                // no longer reflects the live indexes. Fall back to a full
9666                // rewrite rather than leaving the acceleration files stale until
9667                // the next sync notices the gap.
9668                if let Some(detail) = Self::delta_batch_too_large(&error) {
9669                    eprintln!("mtxdb: rotating the delta log: {detail}; rewriting the checkpoint");
9670                } else {
9671                    eprintln!("mtxdb: delta log append failed, rewriting checkpoint: {error}");
9672                }
9673                let checkpoint_started = std::time::Instant::now();
9674                self.persist_index_checkpoint_for_sync();
9675                self.note_checkpoint_rewrite();
9676                timings.checkpoint = checkpoint_started.elapsed();
9677                sidecar_anchor = true;
9678            } else {
9679                timings.delta_log = delta_started.elapsed();
9680                // A missing/invalid sidecar must still be regenerated, but a
9681                // normal delta append defers it: the on-disk copy is merely
9682                // stale and the next open rebuilds it from the slot walk.
9683                if self.shard_collections_dirty.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
9684                    sidecar_anchor = true;
9685                } else {
9686                    self.shard_collections_stale.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
9687                }
9688            }
9689        }
9690        if sidecar_anchor {
9691            let sidecar_started = std::time::Instant::now();
9692            self.persist_shard_collections_best_effort();
9693            timings.sidecar = sidecar_started.elapsed();
9694        }
9695    }

9697    /// Fingerprint of the current on-disk pack set, computed from each
9698    /// shard's committed length. Must be called after the flush that made the
9699    /// bytes corresponding to outstanding index frames durable, so the file
9700    /// lengths reflect exactly what the indexes' offsets point at.
9701    fn current_pack_fingerprint(&self) -> u64 {
9702        let packs: Vec<(u64, u64)> = self
9703            .shards
9704            .all_shards()
9705            .into_iter()
9706            .map(|(_, shard)| (shard.pack_id, shard.file_len()))
9707            .collect();
9708        crate::index::checkpoint::pack_fingerprint(&packs)
9709    }

9712    /// which index-loading path was taken. Set at construction; every store
9713    /// returned by a `PackfileStorage::open*` constructor carries it.

9716        *self.last_open_timings.lock()
9717    }

9720    /// or the bench's internal sync calls — by phase.
9721    #[must_use]
9722    pub fn sync_timings(&self) -> Option<SyncTimings> {
9723        *self.last_sync_timings.lock()
9724    }

9728    pub fn checkpoint_breakdown(&self) -> Option<CheckpointBreakdown> {

9732    /// Commit every open shard's buffered frames to the page cache without
9733    /// fsyncing (see [`ShardPool::flush_all`]). No-op under the default
9734    /// [`crate::shard::AppendPolicy::Eager`], where every put already wrote
9735    /// its own frame.
9736    ///
9737    /// Under [`crate::shard::AppendPolicy::Buffered`], a put's bytes live
9738    /// only in process memory until a flush, and only in the page cache
9739    /// until a `sync_all`. This is the explicit way to advance that boundary
9740    /// for all shards. A flushed store also means a subsequent
9741    /// `PackfileStorage::open`/`open_read_only` against the same directory
9742    /// sees the data.
9743    ///
9744    /// # Errors
9745    /// Returns `StorageError` on I/O failure.
9746    pub fn flush_all(&self) -> Result<(), StorageError> {
9747        Ok(self.shards.flush_all()?)
9748    }
9749
9750    /// Replace this store's append policy — whether frames go to disk per
9751    /// put (the default [`crate::shard::AppendPolicy::Eager`], historical
9752    /// behavior) or accumulate for one positioned write per flush
9753    /// ([`crate::shard::AppendPolicy::Buffered`]). See
9754    /// [`crate::shard::AppendPolicy`] for the visibility/durability trade.
9755    ///
9756    /// Only affects future puts, so call it before the store starts handling
9757    /// concurrent writes. For a batch import that ends in `sync_all` — or a
9758    /// benchmark that syncs explicitly — `Buffered` usually wins:
9759    ///
9760    /// ```
9761    /// use mtxdb::shard::AppendPolicy;
9762    /// use mtxdb::PackfileStorage;
9763    /// # let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("mtxdb-doc-with-append-policy-{}", std::process::id()));
9764    /// let store = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone())
9765    ///     .unwrap()
9766    ///     .with_append_policy(AppendPolicy::buffered());
9767    /// # std::fs::remove_dir_all(dir).ok();
9768    /// ```
9769    #[must_use]
9770    pub fn with_append_policy(mut self, policy: shard::AppendPolicy) -> Self {
9771        self.shards.set_append_policy(policy);
9772        self
9773    }
9774
9775    /// Best-effort, rate-limited flush of the shard→collection directory for a
9776    /// writer's own periodic tick — same contract as
9777    /// `ShardPool::maybe_persist_stats`: a no-op if called again before
9778    /// `min_interval` has passed since the last flush from here.
9779    pub fn maybe_persist_shard_collections(&self, min_interval: std::time::Duration) {
9780        let now = std::time::Instant::now();
9781        {
9782            let mut last = self.last_shard_collections_flush.write();
9783            if last.is_some_and(|prev| now.duration_since(prev) < min_interval) {
9784                return;
9785            }
9786            *last = Some(now);
9787        }
9788        self.persist_shard_collections_best_effort();
9789    }

9834    /// Opt in to the logical read-path counters (`get`/`get_many`). Read
9835    /// counters are off by default so the read hot path pays a single relaxed
9836    /// load per logical read at most (never a per-record `fetch_add`); write,
9837    /// batch, and sync counters are always on regardless.
9838    ///
9839    /// Changing the flag is safe at any point and affects only subsequent
9840    /// operations; logical read counters are monotone, so reads disabled by a
9841    /// false-to-true transition are reflected as fewer `get_*` calls, not as
9842    /// zeros.
9843    /// When enabled, it also records wall-clock totals and fixed latency
9844    /// buckets plus maxima for `get`, `get_many`, `get_many_with_refresh`,
9845    /// `put`, and `put_many` in [`Self::stats`].
9846    pub fn set_stats_enabled(&self, enabled: bool) {
9847        self.stats_enabled.store(enabled, Ordering::Relaxed);
9848    }
9849
9850    /// Set whether [`Self::get_many_with_refresh`] refreshes a collection's
9851    /// index when the caller's in-memory snapshot misses. Defaults to `true`
9852    /// (multi-process readers). A single writer -- whose in-memory index is
9853    /// authoritative for everything it has written -- sets this `false` so a
9854    /// negative lookup degrades to a plain [`StorageEngine::get_many`] and
9855    /// never touches the refresh lock or the durable fingerprint. See the
9856    /// `refresh_on_miss` field docs.
9857    pub fn set_refresh_on_miss(&self, enabled: bool) {
9858        self.refresh_on_miss.store(enabled, Ordering::Relaxed);
9859    }
9860
9861    /// Point-in-time snapshot of this store's runtime counters, plus the
9862    /// always-persisted pool stats embedded alongside them ([`RepackStats`],
9863    /// aggregate [`CacheStats`], per-shard `ShardStats`, index bytes).
9864    ///
9865    /// The logical read counters reflect only reads performed while stats were
9866    /// enabled ([`Self::set_stats_enabled`]); all other counters are lifetime
9867    /// totals since the store was assembled. See [`Self::reset_stats`] for the
9868    /// reset semantics — `shards`/`cache`/`repack` reflect persisted state and
9869    /// are deliberately excluded from the reset.
9870    #[must_use]
9871    #[allow(
9872        clippy::cast_precision_loss,
9873        reason = "a hit-rate is inherently an approximate floating-point presentation; counters retain their exact u64 values"
9874    )]
9875    pub fn stats(&self) -> RuntimeStats {
9876        let mut cache = CacheStats::default();
9877        let mut index_bytes: u64 = 0;
9878        let summaries = self.collection_summaries();
9879        for summary in &summaries {
9880            index_bytes = index_bytes.saturating_add(u64::try_from(summary.2).unwrap_or(u64::MAX));
9881            if let Some(stats) = self.cache_stats_for(&summary.0) {
9882                cache.hits = cache.hits.saturating_add(stats.hits);
9883                cache.misses = cache.misses.saturating_add(stats.misses);
9884            }
9885        }
9886        // Longest linear-probe chain observed across every live collection's
9887        // index, for operator visibility into collision-chain growth (see
9888        // `LossyIndex::max_probe_len` — pure observability, no cap, no
9889        // effect on control flow).
9890        let max_index_probe_len = self
9891            .collections_read()
9892            .values()
9893            .map(|generation| generation.load().index.max_probe_len())
9894            .max()
9895            .unwrap_or(0);
9896        let cache_accesses = cache.hits.saturating_add(cache.misses);
9897        cache.hit_rate = if cache_accesses > 0 {
9898            cache.hits as f64 / cache_accesses as f64
9899        } else {
9900            0.0
9901        };
9902        RuntimeStats {
9903            open_count: self.open_count.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
9904            get_calls: self.get_calls.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
9905            get_misses: self.get_misses.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
9906            get_many_calls: self.get_many_calls.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
9907            get_many_records: self.get_many_records.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
9908            get_many_misses: self.get_many_misses.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
9909            miss_refreshes: self.miss_refreshes.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
9910            miss_refresh_skips: self.miss_refresh_skips.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
9911            miss_refresh_recovered: self.miss_refresh_recovered.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
9912            miss_refresh_retry_ids: self.miss_refresh_retry_ids.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
9913            miss_refresh_fp_errors: self.miss_refresh_fp_errors.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
9914            index_candidates: self.index_candidates.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
9915            candidate_reads: self.candidate_reads.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
9916            candidate_hash_mismatches: self.candidate_hash_mismatches.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
9917            get_many_shards_touched: self.get_many_shards_touched.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
9918            candidate_frame_bytes: self.candidate_frame_bytes.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
9919            read_many_runs: self.read_many_runs.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
9920            read_many_span_bytes: self.read_many_span_bytes.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
9921            read_plan_extents: self.read_plan_extents.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
9922            read_plan_prefetch_bytes: self.read_plan_prefetch_bytes.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
9923            read_plan_skipped_extents: self.read_plan_skipped_extents.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
9924            put_calls: self.put_calls.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
9925            put_bytes: self.put_bytes.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
9926            put_many_calls: self.put_many_calls.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
9927            put_many_records: self.put_many_records.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
9928            put_many_bytes: self.put_many_bytes.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
9929            put_many_fast_path_calls: self.put_many_fast_path_calls.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
9930            put_many_clone_path_calls: self.put_many_clone_path_calls.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
9931            index_clone_time: std::time::Duration::from_nanos(
9932                self.index_clone_time_ns.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
9933            ),
9934            index_grow_count: self.index_grow_count.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
9935            index_rebuild_count: self.index_rebuild_count.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
9936            delta_invalidations: self.delta_invalidations.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
9937            checkpoint_writes: self.checkpoint_writes.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
9938            checkpoint_tails_started: self.checkpoint_tails_started.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
9939            syncs_with_tail_in_flight: self.syncs_with_tail_in_flight.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
9940            syncs_waited_for_tail: self.syncs_waited_for_tail.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
9941            checkpoint_skips: self.checkpoint_skips.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
9942            delta_appends: self.delta_appends.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
9943            read_reloads: self.read_reloads.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
9944            read_reload_failures: self.read_reload_failures.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
9945            sidecar_writes: self.sidecar_writes.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
9946            sync_calls: self.sync_calls.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
9947            get_latency: self.operation_timings.get.snapshot(),
9948            get_many_latency: self.operation_timings.get_many.snapshot(),
9949            get_many_with_refresh_latency: self.operation_timings.get_many_with_refresh.snapshot(),
9950            put_latency: self.operation_timings.put.snapshot(),
9951            put_many_latency: self.operation_timings.put_many.snapshot(),
9952            last_open_timings: self.open_timings(),
9953            last_sync_timings: self.sync_timings(),
9954            sync_totals: self.sync_totals.snapshot(),
9955            sync_diagnostics: self.sync_diagnostics.lock().snapshot(),
9956            publish_calls: self.publish_calls.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
9957            publish_time: std::time::Duration::from_nanos(
9958                self.publish_time_ns.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
9959            ),
9960            background_commits: self
9961                .journal()
9962                .map_or(0, |journal| journal.background_commits()),
9963            background_coalesced: self
9964                .journal()
9965                .map_or(0, |journal| journal.background_coalesced()),
9966            durability: self
9967                .journal()
9968                .map_or_else(Default::default, |journal| journal.durability_stats()),
9969            repack: self.repack_stats(),
9970            cache,
9971            shards: self.shard_stats(),
9972            index_bytes,
9973            collection_count: summaries.len(),
9974            max_index_probe_len,
9975            dirty_lock_wait: self.shards.dirty_lock_wait(),
9976        }
9977    }
9978
9979    /// Atomically take the current sync diagnostics and reset only those
9980    /// diagnostics for the next observation interval.
9981    ///
9982    /// Unlike [`Self::reset_stats`], this leaves all runtime counters and
9983    /// cumulative sync totals untouched. The returned histograms, peak
9984    /// in-flight count, interval maxima (`max_journal_lock_wait` and
9985    /// `max_journal_fsync`), and worst-operation samples therefore describe
9986    /// the interval ending at this call; the interval maxima reset to zero
9987    /// alongside the histograms. Syncs racing with the call are recorded in
9988    /// either the returned snapshot or the next interval, never partially in
9989    /// both.
9990    #[must_use]
9991    pub fn take_sync_diagnostics(&self) -> SyncDiagnosticsSnapshot {
9992        let mut diagnostics = self.sync_diagnostics.lock();
9993        let snapshot = diagnostics.snapshot();
9994        diagnostics.reset();
9995        snapshot
9996    }
9997
9998    /// Zero every runtime counter except `open_count` (counts stores
9999    /// assembled, not work) and the persisted pool stats — `shards`,
10000    /// `cache`, `repack`, `index_bytes`, and the collection count reflect
10001    /// on-disk state plus this process's decoded-cache and repack history and
10002    /// are kept as-is so a reset means "restart the runtime accounting," not
10003    /// "lie about the database."
10004    ///
10005    /// Also clears the retained `last_open_timings`/`last_sync_timings`
10006    /// breakdowns and the lifetime `sync_totals` accumulator, and leaves the
10007    /// `stats_enabled` flag untouched.
10008    pub fn reset_stats(&self) {
10009        for counter in [
10010            &self.get_calls,
10011            &self.get_misses,
10012            &self.get_many_calls,
10013            &self.get_many_records,
10014            &self.get_many_misses,
10015            &self.miss_refreshes,
10016            &self.miss_refresh_skips,
10017            &self.miss_refresh_recovered,
10018            &self.miss_refresh_retry_ids,
10019            &self.miss_refresh_fp_errors,
10020            &self.index_candidates,
10021            &self.candidate_reads,
10022            &self.candidate_hash_mismatches,
10023            &self.get_many_shards_touched,
10024            &self.candidate_frame_bytes,
10025            &self.read_many_runs,
10026            &self.read_many_span_bytes,
10027            &self.read_plan_extents,
10028            &self.read_plan_prefetch_bytes,
10029            &self.read_plan_skipped_extents,
10030            &self.put_calls,
10031            &self.put_bytes,
10032            &self.put_many_calls,
10033            &self.put_many_records,
10034            &self.put_many_bytes,
10035            &self.put_many_fast_path_calls,
10036            &self.put_many_clone_path_calls,
10037            &self.index_clone_time_ns,
10038            &self.index_grow_count,
10039            &self.index_rebuild_count,
10040            &self.delta_invalidations,
10041            &self.checkpoint_writes,
10042            &self.checkpoint_skips,
10043            &self.delta_appends,
10044            &self.read_reloads,
10045            &self.read_reload_failures,
10046            &self.sidecar_writes,
10047            &self.sync_calls,
10048        ] {
10049            counter.store(0, Ordering::Relaxed);
10050        }
10051        self.operation_timings.reset();
10052        *self.last_open_timings.lock() = None;
10053        *self.last_sync_timings.lock() = None;
10054        self.sync_totals.reset();
10055        self.sync_diagnostics.lock().reset();
10056    }

10104/// Point-in-time snapshot of a store's runtime counters and the persisted
10105/// pool stats embedded alongside them — see [`PackfileStorage::stats`].
10106///
10107/// All fields are relaxed reads of independent atomics (no shared snapshot
10108/// lock), so a snapshot is a consistent-enough picture, not a single instant
10109/// in time. The read-path counters (`get_*`) are only meaningful while
10110/// [`PackfileStorage::set_stats_enabled`] was true.
10111#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
10112pub struct RuntimeStats {
10113    /// Stores assembled in this process against this directory (1 for a fresh
10114    /// open; not reset by `reset_stats`).
10115    pub open_count: u64,
10116    /// Logical `get` calls (while stats enabled).
10117    pub get_calls: u64,
10118    /// Logical `get` calls that resolved to no record.
10119    pub get_misses: u64,
10120    /// Logical `get_many` calls (while stats enabled).
