10284/// Flush a dirty/stale shard→collection sidecar on shutdown so a clean exit
10285/// leaves the sidecar pinned to the last *durable* pack set.
10286///
10287/// This covers state that a completed `sync`/`sync_all` left deferred (a delta
10288/// append or a budget-deferred checkpoint rewrite set `shard_collections_stale`)
10289/// plus a sidecar lost at open (`shard_collections_dirty`). It deliberately
10290/// does **not** flush bookkeeping changed by writes that were never synced:
10291/// such a write grows a pack past the last checkpoint, so the next open cannot
10292/// take the checkpoint fast path at all and full-scans instead — it never
10293/// consults the sidecar. Writing one there would be unownable I/O, so the
10294/// narrower contract is the correct one.
10295///
10296/// Best-effort and gated: a read-only handle never sets either flag, and any
10297/// write error is swallowed by the best-effort wrapper. Even skipping the flush
10298/// entirely is safe — the sidecar is rebuildable acceleration metadata — so
10299/// correctness never depends on `Drop`.
10300/// [`PackfileStorage::write_journal_lsn`] on owned handles, for the tail.
10301fn write_journal_lsn_file(
10302    base_dir: &Path,
10303    durable_coverage: &AtomicU64,
10304    lsn: u64,
10305) -> Result<(), StorageError> {
10306    let path = PackfileStorage::journal_lsn_path(base_dir);
10307    let tmp = path.with_extension("lsn.tmp");
10308    fs::write(&tmp, lsn.to_le_bytes()).map_err(StorageError::Io)?;
10309    // Windows requires a write-capable handle for FlushFileBuffers,
10310    // which is what `sync_all` uses. A read-only handle works on Unix
10311    // but fails with ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED on Windows.
10312    fs::OpenOptions::new()
10313        .read(true)
10314        .write(true)
10315        .open(&tmp)
10316        .and_then(|file| file.sync_all())
10317        .map_err(StorageError::Io)?;
10318    fs::rename(&tmp, &path).map_err(StorageError::Io)?;
10319    let _ = crate::shard::sync_directory(base_dir);
10320    durable_coverage.fetch_max(lsn, Ordering::AcqRel);
10321    Ok(())
10322}
10323
10324/// Remove the superseded delta-log epoch once the checkpoint that makes it safe
10325/// to discard is durably renamed. Best-effort: a leftover file names a
10326/// fingerprint no future checkpoint carries, so it is inert.
10327fn retire_delta_epoch_file(base_dir: &Path, old_base_fingerprint: Option<u64>) {
10328    let Some(old_base_fingerprint) = old_base_fingerprint else {
10329        return;
10330    };
10331    let path = PackfileStorage::delta_path(base_dir, old_base_fingerprint);
10332    if fs::remove_file(&path).is_ok() {
10333        // The checkpoint rename's own durability is already covered by the
10334        // directory fsync after `write_checkpoint`; this one covers the unlink,
10335        // so the retired file does not linger past a crash.
10336        let _ = crate::shard::sync_directory(base_dir);
10337    }
10338}
10339
10340/// Tell the journal a pool's packs durably cover its frames through `lsn`, and
10341/// reclaim what that lets go of. `tag` is the pool's journal tag.
10342/// Report this pool's durable coverage and reclaim the journal, returning the
10343/// reclaim's phase breakdown when one ran (for the sync-path timings).
10344fn report_coverage_and_reclaim_via(
10345    journal: &JournalCoordinator,
10346    tag: u8,
10347    lsn: u64,
10348) -> Option<crate::journal::Reclaim> {
10349    match pool_from_tag(tag) {
10350        // A per-pool segment holds only this pool's frames, so this coverage
10351        // means the segment can drop everything at or below `lsn`.
10352        None => match journal.reclaim_through(lsn) {
10353            Ok(reclaim) => Some(reclaim),
10354            Err(error) => {
10355                eprintln!("warning: journal reclaim through LSN {lsn} failed: {error}");
10356                None
10357            }
10358        },
10359        // A shared segment also holds other pools' frames. Record this pool's
10360        // coverage and reclaim only what every contributing pool has covered.
10361        #[cfg(feature = "multi-reader")]
10362        Some(pool) => {
10363            journal.report_pool_coverage(pool, lsn);
10364            match journal.reclaim_shared() {
10365                Ok(reclaim) => reclaim,
10366                Err(error) => {
10367                    eprintln!("warning: shared journal reclaim failed: {error}");
10368                    None
10369                }
10370            }
10371        }
10372        #[cfg(not(feature = "multi-reader"))]
10373        Some(_) => unreachable!("shared journal state requires multi-reader"),
10374    }
10375}

10377/// Everything a checkpoint needs after the handoff, owned so it can run on any
10378/// thread. Built under the locks by [`PackfileStorage::capture_checkpoint`]:
10379/// the image is the captured bytes, never the live table, and the delta epoch
10380/// has already been rotated. Running it writes and fsyncs the image, installs
10381/// it, records the coverage it carries, reclaims the WAL and retires the old
10382/// epoch, in that order; the WAL is not touched until the image is durable.
10383struct CheckpointTail {
10384    base_dir: PathBuf,
10385    fingerprint: u64,
10386    covered_lsn: Option<u64>,
10387    base_delta_seq: u64,
10388    blobs: Vec<([u8; 16], u64, Vec<u8>)>,
10389    pack_table: Vec<(u16, u64)>,
10390    old_base_fingerprint: Option<u64>,
10391    journal: Option<Arc<JournalCoordinator>>,
10392    pool_tag: u8,
10393    durable_coverage: Arc<AtomicU64>,
10394    #[cfg(test)]
10395    hook: Option<TailHook>,
10396}
10397
10398/// Test-only control over a checkpoint tail: it waits for `gate` to be
10399/// released (or dropped), then fails if `fail` is set.
10400#[cfg(test)]
10401struct TailHook {
10402    gate: std::sync::mpsc::Receiver<()>,
10403    fail: bool,
10404}
10405
10406impl CheckpointTail {
10407    /// Run the tail; the returned breakdown holds only the phases it ran.
10408    fn run(self) -> Result<CheckpointBreakdown, StorageError> {
10409        #[cfg(test)]
10410        if let Some(hook) = &self.hook {
10411            let _ = hook.gate.recv();
10412            if hook.fail {
10413                return Err(StorageError::Io(std::io::Error::other(
10414                    "injected checkpoint tail failure",
10415                )));
10416            }
10417        }
10418        let tail_started = std::time::Instant::now();
10419        let mut done = CheckpointBreakdown::default();
10420        let path = PackfileStorage::index_checkpoint_path(&self.base_dir);
10421        let write_started = std::time::Instant::now();
10422        let blobs: Vec<([u8; 16], u64, &[u8])> = self
10423            .blobs
10424            .iter()
10425            .map(|(collection_id, generation, blob)| (*collection_id, *generation, blob.as_slice()))
10426            .collect();
10427        crate::index::checkpoint::write_checkpoint(
10428            &path,
10429            self.fingerprint,
10430            self.covered_lsn.unwrap_or(0),
10431            self.base_delta_seq,
10432            &blobs,
10433            &self.pack_table,
10434        )
10435        .map_err(StorageError::Io)?;
10436        done.write = write_started.elapsed();
10437        done.checkpoint_bytes = fs::metadata(&path).map_or(0, |meta| meta.len());
10438        // The rename is only durable once the directory is synced. Best-effort:
10439        // a crash before it either observes the rename or falls back to the
10440        // still-valid predecessor checkpoint, never a torn one.
10441        let directory_started = std::time::Instant::now();
10442        let _ = crate::shard::sync_directory(&self.base_dir);
10443        done.directory_sync = directory_started.elapsed();
10444        // The image is durable; record the LSN it covers so a reopen replays only
10445        // what follows, and let the journal drop what the packs now cover. The
10446        // pack fsync happened before the handoff, so everything through the LSN
10447        // is durable in the packs. A failed compaction costs disk, not
10448        // correctness.
10449        if let (Some(journal), Some(lsn)) = (&self.journal, self.covered_lsn) {
10450            let lsn_started = std::time::Instant::now();
10451            write_journal_lsn_file(&self.base_dir, &self.durable_coverage, lsn)?;
10452            done.journal_lsn = lsn_started.elapsed();
10453            let reclaim_started = std::time::Instant::now();
10454            let _ = report_coverage_and_reclaim_via(journal, self.pool_tag, lsn);
10455            done.reclaim = reclaim_started.elapsed();
10456        }
10457        let retire_started = std::time::Instant::now();
10458        retire_delta_epoch_file(&self.base_dir, self.old_base_fingerprint);
10459        done.retire = retire_started.elapsed();
10460        done.total = tail_started.elapsed();
10461        Ok(done)
10462    }
10463}
10464
10465/// A checkpoint captured under the locks, ready for its tail.
10466struct CapturedCheckpoint {
10467    tail: CheckpointTail,
10468    breakdown: CheckpointBreakdown,
10469}

10471/// A tail running on its own thread, with the capture's phase timings.
10472struct CheckpointWorker {
10473    handle: std::thread::JoinHandle<Result<CheckpointBreakdown, StorageError>>,
10474    breakdown: CheckpointBreakdown,
10475}
10476
10477impl Drop for PackfileStorage {
10478    fn drop(&mut self) {
10479        self.finish_checkpoint_worker(true);
10480        if self.shard_collections_dirty.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
10481            || self.shard_collections_stale.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
10482        {
10483            self.persist_shard_collections_best_effort();
10484        }
10485    }
10486}

10558#[cfg(test)]
10559thread_local! {
10560    /// Test-only hook run by `get`/`get_many` after candidate shard ids are
10561    /// collected but before they are pinned, allowing deterministic repack
10562    /// interleavings in the read-path race tests.
10563    static TEST_BEFORE_PIN: std::cell::RefCell<Option<Box<dyn Fn()>>> =
10564        std::cell::RefCell::new(None);
10565}
10566
10567#[cfg(test)]
10568impl PackfileStorage {
10569    fn set_test_before_pin(hook: Option<Box<dyn Fn()>>) {
10570        TEST_BEFORE_PIN.with(|slot| *slot.borrow_mut() = hook);
10571    }
10572
10573    fn run_test_before_pin() {
10574        TEST_BEFORE_PIN.with(|slot| {
10575            if let Some(hook) = slot.borrow().as_ref() {
10576                hook();
10577            }
10578        });
10579    }
10580}

10582#[cfg(test)]
10583#[cfg_attr(coverage_nightly, coverage(off))]
10584mod tests {
10585    use super::*;
10586    use std::time::Duration;
10587
10588    const TEST_COLLECTION: [u8; 16] = [0x01; 16];
10589    const SECOND_COLLECTION: [u8; 16] = [0x02; 16];
10590
10591    /// A node id distinct across both the bucket bytes (0..8) and tag bytes
10592    /// (8..12) the lossy index actually reads — an id that only varies byte
10593    /// 0 collapses every entry onto the same 24-bit tag, which is not a
10594    /// realistic content hash and defeats the index in ways unrelated to
10595    /// whatever a test using it is meant to check.
10596    fn distinct_id(byte: u8) -> [u8; 16] {
10597        let mut id = [0u8; 16];
10598        id[0] = byte;
10599        id[9] = byte.wrapping_mul(37).wrapping_add(11);
10600        id[15] = byte.wrapping_mul(7);
10601        id
10602    }
10603    const OTHER_COLLECTION: [u8; 16] = [0x02; 16];
10604
10605    fn test_dir(name: &str) -> PathBuf {
10606        use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};
10607        static COUNTER: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);
10608        let id = COUNTER.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
10609        let dir =
10610            std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("mdb_test_pfs_{name}_{}_{id}", std::process::id()));
10611        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
10612        fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
10613        dir
10614    }
10615
10616    #[cfg(feature = "multi-reader")]
10617    #[test]
10618    fn read_committed_overlay_sees_a_committed_but_unflushed_group() {
10619        let dir = test_dir("read_committed_unflushed");
10620        let wal = dir.join("wal.bin");
10621        let collection = [0x42u8; 16];
10622        let node = [0x07u8; 16];
10623
10624        // A read-only open needs at least one shard on disk, so seed a
10625        // durable record first.
10626        let seed = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
10627        seed.put(
10628            &[0x99u8; 16],
10629            &[0x99u8; 16],
10630            &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"seed")),
10631        )
10632        .unwrap();
10633        seed.sync().unwrap();
10634        drop(seed);
10635
10636        // A complete group (trailer present) with no fsync: committed, but
10637        // invisible to the durable fingerprint gate.
10638        let (mut journal, _) = Journal::open(&wal).unwrap();
10639        journal
10640            .append_group(&[JournalMutation::Put {
10641                collection_id: collection,
10642                node_id: node,
10643                payload: b"committed-unflushed".to_vec(),
10644            }])
10645            .unwrap();
10646        drop(journal);
10647
10648        let store = PackfileStorage::open_read_only(dir.clone()).unwrap();
10649        store.enable_read_journal(&wal).unwrap();
10650
10651        let read_committed = store.get_read_committed(&collection, &[node]).unwrap();
10652        assert_eq!(
10653            read_committed[0].as_ref().map(|data| data.bytes.as_ref()),
10654            Some(&b"committed-unflushed"[..])
10655        );
10656
10657        // The durable API still hides the unflushed group.
10658        let durable = store.get_many_with_refresh(&collection, &[node]).unwrap();
10659        assert!(
10660            durable[0].is_none(),
10661            "durable read must not observe an unflushed journal group"
10662        );
10663    }
10664
10665    /// Journal state for a writer-restart scenario: LSN 1 is durable and LSN 2
10666    /// is visible but never reached the disk. Returns the segment length that
10667    /// covers only LSN 1, so a test can cut the file back to what a crash would
10668    /// have kept.
10669    #[cfg(feature = "multi-reader")]
10670    fn journal_with_a_visible_but_undurable_group(
10671        wal: &std::path::Path,
10672        collection: [u8; 16],
10673        stable: [u8; 16],
10674        reused: [u8; 16],
10675    ) -> u64 {
10676        let (mut journal, _) = Journal::open(wal).unwrap();
10677        journal
10678            .commit_group(&[JournalMutation::Put {
10679                collection_id: collection,
10680                node_id: stable,
10681                payload: b"stable".to_vec(),
10682            }])
10683            .unwrap();
10684        let durable_len = std::fs::metadata(wal).unwrap().len();
10685        journal
10686            .append_group(&[JournalMutation::Put {
10687                collection_id: collection,
10688                node_id: reused,
10689                payload: b"stale-".to_vec(),
10690            }])
10691            .unwrap();
10692        durable_len
10693    }
10694
10695    /// A read-only store with a live reader journal that has already applied a
10696    /// visible-but-undurable group (`stale-` at the `reused` id, collection
10697    /// `0x42`), for the restarted-writer tests. Returns the
10698    /// journal path, the store and the journal's durable length.
10699    #[cfg(feature = "multi-reader")]
10700    fn reader_over_an_undurable_group(name: &str) -> (PathBuf, PackfileStorage, u64) {
10701        let dir = test_dir(name);
10702        let wal = dir.join("wal.bin");
10703        let collection = [0x42u8; 16];
10704        let stable = [0x01u8; 16];
10705        let reused = [0x02u8; 16];
10706        let seed = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
10707        seed.put(
10708            &[0x99u8; 16],
10709            &[0x99u8; 16],
10710            &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"seed")),
10711        )
10712        .unwrap();
10713        seed.sync().unwrap();
10714        drop(seed);
10715        let durable_len =
10716            journal_with_a_visible_but_undurable_group(&wal, collection, stable, reused);
10717        let store = PackfileStorage::open_read_only(dir.clone()).unwrap();
10718        store.enable_read_journal(&wal).unwrap();
10719        let before_restart = store.get_read_committed(&collection, &[reused]).unwrap();
10720        assert_eq!(
10721            before_restart[0].as_ref().map(|data| data.bytes.as_ref()),
10722            Some(&b"stale-"[..])
10723        );
10724        (wal, store, durable_len)
10725    }
10726
10727    /// A writer that crashes loses its visible-but-undurable tail, and the
10728    /// restarted writer reuses those LSNs. A live reader that already applied
10729    /// the lost group must not keep serving it. The reissued group has the same
10730    /// length, so the file is exactly as long as when the reader last scanned.
10731    #[cfg(feature = "multi-reader")]
10732    #[test]
10733    fn read_committed_overlay_drops_a_group_the_restarted_writer_discarded() {
10734        let (wal, store, durable_len) =
10735            reader_over_an_undurable_group("read_committed_writer_restart_same_len");
10736        let collection = [0x42u8; 16];
10737        let reused = [0x02u8; 16];
10738
10739        // The crash: LSN 2 never reached the disk. The restarted writer
10740        // recovers LSN 1 and publishes a different LSN 2 of the same length.
10741        std::fs::OpenOptions::new()
10742            .write(true)
10743            .open(&wal)
10744            .unwrap()
10745            .set_len(durable_len)
10746            .unwrap();
10747        let (mut journal, scan) = Journal::open(&wal).unwrap();
10748        assert_eq!(scan.groups.len(), 1);
10749        journal
10750            .append_group(&[JournalMutation::Put {
10751                collection_id: collection,
10752                node_id: reused,
10753                payload: b"fresh-".to_vec(),
10754            }])
10755            .unwrap();
10756        drop(journal);
10757
10758        let after = store.get_read_committed(&collection, &[reused]).unwrap();
10759        assert_eq!(
10760            after[0].as_ref().map(|data| data.bytes.as_ref()),
10761            Some(&b"fresh-"[..]),
10762            "the reader must not keep the group the restarted writer discarded"
10763        );
10764    }
10765
10766    /// Same restart, but the reissued LSN 2 is followed by an LSN 3, so the file
10767    /// has grown and the reader takes its incremental-scan path.
10768    #[cfg(feature = "multi-reader")]
10769    #[test]
10770    fn read_committed_overlay_drops_a_discarded_group_when_the_file_grew() {
10771        let (wal, store, durable_len) =
10772            reader_over_an_undurable_group("read_committed_writer_restart_grew");
10773        let collection = [0x42u8; 16];
10774        let reused = [0x02u8; 16];
10775        let later = [0x03u8; 16];
10776
10777        std::fs::OpenOptions::new()
10778            .write(true)
10779            .open(&wal)
10780            .unwrap()
10781            .set_len(durable_len)
10782            .unwrap();
10783        let (mut journal, _) = Journal::open(&wal).unwrap();
10784        for (node, payload) in [(reused, &b"fresh-"[..]), (later, &b"after-"[..])] {
10785            journal
10786                .append_group(&[JournalMutation::Put {
10787                    collection_id: collection,
10788                    node_id: node,
10789                    payload: payload.to_vec(),
10790                }])
10791                .unwrap();
10792        }
10793        drop(journal);
10794
10795        let after = store
10796            .get_read_committed(&collection, &[reused, later])
10797            .unwrap();
10798        assert_eq!(
10799            after[0].as_ref().map(|data| data.bytes.as_ref()),
10800            Some(&b"fresh-"[..]),
10801            "the reissued LSN must replace the discarded group's content"
10802        );
10803        assert_eq!(
10804            after[1].as_ref().map(|data| data.bytes.as_ref()),
10805            Some(&b"after-"[..])
10806        );
10807    }

10996    #[test]
10997    fn read_committed_overlay_fails_closed_when_reclaim_skips_its_covered_lsn() {
10998        let dir = test_dir("read_committed_reclaim_gap");
10999        let wal = dir.join("wal.bin");
11000        let collection = [0x48u8; 16];
11001        let node = [0x0fu8; 16];
11002
11003        let seed = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
11004        seed.put(
11005            &[0x95u8; 16],
11006            &[0x95u8; 16],
11007            &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"seed")),
11008        )
11009        .unwrap();
11010        seed.sync().unwrap();
11011        drop(seed);
11012
11013        let (mut journal, _) = Journal::open(&wal).unwrap();
11014        journal
11015            .append_group(&[JournalMutation::Put {
11016                collection_id: collection,
11017                node_id: node,
11018                payload: b"first".to_vec(),
11019            }])
11020            .unwrap();
11021        journal
11022            .append_group(&[JournalMutation::Put {
11023                collection_id: collection,
11024                node_id: [0x10u8; 16],
11025                payload: b"second".to_vec(),
11026            }])
11027            .unwrap();
11028        drop(journal);
11029
11030        let store = PackfileStorage::open_read_only(dir.clone()).unwrap();
11031        store.enable_read_journal(&wal).unwrap();
11032
11033        // Reclaim drops LSN 1, so the segment now begins at LSN 2 while the
11034        // reader's index only incorporated coverage 0. Those records are in
11035        // neither source, so the read must fail closed rather than serve a gap.
11036        let (mut journal, _) = Journal::open(&wal).unwrap();
11037        journal.reclaim_through(1).unwrap();
11038        drop(journal);
11039
11040        assert!(
11041            store.get_read_committed(&collection, &[node]).is_err(),
11042            "a reclaimed segment base beyond the reader's covered LSN must error"
11043        );

11147    #[cfg(feature = "multi-reader")]
11148    #[test]
11149    fn read_committed_overlay_reloads_after_reclaim_advances_coverage() {
11150        let dir = test_dir("read_committed_reclaim_reload");
11151        let wal = dir.join("wal.bin");
11152        let collection = [0x49u8; 16];
11153        let first = [0x11u8; 16];
11154        let second = [0x12u8; 16];
11155
11156        // Durable seed, then an empty journal segment the reader can attach to.
11157        let seed = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
11158        seed.put(
11159            &[0x94u8; 16],
11160            &[0x94u8; 16],
11161            &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"seed")),
11162        )
11163        .unwrap();
11164        seed.sync().unwrap();
11165        drop(seed);
11166        let (journal, _) = Journal::open(&wal).unwrap();
11167        drop(journal);
11168
11169        // Reader attaches with the pre-advance index (coverage 0).
11170        let store = PackfileStorage::open_read_only(dir.clone()).unwrap();
11171        store.enable_read_journal(&wal).unwrap();
11172
11173        // Remove the seed checkpoint so the writer's sync must write a full
11174        // checkpoint instead of appending to its existing delta log. A delta
11175        // append extends the loaded index but does not advance checkpoint
11176        // coverage; this test specifically needs a checkpoint that covers LSN 1.
11177        fs::remove_file(PackfileStorage::index_checkpoint_path(&dir)).unwrap();
11178
11179        // A real writer checkpoints `first` and reclaims through its LSN, so the
11180        // checkpoint embeds coverage 1 and its index contains `first`.
11181        let writer = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
11182        writer.enable_journal(&wal).unwrap();
11183        writer
11184            .put(
11185                &collection,
11186                &first,
11187                &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"first")),
11188            )
11189            .unwrap();
11190        writer.sync().unwrap();
11191
11192        let checkpoint = crate::index::checkpoint::read_checkpoint(
11193            &PackfileStorage::index_checkpoint_path(&dir),
11194        )
11195        .unwrap();
11196        assert_eq!(checkpoint.covered_lsn, 1);
11197        let after_checkpoint = Journal::scan_read_only(&wal).unwrap();
11198        assert!(after_checkpoint.base_lsn > checkpoint.covered_lsn);
11199
11200        // Append a new record after the checkpoint, then sync the writer. The
11201        // sync commits its journal group and extends the checkpoint's delta
11202        // log without rewriting the checkpoint. Reload must accept that delta
11203        // tail despite the live pack having grown.
11204        writer
11205            .put(
11206                &collection,
11207                &second,
11208                &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"second")),
11209            )
11210            .unwrap();
11211        writer.sync().unwrap();
11212
11213        let read_committed = store
11214            .get_read_committed(&collection, &[first, second])
11215            .unwrap();
11216        assert_eq!(store.read_covered_lsn.load(Ordering::Acquire), 1);
11217        assert!(
11218            store.stats().read_reloads >= 1,
11219            "the reclaim must have driven at least one checkpoint-bound reload"
11220        );
11221        assert_eq!(
11222            read_committed[0].as_ref().map(|data| data.bytes.as_ref()),
11223            Some(&b"first"[..]),
11224            "the reloaded checkpoint index must serve the covered record, not a hole"
11225        );
11226        assert_eq!(
11227            read_committed[1].as_ref().map(|data| data.bytes.as_ref()),
11228            Some(&b"second"[..]),
11229            "the post-checkpoint group must be served from the overlay"
11230        );
11231    }

11234    #[test]
11235    fn read_committed_reload_skips_the_exact_pack_gate() {
11236        let dir = test_dir("read_committed_reload_skip_gate");
11237        let wal = dir.join("wal.bin");
11238        let collection = [0x4Bu8; 16];
11239        let first = [0x31u8; 16];
11240        let second = [0x32u8; 16];
11241        let third = [0x33u8; 16];
11242
11243        // Durable seed, then an empty segment the reader can attach to.
11244        let seed = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
11245        seed.put(
11246            &[0x97u8; 16],
11247            &[0x97u8; 16],
11248            &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"seed")),
11249        )
11250        .unwrap();
11251        seed.sync().unwrap();
11252        drop(seed);
11253        let (journal, _) = Journal::open(&wal).unwrap();
11254        drop(journal);
11255
11256        let store = PackfileStorage::open_read_only(dir.clone()).unwrap();
11257        store.enable_read_journal(&wal).unwrap();
11258
11259        // Force the writer's next sync to write a full checkpoint so coverage
11260        // advances and the segment is reclaimed through it.
11261        fs::remove_file(PackfileStorage::index_checkpoint_path(&dir)).unwrap();
11262        let writer = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
11263        writer.enable_journal(&wal).unwrap();
11264        writer
11265            .put(
11266                &collection,
11267                &first,
11268                &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"first")),
11269            )
11270            .unwrap();
11271        writer.sync().unwrap();
11272        let checkpoint = crate::index::checkpoint::read_checkpoint(
11273            &PackfileStorage::index_checkpoint_path(&dir),
11274        )
11275        .unwrap();
11276        assert_eq!(checkpoint.covered_lsn, 1);
11277
11278        // A synced second record extends the delta log.
11279        writer
11280            .put(
11281                &collection,
11282                &second,
11283                &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"second")),
11284            )
11285            .unwrap();
11286        writer.sync().unwrap();
11287
11288        // A third record is appended (eagerly) but never synced, so the live
11289        // packs grow past the delta log's tail. An exact-pack gate would reject
11290        // the checkpoint here and fail the read closed; the read-journal reload
11291        // must skip that gate and let the overlay supply the suffix.
11292        writer
11293            .put(
11294                &collection,
11295                &third,
11296                &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"third")),
11297            )
11298            .unwrap();
11299
11300        // The relaxation is scoped to the read-journal reload: a normal open
11301        // runs `ReloadMode::Strict` and must still reject the checkpoint the
11302        // eager append has outgrown, falling back to a full rescan rather than
11303        // trusting a stale fingerprint.
11304        let strict_reader = PackfileStorage::open_read_only(dir.clone()).unwrap();
11305        assert_eq!(
11306            strict_reader.open_timings().unwrap().path,
11307            OpenPath::FullScan,
11308            "a strict open must not accept a checkpoint the live packs have outgrown"
11309        );
11310
11311        let read_committed = store
11312            .get_read_committed(&collection, &[first, second, third])
11313            .unwrap();
11314        assert!(
11315            store.stats().read_reloads >= 1,
11316            "the reclaim must have driven the read-journal reload path"
11317        );
11318        for (value, expected) in read_committed
11319            .iter()
11320            .zip([&b"first"[..], b"second", b"third"])
11321        {
11322            assert_eq!(
11323                value.as_ref().map(|data| data.bytes.as_ref()),
11324                Some(expected),
11325                "every committed record must be visible after a gated reload"
11326            );
11327        }
11328    }

11330    #[cfg(feature = "multi-reader")]
11331    #[test]
11332    fn repack_persists_checkpoint_so_read_journal_reload_survives_retirement() {
11333        // Repack moves a collection's records into a fresh destination shard
11334        // and retires the old one once nothing else references it. A reader
11335        // reloading from the checkpoint afterward must see the new shard
11336        // layout — otherwise it reloads a checkpoint whose index still names
11337        // a shard repack already unlinked, and the read fails closed.
11338        let dir = test_dir("repack_persists_checkpoint");
11339        let wal = dir.join("wal.bin");
11340        let collection = [0x51u8; 16];
11341        let node = [0x61u8; 16];
11342
11343        // `collection` is the only collection in this store, so its shard is
11344        // never shared with anything else: repack's retirement of the
11345        // now-empty source shard actually unlinks the file, rather than
11346        // leaving it alive because another collection still references it.
11347        let writer = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
11348        writer.enable_journal(&wal).unwrap();
11349        writer
11350            .put(
11351                &collection,
11352                &node,
11353                &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"first")),
11354            )
11355            .unwrap();
11356        writer.sync().unwrap();
11357        let before = crate::index::checkpoint::read_checkpoint(
11358            &PackfileStorage::index_checkpoint_path(&dir),
11359        )
11360        .unwrap();
11361        assert_eq!(before.covered_lsn, 1);
11362
11363        // Repack `collection`: it moves `node` into a fresh non-source shard
11364        // and, since no other collection references the old one, retires
11365        // (unlinks) it.
11366        writer
11367            .repack_collection_reachable(&collection, |_hash, _data| Vec::new())
11368            .unwrap();
11369
11370        let after = crate::index::checkpoint::read_checkpoint(
11371            &PackfileStorage::index_checkpoint_path(&dir),
11372        )
11373        .unwrap();
11374        assert_eq!(
11375            after.covered_lsn, before.covered_lsn,
11376            "repack must carry the checkpoint's covered_lsn forward unchanged, not reset it"
11377        );
11378
11379        // Open a reader only now, after retirement already unlinked the
11380        // source shard: it must never hold an open handle to the retired
11381        // file, or the read would trivially keep succeeding through the
11382        // stale-but-still-open fd (Linux keeps an unlinked file's bytes
11383        // readable through any fd opened before the unlink) and the test
11384        // would not actually exercise the checkpoint staleness at all.
11385        let store = PackfileStorage::open_read_only(dir.clone()).unwrap();
11386        store.enable_read_journal(&wal).unwrap();
11387
11388        // Drive the checkpoint reload directly rather than through
11389        // get_read_committed: the journal overlay can serve a still-covered
11390        // record straight from its segment without ever touching the index,
11391        // which would leave this test unable to distinguish a correct reload
11392        // from a mismatched one. reload_index_from_checkpoint is what
11393        // discovers the live shard set and must succeed against the
11394        // checkpoint repack just wrote.
11395        assert!(
11396            store.reload_index_from_checkpoint(),
11397            "reload must succeed against the checkpoint repack persisted, not a stale one \
11398             naming a shard repack already unlinked"
11399        );
11400    }

11404    fn repack_persisted_checkpoint_reload_resolves_record_by_post_repack_offset() {
11405        let dir = test_dir("repack_persists_checkpoint_read");
11406        let wal = dir.join("wal.bin");
11407        let collection = [0x51u8; 16];
11408        let node = [0x61u8; 16];
11409
11410        let writer = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
11411        writer.enable_journal(&wal).unwrap();
11412        writer
11413            .put(
11414                &collection,

11417            )
11418            .unwrap();
11419        writer.sync().unwrap();
11420        writer
11421            .repack_collection_reachable(&collection, |_hash, _data| Vec::new())
11422            .unwrap();
11423

11425        store.enable_read_journal(&wal).unwrap();

11436    /// Coverage for a post-repack delta epoch over *existing* pack identities:
11437    /// a delta written after repack's fresh checkpoint must replay for a cold
11438    /// reader and resolve through the checkpoint's v6 pack table, not the
11439    /// reader's own shard numbering.
11440    ///
11441    /// `repack_collection_reachable` persists a checkpoint (C1) naming the
11442    /// post-retirement pack set, so the pre-retirement delta epoch is retired
11443    /// with it. A later `sync_all` appends a fresh epoch continuing C1; this
11444    /// test pins that a cold open *replays* that epoch (nonzero `delta_replay`,
11445    /// not a checkpoint rewrite that already included `third`) and returns all
11446    /// three records.
11447    ///
11448    /// `third` must be durably synced, not merely shard-flushed: only a sync
11449    /// persists the index. An uncommitted record is invisible to checkpoint
11450    /// replay and recoverable only by a fallback full scan — a different
11451    /// property, and the one the previous version of this test accidentally
11452    /// measured.
11453    ///
11454    /// Out of scope: a delta frame referencing a pack created *after* C1 (a
11455    /// pack absent from C1's pack table), and any claim that a delta-side
11456    /// `SlotBinding` is unnecessary.
11457    #[cfg(feature = "multi-reader")]
11458    #[test]
11459    fn post_repack_delta_epoch_replays_for_a_cold_reader() {
11460        let dir = test_dir("delta_across_retirement");
11461        let wal = dir.join("wal.bin");
11462        let collection = [0x71u8; 16];
11463        let first = [0x81u8; 16];
11464        let second = [0x82u8; 16];
11465        let third = [0x83u8; 16];
11466
11467        let writer = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
11468        writer.enable_journal(&wal).unwrap();
11469
11470        // Commit enough that a checkpoint lands and rotates the delta epoch.
11471        writer
11472            .put(
11473                &collection,
11474                &first,
11475                &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"first")),
11476            )
11477            .unwrap();
11478        writer.sync().unwrap();
11479
11480        // A post-checkpoint write leaves a delta epoch whose base is the
11481        // current checkpoint and whose tail names the current pack set.
11482        writer
11483            .put(
11484                &collection,
11485                &second,
11486                &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"second")),
11487            )
11488            .unwrap();
11489        writer.sync_all().unwrap();
11490
11491        // Repack moves the collection's records into a fresh destination shard
11492        // and unlinks the source. The writer's slot table now has a hole, so a
11493        // fresh reader's `discover_shards` will not reproduce the writer's
11494        // numbering. Repack persists a checkpoint for the new layout.
11495        writer
11496            .repack_collection_reachable(&collection, |_hash, _data| Vec::new())
11497            .unwrap();
11498
11499        // Commit `third` into the delta epoch continuing the post-repack
11500        // checkpoint. A shard flush alone would not persist the index.
11501        writer
11502            .put(
11503                &collection,
11504                &third,
11505                &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"third")),
11506            )
11507            .unwrap();
11508        writer.sync_all().unwrap();
11509        drop(writer);
11510
11511        let reader = PackfileStorage::open_read_only(dir.clone()).unwrap();
11512        reader.enable_read_journal(&wal).unwrap();
11513
11514        let timings = reader
11515            .stats()
11516            .last_open_timings
11517            .expect("open must record timings");
11518        // The post-repack checkpoint and its delta epoch must both validate, so
11519        // the cold open takes the checkpoint fast path rather than a full scan.
11520        assert_eq!(
11521            timings.path,
11522            OpenPath::Checkpoint,
11523            "the post-repack checkpoint and the epoch continuing it must be usable"
11524        );
11525        // Prove the records below come from a gated delta replay, not from a
11526        // checkpoint rewrite that already included `third`. This is a
11527        // deterministic count, unlike the `delta_replay` duration.
11528        assert!(
11529            timings.delta_replay_operations > 0,
11530            "cold open must have replayed the post-repack delta epoch: {timings:?}"
11531        );
11532        assert_eq!(
11533            timings.full_scan,
11534            Duration::ZERO,
11535            "cold open must not have fallen back to a full scan"
11536        );
11537
11538        // All three records must resolve to their exact bytes through the
11539        // replayed delta — never to a wrong shard's bytes.
11540        for (id, expected) in [
11541            (first, &b"first"[..]),
11542            (second, &b"second"[..]),
11543            (third, &b"third"[..]),
11544        ] {
11545            let data = reader
11546                .get(&collection, &id)
11547                .unwrap()
11548                .expect("record must exist");
11549            assert_eq!(data.bytes.as_ref(), expected);
11550        }
11551    }

11553    #[test]
11554    fn repack_persists_checkpoint_so_fresh_cold_open_survives_retirement() {
11555        // Same failure shape as the read-journal test above, but through the
11556        // *plain* open() path and no journal at all. After repack, the
11557        // checkpoint's pack set is exactly the live pack set (one pack), so
11558        // a fresh open's fingerprint matches exactly and the exact-pack gate
11559        // takes no action (replay_needed is false) — the checkpoint's raw
11560        // index slots are trusted directly. A brand-new reader's own
11561        // discover_shards, seeing only that one surviving pack from an
11562        // empty slot table, assigns it local slot 0; the checkpoint's index
11563        // still names the writer's slot 1 (assigned before the original
11564        // slot-0 shard was retired). Without the pack-table remap, get()
11565        // resolves against the wrong (nonexistent, for this reader) slot.
11566        let dir = test_dir("repack_persists_checkpoint_cold_open");
11567        let collection = [0x52u8; 16];
11568        let node = [0x62u8; 16];
11569
11570        let writer = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
11571        writer
11572            .put(
11573                &collection,
11574                &node,
11575                &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"first")),
11576            )
11577            .unwrap();
11578        writer.sync().unwrap();
11579
11580        writer
11581            .repack_collection_reachable(&collection, |_hash, _data| Vec::new())
11582            .unwrap();
11583        drop(writer);
11584
11585        // Fresh process-equivalent open: no history, no shard ever open
11586        // before this point, so this reader's own discover_shards renumbers
11587        // from scratch.
11588        let reopened = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
11589        let got = reopened.get(&collection, &node).unwrap();
11590        assert_eq!(
11591            got.map(|data| data.bytes.to_vec()),
11592            Some(b"first".to_vec()),
11593            "a fresh cold open after repack must resolve the record through \
11594             the checkpoint's pack table, not the writer's raw (unstable) slot number"
11595        );
11596    }

11618        // the packs: the durable API cannot see it, only the overlay can.

11638            store.get_read_committed(&collection, &[node]).unwrap()[0]

11646    #[test]
11647    fn force_index_checkpoint_rewrites_with_and_without_pending_delta() {
11648        let dir = test_dir("force_index_checkpoint");
11649        let wal = dir.join("wal.bin");
11650        let checkpoint_path = PackfileStorage::index_checkpoint_path(&dir);
11651        let store = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
11652        store.enable_journal(&wal).unwrap();
11653
11654        // Empty delta log: no mutations yet. A normal sync would be a no-op;
11655        // forcing still writes a checkpoint with no committed coverage.
11656        store.force_index_checkpoint().unwrap();
11657        let empty = crate::index::checkpoint::read_checkpoint(&checkpoint_path).unwrap();
11658
11659        // Non-empty delta: the put commits a journal group, and sync_all takes
11660        // the delta fast path, which does not advance checkpoint coverage.
11661        store
11662            .put(
11663                &TEST_COLLECTION,
11664                &[0x11; 16],
11665                &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"x")),
11666            )
11667            .unwrap();
11668        store.sync_all().unwrap();
11669        let after_sync = crate::index::checkpoint::read_checkpoint(&checkpoint_path).unwrap();
11670        assert_eq!(
11671            after_sync.covered_lsn, empty.covered_lsn,
11672            "a delta append must not advance checkpoint coverage"
11673        );
11674
11675        // Forcing must take the full-rewrite path and record the committed
11676        // journal tail. Read the tail from the journal rather than hardcoding
11677        // an LSN, so this survives any change to how the first mutation is
11678        // numbered.
11679        let committed = store.journal().expect("journal enabled").committed_lsn();
11680        assert!(
11681            committed > after_sync.covered_lsn,
11682            "the put must have committed past the loaded coverage"
11683        );
11684        store.force_index_checkpoint().unwrap();
11685        let forced = crate::index::checkpoint::read_checkpoint(&checkpoint_path).unwrap();
11686        assert_eq!(
11687            forced.covered_lsn, committed,
11688            "force must advance coverage to the committed journal tail"
11689        );
11690    }

11692    #[cfg(feature = "multi-reader")]
11693    #[test]
11694    fn reset_has_coverage_gap_is_a_pure_base_jump() {
11695        // A fully reclaimed segment carries no groups, only a moved base LSN.
11696        // Keying the gap check off the first group would miss it entirely.
11697        let header_only = crate::journal::Scan {
11698            groups: Vec::new(),
11699            valid_len: 0,
11700            truncated_tail: false,
11701            base_lsn: 3,
11702            consumed_tail: Vec::new(),
11703            group_ends: Vec::new(),
11704        };
11705        let per_pool = |covered: u64| ReadJournal::empty(std::path::PathBuf::new(), covered, None);
11706        let shared = |covered: u64| {
11707            ReadJournal::empty(
11708                std::path::PathBuf::new(),
11709                covered,
11710                Some(crate::layout::ShardType::State),
11711            )
11712        };
11713        // The base jumped from covered + 1 = 2 to 3, so the reclaimed prefix may
11714        // hold a frame this reader lacks. Both layouts must ask for a reload;
11715        // whether the jump is a real gap for this pool is decided after the
11716        // reload, not by inspecting the surviving groups. A previous check that
11717        // looked for this pool's frames in those groups both missed reclaimed
11718        // frames (silent staleness) and rejected valid frames when another pool
11719        // opened the gap.
11720        assert!(per_pool(1).reset_has_coverage_gap(&header_only));
11721        assert!(shared(1).reset_has_coverage_gap(&header_only));
11722        // covered + 1 reaches the base, so nothing at or below covered moved.
11723        assert!(!per_pool(2).reset_has_coverage_gap(&header_only));
11724        assert!(!shared(2).reset_has_coverage_gap(&header_only));
11725        assert!(
11726            !per_pool(0).reset_has_coverage_gap(&crate::journal::Scan::empty()),
11727            "a missing/short segment reports base 0 and is not a gap"
11728        );
11729    }

11793    fn test_put_and_get() {
11794        let dir = test_dir("putget");
11795        let store = PackfileStorage::open(dir).unwrap();
11796
11797        let id = [0x42u8; 16];
11798        let data = NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"hello world"));

11840    #[test]
11841    fn checkpoint_index_growth_recovers_hashes_from_indexed_frames() {
11842        // A batch large enough to be a "real" collection. The checkpoint
11843        // this reopen loads stores locations but not home hashes, so
11844        // growing it (via the `put_many` call below) used to rescan every
11845        // pack for this collection instead of recovering hashes from the
11846        // indexed delta frames.
11847        const ENTRIES: usize = 3_072;
11848        let dir = test_dir("checkpoint_growth_recovery");
11849        let store = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone())
11850            .unwrap()
11851            .with_append_policy(crate::shard::AppendPolicy::buffered());
11852        let entries: Vec<_> = (0..ENTRIES)
11853            .map(|i| {
11854                let mut id = [0u8; 16];
11855                let mixed = (i as u64).wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15);
11856                id[..8].copy_from_slice(&mixed.to_be_bytes());
11857                id[8] = u8::try_from((i >> 16) & 0xFF).unwrap();
11858                id[9] = u8::try_from((i >> 8) & 0xFF).unwrap();
11859                id[10] = u8::try_from(i & 0xFF).unwrap();
11860                (id, NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"payload")))
11861            })
11862            .collect();
11863        store.put_many(&TEST_COLLECTION, &entries).unwrap();
11864        store.sync_all().unwrap();
11865        drop(store);
11866
11867        let reopened = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
11868        let checkpoint_index = reopened
11869            .generation(&TEST_COLLECTION)
11870            .expect("checkpoint collection exists");
11871        assert!(checkpoint_index.index.is_mmap_backed());
11872        let grown = reopened
11873            .grow_checkpoint_index(&TEST_COLLECTION, &checkpoint_index.index)
11874            .unwrap()
11875            .expect("4K checkpoint index can grow");
11876        assert_eq!(grown.len(), ENTRIES);
11877        for (id, _) in &entries {
11878            assert!(grown.lookup(id).is_some(), "recovered hash remains indexed");
11879        }
11880        drop(checkpoint_index);
11881
11882        // Exercise the actual put_many fallback too. `insert_index` fails
11883        // closed once `len >= capacity * 3 / 4`, and the reopened generation
11884        // is mmap-backed (so `LossyIndex::grow` — which needs the original
11885        // homes — can't apply): crossing that threshold therefore always
11886        // routes through `grow_checkpoint_index`, never a silent plain grow
11887        // or a full pack rescan. Compute the threshold from the checkpoint's
11888        // actual on-disk capacity and add enough unique post-reopen entries
11889        // to be certain we cross it, instead of relying on one extra record
11890        // that may land comfortably under it.
11891        let checkpoint_capacity = u64::from(
11892            reopened
11893                .generation(&TEST_COLLECTION)
11894                .expect("checkpoint collection exists")
11895                .index
11896                .capacity(),
11897        );
11898        let threshold = checkpoint_capacity * 3 / 4;
11899        // Add enough unique entries to certainly cross the threshold,
11900        // regardless of exactly how much headroom the checkpoint's
11901        // persisted capacity happens to have.
11902        let needed = threshold.saturating_sub(u64::try_from(ENTRIES).unwrap_or(0)) + 64;
11903        let extra_entries: Vec<_> = (0..needed)
11904            .map(|i| {
11905                let mut id = [0xA5; 16];
11906                id[..8].copy_from_slice(&i.to_be_bytes());
11907                (id, NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"extra")))
11908            })
11909            .collect();
11910        reopened.put_many(&TEST_COLLECTION, &extra_entries).unwrap();
11911        let grown_capacity = reopened
11912            .generation(&TEST_COLLECTION)
11913            .expect("collection still exists")
11914            .index
11915            .capacity();
11916        assert!(
11917            u64::from(grown_capacity) > checkpoint_capacity,
11918            "put_many must have grown the index past its checkpoint capacity"
11919        );
11920        for (id, _) in &extra_entries {
11921            assert!(reopened.get(&TEST_COLLECTION, id).unwrap().is_some());
11922        }
11923        assert!(reopened
11924            .get(&TEST_COLLECTION, &entries[0].0)
11925            .unwrap()
11926            .is_some());
11927    }

11929    /// A writable open must not silently skip a corrupt pack and publish a
11930    /// partial index. The caller needs an error so it can repair or restore
11931    /// the pack before accepting writes.
11932    #[test]
11933    fn test_writable_open_rejects_corrupt_pack_instead_of_skipping_it() {
11934        let dir = test_dir("open_corrupt_pack");
11935        let store = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
11936        let id = distinct_id(0x42);
11937        store
11938            .put(
11939                &TEST_COLLECTION,
11940                &id,
11941                &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"payload")),
11942            )
11943            .unwrap();
11944        // Commit the buffered frame so the tamper below actually overwrites
11945        // on-disk bytes (the record is otherwise only in the append buffer).
11946        store.sync_all().unwrap();
11947        let path = store.shards.active_shard().path.clone();
11948        drop(store);
11949
11950        let mut bytes = fs::read(&path).unwrap();
11951        let payload_byte =
11952            crate::packfile::HEADER_LEN + 4 + crate::packfile::FRAME_FIXED_LEN as usize;
11953        bytes[payload_byte] ^= 0xff;
11954        fs::write(path, bytes).unwrap();
11955
11956        assert!(PackfileStorage::open(dir).is_err());
11957    }

11959    /// Full and `WriteOnly` keep writing real CRCs, so a reopen scan still
11960    /// verifies them: a physically tampered pack must fail to reopen.
11961    /// `Disabled` frames carry no checksum, so a tampered pack reopens and
11962    /// the engine serves the corrupted bytes as data.
11963    #[test]
11964    fn test_checksum_policy_gates_verification_on_reopen_scan() {
11965        for (policy, expect_reopen_ok) in [
11966            (crate::packfile::ChecksumPolicy::Full, false),
11967            (crate::packfile::ChecksumPolicy::WriteOnly, false),
11968            (crate::packfile::ChecksumPolicy::Disabled, true),
11969        ] {
11970            let dir = test_dir(&format!("checksum_policy_reopen_{policy:?}"));
11971            {
11972                let store = PackfileStorage::open_with_policies(dir.clone(), true, policy).unwrap();
11973                let id = distinct_id(0x52);
11974                store
11975                    .put(
11976                        &TEST_COLLECTION,
11977                        &id,
11978                        &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"tamper target")),
11979                    )
11980                    .unwrap();
11981                let (slot, offset) = store
11982                    .generation(&TEST_COLLECTION)
11983                    .unwrap()
11984                    .index
11985                    .lookup(&id)
11986                    .expect("just-written record must be indexed");
11987                // Tampering happens on-disk: commit the buffered frame so the
11988                // tamper site computed from `offset` actually lands in the file.
11989                store.sync_all().unwrap();
11990                let path = store.shards.get_shard(slot).unwrap().path.clone();
11991                drop(store);
11992
11993                let mut bytes = fs::read(&path).unwrap();
11994                let payload_byte = usize::try_from(offset)
11995                    .expect("u64 offset fits usize on any supported host")
11996                    .saturating_add(4)
11997                    .saturating_add(crate::packfile::FRAME_FIXED_LEN as usize);
11998                assert!(payload_byte < bytes.len(), "tamper site must be in-file");
11999                bytes[payload_byte] ^= 0xff;
12000                bytes[payload_byte + 1] ^= 0x0f;
12001                fs::write(path, bytes).unwrap();
12002            }
12003
12004            if expect_reopen_ok {
12005                let store = PackfileStorage::open_with_policies(dir, true, policy).unwrap();
12006                let got = store
12007                    .get(&TEST_COLLECTION, &distinct_id(0x52))
12008                    .unwrap()
12009                    .expect("Disabled reopen must serve the record");
12010                assert_eq!(
12011                    got.bytes.as_ref().len(),
12012                    b"tamper target".len(),
12013                    "payload frame must still decode"
12014                );
12015            } else {
12016                let reopened = PackfileStorage::open_with_policies(dir.clone(), true, policy);
12017                match reopened {
12018                    Ok(_) => panic!("reopen scan must reject a tampered pack"),
12019                    Err(err) => {
12020                        assert!(
12021                            matches!(err, std::io::Error { .. }),
12022                            "expected I/O error from scan_and_recover, got {err:?}"
12023                        );
12024                    }
12025                }
12026                // Remove the trusted checkpoint to exercise the read-only
12027                // full-scan fallback. A valid checkpoint deliberately avoids
12028                // scanning frames and verifies them lazily on lookup.
12029                fs::remove_file(PackfileStorage::index_checkpoint_path(&dir)).unwrap();
12030                let read_only = PackfileStorage::open_read_only_with_policies(dir, policy);
12031                assert!(
12032                    read_only.is_err(),
12033                    "read-only recovery must fail closed instead of omitting a corrupt shard"
12034                );
12035            }
12036        }
12037    }

12220    #[test]
12221    fn test_walk_ancestors_stops_at_boundary() {
12222        let dir = test_dir("walk_basic");
12223        let store = PackfileStorage::open(dir).unwrap();
12224
12225        // A -> B -> C -> D -> E, linear chain, edges point to predecessors.
12226        let ids: Vec<NodeId> = (0..5u8).map(distinct_id).collect();
12227        for (i, id) in ids.iter().enumerate() {
12228            let byte = u8::try_from(i).unwrap();
12229            store
12230                .put(
12231                    &TEST_COLLECTION,
12232                    id,
12233                    &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from(vec![b'A' + byte])),
12234                )
12235                .unwrap();
12236        }
12237        let edges = std::collections::HashMap::from([
12238            (ids[1], vec![ids[0]]),
12239            (ids[2], vec![ids[1]]),
12240            (ids[3], vec![ids[2]]),
12241            (ids[4], vec![ids[3]]),
12242        ]);
12243        let extract = |hash: &[u8; 16], _data: &[u8]| edges.get(hash).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
12244
12245        // frontier=[D], stop_at=[B]: should yield C, D in ancestor-first
12246        // order — stopping at and excluding B, including the D frontier.
12247        let walked: Vec<(NodeId, NodeData)> = store
12248            .walk_ancestors(
12249                &TEST_COLLECTION,
12250                &[ids[3]],
12251                &[ids[1]],
12252                extract,
12253                WalkLimits::default(),
12254            )
12255            .unwrap()
12256            .collect::<Result<_, _>>()
12257            .unwrap();
12258        let bytes: Vec<u8> = walked.iter().map(|(_, d)| d.bytes[0]).collect();
12259        assert_eq!(
12260            bytes,
12261            vec![b'C', b'D'],
12262            "walk must be ancestor-first, excluding the stop_at boundary"
12263        );
12264
12265        // Empty stop_at: walks all the way back to the collection's true roots.
12266        let full: Vec<(NodeId, NodeData)> = store
12267            .walk_ancestors(
12268                &TEST_COLLECTION,
12269                &[ids[4]],
12270                &[],
12271                extract,
12272                WalkLimits::default(),
12273            )
12274            .unwrap()
12275            .collect::<Result<_, _>>()
12276            .unwrap();
12277        let full_bytes: Vec<u8> = full.iter().map(|(_, d)| d.bytes[0]).collect();
12278        assert_eq!(full_bytes, vec![b'A', b'B', b'C', b'D', b'E']);
12279    }

12281    #[test]
12282    fn test_walk_ancestors_branching_dag() {
12283        let dir = test_dir("walk_branch");
12284        let store = PackfileStorage::open(dir).unwrap();
12285
12286        //   A
12287        //  / \
12288        // B   C
12289        //  \ /
12290        //   D
12291        let ids: Vec<NodeId> = (0..4u8).map(distinct_id).collect();
12292        for (i, id) in ids.iter().enumerate() {
12293            let byte = u8::try_from(i).unwrap();
12294            store
12295                .put(
12296                    &TEST_COLLECTION,
12297                    id,
12298                    &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from(vec![b'A' + byte])),
12299                )
12300                .unwrap();
12301        }
12302        let edges = std::collections::HashMap::from([
12303            (ids[1], vec![ids[0]]),
12304            (ids[2], vec![ids[0]]),
12305            (ids[3], vec![ids[1], ids[2]]),
12306        ]);
12307        let extract = |hash: &[u8; 16], _data: &[u8]| edges.get(hash).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
12308
12309        // frontier=[D], stop_at=[A]: should yield exactly {B, C, D} — A
12310        // excluded as the boundary, both branches merge back in correctly.
12311        let walked: Vec<(NodeId, NodeData)> = store
12312            .walk_ancestors(
12313                &TEST_COLLECTION,
12314                &[ids[3]],
12315                &[ids[0]],
12316                extract,
12317                WalkLimits::default(),
12318            )
12319            .unwrap()
12320            .collect::<Result<_, _>>()
12321            .unwrap();
12322        let mut bytes: Vec<u8> = walked.iter().map(|(_, d)| d.bytes[0]).collect();
12323        // D must come last (ancestor-first order); B/C order between them
12324        // is unconstrained since they're siblings.
12325        assert_eq!(*bytes.last().unwrap(), b'D');
12326        bytes.sort_unstable();
12327        assert_eq!(bytes, vec![b'B', b'C', b'D']);
12328    }

12330    #[test]
12331    fn test_walk_ancestors_never_reaching_stop_at_walks_to_roots() {
12332        // A fork that never crosses the supplied stop_at boundary must not
12333        // be silently truncated there — it's an ancestor walk with stop
12334        // markers, not a from/to span, so it walks to the collection's true
12335        // roots instead.
12336        let dir = test_dir("walk_fork_misses_boundary");
12337        let store = PackfileStorage::open(dir).unwrap();
12338
12339        //   ROOT
12340        //   /  \
12341        // MAIN  FORK
12342        //  |
12343        // TIP
12344        let root = distinct_id(0);
12345        let main = distinct_id(1);
12346        let fork = distinct_id(2);
12347        let tip = distinct_id(3);
12348        for (id, byte) in [(root, b'R'), (main, b'M'), (fork, b'F'), (tip, b'T')] {
12349            store
12350                .put(
12351                    &TEST_COLLECTION,
12352                    &id,
12353                    &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from(vec![byte])),
12354                )
12355                .unwrap();
12356        }
12357        let edges = std::collections::HashMap::from([
12358            (main, vec![root]),
12359            (fork, vec![root]),
12360            (tip, vec![main]),
12361        ]);
12362        let extract = |hash: &[u8; 16], _data: &[u8]| edges.get(hash).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
12363
12364        // stop_at names `fork`, which TIP's history never crosses — the
12365        // walk from TIP must still reach ROOT rather than stopping short.
12366        let walked: Vec<(NodeId, NodeData)> = store
12367            .walk_ancestors(
12368                &TEST_COLLECTION,
12369                &[tip],
12370                &[fork],
12371                extract,
12372                WalkLimits::default(),
12373            )
12374            .unwrap()
12375            .collect::<Result<_, _>>()
12376            .unwrap();
12377        let mut bytes: Vec<u8> = walked.iter().map(|(_, d)| d.bytes[0]).collect();
12378        bytes.sort_unstable();
12379        assert_eq!(bytes, vec![b'M', b'R', b'T']);
12380    }

12423    #[test]
12424    fn test_walk_ancestors_survives_concurrent_repack_gc() {
12425        // Regression test for the exact concurrency bug flagged in review:
12426        // an earlier draft resolved each node lazily, at drain time,
12427        // against whatever generation happened to be live *then* — so a
12428        // repack that GC'd a node between building the walk and draining
12429        // it would silently drop that node from the results. Resolving
12430        // eagerly against one frozen generation snapshot up front (what
12431        // walk_ancestors does now) must not exhibit that.
12432        let dir = test_dir("walk_survives_repack");
12433        let store = PackfileStorage::open(dir).unwrap();
12434
12435        let a = distinct_id(0);
12436        let b = distinct_id(1);
12437        store
12438            .put(
12439                &TEST_COLLECTION,
12440                &a,
12441                &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"A")),
12442            )
12443            .unwrap();
12444        store
12445            .put(
12446                &TEST_COLLECTION,
12447                &b,
12448                &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"B")),
12449            )
12450            .unwrap();
12451        let edges = std::collections::HashMap::from([(b, vec![a])]);
12452        let extract = |hash: &[u8; 16], _data: &[u8]| edges.get(hash).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
12453
12454        // Build the walk (resolves and captures A and B eagerly)...
12455        let walk = store
12456            .walk_ancestors(&TEST_COLLECTION, &[b], &[], extract, WalkLimits::default())
12457            .unwrap();
12458
12459        // ...then, before draining it, run a repack that only keeps B as
12460        // a live root — A becomes unreachable and gets GC'd out of the
12461        // collection's index/cache entirely.
12462        store.set_live_roots(&TEST_COLLECTION, vec![b]);
12463        let (kept, dropped) = store
12464            .repack_collection_reachable(&TEST_COLLECTION, |_hash, _data| Vec::new())
12465            .unwrap();
12466        assert_eq!((kept, dropped), (1, 1), "repack must have GC'd A");
12467
12468        // The already-built walk must still yield both A and B: it
12469        // captured its data before the repack ran, so it isn't affected
12470        // by the generation swap that just happened.
12471        let results: Vec<(NodeId, NodeData)> = walk.collect::<Result<_, _>>().unwrap();
12472        let mut bytes: Vec<u8> = results.iter().map(|(_, d)| d.bytes[0]).collect();
12473        bytes.sort_unstable();
12474        assert_eq!(
12475            bytes,
12476            vec![b'A', b'B'],
12477            "a walk built before a concurrent repack must not lose nodes that repack GC'd afterward"
12478        );
12479    }

12481    fn setup_repack_mid_lookup(
12482        test_name: &str,
12483        id: NodeId,
12484    ) -> (Arc<PackfileStorage>, u16, Arc<AtomicBool>) {
12485        // Put the repack in the exact window between candidate collection and
12486        // shard pinning, and force its output onto a new shard so the original
12487        // candidate shard is actually retired.
12488        let dir = test_dir(test_name);
12489        let store = Arc::new(PackfileStorage::open(dir).unwrap());
12490        store
12491            .put(
12492                &TEST_COLLECTION,
12493                &id,
12494                &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"payload")),
12495            )
12496            .unwrap();
12497        store.sync().unwrap();
12498        store.generation(&TEST_COLLECTION).unwrap().cache.clear();
12499        let old_shard = store
12500            .generation(&TEST_COLLECTION)
12501            .unwrap()
12502            .index
12503            .lookup_all(&id)
12504            .next()
12505            .expect("id is indexed")
12506            .0;
12507
12508        let fired = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
12509        let hook_fired = Arc::clone(&fired);
12510        let hook_store = Arc::clone(&store);
12511        PackfileStorage::set_test_before_pin(Some(Box::new(move || {
12512            if !hook_fired.swap(true, Ordering::Relaxed) {
12513                hook_store.shards.active_shard().file_len.store(
12514                    shard::MAX_SHARD_BYTES - 10,
12515                    std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Release,
12516                );
12517                hook_store.set_live_roots(&TEST_COLLECTION, vec![id]);
12518                hook_store
12519                    .repack_collection_reachable(&TEST_COLLECTION, |_hash, _data| Vec::new())
12520                    .unwrap();
12521            }
12522        })));
12523        (store, old_shard, fired)
12524    }

12526    #[test]
12527    fn test_get_retries_when_a_repack_retires_the_shard_mid_lookup() {
12528        let id = distinct_id(0x77);
12529        let (store, old_shard, fired) = setup_repack_mid_lookup("get_retry_mid_repack", id);
12530        let result = store.get(&TEST_COLLECTION, &id).unwrap();
12531        PackfileStorage::set_test_before_pin(None);
12532
12533        assert!(fired.load(Ordering::Relaxed), "the test hook must have run");
12534        assert!(
12535            store.shards.get_shard(old_shard).is_none(),
12536            "the repack must have retired the looked-up shard, or this test proves nothing"
12537        );
12538        assert!(
12539            result.is_some(),
12540            "get must retry and still find a record whose shard a repack retired mid-lookup"
12541        );
12542    }

12562    #[test]
12563    fn test_walk_ancestors_pins_shards_against_a_mid_walk_repack() {
12564        // The walk freezes one generation, but a concurrent repack can still
12565        // retire the shards that generation's index points at. `extract_edges`
12566        // runs between node resolutions, so triggering the repack from it
12567        // deterministically reproduces a mid-walk swap; every node must still
12568        // resolve.
12569        let dir = test_dir("walk_pins_mid_repack");
12570        let store = PackfileStorage::open(dir).unwrap();
12571
12572        let a = distinct_id(0xA0);
12573        let b = distinct_id(0xA1);
12574        let c = distinct_id(0xA2);
12575        for (id, byte) in [(&a, b'A'), (&b, b'B'), (&c, b'C')] {
12576            store
12577                .put(
12578                    &TEST_COLLECTION,
12579                    id,
12580                    &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::copy_from_slice(&[byte])),
12581                )
12582                .unwrap();
12583        }
12584        store.sync().unwrap();
12585        let old_shard = store
12586            .generation(&TEST_COLLECTION)
12587            .unwrap()
12588            .index
12589            .lookup_all(&c)
12590            .next()
12591            .expect("c is indexed")
12592            .0;
12593
12594        let edges = std::collections::HashMap::from([(c, vec![b]), (b, vec![a])]);
12595        let fired = std::cell::Cell::new(false);
12596        let extract = |hash: &[u8; 16], _data: &[u8]| {
12597            if !fired.replace(true) {
12598                // Force the repack's output onto a new shard so the snapshot's
12599                // shard is retired rather than reused as the live write shard.
12600                store.shards.active_shard().file_len.store(
12601                    shard::MAX_SHARD_BYTES - 10,
12602                    std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Release,
12603                );
12604                store.set_live_roots(&TEST_COLLECTION, vec![c]);
12605                let (kept, dropped) = store
12606                    .repack_collection_reachable(&TEST_COLLECTION, |h, _d| {
12607                        edges.get(h).cloned().unwrap_or_default()
12608                    })
12609                    .unwrap();
12610                assert_eq!((kept, dropped), (3, 0), "all three nodes stay reachable");
12611            }
12612            edges.get(hash).cloned().unwrap_or_default()
12613        };
12614
12615        let walk = store
12616            .walk_ancestors(&TEST_COLLECTION, &[c], &[], extract, WalkLimits::default())
12617            .unwrap();
12618        let results: Vec<(NodeId, NodeData)> = walk.collect::<Result<_, _>>().unwrap();
12619
12620        assert!(
12621            store.shards.get_shard(old_shard).is_none(),
12622            "the repack must have retired the snapshot's shard, or this test proves nothing"
12623        );
12624        assert_eq!(
12625            results.len(),
12626            3,
12627            "the walk must resolve every node even though a repack retired the snapshot's shards mid-walk"
12628        );
12629    }
