12678    #[test]
12679    fn test_concurrent_federation_swarm() {
12680        use std::sync::Mutex;
12681        use std::thread;
12682
12683        const NUM_WRITERS: usize = 8;
12684        const EVENTS_PER_WRITER: usize = 500;
12685        const NUM_READERS: usize = 8;
12686        const READS_PER_READER: usize = 2000;
12687
12688        let dir = test_dir("concurrent_federation");
12689        let store = PackfileStorage::open(dir).unwrap();
12690
12691        let collection = [0x77u8; 16];
12692        let written: Mutex<Vec<(NodeId, bytes::Bytes)>> = Mutex::new(Vec::new());
12693        let read_ok = std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize::new(0);
12694        let read_not_found = std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize::new(0);
12695
12696        thread::scope(|scope| {
12697            for w in 0..NUM_WRITERS {
12698                let store = &store;
12699                let written = &written;
12700                scope.spawn(move || {
12701                    for i in 0..EVENTS_PER_WRITER {
12702                        let mut id = [0u8; 16];
12703                        id[0] = u8::try_from(w).unwrap();
12704                        id[1..9].copy_from_slice(&(i as u64).to_le_bytes());
12705                        let bytes = bytes::Bytes::from(format!("writer {w} event {i}"));
12706                        let data = NodeData::new(bytes.clone());
12707                        store.put(&collection, &id, &data).unwrap();
12708                        written.lock().unwrap().push((id, bytes));
12709                    }
12710                });
12711            }
12712
12713            for _ in 0..NUM_READERS {
12714                let store = &store;
12715                let written = &written;
12716                let read_ok = &read_ok;
12717                let read_not_found = &read_not_found;
12718                scope.spawn(move || {
12719                    for i in 0..READS_PER_READER {
12720                        let snapshot_len = written.lock().unwrap().len();
12721                        if snapshot_len == 0 {
12722                            continue;
12723                        }
12724                        let idx = i % snapshot_len;
12725                        let (id, expected_bytes) = written.lock().unwrap()[idx].clone();
12726                        match store.get(&collection, &id).unwrap() {
12727                            Some(data) => {
12728                                assert_eq!(data.bytes, expected_bytes);
12729                                read_ok.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
12730                            }
12731                            None => {
12732                                read_not_found.fetch_add(1, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
12733                            }
12734                        }
12735                    }
12736                });
12737            }
12738        });
12739
12740        let written = written.into_inner().unwrap();
12741        assert_eq!(written.len(), NUM_WRITERS * EVENTS_PER_WRITER);
12742
12743        let mut lost = Vec::new();
12744        for (id, expected_bytes) in &written {
12745            match store.get(&collection, id).unwrap() {
12746                Some(data) => assert_eq!(data.bytes, *expected_bytes),
12747                None => lost.push(*id),
12748            }
12749        }
12750
12751        eprintln!(
12752            "concurrent federation swarm: {} writes, {} reads ok, {} reads not-found, {} lost",
12753            written.len(),
12754            read_ok.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed),
12755            read_not_found.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed),
12756            lost.len()
12757        );
12758
12759        assert!(
12760            lost.is_empty(),
12761            "{} of {} records lost: {lost:?}",
12762            lost.len(),
12763            written.len()
12764        );
12765    }
12766
12767    /// Regression for the epoch-handoff protocol in `persist_index_checkpoint`:
12768    /// full checkpoint rewrites now hold every collection's `put_mutex` only
12769    /// across the fingerprint/index snapshot and delta-epoch rotation, not
12770    /// across the (unlocked) serialize + fsync + rename. Concurrent `put`s
12771    /// landing in that unlocked window must all still be durable after the
12772    /// next sync and a reopen — none may be silently dropped by the epoch
12773    /// rotation, and none may be lost to a torn straddle between the pack
12774    /// fingerprint and the index snapshot.
12775    #[test]
12776    fn test_concurrent_put_survives_checkpoint_rewrites() {
12777        use std::sync::Mutex;
12778        use std::thread;
12779
12780        const NUM_WRITERS: usize = 6;
12781        const PUTS_PER_WRITER: usize = 300;
12782        // Force many full rewrites during the run: each rewrite thread
12783        // iteration invalidates the delta log (via a collection delete on an
12784        // otherwise-untouched collection) then rewrites, so persistence keeps
12785        // taking the epoch-rotation path instead of the cheap delta append.
12786        const REWRITES: usize = 40;
12787
12788        let dir = test_dir("concurrent_put_checkpoint_rewrite");
12789        let store = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
12790
12791        // Seed one throwaway collection per rewrite so each rewrite iteration
12792        // has a fresh structural invalidation to force (deleting an
12793        // already-deleted collection is a no-op and wouldn't force a rewrite).
12794        for r in 0..REWRITES {
12795            let mut collection = [0u8; 16];
12796            collection[0] = 0xEE;
12797            collection[1..9].copy_from_slice(&(r as u64).to_le_bytes());
12798            let mut id = [0u8; 16];
12799            id[15] = 1;
12800            store
12801                .put(&collection, &id, &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from("seed")))
12802                .unwrap();
12803        }
12804        store.sync_all().unwrap();
12805
12806        let written: Mutex<Vec<([u8; 16], NodeId, bytes::Bytes)>> = Mutex::new(Vec::new());
12807
12808        thread::scope(|scope| {
12809            for w in 0..NUM_WRITERS {
12810                let store = &store;
12811                let written = &written;
12812                scope.spawn(move || {
12813                    let mut collection = [0u8; 16];
12814                    collection[0] = 0xAA;
12815                    collection[1] = u8::try_from(w).unwrap();
12816                    for i in 0..PUTS_PER_WRITER {
12817                        let mut id = [0u8; 16];
12818                        id[0] = u8::try_from(w).unwrap();
12819                        id[1..9].copy_from_slice(&(i as u64).to_le_bytes());
12820                        let bytes = bytes::Bytes::from(format!("writer {w} put {i}"));
12821                        let data = NodeData::new(bytes.clone());
12822                        store.put(&collection, &id, &data).unwrap();
12823                        written.lock().unwrap().push((collection, id, bytes));
12824                    }
12825                });
12826            }
12827
12828            scope.spawn(|| {
12829                for r in 0..REWRITES {
12830                    let mut throwaway = [0u8; 16];
12831                    throwaway[0] = 0xEE;
12832                    throwaway[1..9].copy_from_slice(&(r as u64).to_le_bytes());
12833                    store.delete_collection(&throwaway).unwrap();
12834                    store.persist_index_checkpoint_best_effort();
12835                }
12836            });
12837        });
12838
12839        store.sync_all().unwrap();
12840        drop(store);
12841
12842        let reopened = PackfileStorage::open(dir).unwrap();
12843        let written = written.into_inner().unwrap();
12844        assert_eq!(written.len(), NUM_WRITERS * PUTS_PER_WRITER);
12845
12846        let mut lost = Vec::new();
12847        for (collection, id, expected_bytes) in &written {
12848            match reopened.get(collection, id).unwrap() {
12849                Some(data) => assert_eq!(data.bytes, *expected_bytes),
12850                None => lost.push(*id),
12851            }
12852        }
12853        assert!(
12854            lost.is_empty(),
12855            "{} of {} records lost to a concurrent checkpoint rewrite: {lost:?}",
12856            lost.len(),
12857            written.len()
12858        );
12859    }
12860
12861    /// Deterministic, fast regression guard for the epoch-handoff protocol's
12862    /// actual point: a concurrent `put()` must not block on the checkpoint
12863    /// rewrite's serialize/write/rename, no matter how long that takes.
12864    /// Rather than inferring "not blocked" from a wall-clock race against
12865    /// real disk I/O (slow, and only as reliable as the dataset is large
12866    /// enough to make a real rewrite slow relative to test-machine noise —
12867    /// see the git history on this function for the timing-based version
12868    /// this replaced), this injects an artificial, arbitrarily long delay
12869    /// into the unlocked window via a test-only hook and asserts a `put()`
12870    /// issued after the rewrite has entered that window returns in a small
12871    /// fraction of it. A proper wall-clock benchmark of this same property
12872    /// lives in `benches/storage.rs` (`cargo bench`), where it belongs.
12873    #[test]
12874    fn test_put_does_not_block_on_slow_checkpoint_rewrite() {
12875        use std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool;
12876        use std::thread;
12877        use std::time::{Duration, Instant};
12878
12879        const ARTIFICIAL_DELAY: Duration = Duration::from_millis(300);
12880
12881        let dir = test_dir("put_not_blocked_by_slow_rewrite");
12882        let store = PackfileStorage::open(dir).unwrap();
12883
12884        // Establish a first checkpoint so the forced rewrite below has
12885        // something real to serialize and rewrite.
12886        let cid = [0x33u8; 16];
12887        store
12888            .put(&cid, &[0u8; 16], &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from("seed")))
12889            .unwrap();
12890        store.sync_all().unwrap();
12891
12892        // Force the next rewrite via a structural invalidation.
12893        let throwaway = [0x44u8; 16];
12894        store
12895            .put(
12896                &throwaway,
12897                &[0u8; 16],
12898                &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from("x")),
12899            )
12900            .unwrap();
12901        store.delete_collection(&throwaway).unwrap();
12902
12903        let entered_unlocked_window = std::sync::Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
12904        let put_elapsed = std::sync::Mutex::new(None::<Duration>);
12905
12906        thread::scope(|scope| {
12907            {
12908                let store = &store;
12909                let hook_flag = std::sync::Arc::clone(&entered_unlocked_window);
12910                scope.spawn(move || {
12911                    store
12912                        .test_persist_index_checkpoint_with_delay(ARTIFICIAL_DELAY, &hook_flag)
12913                        .unwrap();
12914                });
12915            }
12916            // Wait for the hook to confirm it has released every lock and is
12917            // now sleeping inside the artificial delay — a real signal from
12918            // the rewrite thread, not a fixed-sleep guess that depends on
12919            // test-machine timing. The put issued below then provably runs
12920            // concurrently with the unlocked rewrite window.
12921            while !entered_unlocked_window.load(Ordering::Acquire) {
12922                thread::yield_now();
12923            }
12924
12925            let started = Instant::now();
12926            store
12927                .put(
12928                    &cid,
12929                    &[1u8; 16],
12930                    &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from("concurrent")),
12931                )
12932                .unwrap();
12933            *put_elapsed.lock().unwrap() = Some(started.elapsed());
12934        });
12935
12936        let put_elapsed = put_elapsed.into_inner().unwrap().unwrap();
12937        assert!(
12938            put_elapsed < ARTIFICIAL_DELAY / 3,
12939            "a put() issued while a rewrite was sleeping in its unlocked window took \
12940             {put_elapsed:?} — it should return almost immediately, not wait anywhere near the \
12941             artificial {ARTIFICIAL_DELAY:?} delay; did the lock scope regress to holding \
12942             put_mutex across the serialize/write/rename again?"
12943        );
12944    }
12945
12946    /// Crash-boundary: a crash between the D0→D1 epoch rotation and C1's
12947    /// checkpoint rename. D1 exists only in the (now-lost) in-memory state;
12948    /// nothing on disk names its fingerprint. The pack bytes for whatever
12949    /// prompted the rotation are already physically flushed (rotation always
12950    /// flushes first), so the reopen's local fingerprint has already moved
12951    /// past D0's sealed tail — the trusted-log check fails and this must fall
12952    /// back to a full rescan (packfiles stay authoritative), never silently
12953    /// lose the data.
12954    #[test]
12955    fn test_crash_between_rotation_and_checkpoint_rename_falls_back_to_rescan() {
12956        let dir = test_dir("crash_between_rotation_and_rename");
12957        let store = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
12958
12959        let cid = [0x11u8; 16];
12960        let mut written = Vec::new();
12961
12962        // Round 1: establish C0 via a full (first-ever) rewrite.
12963        for i in 0..50u64 {
12964            let mut id = [0u8; 16];
12965            id[1..9].copy_from_slice(&i.to_le_bytes());
12966            let bytes = bytes::Bytes::from(format!("round1 {i}"));
12967            store.put(&cid, &id, &NodeData::new(bytes.clone())).unwrap();
12968            written.push((id, bytes));
12969        }
12970        store.sync_all().unwrap();
12971
12972        // Round 2: a plain write's sync appends a delta batch continuing C0
12973        // (D0), never rewriting the checkpoint.
12974        for i in 50..100u64 {
12975            let mut id = [0u8; 16];
12976            id[1..9].copy_from_slice(&i.to_le_bytes());
12977            let bytes = bytes::Bytes::from(format!("round2 {i}"));
12978            store.put(&cid, &id, &NodeData::new(bytes.clone())).unwrap();
12979            written.push((id, bytes));
12980        }
12981        store.sync_all().unwrap();
12982
12983        // Round 3: more writes, then simulate a crash exactly between the
12984        // epoch rotation (which flushes these bytes and discards their
12985        // not-yet-appended delta frames) and the checkpoint that would have
12986        // validated the new epoch.
12987        for i in 100..150u64 {
12988            let mut id = [0u8; 16];
12989            id[1..9].copy_from_slice(&i.to_le_bytes());
12990            let bytes = bytes::Bytes::from(format!("round3 {i}"));
12991            store.put(&cid, &id, &NodeData::new(bytes.clone())).unwrap();
12992            written.push((id, bytes));
12993        }
12994        let _ = store.test_rotate_epoch_without_checkpoint();
12995        drop(store); // simulated crash: no checkpoint, no retirement.
12996
12997        let reopened = PackfileStorage::open(dir).unwrap();
12998        let open = reopened.open_timings().expect("open must record timings");
12999        assert!(open.total > Duration::ZERO);
13000        assert!(open.packfile_recovery_calls >= 1);
13001        assert!(open.packfile_open_calls >= 1);
13002        assert!(open.packfile_recovery + open.packfile_open <= open.shard_open);
13003        assert_eq!(
13004            open.path,
13005            OpenPath::FullScan,
13006            "D0's sealed tail can no longer match the post-rotation pack state, so the \
13007             stale-but-still-present log must be rejected wholesale, not partially replayed"
13008        );
13009        for (id, expected_bytes) in &written {
13010            let got = reopened
13011                .get(&cid, id)
13012                .unwrap()
13013                .expect("every write, including the un-appended round 3, survives via the packs");
13014            assert_eq!(got.bytes.as_ref(), expected_bytes.as_ref());
13015        }
13016    }
13017
13018    /// Crash-boundary: a crash between C1's checkpoint rename becoming
13019    /// durable and D0's retirement. Both C1 (+ the fresh, still-empty D1) and
13020    /// the now-stale D0 exist on disk at once; the reopen must select C1 and
13021    /// ignore D0 (base fingerprint no longer matches), and the orphaned D0
13022    /// file must be swept away by the sweep-on-open cleanup.
13023    #[test]
13024    fn test_crash_between_checkpoint_rename_and_retirement_uses_new_checkpoint() {
13025        let dir = test_dir("crash_between_rename_and_retire");
13026        let store = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
13027
13028        let cid = [0x22u8; 16];
13029        let mut written = Vec::new();
13030
13031        // Stay well under `NEW_COLLECTION_INDEX_FLOOR`'s 75%-load grow
13032        // threshold (48 entries at the floor of 64): this test exercises
13033        // checkpoint/epoch continuity across a simulated crash, not the
13034        // index's grow() behavior, and a grow mid-round would invalidate
13035        // the delta log this test is asserting still exists on disk.
13036        for i in 0..10u64 {
13037            let mut id = [0u8; 16];
13038            id[1..9].copy_from_slice(&i.to_le_bytes());
13039            let bytes = bytes::Bytes::from(format!("round1 {i}"));
13040            store.put(&cid, &id, &NodeData::new(bytes.clone())).unwrap();
13041            written.push((id, bytes));
13042        }
13043        store.sync_all().unwrap(); // C0, D0 exists once round 2 appends below.
13044
13045        for i in 10..20u64 {
13046            let mut id = [0u8; 16];
13047            id[1..9].copy_from_slice(&i.to_le_bytes());
13048            let bytes = bytes::Bytes::from(format!("round2 {i}"));
13049            store.put(&cid, &id, &NodeData::new(bytes.clone())).unwrap();
13050            written.push((id, bytes));
13051        }
13052        store.sync_all().unwrap(); // D0 now has a committed batch continuing C0.
13053
13054        let old_d0_fingerprint = {
13055            let (_new_fingerprint, old_base_fingerprint) =
13056                store.test_write_checkpoint_without_retire().unwrap();
13057            old_base_fingerprint.expect("this session had a prior epoch (C0/D0) to retire")
13058        };
13059        let d0_path = PackfileStorage::delta_path(&dir, old_d0_fingerprint);
13060        assert!(
13061            d0_path.exists(),
13062            "D0 must still be on disk immediately after the simulated crash point"
13063        );
13064        drop(store); // simulated crash: retire_delta_epoch never ran.
13065
13066        let reopened = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
13067        let open = reopened.open_timings().expect("open must record timings");
13068        assert_eq!(
13069            open.path,
13070            OpenPath::Checkpoint,
13071            "C1 is durable and matches the current pack state exactly (no writes happened \
13072             after the snapshot), so the reopen must take the fast path"
13073        );
13074        assert!(
13075            !d0_path.exists(),
13076            "the orphaned, now-unreachable D0 must be swept away by the writable open's cleanup"
13077        );
13078        for (id, expected_bytes) in &written {
13079            let got = reopened
13080                .get(&cid, id)
13081                .unwrap()
13082                .expect("every write survives a reopen onto the new checkpoint");
13083            assert_eq!(got.bytes.as_ref(), expected_bytes.as_ref());
13084        }
13085    }

13087    /// Collection creation and growth become per-collection v3 snapshots, so
13088    /// neither mutation requires a store-wide checkpoint rewrite.
13089    #[test]
13090    fn delta_invalidation_triggers_are_new_collections_and_growth() {
13091        const ROUNDS: u8 = 5;
13092
13093        // Arm A: one new collection per barrier -- the Complement room-churn
13094        // shape. Each create adds a collection snapshot to the v3 log.
13095        let store_a = PackfileStorage::open(test_dir("delta_triggers_new_collections")).unwrap();
13096        let before_a = store_a.stats();
13097        for round in 0..ROUNDS {
13098            let mut cid = [0u8; 16];
13099            cid[0] = 0xA0;
13100            cid[1] = round;
13101            for i in 0..3u8 {
13102                store_a
13103                    .put(
13104                        &cid,
13105                        &distinct_id(i),
13106                        &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from(format!("round {round} node {i}"))),
13107                    )
13108                    .unwrap();
13109            }
13110            store_a.sync_all().unwrap();
13111        }
13112        let after_a = store_a.stats();
13113        assert_eq!(
13114            after_a.delta_invalidations - before_a.delta_invalidations,
13115            u64::from(ROUNDS),
13116            "one is_new invalidation per collection created between barriers"
13117        );
13118        assert_eq!(
13119            after_a.checkpoint_writes - before_a.checkpoint_writes,
13120            1,
13121            "only the initial empty-store baseline needs a checkpoint"
13122        );
13123        assert_eq!(
13124            after_a.delta_appends - before_a.delta_appends,
13125            u64::from(ROUNDS - 1),
13126            "new collections after the baseline append snapshots"
13127        );
13128
13129        // Arm B: one collection that never grows. Its first sync establishes
13130        // the baseline; subsequent writes append incrementals.
13131        let store_b = PackfileStorage::open(test_dir("delta_triggers_single_collection")).unwrap();
13132        let before_b = store_b.stats();
13133        let mut next = 0u8;
13134        for _ in 0..ROUNDS {
13135            for _ in 0..3u8 {
13136                store_b
13137                    .put(
13138                        &TEST_COLLECTION,
13139                        &distinct_id(next),
13140                        &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from(format!("node {next}"))),
13141                    )
13142                    .unwrap();
13143                next = next.wrapping_add(1);
13144            }
13145            store_b.sync_all().unwrap();
13146        }
13147        let after_b = store_b.stats();
13148        assert_eq!(
13149            after_b.delta_invalidations - before_b.delta_invalidations,
13150            1,
13151            "only collection creation is structural"
13152        );
13153        assert_eq!(
13154            after_b.checkpoint_writes - before_b.checkpoint_writes,
13155            1,
13156            "one rewrite re-bases the log, then it is continuable"
13157        );
13158        assert_eq!(
13159            after_b.delta_appends - before_b.delta_appends,
13160            u64::from(ROUNDS - 1),
13161            "every barrier after the re-base appends the delta"
13162        );
13163
13164        // Arm C: force that same collection past the index's 75%-load grow
13165        // threshold with a batch (`put_many` is the path that sizes and grows
13166        // an index; the single-record `put` grow path is not what
13167        // `index_grow_count` tracks). Growth is logical: it emits redo records,
13168        // not a replacement snapshot.
13169        let before_c = store_b.stats();
13170        let entries: Vec<(NodeId, NodeData)> = (next..80u8)
13171            .map(|i| {
13172                (
13173                    distinct_id(i),
13174                    NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from(format!("node {i}"))),
13175                )
13176            })
13177            .collect();
13178        store_b.put_many(&TEST_COLLECTION, &entries).unwrap();
13179        store_b.sync_all().unwrap();
13180        let after_c = store_b.stats();
13181        let grows = after_c.index_grow_count - before_c.index_grow_count;
13182        assert!(
13183            grows >= 1,
13184            "crossing the load threshold must grow the index"
13185        );
13186        assert_eq!(
13187            after_c.delta_invalidations - before_c.delta_invalidations,
13188            0,
13189            "growth does not invalidate the log: replay grows the table itself"
13190        );
13191        assert_eq!(
13192            after_c.delta_appends - before_c.delta_appends,
13193            1,
13194            "a growing collection appends its redo records in one batch"
13195        );
13196        assert_log_has_redo_and_no_snapshot(&store_b, entries.len());
13197        assert_eq!(
13198            after_c.checkpoint_writes - before_c.checkpoint_writes,
13199            0,
13200            "growth no longer rewrites the whole checkpoint"
13201        );
13202    }

13204    /// The store's current delta log holds at least `min_redo` redo records and
13205    /// no whole-index snapshot.
13206    fn assert_log_has_redo_and_no_snapshot(store: &PackfileStorage, min_redo: usize) {
13207        let base = store.delta_state.lock().base_fingerprint.unwrap();
13208        let log =
13209            delta::read_delta_log_v3(&PackfileStorage::delta_path(&store.base_dir, base)).unwrap();
13210        assert!(
13211            log.operations
13212                .iter()
13213                .all(|operation| !matches!(operation, DeltaOperation::CollectionSnapshot { .. })),
13214            "no whole-index snapshot for a growth"
13215        );
13216        let redo_ops = log
13217            .operations
13218            .iter()
13219            .filter(|operation| matches!(operation, DeltaOperation::Redo(_)))
13220            .count();
13221        assert!(redo_ops >= min_redo, "the batch's records are logged");
13222    }

13224    fn batch_node(index: u32) -> NodeId {
13225        let mut id = [0u8; 16];
13226        id[..4].copy_from_slice(&index.to_le_bytes());
13227        id[15] = 0xB7;
13228        id
13229    }

13231    /// A batch that does not fit under the cap rotates the log, though the log is
13232    /// still well below the rotation length: the batch (which can carry
13233    /// whole-index snapshots) is bigger than the room left. The rotation is
13234    /// planned and reported as such, and nothing is lost.
13235    #[test]
13236    fn a_batch_that_crosses_the_cap_below_the_rotation_length_rotates_the_log() {
13237        let dir = test_dir("v3_delta_cap_batch");
13238        let store = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
13239        let collection = [0xD3; 16];
13240        store
13241            .put(
13242                &collection,
13243                &distinct_id(90),
13244                &NodeData::from_slice(b"base"),
13245            )
13246            .unwrap();
13247        store.sync_all().unwrap();
13248
13249        store.delta_log_cap_override.store(8192, Ordering::Relaxed);
13250        store.delta_state.lock().log_bytes = 100;
13251        assert!(
13252            100 < store.delta_log_rotate_bytes(),
13253            "below the rotation length"
13254        );
13255        // Enough frames that the batch alone is larger than the room under the
13256        // (test) cap.
13257        for id in 0..400u32 {
13258            store
13259                .put(&collection, &batch_node(id), &NodeData::from_slice(b"v"))
13260                .unwrap();
13261        }
13262        let before = store.stats();
13263        store.sync_all().unwrap();
13264        let after = store.stats();
13265        assert_eq!(after.delta_appends - before.delta_appends, 0);
13266        assert_eq!(after.checkpoint_writes - before.checkpoint_writes, 1);
13267        assert!(
13268            store.delta_state.lock().log_bytes < 100,
13269            "the rotation starts a fresh log"
13270        );
13271        drop(store);
13272
13273        let reopened = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
13274        for id in 0..400u32 {
13275            assert!(reopened
13276                .get(&collection, &batch_node(id))
13277                .unwrap()
13278                .is_some());
13279        }
13280        drop(reopened);
13281        fs::remove_dir_all(dir).unwrap();
13282    }

13284    /// A pending whole-index snapshot that cannot fit is refused from its
13285    /// projected length while the batch is being built, before the index is
13286    /// serialized, and the projection is the length the batch would have had.
13287    #[test]
13288    fn a_snapshot_that_cannot_fit_is_refused_before_it_is_serialized() {
13289        let dir = test_dir("v3_snapshot_preflight");
13290        let store = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
13291        let collection = [0xD6; 16];
13292        store
13293            .put(&collection, &batch_node(1), &NodeData::from_slice(b"one"))
13294            .unwrap();
13295        store.sync_all().unwrap();
13296        store.delta_log_cap_override.store(1024, Ordering::Relaxed);
13297        store.invalidate_delta_log(&collection);
13298
13299        let state = store.delta_state.lock().clone();
13300        let Err(error) = store.build_v3_pending_batch(&state, false) else {
13301            panic!("the snapshot must not fit under a 1 KiB cap");
13302        };
13303        let detail = PackfileStorage::delta_batch_too_large(&error).expect("a too-large batch");
13304        let blob_len = store
13305            .collections_read()
13306            .get(&collection)
13307            .map(|room| room.load_full().index.serialized_len())
13308            .unwrap();
13309        let expected =
13310            delta::v3_empty_batch_len() + delta::v3_snapshot_frame_len(blob_len).unwrap();
13311        assert_eq!(detail.batch_bytes, expected);
13312        assert_eq!(detail.cap, 1024);
13313
13314        // With the real cap the same pending snapshot builds.
13315        store.delta_log_cap_override.store(0, Ordering::Relaxed);
13316        assert!(store.build_v3_pending_batch(&state, false).is_ok());
13317        drop(store);
13318        fs::remove_dir_all(dir).unwrap();
13319    }

13321    /// A delta error that is not "does not fit" stays a failure, not a rotation.

13323    fn only_a_batch_that_does_not_fit_counts_as_a_planned_rotation() {

13334    /// A log that has grown to the rotation length is replaced by a checkpoint
13335    /// at the next sync, on purpose and before the cap; below it, the append
13336    /// path is untouched.
13337    #[test]
13338    fn a_delta_log_is_rotated_before_it_reaches_the_cap() {
13339        let dir = test_dir("delta_log_rotation");
13340        let store = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
13341        let collection = [0xD4; 16];
13342        store
13343            .put(&collection, &distinct_id(1), &NodeData::from_slice(b"base"))
13344            .unwrap();
13345        store.sync_all().unwrap();
13346
13347        // Well under the rotation length: an ordinary append.
13348        store
13349            .put(
13350                &collection,
13351                &distinct_id(2),
13352                &NodeData::from_slice(b"below"),
13353            )
13354            .unwrap();
13355        let before = store.stats();
13356        store.sync_all().unwrap();
13357        let after = store.stats();
13358        assert_eq!(after.delta_appends - before.delta_appends, 1);
13359        assert_eq!(after.checkpoint_writes - before.checkpoint_writes, 0);
13360
13361        // At the rotation length: a checkpoint, with no failed append first.
13362        let at = store.delta_log_rotate_bytes();
13363        store.delta_state.lock().log_bytes = at;
13364        store
13365            .put(&collection, &distinct_id(3), &NodeData::from_slice(b"at"))
13366            .unwrap();
13367        let before = store.stats();
13368        store.sync_all().unwrap();
13369        let after = store.stats();
13370        assert_eq!(after.delta_appends - before.delta_appends, 0);
13371        assert_eq!(after.checkpoint_writes - before.checkpoint_writes, 1);
13372        assert!(
13373            store.delta_state.lock().log_bytes < store.delta_log_rotate_bytes(),
13374            "the rotation starts a fresh log"
13375        );
13376        drop(store);
13377        let reopened = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
13378        for id in 1..=3 {
13379            assert!(reopened
13380                .get(&collection, &distinct_id(id))
13381                .unwrap()
13382                .is_some());
13383        }
13384        drop(reopened);
13385        fs::remove_dir_all(dir).unwrap();
13386    }

13388    /// A full checkpoint records where its time went. The phases are disjoint
13389    /// stretches of one call, so they never add up to more than it; what they do
13390    /// not cover is reported by `unaccounted`.
13391    #[test]
13392    fn a_checkpoint_records_a_phase_breakdown() {

13398            .unwrap();

13401        assert!(breakdown.total > Duration::ZERO);

13403            breakdown.unaccounted() <= breakdown.total,

13405        );
13406        assert!(breakdown.write > Duration::ZERO, "the write fsyncs");
13407        drop(store);

13409    }

13468    #[test]
13469    fn checkpoint_rewrite_budget_defers_invalidated_rewrites() {
13470        const ROUNDS: u8 = 5;
13471        let dir = test_dir("checkpoint_rewrite_budget");
13472        let store = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
13473        // Once a rewrite has run, defer the next for an hour; no size budget.
13474        store.set_checkpoint_rewrite_budget(Duration::from_secs(3600), 0);
13475        let before = store.stats();
13476        let mut written: Vec<([u8; 16], [u8; 16], Vec<u8>)> = Vec::new();
13477        for round in 0..ROUNDS {
13478            let mut cid = [0u8; 16];
13479            cid[0] = 0xB0;
13480            cid[1] = round;
13481            for i in 0..3u8 {
13482                let id = distinct_id(i);
13483                let value = format!("budget round {round} node {i}").into_bytes();
13484                store
13485                    .put(&cid, &id, &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from(value.clone())))
13486                    .unwrap();
13487                written.push((cid, id, value));
13488            }
13489            store.sync_all().unwrap();
13490        }
13491        let after = store.stats();
13492        let checkpoints = after.checkpoint_writes - before.checkpoint_writes;
13493        let skips = after.checkpoint_skips - before.checkpoint_skips;
13494        eprintln!(
13495            "rewrite-budget impact over {ROUNDS} barriers: checkpoint_writes={checkpoints} \
13496             checkpoint_skips={skips} delta_appends={}",
13497            after.delta_appends - before.delta_appends
13498        );
13499        assert_eq!(
13500            checkpoints, 1,
13501            "one baseline rewrite, then the budget defers"
13502        );
13503        assert_eq!(
13504            skips, 0,
13505            "v3 snapshots avoid checkpoint skips for ordinary structural changes"
13506        );
13507        assert_eq!(
13508            after.delta_appends - before.delta_appends,
13509            u64::from(ROUNDS - 1)
13510        );
13511        drop(store);
13512
13513        // The v3 log replays the collection snapshots on reopen.
13514        let reopened = PackfileStorage::open(dir).unwrap();
13515        assert_eq!(
13516            reopened
13517                .open_timings()
13518                .expect("open must record timings")
13519                .path,
13520            OpenPath::Checkpoint,
13521            "the checkpoint plus v3 log should avoid a full scan"
13522        );
13523        for (cid, id, expected) in &written {
13524            let got = reopened
13525                .get(cid, id)
13526                .unwrap()
13527                .expect("record survives the rescan");
13528            assert_eq!(got.bytes.as_ref(), expected.as_slice());
13529        }
13530    }

13532    /// With a journal enabled, `sync` makes the WAL group commit the
13533    /// durability point rather than the per-shard pack fsyncs.
13534    #[test]
13535    fn journal_sync_routes_durability_through_wal() {
13536        let dir = test_dir("journal_sync_routing");
13537        let store = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
13538        store.enable_journal(dir.join("wal.bin")).unwrap();
13539        let id = distinct_id(7);
13540        store
13541            .put(
13542                &TEST_COLLECTION,
13543                &id,
13544                &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"wal")),
13545            )
13546            .unwrap();
13547        store.sync_all().unwrap();
13548        let timings = store.sync_timings().expect("sync must record timings");
13549        assert!(
13550            timings.wal > Duration::ZERO,
13551            "the journal group commit is the durability point"
13552        );
13553        assert_eq!(
13554            timings.pack_fsync,
13555            Duration::ZERO,
13556            "the barrier path must not fsync pack shards with a WAL"
13557        );
13558        assert_eq!(timings.journal_sync_calls, 1);
13559        assert!(timings.journal_records >= 1);
13560        assert!(timings.journal_fsync > Duration::ZERO);
13561        assert!(
13562            timings.journal_lock_wait + timings.journal_fsync <= timings.wal,
13563            "reported journal phases cannot exceed the WAL phase"
13564        );
13565        let stats = store.stats();
13566        assert_eq!(stats.publish_calls, 1);
13567        assert_eq!(stats.sync_diagnostics.worst_syncs.len(), 1);
13568        assert_eq!(stats.sync_diagnostics.peak_journal_in_flight, 1);
13569        assert_eq!(
13570            stats
13571                .sync_diagnostics
13572                .fsync_latency
13573                .buckets
13574                .iter()
13575                .sum::<u64>(),
13576            1
13577        );
13578        assert_eq!(
13579            stats
13580                .sync_diagnostics
13581                .lock_wait_latency
13582                .buckets
13583                .iter()
13584                .sum::<u64>(),
13585            1
13586        );
13587        let interval = store.take_sync_diagnostics();
13588        assert_eq!(interval.peak_journal_in_flight, 1);
13589        assert!(interval.max_journal_fsync > Duration::ZERO);
13590        assert_eq!(interval.max_journal_lock_wait, timings.journal_lock_wait);
13591        assert_eq!(interval.worst_syncs.len(), 1);
13592        assert_eq!(
13593            interval.fsync_latency.buckets.iter().sum::<u64>(),
13594            1,
13595            "taking diagnostics must return the completed interval"
13596        );
13597        assert_eq!(
13598            store.take_sync_diagnostics(),
13599            SyncDiagnosticsSnapshot::default(),
13600            "taking diagnostics must reset only the diagnostics interval"
13601        );
13602        assert_eq!(
13603            store.stats().sync_totals.calls,
13604            1,
13605            "taking diagnostics must preserve cumulative sync totals"
13606        );
13607        assert!(store.get(&TEST_COLLECTION, &id).unwrap().is_some());
13608        assert!(store.journal().expect("journal enabled").committed_lsn() >= 1);
13609    }

13611    /// A mutation committed to the journal after the last checkpoint is
13612    /// re-applied by `replay_journal` on a fresh open.
13613    #[test]
13614    fn journal_replays_post_checkpoint_mutations_on_reopen() {
13615        let dir = test_dir("journal_replay");
13616        let journal_path = dir.join("wal.bin");
13617        let id = distinct_id(9);
13618        {
13619            let store = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
13620            store.enable_journal(&journal_path).unwrap();
13621            store
13622                .put(
13623                    &TEST_COLLECTION,
13624                    &distinct_id(8),
13625                    &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"checkpointed")),
13626                )
13627                .unwrap();
13628            store.sync_all().unwrap();
13629            // A second, non-structural put: the next sync's delta path does not
13630            // write a checkpoint, so this mutation stays journal-only.
13631            store
13632                .put(
13633                    &TEST_COLLECTION,
13634                    &id,
13635                    &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"wal-only")),
13636                )
13637                .unwrap();
13638            store.sync_all().unwrap();
13639        }
13640        let reopened = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
13641        reopened.enable_journal(&journal_path).unwrap();
13642        let replayed = reopened.replay_journal().unwrap();
13643        assert!(
13644            replayed >= 1,
13645            "the post-checkpoint mutation must be replayed"
13646        );
13647        assert!(reopened.get(&TEST_COLLECTION, &id).unwrap().is_some());
13648    }

13650    /// A single-pool journal may reclaim an older committed group while a
13651    /// later group remains in the segment. Reopening that same store must
13652    /// still replay the surviving suffix.
13653    #[test]
13654    fn single_pool_reclaim_then_replay_surviving_group() {
13655        let dir = test_dir("single_pool_reclaim_replay");
13656        let journal_path = dir.join("wal.bin");
13657        let reclaimed_id = distinct_id(10);
13658        let surviving_id = distinct_id(11);
13659        {
13660            let store = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
13661            store.enable_journal(&journal_path).unwrap();
13662            store
13663                .put(
13664                    &TEST_COLLECTION,
13665                    &distinct_id(8),
13666                    &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"checkpointed")),
13667                )
13668                .unwrap();
13669            store.sync_all().unwrap();
13670
13671            store
13672                .put(
13673                    &TEST_COLLECTION,
13674                    &reclaimed_id,
13675                    &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"reclaimed")),
13676                )
13677                .unwrap();
13678            let reclaimed_lsn = store.journal().unwrap().published_lsn();
13679            store.sync_all().unwrap();
13680
13681            store
13682                .put(
13683                    &TEST_COLLECTION,
13684                    &surviving_id,
13685                    &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"surviving")),
13686                )
13687                .unwrap();
13688            store.sync_all().unwrap();
13689            let journal = store.journal().unwrap();
13690            let surviving_lsn = journal.published_lsn();
13691            assert!(surviving_lsn > reclaimed_lsn);
13692            journal.reclaim_through(reclaimed_lsn).unwrap();
13693        }
13694
13695        let reopened = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
13696        reopened.enable_journal(&journal_path).unwrap();
13697        assert_eq!(reopened.replay_journal().unwrap(), 1);
13698        assert!(reopened
13699            .get(&TEST_COLLECTION, &surviving_id)
13700            .unwrap()
13701            .is_some());
13702        assert!(reopened
13703            .get(&TEST_COLLECTION, &reclaimed_id)
13704            .unwrap()
13705            .is_some());
13706    }

13708    /// A checkpoint must bound journal replay by the LSN that is actually
13709    /// *committed*, never the published one. A concurrent put can publish
13710    /// above the last WAL commit, and LSNs above `committed_lsn` are discarded
13711    /// and reused after a crash -- recording one as covered would make a
13712    /// reopen skip a future mutation that reuses it. Drive the full-checkpoint
13713    /// path directly so a pending (published, uncommitted) put is live without
13714    /// the barrier commit that a real `sync` would have done first.
13715    #[test]
13716    fn checkpoint_records_the_committed_journal_lsn() {
13717        let dir = test_dir("journal_checkpoint_committed_lsn");
13718        let journal_path = dir.join("wal.bin");
13719        let store = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
13720        store.enable_journal(&journal_path).unwrap();
13721
13722        // Commit one mutation so the journal has a non-zero durable prefix.
13723        store
13724            .put(
13725                &TEST_COLLECTION,
13726                &distinct_id(41),
13727                &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"committed")),
13728            )
13729            .unwrap();
13730        store.sync_all().unwrap();
13731        let journal = store.journal().expect("journal enabled");
13732        let committed = journal.committed_lsn();
13733        assert_eq!(
13734            journal.published_lsn(),
13735            committed,
13736            "test setup: a completed sync leaves nothing published-but-uncommitted"
13737        );
13738        assert!(
13739            committed > 0,
13740            "test setup: the first sync must commit an LSN"
13741        );
13742
13743        // Publish a second mutation into a new collection WITHOUT committing:
13744        // this is the state a concurrent `put` leaves behind after a barrier.
13745        store
13746            .put(
13747                &SECOND_COLLECTION,
13748                &distinct_id(42),
13749                &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"pending")),
13750            )
13751            .unwrap();
13752        let journal = store.journal().expect("journal enabled");
13753        let published = journal.published_lsn();
13754        assert!(
13755            published > journal.committed_lsn(),
13756            "test setup: the second put must be published but uncommitted"
13757        );
13758
13759        // Run the full-checkpoint path as a sync would, but without the
13760        // barrier that would advance `committed_lsn` past the pending put.
13761        store
13762            .persist_index_checkpoint()
13763            .expect("checkpoint must succeed");
13764
13765        let covered = PackfileStorage::read_journal_lsn(&dir);
13766        assert_eq!(
13767            covered, committed,
13768            "the checkpoint must record the committed LSN, not a published-only one"
13769        );
13770        assert!(
13771            covered < published,
13772            "recording the published LSN would let a reopen skip a reused LSN"
13773        );
13774    }

13776    /// Hold the next background checkpoint tail until the returned sender is
13777    /// used or dropped; with `fail` the tail then errors instead of installing.
13778    fn hold_next_checkpoint_tail(
13779        store: &PackfileStorage,
13780        fail: bool,
13781    ) -> std::sync::mpsc::Sender<()> {
13782        store.hold_next_checkpoint_tail(fail)
13783    }

13807    /// Copy every file of `from` into a fresh directory `name`, the disk a crash
13808    /// at this instant would leave (files here are all fsynced or rebuildable).
13809    fn copy_store_dir(from: &Path, name: &str) -> PathBuf {
13810        let to = test_dir(name);
13811        for entry in fs::read_dir(from).unwrap() {
13812            let entry = entry.unwrap();
13813            if entry.file_type().unwrap().is_file() {
13814                fs::copy(entry.path(), to.join(entry.file_name())).unwrap();
13815            }
13816        }
13817        to
13818    }

13820    /// The first sync of a store that opened without a checkpoint takes the full
13821    /// path. While its tail is held the WAL is neither covered nor reclaimed, a
13822    /// second sync starts no second checkpoint, everything synced in the window
13823    /// survives a crash at that instant, and releasing the tail installs the
13824    /// image and advances coverage.
13825    #[test]
13826    fn a_background_checkpoint_holds_the_wal_until_its_image_is_durable() {
13827        let dir = test_dir("bg_checkpoint_holds_wal");
13828        let journal_path = dir.join("wal.bin");
13829        let store = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
13830        store.enable_journal(&journal_path).unwrap();
13831        store.set_background_checkpoint(true);
13832        let covered_before = store.durable_coverage();
13833        put_bytes(&store, 1);
13834        let release = hold_next_checkpoint_tail(&store, false);
13835        store.sync().unwrap();
13836        assert!(store.checkpoint_in_flight(), "the tail runs on a worker");
13837        assert_eq!(store.durable_coverage(), covered_before);
13838
13839        put_bytes(&store, 2);
13840        store.sync().unwrap();
13841        assert!(store.checkpoint_in_flight(), "one worker, not two");
13842        assert_eq!(
13843            store.durable_coverage(),
13844            covered_before,
13845            "no coverage before the image is durable"
13846        );
13847
13848        // A crash now finds no new image, the old (absent) one, and the WAL.
13849        let crashed = copy_store_dir(&dir, "bg_checkpoint_holds_wal_crash");
13850        let after_crash = PackfileStorage::open(crashed.clone()).unwrap();
13851        after_crash.enable_journal(crashed.join("wal.bin")).unwrap();
13852        after_crash.replay_journal().unwrap();
13853        assert_all_present(&after_crash, &[1, 2]);
13854        drop(after_crash);
13855
13856        drop(release);
13857        store.wait_for_checkpoint();
13858        assert!(!store.checkpoint_in_flight());
13859        assert!(
13860            store.durable_coverage() > covered_before,
13861            "the installed image advances coverage"
13862        );
13863        assert!(store.checkpoint_breakdown().is_some());
13864        drop(store);
13865        let reopened = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
13866        reopened.enable_journal(&journal_path).unwrap();
13867        reopened.replay_journal().unwrap();
13868        assert_all_present(&reopened, &[1, 2]);
13869    }

13871    /// A collection created after the handoff, while the tail is held, is in
13872    /// neither the captured image nor a log the image names. It must survive a
13873    /// crash before the tail finishes and a reopen after it: the creation lock
13874    /// is released at the handoff on the strength of this.
13875    #[test]
13876    fn a_collection_created_during_a_background_checkpoint_is_not_lost() {
13877        let dir = test_dir("bg_checkpoint_new_collection");
13878        let journal_path = dir.join("wal.bin");

13880        store.enable_journal(&journal_path).unwrap();
13881        store.set_background_checkpoint(true);
13882        put_bytes(&store, 1);
13883        let release = hold_next_checkpoint_tail(&store, false);
13884        store.sync().unwrap();
13885        assert!(store.checkpoint_in_flight());
13886        store
13887            .put(
13888                &SECOND_COLLECTION,
13889                &distinct_id(9),
13890                &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"late")),
13891            )
13892            .unwrap();
13893        store.sync().unwrap();
13894        let crashed = copy_store_dir(&dir, "bg_checkpoint_new_collection_crash");
13895        let after_crash = PackfileStorage::open(crashed.clone()).unwrap();
13896        after_crash.enable_journal(crashed.join("wal.bin")).unwrap();
13897        after_crash.replay_journal().unwrap();
13898        assert!(after_crash
13899            .get(&SECOND_COLLECTION, &distinct_id(9))
13900            .unwrap()
13901            .is_some());
13902        drop(after_crash);
13903        drop(release);
13904        store.wait_for_checkpoint();
13905        drop(store);
13906        let reopened = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
13907        reopened.enable_journal(&journal_path).unwrap();
13908        reopened.replay_journal().unwrap();
13909        assert_all_present(&reopened, &[1]);
13910        assert!(reopened
13911            .get(&SECOND_COLLECTION, &distinct_id(9))
13912            .unwrap()
13913            .is_some());
13914    }

13916    /// A failed tail leaves the old state valid, reports, and the next sync
13917    /// rewrites the checkpoint instead of appending to the orphaned epoch.
13918    #[test]
13919    fn a_failed_background_checkpoint_keeps_the_wal_and_is_retried() {
13920        let dir = test_dir("bg_checkpoint_fails");
13921        let journal_path = dir.join("wal.bin");
13922        let store = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
13923        store.enable_journal(&journal_path).unwrap();
13924        store.set_background_checkpoint(true);
13925        put_bytes(&store, 1);
13926        let release = hold_next_checkpoint_tail(&store, true);
13927        store.sync().unwrap();
13928        assert!(store.checkpoint_in_flight());
13929        drop(release);
13930        store.wait_for_checkpoint();
13931        assert!(!store.checkpoint_in_flight());
13932        assert_eq!(store.durable_coverage(), 0, "a failed tail claims nothing");
13933        assert!(
13934            store.delta_state.lock().base_fingerprint.is_none(),
13935            "the orphaned epoch is forgotten"
13936        );
13937        put_bytes(&store, 2);
13938        store.sync().unwrap();
13939        store.wait_for_checkpoint();
13940        assert!(store.durable_coverage() > 0, "the retry installed an image");
13941        drop(store);
13942        let reopened = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
13943        reopened.enable_journal(&journal_path).unwrap();
13944        reopened.replay_journal().unwrap();
13945        assert_all_present(&reopened, &[1, 2]);
13946    }

13949    /// Near the WAL cap a sync waits for the tail instead of letting it run on
13950    /// with reclaim suppressed.
13951    #[test]
13952    fn a_sync_in_the_wal_emergency_zone_waits_for_the_tail() {
13953        let dir = test_dir("bg_checkpoint_emergency");
13954        let journal_path = dir.join("wal.bin");
13955        let store = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
13956        store.enable_journal(&journal_path).unwrap();
13957        store.set_background_checkpoint(true);
13958        put_bytes(&store, 1);
13959        let release = hold_next_checkpoint_tail(&store, false);
13960        store.sync().unwrap();
13961        assert!(store.checkpoint_in_flight());
13962        let journal = store.journal().expect("journal enabled");
13963        journal.set_segment_cap(journal.segment_len() + journal.segment_len() / 4);
13964        assert!(journal.in_emergency_zone());
13965        put_bytes(&store, 2);
13966        let releaser = std::thread::spawn(move || {
13967            std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(100));
13968            drop(release);
13969        });
13970        store.sync().unwrap();
13971        releaser.join().unwrap();
13972        assert!(
13973            !store.checkpoint_in_flight(),
13974            "the sync had to wait for the tail"
13975        );
13976        assert!(store.durable_coverage() > 0);
13977    }

13979    #[test]
13980    fn test_swizzle_callback() {
13981        static SWIZZLE_CALLS: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);
13982        static CACHED_CHILDREN_FOUND: AtomicU64 = AtomicU64::new(0);
13983
13984        fn test_swizzle(
13985            data: &NodeData,
13986            children: &[NodeId],
13987            cached: &[Option<Arc<NodeData>>],
13988        ) -> NodeData {
13989            SWIZZLE_CALLS.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
13990            assert_eq!(children.len(), 2);
13991            for entry in cached {
13992                if entry.is_some() {
13993                    CACHED_CHILDREN_FOUND.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
13994                }
13995            }
13996            data.clone()
13997        }
13998
13999        let dir = test_dir("swizzle");
14000        let store = PackfileStorage::open_with_swizzle(dir, 100, test_swizzle).unwrap();
14001
14002        let parent_id = [0x10u8; 16];
14003        let child_a = [0x20u8; 16];
14004        let child_b = [0x30u8; 16];
14005
14006        let data_a = NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"child A"));
14007        let data_b = NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"child B"));
14008        let parent_data = NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"parent with children"));
14009
14010        store.put(&TEST_COLLECTION, &child_a, &data_a).unwrap();
14011        store.put(&TEST_COLLECTION, &child_b, &data_b).unwrap();
14012        store
14013            .put(&TEST_COLLECTION, &parent_id, &parent_data)
14014            .unwrap();
14015
14016        if let Some(gen) = store.generation(&TEST_COLLECTION) {
14017            gen.cache.clear();
14018        }
14019        store.put(&TEST_COLLECTION, &child_a, &data_a).unwrap();
14020        store.put(&TEST_COLLECTION, &child_b, &data_b).unwrap();
14021
14022        let extract = |_data: &NodeData| -> Vec<NodeId> { vec![child_a, child_b] };
14023
14024        let result = store
14025            .get_swizzled(&TEST_COLLECTION, &parent_id, extract)
14026            .unwrap();
14027        assert!(result.is_some());
14028        let node_ref = result.unwrap();
14029        assert!(node_ref.is_resolved());
14030        assert_eq!(node_ref.structural_hash(), &parent_id);
14031
14032        assert_eq!(SWIZZLE_CALLS.load(Ordering::Relaxed), 1);
14033        assert_eq!(CACHED_CHILDREN_FOUND.load(Ordering::Relaxed), 2);
14034    }

14036    #[test]
14037    fn test_sync() {
14038        let dir = test_dir("sync");
14039        let store = PackfileStorage::open(dir).unwrap();
14040        store
14041            .put(
14042                &TEST_COLLECTION,
14043                &[0xAA; 16],
14044                &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"hi")),
14045            )
14046            .unwrap();
14047        store.sync().unwrap();
14048    }

14050    #[test]
14051    fn test_probe_reopen_first_append_sync_path_no_growth() {
14052        // Discriminates reopen-materialization cost from real capacity-growth
14053        // cost: build to a load well under the 75% grow threshold (so the
14054        // post-reopen append batch cannot trigger `index_grow_count`), then
14055        // reopen and append. Reopen should continue the v3 epoch directly.
14056        let dir = test_dir("probe_reopen_sync_no_growth");
14057        let total = 2000u32; // 2032 / 4096 is well under the 75% grow threshold.
14058        build_reopen_probe_checkpoint(&dir, total);
14059        {
14060            let store = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
14061            let before = store.stats();
14062            reopen_probe_put_range(&store, total..(total + 32), 32, |_| {
14063                NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"y"))
14064            });
14065            let after_put = store.stats();
14066            let d = store.delta_state.lock();
14067            let room = store.generation(&REOPEN_PROBE_COLLECTION).unwrap();
14068            eprintln!(
14069                "AFTER REOPEN PUT: cap={} len={} load={:.3} clones+={} grows+={} invalids+={} | pending={:?}",
14070                room.index.capacity(),
14071                room.index.len(),
14072                reopen_probe_load_factor(&room),
14073                after_put.put_many_clone_path_calls - before.put_many_clone_path_calls,
14074                after_put.index_grow_count - before.index_grow_count,
14075                after_put.delta_invalidations - before.delta_invalidations,
14076                d.pending.keys().collect::<Vec<_>>(),
14077            );
14078            assert_eq!(
14079                after_put.index_grow_count - before.index_grow_count,
14080                0,
14081                "test setup invariant violated: this batch must not trigger real growth"
14082            );
14083            assert_eq!(
14084                after_put.delta_invalidations - before.delta_invalidations,
14085                0
14086            );
14087            assert!(matches!(
14088                d.pending.get(&REOPEN_PROBE_COLLECTION),
14089                Some(PendingDelta::Redo(_))
14090            ));
14091            drop(d);
14092            store.sync().unwrap();
14093            let st = store.stats();
14094            let ts = store.sync_timings().unwrap();
14095            eprintln!(
14096                "REOPEN SYNC TIMINGS (no growth): checkpoint={:?} delta={:?} total={:?}",
14097                ts.checkpoint, ts.delta_log, ts.total
14098            );
14099            eprintln!(
14100                "REOPEN SYNC STATS (no growth): ckpt_writes+={} delta_appends+={}",
14101                st.checkpoint_writes - before.checkpoint_writes,
14102                st.delta_appends - before.delta_appends,
14103            );
14104            assert_eq!(st.checkpoint_writes - before.checkpoint_writes, 0);
14105            assert_eq!(st.delta_appends - before.delta_appends, 1);
14106            assert_eq!(ts.checkpoint, std::time::Duration::ZERO);
14107            assert!(ts.delta_log > std::time::Duration::ZERO);
14108        }
14109    }
14110
14111    const REOPEN_PROBE_COLLECTION: [u8; 16] = [0x11; 16];
14112
14113    fn reopen_probe_id(i: u32) -> NodeId {
14114        let mut id = [0u8; 16];
14115        id[0..4].copy_from_slice(&i.to_le_bytes());
14116        id[8..12].copy_from_slice(&(i ^ 0x9E37_79B9).to_le_bytes());
14117        id
14118    }
14119
14120    fn reopen_probe_payload(i: u32) -> NodeData {
14121        let mut payload = vec![0u8; 1024];
14122        let seed = u64::from(i).wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15) ^ 0xDEAD_BEEF;
14123        payload[..2].copy_from_slice(&seed.to_le_bytes()[..2]);
14124        NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from(payload))
14125    }
14126
14127    fn reopen_probe_put_range(
14128        store: &PackfileStorage,
14129        range: std::ops::Range<u32>,
14130        batch_size: usize,
14131        payload: impl Fn(u32) -> NodeData,
14132    ) {
14133        let mut batch = Vec::with_capacity(batch_size);
14134        for i in range {
14135            batch.push((reopen_probe_id(i), payload(i)));
14136            if batch.len() == batch_size {
14137                store.put_many(&REOPEN_PROBE_COLLECTION, &batch).unwrap();
14138                batch.clear();
14139            }
14140        }
14141        if !batch.is_empty() {
14142            store.put_many(&REOPEN_PROBE_COLLECTION, &batch).unwrap();
14143        }
14144    }
14145
14146    fn reopen_probe_load_factor(room: &RoomGeneration) -> f64 {
14147        f64::from(u32::try_from(room.index.len()).expect("probe index length fits in u32"))
14148            / f64::from(room.index.capacity())
14149    }
14150
14151    fn build_reopen_probe_checkpoint(dir: &std::path::Path, total: u32) {
14152        let store = PackfileStorage::open_with_cache_and_policies(
14153            dir.to_path_buf(),
14154            0,
14155            true,
14156            packfile::ChecksumPolicy::Full,
14157        )
14158        .unwrap()
14159        .with_append_policy(shard::AppendPolicy::buffered());
14160        reopen_probe_put_range(&store, 0..total, 256, reopen_probe_payload);
14161        store.sync_all().unwrap();
14162        let stats = store.stats();
14163        let room = store.generation(&REOPEN_PROBE_COLLECTION).unwrap();
14164        eprintln!(
14165            "BUILD done: cap={} len={} load={:.3} gen={} | clones={} grows={} ckpt_writes={} delta_appends={}",
14166            room.index.capacity(), room.index.len(), reopen_probe_load_factor(&room), room.generation,
14167            stats.put_many_clone_path_calls, stats.index_grow_count, stats.checkpoint_writes,
14168            stats.delta_appends,
14169        );
14170    }

14173    fn test_probe_reopen_first_append_sync_path() {

14177        {

14179            let d = store.delta_state.lock();

14185            );
14186            let room = store.generation(&REOPEN_PROBE_COLLECTION).unwrap();
14187            eprintln!(
14188                "REOPEN room: cap={} len={} load={:.3} gen={} base_gen={:?}",
14189                room.index.capacity(),
14190                room.index.len(),
14191                reopen_probe_load_factor(&room),
14192                room.generation,
14193                d.base_generations.get(&REOPEN_PROBE_COLLECTION),
14194            );
14195            drop(d);
14196            drop(room);
14197
14198            let before = store.stats();
14199            reopen_probe_put_range(&store, total..(total + 32), 32, |_| {
14200                NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"y"))
14201            });
14202            let after_put = store.stats();
14203            let d = store.delta_state.lock();
14204            eprintln!(
14205                "AFTER REOPEN PUT: clones+={} grows+={} invalids+={} | pending={:?}",
14206                after_put.put_many_clone_path_calls - before.put_many_clone_path_calls,
14207                after_put.index_grow_count - before.index_grow_count,
14208                after_put.delta_invalidations - before.delta_invalidations,
14209                d.pending.keys().collect::<Vec<_>>(),

14211            assert_eq!(
14212                after_put.put_many_clone_path_calls - before.put_many_clone_path_calls,

14214            );
14215            assert_eq!(after_put.index_grow_count - before.index_grow_count, 1);
14216            assert_eq!(
14217                after_put.delta_invalidations - before.delta_invalidations,
14218                0,
14219                "growth of a reopened index is logical, not a snapshot"
14220            );
14221            assert!(matches!(
14222                d.pending.get(&REOPEN_PROBE_COLLECTION),
14223                Some(PendingDelta::Redo(_))
14224            ));
14225            drop(d);
14226            store.sync().unwrap();
14227            let st = store.stats();
14228            let ts = store.sync_timings().unwrap();
14229            eprintln!(
14230                "REOPEN SYNC TIMINGS: flush={:?} fsync={:?} checkpoint={:?} delta={:?} total={:?}",
14231                ts.pack_flush, ts.pack_fsync, ts.checkpoint, ts.delta_log, ts.total
14232            );
14233            eprintln!(
14234                "REOPEN SYNC STATS: ckpt_writes+={} delta_appends+={}",
14235                st.checkpoint_writes - before.checkpoint_writes,
14236                st.delta_appends - before.delta_appends,
14237            );
14238            assert_eq!(st.checkpoint_writes - before.checkpoint_writes, 0);
14239            assert_eq!(st.delta_appends - before.delta_appends, 1);
14240            assert_eq!(ts.checkpoint, std::time::Duration::ZERO);
14241            assert!(ts.delta_log > std::time::Duration::ZERO);
14242
14243            reopen_probe_put_range(&store, (total + 32)..(total + 288), 256, |_| {
14244                NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"z"))
14245            });
14246            store.sync().unwrap();
14247            let ts = store.sync_timings().unwrap();
14248            eprintln!(
14249                "SECOND SYNC TIMINGS: checkpoint={:?} delta={:?} total={:?}",
14250                ts.checkpoint, ts.delta_log, ts.total
14251            );
14252            assert_eq!(ts.checkpoint, std::time::Duration::ZERO);
14253            assert!(ts.delta_log > std::time::Duration::ZERO);
14254        }
14255        let reopened = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
14256        for i in total..(total + 288) {
14257            let got = reopened
14258                .get(&REOPEN_PROBE_COLLECTION, &reopen_probe_id(i))
14259                .unwrap()
14260                .expect("snapshot and following incrementals survive reopen");
14261            assert_eq!(got.bytes.as_ref(), if i < total + 32 { b"y" } else { b"z" });
14262        }
14263    }

14333    #[test]
14334    fn test_runtime_stats_counters_round_trip() {
14335        let dir = test_dir("runtime_stats_counters");
14336        let store = PackfileStorage::open(dir).unwrap();
14337
14338        // Fresh store: every counter starts at zero (open_count counts the
14339        // one store assembled, not work).
14340        let snapshot = store.stats();
14341        assert_eq!(snapshot.open_count, 1);
14342        assert_eq!(snapshot.put_calls, 0);
14343        assert_eq!(snapshot.put_many_calls, 0);
14344        assert_eq!(snapshot.sync_calls, 0);
14345        assert_eq!(snapshot.get_calls, 0);
14346
14347        // Read counters are opt-in: with stats disabled a get is invisible.
14348        store
14349            .put(
14350                &TEST_COLLECTION,
14351                &[0u8; 16],
14352                &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from("solo")),
14353            )
14354            .unwrap();
14355        assert_eq!(store.stats().put_calls, 1);
14356        assert!(store.get(&TEST_COLLECTION, &[0u8; 16]).unwrap().is_some());
14357        assert_eq!(store.stats().get_calls, 0);
14358        assert_eq!(store.stats().get_misses, 0);
14359
14360        // Enable read tracking, then a hit and a miss both count.
14361        store.set_stats_enabled(true);
14362        assert!(store.get(&TEST_COLLECTION, &[0u8; 16]).unwrap().is_some());
14363        assert!(store
14364            .get(&TEST_COLLECTION, &[0xFFu8; 16])
14365            .unwrap()
14366            .is_none());
14367        let snapshot = store.stats();
14368        assert_eq!(snapshot.get_calls, 2);
14369        assert_eq!(snapshot.get_misses, 1);
14370        assert_eq!(snapshot.get_latency.calls, 2);
14371        assert!(snapshot.get_latency.total > std::time::Duration::ZERO);
14372        assert!(snapshot.get_latency.max > std::time::Duration::ZERO);
14373        assert!(snapshot.get_latency.max >= snapshot.get_latency.total / 2);
14374        assert!(snapshot.get_latency.max <= snapshot.get_latency.total);
14375        assert_eq!(snapshot.get_latency.buckets.iter().sum::<u64>(), 2);
14376
14377        // Batched writes against an already-materialized (non-mmap) index
14378        // mutate it in place and roll back via an undo log on failure,
14379        // rather than cloning -- so only the very first batch (which
14380        // creates the collection) pays the clone/materialize cost.
14381        let batches: Vec<Vec<(NodeId, NodeData)>> = (0..8u32)
14382            .map(|batch| {
14383                (0..8u32)
14384                    .map(|i| {
14385                        let mut id = [2u8; 16];
14386                        id[0..4].copy_from_slice(&batch.to_le_bytes());
14387                        id[4..8].copy_from_slice(&i.to_le_bytes());
14388                        (
14389                            id,
14390                            NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from(format!("b{batch}-{i}"))),
14391                        )
14392                    })
14393                    .collect()
14394            })
14395            .collect();
14396        for entries in &batches {
14397            store.put_many(&SECOND_COLLECTION, entries).unwrap();
14398        }
14399        let snapshot = store.stats();
14400        assert_eq!(snapshot.put_many_calls, 8);
14401        assert_eq!(snapshot.put_many_records, 64);
14402        assert!(snapshot.put_many_bytes > 0);
14403        // Only the first batch creates `SECOND_COLLECTION` (the `None` arm,
14404        // which always materializes); every later batch finds an
14405        // already-owned, non-mmap index and takes the in-place fast path.
14406        assert_eq!(snapshot.put_many_clone_path_calls, 1);
14407        assert_eq!(snapshot.put_many_fast_path_calls, 7);
14408        assert_eq!(snapshot.put_many_latency.calls, 8);
14409        assert_eq!(snapshot.put_many_latency.buckets.iter().sum::<u64>(), 8);
14410        // 64 distinct records into a floor-sized 64-slot index must cross the
14411        // grow threshold at least once.
14412        assert!(snapshot.index_grow_count >= 1);
14413        assert!(snapshot.index_clone_time > std::time::Duration::ZERO);
14414
14415        // Every put_many byte is the sum of entry payloads.
14416        let expected_bytes: u64 = batches
14417            .iter()
14418            .flatten()
14419            .map(|(_, data)| data.bytes.len() as u64)
14420            .sum();
14421        assert_eq!(snapshot.put_many_bytes, expected_bytes);
14422
14423        // reset_stats zeroes the runtime counters but not open_count.
14424        store.reset_stats();
14425        let snapshot = store.stats();
14426        assert_eq!(snapshot.open_count, 1);
14427        assert_eq!(snapshot.put_many_calls, 0);
14428        assert_eq!(snapshot.get_calls, 0);
14429        assert_eq!(snapshot.get_misses, 0);
14430        assert_eq!(snapshot.get_latency.calls, 0);
14431        assert_eq!(snapshot.get_latency.max, std::time::Duration::ZERO);
14432        assert_eq!(snapshot.put_many_latency.calls, 0);
14433
14434        // Sync accounting: the first (structurally invalidated) sync rewrites
14435        // the checkpoint; a later clean batch sync appends the delta log.
14436        store.sync().unwrap();
14437        assert_eq!(store.stats().sync_calls, 1);
14438        assert_eq!(store.stats().checkpoint_writes, 1);
14439        assert_eq!(store.stats().delta_appends, 0);
14440        store.put_many(&SECOND_COLLECTION, &batches[0]).unwrap();
14441        store.sync().unwrap();
14442        let snapshot = store.stats();
14443        assert_eq!(snapshot.sync_calls, 2);
14444        assert_eq!(snapshot.delta_appends, 1);
14445    }

14447    #[test]
14448    fn stats_surfaces_max_index_probe_len_and_dirty_lock_wait() {
14449        let dir = test_dir("stats_probe_len_and_lock_wait");
14450        let store = PackfileStorage::open(dir).unwrap();
14451
14452        // Fresh store, no writes: neither counter has anything to report.
14453        let snapshot = store.stats();
14454        assert_eq!(snapshot.max_index_probe_len, 0);
14455        assert_eq!(snapshot.dirty_lock_wait, std::time::Duration::ZERO);
14456
14457        for i in 0..20u8 {
14458            let mut id = [0u8; 16];
14459            id[0] = i;
14460            store
14461                .put(
14462                    &TEST_COLLECTION,
14463                    &id,
14464                    &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from(vec![i])),
14465                )
14466                .unwrap();
14467        }
14468        // A real sync exercises the dirty-set lock at least once; the exact
14469        // wait duration is unmeasurable deterministically (uncontended in a
14470        // single-threaded test), but the field must be wired through from
14471        // `ShardPool::dirty_lock_wait` and never decrease.
14472        store.sync().unwrap();
14473        let after_sync = store.stats();
14474        assert!(after_sync.dirty_lock_wait >= snapshot.dirty_lock_wait);
14475        // 20 inserts into a real index will very likely walk at least one
14476        // non-trivial probe chain, but this is observability, not a
14477        // guarantee -- assert the field is wired through and sane
14478        // (bounded by the collection's own capacity) rather than a specific
14479        // value.
14480        assert!(after_sync.max_index_probe_len < 1000);
14481    }

14515    #[test]
14516    fn test_read_scatter_counters_track_runs_span_and_bytes() {
14517        let dir = test_dir("read_scatter_counters");
14518        let writer = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
14519        let entries: Vec<_> = (0..8u8)
14520            .map(|value| {
14521                let mut id = [0u8; 16];
14522                id[0] = value;
14523                id[9] = value.wrapping_mul(37).wrapping_add(11);
14524                (id, NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from(vec![value; 16])))
14525            })
14526            .collect();
14527        writer.put_many(&TEST_COLLECTION, &entries).unwrap();
14528        writer.sync_all().unwrap();
14529        drop(writer);
14530
14531        let reader = PackfileStorage::open_read_only(dir).unwrap();
14532        reader.set_stats_enabled(true);
14533
14534        // One batch read of all eight records: the plan covers one shard,
14535        // its offsets are a single sequential run, and span/bytes record the
14536        // extent the batch drags in.
14537        let before = reader.stats();
14538        let ids: Vec<_> = entries.iter().map(|(id, _)| *id).collect();
14539        let results = reader.get_many(&TEST_COLLECTION, &ids).unwrap();
14540        assert_eq!(
14541            results.iter().filter(|value| value.is_some()).count(),
14542            entries.len()
14543        );
14544        let after = reader.stats();
14545        assert_eq!(
14546            after.get_many_shards_touched - before.get_many_shards_touched,
14547            1
14548        );
14549        assert_eq!(after.read_many_runs - before.read_many_runs, 1);
14550        assert!(after.read_many_span_bytes > before.read_many_span_bytes);
14551        assert!(after.candidate_frame_bytes > before.candidate_frame_bytes);
14552
14553        // A single `get` adds candidate frame bytes but is not a batch, so
14554        // the batch-scatter shape counters (`runs`, `span`) must not move.
14555        let single_before = reader.stats();
14556        reader
14557            .get(&TEST_COLLECTION, &entries[0].0)
14558            .unwrap()
14559            .unwrap();
14560        let single_after = reader.stats();
14561        assert!(single_after.candidate_frame_bytes > single_before.candidate_frame_bytes);
14562        assert_eq!(single_after.read_many_runs, single_before.read_many_runs);
14563        assert_eq!(
14564            single_after.read_many_span_bytes,
14565            single_before.read_many_span_bytes
14566        );
14567    }
