14569    #[test]
14570    fn test_plan_read_extents_melds_gaps_and_splits_on_cap() {
14571        let mut per_shard: HashMap<u16, Vec<u64>> = HashMap::new();
14572
14573        // Meld runs across gaps within the threshold, split across larger ones.
14574        per_shard.insert(3, vec![0, 50_000, 400_000, 450_000, 10_000_000]);
14575        let extents = plan_read_extents(
14576            &per_shard,
14577            ReadPlanPolicy {
14578                merge_gap_bytes: 100_000,
14579                max_extent_bytes: 10_000_000,
14580                min_batch_candidates: 1,
14581                random_advice: false,
14582            },
14583        );
14584        assert_eq!(
14585            extents,
14586            vec![
14587                ReadExtent {
14588                    slot: 3,
14589                    start: 0,
14590                    end: 50_000 + MAX_FRAME_DISK_LEN,
14591                },
14592                ReadExtent {
14593                    slot: 3,
14594                    start: 400_000,
14595                    end: 450_000 + MAX_FRAME_DISK_LEN,
14596                },
14597                ReadExtent {
14598                    slot: 3,
14599                    start: 10_000_000,
14600                    end: 10_000_000 + MAX_FRAME_DISK_LEN,
14601                },
14602            ]
14603        );
14604
14605        // A generous gap threshold still splits once the run would exceed the
14606        // cap: 0 and 100_000 fit under 200_000, but adding 150_000 would not.
14607        per_shard.clear();
14608        per_shard.insert(7, vec![0, 100_000, 150_000]);
14609        let capped = plan_read_extents(
14610            &per_shard,
14611            ReadPlanPolicy {
14612                merge_gap_bytes: 10_000_000,
14613                max_extent_bytes: 200_000,
14614                min_batch_candidates: 1,
14615                random_advice: false,
14616            },
14617        );
14618        assert_eq!(
14619            capped,
14620            vec![
14621                ReadExtent {
14622                    slot: 7,
14623                    start: 0,
14624                    end: 100_000 + MAX_FRAME_DISK_LEN,
14625                },
14626                ReadExtent {
14627                    slot: 7,
14628                    start: 150_000,
14629                    end: 150_000 + MAX_FRAME_DISK_LEN,
14630                },
14631            ]
14632        );
14633    }

14680    #[cfg(unix)]
14681    fn test_get_many_prefetch_plan_counters() {
14682        let dir = test_dir("read_plan_counters");
14683        let writer = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
14684        let entries: Vec<_> = (0..8u8)
14685            .map(|value| {
14686                let mut id = [0u8; 16];
14687                id[0] = value;
14688                id[9] = value.wrapping_mul(37).wrapping_add(11);
14689                (id, NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from(vec![value; 16])))
14690            })
14691            .collect();
14692        writer.put_many(&TEST_COLLECTION, &entries).unwrap();
14693        writer.sync_all().unwrap();
14694        drop(writer);
14695
14696        let reader = PackfileStorage::open_read_only(dir).unwrap();
14697        reader.set_stats_enabled(true);
14698        reader.set_read_plan_policy(ReadPlanPolicy {
14699            merge_gap_bytes: 1024 * 1024,
14700            max_extent_bytes: 8 * 1024 * 1024,
14701            min_batch_candidates: 1,
14702            random_advice: false,
14703        });
14704
14705        let ids: Vec<_> = entries.iter().map(|(id, _)| *id).collect();
14706        let before = reader.stats();
14707        let results = reader.get_many(&TEST_COLLECTION, &ids).unwrap();
14708        assert_eq!(
14709            results.iter().filter(|value| value.is_some()).count(),
14710            entries.len()
14711        );
14712        let after = reader.stats();
14713        assert!(after.read_plan_extents > before.read_plan_extents);
14714        assert!(after.read_plan_prefetch_bytes > before.read_plan_prefetch_bytes);
14715        // Every candidate is committed to disk, so every planned extent is
14716        // prefetchable and none is skipped.
14717        assert_eq!(after.read_plan_skipped_extents, 0);
14718
14719        // A disabled policy prefetches nothing, even for the same batch.
14720        reader.set_read_plan_policy(ReadPlanPolicy::disabled());
14721        let disabled_before = reader.stats();
14722        reader.get_many(&TEST_COLLECTION, &ids).unwrap();
14723        let disabled_after = reader.stats();
14724        assert_eq!(
14725            disabled_after.read_plan_extents,
14726            disabled_before.read_plan_extents
14727        );
14728        assert_eq!(
14729            disabled_after.read_plan_prefetch_bytes,
14730            disabled_before.read_plan_prefetch_bytes
14731        );
14732    }

14734    #[test]
14735    fn test_walk_ancestors_counts_candidate_probes_reads_and_frame_bytes() {
14736        let dir = test_dir("walk_counter_tracking");
14737        let writer = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
14738        let ids: Vec<NodeId> = (0..3u8).map(distinct_id).collect();
14739        for (i, id) in ids.iter().enumerate() {
14740            let byte = b'A' + u8::try_from(i).unwrap();
14741            writer
14742                .put(
14743                    &TEST_COLLECTION,
14744                    id,
14745                    &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from(vec![byte])),
14746                )
14747                .unwrap();
14748        }
14749        writer.sync_all().unwrap();
14750        drop(writer);
14751
14752        // A fresh read-only store has an empty decoded-node cache, so a walk
14753        // must resolve every hash through the lossy index and the packfiles —
14754        // and the counters for that traverse path (`resolve_pinned`, the
14755        // ancestor/frontier hook) must move, not just `get`/`get_many`.
14756        let reader = PackfileStorage::open_read_only(dir).unwrap();
14757        reader.set_stats_enabled(true);
14758        let edges =
14759            std::collections::HashMap::from([(ids[1], vec![ids[0]]), (ids[2], vec![ids[1]])]);
14760        let extract = |hash: &[u8; 16], _data: &[u8]| edges.get(hash).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
14761        let walked: Vec<(NodeId, NodeData)> = reader
14762            .walk_ancestors(
14763                &TEST_COLLECTION,
14764                &[ids[2]],
14765                &[],
14766                extract,
14767                WalkLimits::default(),
14768            )
14769            .unwrap()
14770            .collect::<Result<_, _>>()
14771            .unwrap();
14772        assert_eq!(walked.len(), 3);
14773
14774        let stats = reader.stats();
14775        assert!(stats.index_candidates >= 3);
14776        assert!(stats.candidate_reads >= 3);
14777        assert!(stats.candidate_frame_bytes >= stats.candidate_reads);
14778        assert!(stats.cache.misses >= 3);
14779        // `walk_ancestors` is a traversal, not a `get_many` batch: its
14780        // scatter-shape counters must not be the ones that moved.
14781        assert_eq!(stats.read_many_runs, 0);
14782    }

14784    #[test]
14785    fn test_put_many_growth_mid_batch_keeps_records_inserted_before_the_grow() {
14786        // Exercises the fast path's trickiest transition: some records in
14787        // the batch insert via the live, shared index (no clone), then a
14788        // later record in the *same* batch forces a grow — which must
14789        // materialize an owned index that still contains everything the
14790        // live path already applied, not just what comes after the grow.
14791        let dir = test_dir("put_many_growth_mid_batch");
14792        let store = PackfileStorage::open(dir).unwrap();
14793
14794        // Get the collection's live index past its NEW_COLLECTION_INDEX_FLOOR
14795        // starting capacity via ordinary put_many calls (fast path), then
14796        // issue one big batch that must cross the 75%-load grow threshold
14797        // partway through.
14798        let seed: Vec<_> = (0..40u32)
14799            .map(|i| {
14800                let mut id = [1u8; 16];
14801                id[4..8].copy_from_slice(&i.to_le_bytes());
14802                (id, NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from(format!("seed{i}"))))
14803            })
14804            .collect();
14805        store.put_many(&TEST_COLLECTION, &seed).unwrap();
14806
14807        let growth_batch: Vec<_> = (0..200u32)
14808            .map(|i| {
14809                let mut id = [2u8; 16];
14810                id[4..8].copy_from_slice(&i.to_le_bytes());
14811                (id, NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from(format!("grow{i}"))))
14812            })
14813            .collect();
14814        store.put_many(&TEST_COLLECTION, &growth_batch).unwrap();
14815
14816        for (id, data) in seed.iter().chain(&growth_batch) {
14817            let got = store.get(&TEST_COLLECTION, id).unwrap().unwrap();
14818            assert_eq!(
14819                &got.bytes, &data.bytes,
14820                "record must survive the mid-batch grow"
14821            );
14822        }
14823    }

14860    #[test]
14861    fn test_get_many_with_refresh_disabled_is_authoritative() {
14862        let dir = test_dir("refresh_disabled_authoritative");
14863        let store = Arc::new(PackfileStorage::open(dir).unwrap());
14864        // A single writer's in-memory index is authoritative for every key it
14865        // has written, so a negative lookup must bypass the refresh lock and
14866        // the durable-fingerprint probe entirely rather than paying either.
14867        store.set_refresh_on_miss(false);
14868
14869        let missing = [[0xF0u8; 16], [0xF1u8; 16]];
14870        let refresh_lock = store.refresh_lock(&TEST_COLLECTION);
14871        let refresh_guard = refresh_lock.lock();
14872        let (sender, receiver) = std::sync::mpsc::channel();
14873        let reader_store = Arc::clone(&store);
14874        let reader = std::thread::spawn(move || {
14875            let result = reader_store
14876                .get_many_with_refresh(&TEST_COLLECTION, &missing)
14877                .unwrap()
14878                .iter()
14879                .all(Option::is_none);
14880            sender.send(result).unwrap();
14881        });
14882
14883        // Keep the refresh lock held while the lookup runs. The writer path
14884        // must return from the in-memory index without waiting for it. This is
14885        // a deadlock guard, not a latency assertion: the timeout is generous
14886        // enough that a merely loaded CI worker cannot trip it. The
14887        // timing-independent proof that no durable fingerprint was probed is
14888        // the `miss_refreshes == 0` counter below.
14889        assert!(receiver
14890            .recv_timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(5))
14891            .unwrap());
14892        drop(refresh_guard);
14893        reader.join().unwrap();
14894
14895        let stats = store.stats();
14896        assert_eq!(stats.miss_refreshes, 0);
14897        assert_eq!(stats.miss_refresh_skips, 0);
14898        assert_eq!(stats.miss_refresh_retry_ids, 0);
14899    }

15028    /// Regression for the deferred-checkpoint reader window.
15029    ///
15030    /// A writer that owes a *structurally needed* full checkpoint rewrite
15031    /// (`pending` is empty while the index is dirty — the shape a
15032    /// `refresh_collection` that pulled in another process's appends leaves
15033    /// behind) will skip that rewrite under
15034    /// [`PackfileStorage::set_checkpoint_rewrite_budget`]. The packs are still
15035    /// flushed and fsynced, so the record is durable; but with no checkpoint
15036    /// rewrite and no delta frame, the durable fingerprint does not advance.
15037    /// A reader handle that opened at the previous fingerprint therefore treats
15038    /// its negative as confirmed and never refreshes: a *synced* record stays
15039    /// invisible to [`PackfileStorage::get_many_with_refresh`] for as long as
15040    /// the budget defers the rewrite.
15041    ///
15042    /// Ignored because WAL-off cross-process reads are no longer a supported
15043    /// shape. The journal's [`PackfileStorage::get_read_committed`] overlay is
15044    /// the authoritative cross-process visibility path and serves the committed
15045    /// record before the checkpoint advances, independent of the rewrite
15046    /// budget. This pins the unsupported window so a future change that makes
15047    /// WAL-off reads appear to work by accident (rather than by the overlay) is
15048    /// noticed.
15049    ///
15050    /// Known issue, not exercised here: `post_refresh_fingerprint` records the
15051    /// *post*-refresh durable fingerprint as the collection's refresh baseline,
15052    /// so a sync racing between `refresh_collection` and that read can store a
15053    /// baseline the index never actually incorporated — over-claiming coverage
15054    /// and suppressing a refresh that was needed. A fix must capture the
15055    /// fingerprint the refresh itself observed rather than re-reading it.
15056    #[test]
15057    #[ignore = "WAL-off cross-process reads are unsupported; the journal overlay is authoritative (see test docs)"]
15058    fn deferred_checkpoint_rewrite_leaves_synced_write_invisible() {
15059        let dir = test_dir("deferred_checkpoint_reader_window");
15060        let writer = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
15061
15062        // Baseline checkpoint, so the writer has a prior rewrite timestamp for
15063        // the budget's time headroom to measure against.
15064        let seed = distinct_id(0xC0);
15065        writer
15066            .put(
15067                &TEST_COLLECTION,
15068                &seed,
15069                &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"seed")),
15070            )
15071            .unwrap();
15072        writer.sync().unwrap();
15073
15074        // Reader opens bound to the baseline checkpoint's fingerprint.
15075        let reader = PackfileStorage::open_read_only(dir.clone()).unwrap();
15076
15077        // Once a rewrite has run, defer the next for an hour; no size budget.
15078        writer.set_checkpoint_rewrite_budget(Duration::from_secs(3600), 0);
15079
15080        let id = distinct_id(0xC1);
15081        writer
15082            .put(
15083                &TEST_COLLECTION,
15084                &id,
15085                &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"deferred")),
15086            )
15087            .unwrap();
15088        // The record is eagerly in the pack, but leave no local delta frame:
15089        // this is the `pending.is_empty()` + dirty shape that makes the next
15090        // sync structurally need a full rewrite (as a refresh of external
15091        // appends does).
15092        writer.delta_state.lock().pending.clear();
15093        writer.index_checkpoint_dirty.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
15094
15095        let before = writer.stats();
15096        writer.sync().unwrap();
15097        let after = writer.stats();
15098        assert_eq!(
15099            after.checkpoint_writes - before.checkpoint_writes,
15100            0,
15101            "the structurally-needed rewrite must be deferred, not written"
15102        );
15103        assert_eq!(
15104            after.checkpoint_skips - before.checkpoint_skips,
15105            1,
15106            "the sync must have taken the deferred branch"
15107        );
15108
15109        // The pack bytes are durable, but the durable fingerprint is unchanged,
15110        // so the reader's gate confirms the negative without refreshing.
15111        reader.reset_stats();
15112        let result = reader
15113            .get_many_with_refresh(&TEST_COLLECTION, &[id])
15114            .unwrap();
15115        assert!(
15116            result[0].is_none(),
15117            "a synced record stays invisible while the checkpoint rewrite is deferred"
15118        );
15119        let reader_stats = reader.stats();
15120        assert_eq!(
15121            reader_stats.miss_refreshes, 0,
15122            "an unchanged durable fingerprint suppresses the refresh entirely"
15123        );
15124        assert_eq!(reader_stats.miss_refresh_skips, 1);
15125    }

15183    #[test]
15184    fn test_get_many_with_refresh_concurrent_misses_coalesce() {
15185        use std::sync::Arc;
15186
15187        let dir = test_dir("refresh_concurrent");
15188        let store = Arc::new(PackfileStorage::open(dir).unwrap());
15189
15190        // Seed a record so TEST_COLLECTION exists and has a shard on disk.
15191        let seed_id = distinct_id(0xC0);
15192        store
15193            .put(
15194                &TEST_COLLECTION,
15195                &seed_id,
15196                &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"seed")),
15197            )
15198            .unwrap();
15199        store.sync().unwrap();
15200
15201        let missing = [distinct_id(0xC1), distinct_id(0xC2)];
15202
15203        // Pre-seed: first call populates last_refresh_fingerprint for
15204        // TEST_COLLECTION. Durable fp is the same as stored → skip.
15205        store.reset_stats();
15206        let _ = store
15207            .get_many_with_refresh(&TEST_COLLECTION, &missing)
15208            .unwrap();
15209
15210        // Append and sync to change the durable fingerprint.
15211        let id = distinct_id(0xC3);
15212        store
15213            .put(
15214                &TEST_COLLECTION,
15215                &id,
15216                &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"synced")),
15217            )
15218            .unwrap();
15219        store.sync().unwrap();
15220
15221        // Stored fp is stale → refresh needed. Spawn concurrent readers.
15222        store.reset_stats();
15223        let mut handles = Vec::new();
15224        for _ in 0..4 {
15225            let store = Arc::clone(&store);
15226            handles.push(std::thread::spawn(move || {
15227                let _ = store.get_many_with_refresh(&TEST_COLLECTION, &missing);
15228            }));
15229        }
15230        for h in handles {
15231            h.join().unwrap();
15232        }
15233
15234        // Only one refresh should have actually occurred (coalesced).
15235        let stats = store.stats();
15236        assert_eq!(
15237            stats.miss_refreshes, 1,
15238            "concurrent misses must coalesce into one refresh"
15239        );
15240    }

15242    #[test]
15243    fn test_get_many_with_refresh_negative_then_recovered() {
15244        let dir = test_dir("refresh_negative_then_recovered");
15245        let writer = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
15246        let reader = PackfileStorage::open_read_only(dir.clone()).unwrap();
15247
15248        let missing_id = distinct_id(0xD1);
15249
15250        // First call: reader sees no durable change → confirmed negative.
15251        reader.reset_stats();
15252        let result = reader
15253            .get_many_with_refresh(&TEST_COLLECTION, &[missing_id])
15254            .unwrap();
15255        assert!(result[0].is_none());
15256        let stats = reader.stats();
15257        assert_eq!(stats.miss_refreshes, 0);
15258        assert_eq!(stats.miss_refresh_skips, 1);
15259
15260        // Writer appends and syncs → durable fingerprint changes.
15261        let data = NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"now_here"));
15262        writer.put(&TEST_COLLECTION, &missing_id, &data).unwrap();
15263        writer.sync().unwrap();
15264
15265        // Second call: stored fp != durable fp → refresh → recovered.
15266        let result = reader
15267            .get_many_with_refresh(&TEST_COLLECTION, &[missing_id])
15268            .unwrap();
15269        assert_eq!(
15270            result[0].as_ref().map(|d| &d.bytes),
15271            Some(&bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"now_here")),
15272            "record written after first negative must be recovered"
15273        );
15274        let stats = reader.stats();
15275        assert_eq!(stats.miss_refreshes, 1);
15276        assert_eq!(stats.miss_refresh_recovered, 1);
15277        assert_eq!(stats.miss_refresh_retry_ids, 1);
15278    }

15317    #[test]
15318    fn test_scan_existing_skips_malformed_filenames() {
15319        let dir = test_dir("scan_existing_junk");
15320        std::fs::write(dir.join("nounderscore.pack"), b"").unwrap();
15321        std::fs::write(dir.join("aabb_00.pack"), b"").unwrap();
15322        std::fs::write(dir.join("zzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzz_00.pack"), b"").unwrap();
15323        std::fs::write(dir.join("00000000000000000000000000000000_gg.pack"), b"").unwrap();
15324        // A filename that isn't valid UTF-8 is only creatable on filesystems
15325        // that accept arbitrary bytes (Linux/BSD). APFS on macOS rejects it
15326        // with EILSEQ (os error 92), and Windows has no `std::os::unix`; the
15327        // ASCII-only malformed names above still cover the skip path there.
15328        #[cfg(all(unix, not(target_os = "macos")))]
15329        {
15330            use std::ffi::OsStr;
15331            use std::os::unix::ffi::OsStrExt;
15332            let path = dir.join(OsStr::from_bytes(b"\xff\xfe.pack"));
15333            std::fs::write(path, b"").unwrap();
15334        }
15335
15336        let valid_path = dir.join("pack_0000000000000000.pack");
15337        let mut buf = Vec::new();
15338        packfile::write_header(&mut buf, 0).unwrap();
15339        packfile::write_record(
15340            &mut buf,
15341            &packfile::Record {
15342                collection_id: [0x01; 16],
15343                hash: [0xAA; 16],
15344                data: bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"hello"),
15345                metadata: None,
15346            },
15347        )
15348        .unwrap();
15349        std::fs::write(&valid_path, &buf).unwrap();
15350
15351        let store = PackfileStorage::open(dir).unwrap();
15352        let gen = store.generation(&[0x01u8; 16]).unwrap();
15353        assert_eq!(gen.index.len(), 1);
15354    }

15364        let id_b = [0x20u8; 16];

15460    #[test]
15461    fn test_repack_collection_reachable_drops_unreachable_records() {
15462        let dir = test_dir("repack_reachable_gc");
15463        let store = PackfileStorage::open(dir).unwrap();
15464
15465        // Live chain: root -> p1 -> p0 (p0 has no further dependencies).
15466        let root = distinct_id(1);
15467        let p1 = distinct_id(2);
15468        let p0 = distinct_id(3);
15469
15470        // Garbage island, unreachable from root: garbage -> garbage_dep.
15471        let garbage = distinct_id(4);
15472        let garbage_dep = distinct_id(5);
15473
15474        for (id, bytes) in [
15475            (root, b"root".as_slice()),
15476            (p1, b"p1".as_slice()),
15477            (p0, b"p0".as_slice()),
15478            (garbage, b"garbage".as_slice()),
15479            (garbage_dep, b"garbage_dep".as_slice()),
15480        ] {
15481            store
15482                .put(
15483                    &TEST_COLLECTION,
15484                    &id,
15485                    &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(bytes)),
15486                )
15487                .unwrap();
15488        }
15489
15490        let edges = std::collections::HashMap::from([
15491            (root, vec![p1]),
15492            (p1, vec![p0]),
15493            (garbage, vec![garbage_dep]),
15494        ]);
15495
15496        store.set_live_roots(&TEST_COLLECTION, vec![root]);
15497
15498        let (kept, dropped) = store
15499            .repack_collection_reachable(&TEST_COLLECTION, |hash, _data| {
15500                edges.get(hash).cloned().unwrap_or_default()
15501            })
15502            .unwrap();
15503
15504        assert_eq!(kept, 3, "root, p1, p0 should survive");
15505        assert_eq!(dropped, 2, "garbage and garbage_dep should be collected");
15506
15507        for id in [root, p1, p0] {
15508            assert!(
15509                store.get(&TEST_COLLECTION, &id).unwrap().is_some(),
15510                "live record missing after reachable repack"
15511            );
15512        }
15513        for id in [garbage, garbage_dep] {
15514            assert!(
15515                store.get(&TEST_COLLECTION, &id).unwrap().is_none(),
15516                "garbage record survived reachable repack"
15517            );
15518        }
15519
15520        let stats = store.repack_stats();
15521        assert_eq!(stats.repack_count, 1);
15522        assert_eq!(stats.kept_total, 3);
15523        assert_eq!(stats.dropped_total, 2);
15524        assert_eq!(store.repack_count_for_collection(&TEST_COLLECTION), 1);
15525
15526        // A second repack uses the incremental path: it clones the
15527        // previous live_map (3 entries from the first repack's output)
15528        // and scans only newly-appended bytes (none here).  The garbage
15529        // entries in the old shard are never re-scanned — the live_map
15530        // already excludes them, so dropped is 0.  This is the O(n)
15531        // behavior: each repack does bounded work proportional to new
15532        // bytes, not proportional to total shard size.
15533        let (kept2, dropped2) = store
15534            .repack_collection_reachable(&TEST_COLLECTION, |hash, _data| {
15535                edges.get(hash).cloned().unwrap_or_default()
15536            })
15537            .unwrap();
15538        assert_eq!((kept2, dropped2), (3, 0));
15539
15540        let stats2 = store.repack_stats();
15541        assert_eq!(stats2.repack_count, 2);
15542        assert_eq!(stats2.kept_total, stats.kept_total + kept2 as u64);
15543        assert_eq!(stats2.dropped_total, stats.dropped_total + dropped2 as u64);
15544        assert_eq!(store.repack_count_for_collection(&TEST_COLLECTION), 2);
15545    }
15546
15547    /// Verify the root-removal fallback: if a live root is removed between
15548    /// repacks, nodes exclusively reachable through it must not stay in the
15549    /// cached live set indefinitely. Without the fallback, the incremental
15550    /// adjacency cache only grows and those nodes would never be collected.
15551    #[test]
15552    fn test_repack_incremental_root_removal_forces_full_sweep() {
15553        let dir = test_dir("repack_root_removal_fallback");
15554        let store = PackfileStorage::open(dir).unwrap();
15555
15556        // Graph:
15557        //   root_a -> shared -> base
15558        //   root_b -> shared -> base
15559        //   orphan_a -> orphan_dep    (reachable only via root_a)
15560        //
15561        // First repack: both root_a and root_b are live. Everything survives.
15562        // Second repack: only root_b is live. orphan_a and orphan_dep must be
15563        // collected. Without the root-removal fallback they would remain in the
15564        // incremental live set permanently.
15565        let root_a = distinct_id(1);
15566        let root_b = distinct_id(2);
15567        let shared = distinct_id(3);
15568        let base = distinct_id(4);
15569        let orphan_a = distinct_id(5);
15570        let orphan_dep = distinct_id(6);
15571
15572        for (id, bytes) in [
15573            (root_a, b"root_a".as_slice()),
15574            (root_b, b"root_b".as_slice()),
15575            (shared, b"shared".as_slice()),
15576            (base, b"base".as_slice()),
15577            (orphan_a, b"orphan_a".as_slice()),
15578            (orphan_dep, b"orphan_dep".as_slice()),
15579        ] {
15580            store
15581                .put(
15582                    &TEST_COLLECTION,
15583                    &id,
15584                    &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(bytes)),
15585                )
15586                .unwrap();
15587        }
15588
15589        let edges = std::collections::HashMap::from([
15590            (root_a, vec![shared, orphan_a]),
15591            (root_b, vec![shared]),
15592            (shared, vec![base]),
15593            (orphan_a, vec![orphan_dep]),
15594        ]);
15595        let extract = |hash: &[u8; 16], _data: &[u8]| -> Vec<[u8; 16]> {
15596            edges.get(hash).cloned().unwrap_or_default()
15597        };
15598
15599        // First repack: both roots live — everything reachable from either root
15600        // survives and the incremental adjacency cache is populated.
15601        store.set_live_roots(&TEST_COLLECTION, vec![root_a, root_b]);
15602        let (kept1, dropped1) = store
15603            .repack_collection_reachable(&TEST_COLLECTION, extract)
15604            .unwrap();
15605        assert_eq!(kept1, 6, "all nodes should survive with both roots live");
15606        assert_eq!(dropped1, 0);
15607
15608        // Now remove root_a — switch to root_b only.
15609        // orphan_a and orphan_dep are now exclusively reachable through root_a,
15610        // which was removed. The root-removal fallback must trigger a full BFS
15611        // sweep so they are actually collected, rather than remaining in the
15612        // stale incremental live set forever.
15613        store.set_live_roots(&TEST_COLLECTION, vec![root_b]);
15614        let (kept2, dropped2) = store
15615            .repack_collection_reachable(&TEST_COLLECTION, extract)
15616            .unwrap();
15617        assert_eq!(
15618            kept2, 3,
15619            "root_b, shared, base should survive; root_a, orphan_a, orphan_dep must be GC'd"
15620        );
15621        assert_eq!(
15622            dropped2, 3,
15623            "root_a, orphan_a, and orphan_dep must be collected once root_a is removed from live roots"
15624        );
15625
15626        assert!(
15627            store.get(&TEST_COLLECTION, &orphan_a).unwrap().is_none(),
15628            "orphan_a must be gone after root_a was removed"
15629        );
15630        assert!(
15631            store.get(&TEST_COLLECTION, &orphan_dep).unwrap().is_none(),
15632            "orphan_dep must be gone after root_a was removed"
15633        );
15634        assert!(
15635            store.get(&TEST_COLLECTION, &root_a).unwrap().is_none(),
15636            "root_a itself has no incoming edges so it is unreachable from root_b"
15637        );
15638        assert!(
15639            store.get(&TEST_COLLECTION, &root_b).unwrap().is_some(),
15640            "root_b must still be present"
15641        );
15642        assert!(
15643            store.get(&TEST_COLLECTION, &shared).unwrap().is_some(),
15644            "shared must still be present"
15645        );
15646        assert!(
15647            store.get(&TEST_COLLECTION, &base).unwrap().is_some(),
15648            "base must still be present"
15649        );
15650    }
15651
15652    /// Repack drops unreachable *records* from the index (`dropped` count),
15653    /// but today nothing ever retires the *shard file* they lived in: no
15654    /// code path sets `Shard::is_current` to `false` or clears the pool's
15655    /// slot for it (see `Shard::drop`'s doc and
15656    /// `test_drop_deletes_retired_shard_only_after_last_reference` in
15657    /// shard.rs, which has to simulate retirement manually because nothing
15658    /// production triggers it). `rotate()`'s error message says "repack to
15659    /// reclaim", but repack currently reclaims nothing at the shard level.
15660    ///
15661    /// This fills a small fixed number of pool slots (4), repacks away
15662    /// everything in the non-active ones (100% garbage, nothing live left),
15663    /// and then expects one more rotation to succeed by reusing a
15664    /// now-empty slot.
15665    #[test]
15666    fn test_repack_reclaims_shard_slots_for_rotation() {
15667        // Use a fixed small count rather than MAX_SHARDS — with 4096 slots
15668        // and 256MB each that would be a 1TB test.
15669        const TEST_SHARDS: usize = 4;
15670
15671        let dir = test_dir("repack_reclaims_slots");
15672        let store = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
15673
15674        let mut root = [0u8; 16];
15675        root[0] = 0xFF;
15676        store
15677            .put(
15678                &TEST_COLLECTION,
15679                &root,
15680                &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"root")),
15681            )
15682            .unwrap();
15683
15684        // `root` already occupies the first slot; force rotation through
15685        // the remaining TEST_SHARDS - 1 slots, dumping garbage into each so
15686        // every shard but the last ends up fully unreachable once we
15687        // repack with `root` as the only live node.
15688        for i in 0..TEST_SHARDS - 1 {
15689            store.shards.active_shard().file_len.store(
15690                shard::MAX_SHARD_BYTES - 10,
15691                std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Release,
15692            );
15693            let mut garbage = [0u8; 16];
15694            garbage[0] = u8::try_from(i + 1).unwrap();
15695            store
15696                .put(
15697                    &TEST_COLLECTION,
15698                    &garbage,
15699                    &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"garbage")),
15700                )
15701                .unwrap();
15702        }
15703
15704        // Every slot should now be occupied.
15705        let occupied = (0..u16::try_from(TEST_SHARDS).unwrap())
15706            .filter(|&id| store.shards.get_shard(id).is_some())
15707            .count();
15708        assert_eq!(
15709            occupied, TEST_SHARDS,
15710            "test setup should have filled every shard slot"
15711        );
15712
15713        store.set_live_roots(&TEST_COLLECTION, vec![root]);
15714        let (kept, dropped) = store
15715            .repack_collection_reachable(&TEST_COLLECTION, |_hash, _data| Vec::new())
15716            .unwrap();
15717        assert_eq!(kept, 1, "only root should survive");
15718        assert!(dropped > 0, "the garbage records should have been dropped");
15719        assert!(
15720            store.shards_retired() > 0,
15721            "retire_empty_shards should have retired at least one now-garbage-only shard"
15722        );
15723
15724        // The collection occupied several packs, and repack retired the
15725        // garbage-only source packs. The persisted byte total must follow the
15726        // surviving physical layout rather than retaining bytes for retired
15727        // packs.
15728        store.sync_all().unwrap();
15729        let physical = crate::packfile::layout::physical_layout(&dir).unwrap();
15730        let expected = physical
15731            .collections
15732            .get(&TEST_COLLECTION)
15733            .expect("repacked collection remains on disk")
15734            .disk_bytes;
15735        assert_eq!(
15736            PackfileStorage::collection_disk_bytes_from_disk(&dir)
15737                .unwrap()
15738                .get(&TEST_COLLECTION),
15739            Some(&expected),
15740            "retired packs must not remain in collection byte accounting"
15741        );
15742
15743        // Every shard except the current active one held nothing but
15744        // garbage, and that garbage is now unreachable -- those slots
15745        // should be reclaimable. Forcing one more rotation should reuse
15746        // one of them rather than failing.
15747        store.shards.active_shard().file_len.store(
15748            shard::MAX_SHARD_BYTES - 10,
15749            std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Release,
15750        );
15751        let mut one_more = [0u8; 16];
15752        one_more[0] = 0xEE;
15753        store
15754            .put(
15755                &TEST_COLLECTION,
15756                &one_more,
15757                &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"one more")),
15758            )
15759            .expect(
15760                "rotation should reclaim a garbage-only shard slot after repack, \
15761                 not report the pool as permanently full",
15762            );
15763    }

15765    #[test]
15766    fn test_repack_moves_live_data_out_of_its_source_shard() {
15767        let dir = test_dir("repack_moves_from_source");
15768        let store = PackfileStorage::open(dir).unwrap();
15769        let node = [0xA5; 16];
15770        store
15771            .put(
15772                &TEST_COLLECTION,
15773                &node,
15774                &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"live")),
15775            )
15776            .unwrap();
15777
15778        let source = store
15779            .collection_referenced_shards(&TEST_COLLECTION)
15780            .into_iter()
15781            .next()
15782            .unwrap();
15783        let (kept, dropped) = store
15784            .repack_collection_reachable(&TEST_COLLECTION, |_hash, _data| Vec::new())
15785            .unwrap();
15786
15787        assert_eq!((kept, dropped), (1, 0));
15788        let destination = store
15789            .collection_referenced_shards(&TEST_COLLECTION)
15790            .into_iter()
15791            .next()
15792            .unwrap();
15793        assert_ne!(destination, source);
15794        assert!(store.shards.get_shard(source).is_none());
15795        assert_eq!(
15796            store
15797                .get(&TEST_COLLECTION, &node)
15798                .unwrap()
15799                .unwrap()
15800                .bytes
15801                .as_ref(),
15802            b"live"
15803        );
15804    }

15806    /// Repack must not retire a shard that another collection's index still
15807    /// references.  This test puts live records from two different collections
15808    /// into the same shard, then repacks only collection A — the shared shard
15809    /// must survive because collection B's index still points into it.
15810    #[test]
15811    fn test_repack_does_not_retire_shard_referenced_by_other_collection() {
15812        let dir = test_dir("repack_cross_collection_safety");
15813        let store = PackfileStorage::open(dir).unwrap();
15814
15815        // Put a record for collection A — lands on shard 0.
15816        let mut root_a = [0u8; 16];
15817        root_a[0] = 0xAA;
15818        store
15819            .put(
15820                &TEST_COLLECTION,
15821                &root_a,
15822                &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"collection A root")),
15823            )
15824            .unwrap();
15825
15826        // Force a rotation so the next write goes to a different shard.
15827        store.shards.active_shard().file_len.store(
15828            shard::MAX_SHARD_BYTES - 10,
15829            std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Release,
15830        );
15831
15832        // Put a record for collection B — lands on shard 1.
15833        let mut root_b = [0u8; 16];
15834        root_b[0] = 0xBB;
15835        store
15836            .put(
15837                &OTHER_COLLECTION,
15838                &root_b,
15839                &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"collection B root")),
15840            )
15841            .unwrap();
15842
15843        // Force another rotation and put more collection A garbage on shard 2.
15844        store.shards.active_shard().file_len.store(
15845            shard::MAX_SHARD_BYTES - 10,
15846            std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Release,
15847        );
15848        let mut garbage = [0u8; 16];
15849        garbage[0] = 0xCC;
15850        store
15851            .put(
15852                &TEST_COLLECTION,
15853                &garbage,
15854                &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"garbage")),
15855            )
15856            .unwrap();
15857
15858        // Repack collection A with only root_a as live.  The garbage record
15859        // should be dropped, but shard 1 (which holds collection B's root)
15860        // must NOT be retired.
15861        store.set_live_roots(&TEST_COLLECTION, vec![root_a]);
15862        let (kept, dropped) = store
15863            .repack_collection_reachable(&TEST_COLLECTION, |_hash, _data| Vec::new())
15864            .unwrap();
15865        assert_eq!(kept, 1);
15866        assert!(dropped > 0);
15867
15868        // Collection B's root must still be retrievable — shard 1 was not retired.
15869        let got = store.get(&OTHER_COLLECTION, &root_b).unwrap();
15870        assert!(
15871            got.is_some(),
15872            "collection B root must survive repack of collection A — shared shard must not be retired",
15873        );
15874    }

15876    /// `open_read_only` must actually coexist with a live writer end to
15877    /// end — not just take no lock, but also not touch/truncate the
15878    /// writer's files via the collection-index rebuild scan (the real risk this
15879    /// whole design exists to avoid). Also confirms it sees the writer's
15880    /// already-durable data and that the writer is unaffected afterward.
15881    #[test]
15882    fn test_open_read_only_coexists_with_active_writer() {
15883        let dir = test_dir("open_read_only_coexist");
15884        let writer = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
15885
15886        let mut id = [0u8; 16];
15887        id[0] = 0xAA;
15888        writer
15889            .put(
15890                &TEST_COLLECTION,
15891                &id,
15892                &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"hello")),
15893            )
15894            .unwrap();
15895        // Reads through a second (read-only) process open against the same
15896        // directory only observe committed bytes, so make the write durable
15897        // before opening the reader — buffered bytes are RAM-only.
15898        writer.sync_all().unwrap();
15899
15900        // Open read-only while the writer is still alive — must succeed
15901        // (no lock conflict) and see the write above.
15902        let reader = PackfileStorage::open_read_only(dir.clone()).unwrap();
15903        assert_eq!(
15904            reader.get(&TEST_COLLECTION, &id).unwrap().map(|d| d.bytes),
15905            Some(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"hello"))
15906        );
15907        drop(reader);
15908
15909        // The writer must be completely unaffected — still open, still
15910        // able to write more data afterward.
15911        let mut id2 = [0u8; 16];
15912        id2[0] = 0xBB;
15913        writer
15914            .put(
15915                &TEST_COLLECTION,
15916                &id2,
15917                &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"world")),
15918            )
15919            .unwrap();
15920        assert_eq!(
15921            writer.get(&TEST_COLLECTION, &id2).unwrap().map(|d| d.bytes),
15922            Some(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"world"))
15923        );
15924    }

15926    /// `repack_shard` must find and repack every collection sharing a shard —
15927    /// the targeted way to reclaim one shard without waiting for each
15928    /// collection to independently cross its own repack threshold.
15929    #[test]
15930    fn test_repack_shard_repacks_every_referencing_collection() {
15931        let dir = test_dir("repack_shard");
15932        let store = PackfileStorage::open(dir).unwrap();
15933
15934        let mut root_a = [0u8; 16];
15935        root_a[0] = 0xAA;
15936        let mut garbage_a = [0u8; 16];
15937        garbage_a[0] = 0xA1;
15938        store
15939            .put(
15940                &TEST_COLLECTION,
15941                &root_a,
15942                &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"collection A root")),
15943            )
15944            .unwrap();
15945        store
15946            .put(
15947                &TEST_COLLECTION,
15948                &garbage_a,
15949                &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"collection A garbage")),
15950            )
15951            .unwrap();
15952        store.set_live_roots(&TEST_COLLECTION, vec![root_a]);
15953
15954        let mut root_b = [0u8; 16];
15955        root_b[0] = 0xBB;
15956        store
15957            .put(
15958                &OTHER_COLLECTION,
15959                &root_b,
15960                &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"collection B root")),
15961            )
15962            .unwrap();
15963        // No set_live_roots for collection B: everything must survive its repack.
15964
15965        // Fresh pool, both collections' first writes land on shard 0 (shared).
15966        let referencing = store.collections_referencing_shard(0).unwrap();
15967        assert_eq!(referencing.len(), 2);
15968        assert!(referencing.contains(&TEST_COLLECTION));
15969        assert!(referencing.contains(&OTHER_COLLECTION));
15970
15971        let mut results = store.repack_shard(0, |_hash, _data| Vec::new()).unwrap();
15972        results.sort_unstable_by_key(|(collection_id, _, _)| *collection_id);
15973
15974        let mut expected = vec![
15975            (TEST_COLLECTION, 1usize, 1usize),
15976            (OTHER_COLLECTION, 1usize, 0usize),
15977        ];
15978        expected.sort_unstable_by_key(|(collection_id, _, _)| *collection_id);
15979        assert_eq!(
15980            results, expected,
15981            "repack_shard must repack both collections sharing shard 0"
15982        );
15983
15984        assert!(store.get(&TEST_COLLECTION, &root_a).unwrap().is_some());
15985        assert!(store.get(&TEST_COLLECTION, &garbage_a).unwrap().is_none());
15986        assert!(store.get(&OTHER_COLLECTION, &root_b).unwrap().is_some());
15987    }

15989    /// `collections_referencing_shard` must filter the shard-scan's candidate
15990    /// set against each collection's *current* index, not just report every collection
15991    /// whose bytes ever physically touched the shard. A collection that has
15992    /// since repacked its live data onto a different shard leaves its old
15993    /// bytes sitting there untouched (shards are append-only, never
15994    /// rewritten in place) — that collection must NOT show up as still
15995    /// referencing the shard its data moved away from.
15996    #[test]
15997    fn test_collections_referencing_shard_excludes_collections_already_repacked_away() {
15998        let dir = test_dir("collections_referencing_shard_stale");
15999        let store = PackfileStorage::open(dir).unwrap();
16000
16001        let mut root = [0u8; 16];
16002        root[0] = 0xAA;
16003        store
16004            .put(
16005                &TEST_COLLECTION,
16006                &root,
16007                &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"root")),
16008            )
16009            .unwrap();
16010
16011        // OTHER_COLLECTION also lands on shard 0 (shared, still the pool's
16012        // active shard) and stays live there — this is what keeps shard 0
16013        // from being retired outright once TEST_COLLECTION moves off it, so the
16014        // "stale reference" case below is actually reachable to query.
16015        let mut other_root = [0u8; 16];
16016        other_root[0] = 0xBB;
16017        store
16018            .put(
16019                &OTHER_COLLECTION,
16020                &other_root,
16021                &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"other collection root")),
16022            )
16023            .unwrap();
16024
16025        // Force TEST_COLLECTION's home (shard 0) to look full, so its next write
16026        // rotates *its own* home to shard 1 — root stays physically on
16027        // shard 0, but TEST_COLLECTION's home (and this next record, `garbage`)
16028        // moves to shard 1.
16029        store.shards.active_shard().file_len.store(
16030            shard::MAX_SHARD_BYTES - 10,
16031            std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Release,
16032        );
16033        let mut garbage = [0u8; 16];
16034        garbage[0] = 0xA1;
16035        store
16036            .put(
16037                &TEST_COLLECTION,
16038                &garbage,
16039                &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"garbage")),
16040            )
16041            .unwrap();
16042
16043        // Repack with only root live: TEST_COLLECTION's records now span *two*
16044        // source shards (root on 0, garbage on 1), and a repack must never
16045        // rewrite live data back into one of its own sources (see
16046        // `ShardPool::prepare_collection_repack`'s doc) — so the kept copy lands
16047        // on a *third* shard (2), not shard 1. Shard 1, left holding only
16048        // the now-dropped `garbage` record with nothing live pointing at
16049        // it, gets retired and closed during this same repack.
16050        store.set_live_roots(&TEST_COLLECTION, vec![root]);
16051        store
16052            .repack_collection_reachable(&TEST_COLLECTION, |_hash, _data| Vec::new())
16053            .unwrap();
16054
16055        // Shard 0's raw bytes still physically contain TEST_COLLECTION's
16056        // original root record — a naive scan-only approach would still
16057        // report it. The current index must exclude it.
16058        assert!(
16059            !store.collections_referencing_shard(0).unwrap().contains(&TEST_COLLECTION),
16060            "a collection whose live data has moved off a shard must not be reported as still referencing it"
16061        );
16062
16063        // The real invariant here isn't "the destination is shard 2" —
16064        // that's just where a deterministic, empty-pool allocator happens
16065        // to land today. What must hold is: exactly one destination, and
16066        // it's neither of the two source shards (0 and 1) a repack must
16067        // never write live data back into.
16068        let destinations = store.collection_referenced_shards(&TEST_COLLECTION);
16069        assert_eq!(
16070            destinations.len(),
16071            1,
16072            "TEST_COLLECTION's live data must land on exactly one shard after repack"
16073        );
16074        let destination = destinations[0];
16075        assert!(
16076            ![0, 1].contains(&destination),
16077            "the repack destination must not be one of its own source shards (0: root, 1: garbage)"
16078        );
16079        assert!(
16080            store
16081                .collections_referencing_shard(destination)
16082                .unwrap()
16083                .contains(&TEST_COLLECTION),
16084            "the collection's current shard must still be reported"
16085        );
16086    }

16088    #[test]
16089    fn test_collection_directory_from_disk_matches_collection_summaries_after_sync() {
16090        let dir = test_dir("collection_directory_roundtrip");
16091        let store = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
16092
16093        for i in 0..5u8 {
16094            store
16095                .put(
16096                    &TEST_COLLECTION,
16097                    &distinct_id(i),
16098                    &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from(vec![i])),
16099                )
16100                .unwrap();
16101        }
16102        for i in 0..3u8 {
16103            store
16104                .put(
16105                    &OTHER_COLLECTION,
16106                    &distinct_id(100 + i),
16107                    &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from(vec![i])),
16108                )
16109                .unwrap();
16110        }
16111        store.sync_all().unwrap();
16112
16113        let mut from_disk = PackfileStorage::collection_directory_from_disk(&dir);
16114        from_disk.sort_unstable_by_key(|(collection_id, _)| *collection_id);
16115
16116        let mut expected: Vec<([u8; 16], u64)> = store
16117            .collection_summaries()
16118            .into_iter()
16119            .map(|(collection_id, count, _mem, _cap)| (collection_id, count as u64))
16120            .collect();
16121        expected.sort_unstable_by_key(|(collection_id, _)| *collection_id);
16122
16123        assert_eq!(
16124            from_disk, expected,
16125            "the persisted directory's per-collection totals must match the live index's own counts"
16126        );
16127        let disk_bytes = PackfileStorage::collection_disk_bytes_from_disk(&dir)
16128            .expect("v5 sidecar physical metrics");
16129        assert!(disk_bytes.get(&TEST_COLLECTION).copied().unwrap_or(0) > 0);
16130        assert!(disk_bytes.get(&OTHER_COLLECTION).copied().unwrap_or(0) > 0);
16131        assert!(PackfileStorage::collection_directory_persisted_at(&dir).is_some());
16132    }

16210    #[test]
16211    fn failed_sidecar_recovery_is_retried_and_never_publishes_zero_metrics() {
16212        let dir = test_dir("sidecar_recovery_failure");
16213        let store = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
16214        store
16215            .put(
16216                &TEST_COLLECTION,
16217                &distinct_id(0),
16218                &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"data")),
16219            )
16220            .unwrap();
16221        store.sync_all().unwrap();
16222        let sidecar = PackfileStorage::shard_collections_path(&dir);
16223        let before = fs::read(&sidecar).unwrap();
16224        let expected = crate::packfile::layout::physical_layout(&dir)
16225            .unwrap()
16226            .collections[&TEST_COLLECTION]
16227            .disk_bytes;
16228
16229        // Model an open whose recovery scan failed: byte totals unknown, flag set.
16230        store.index_tables.write().collection_disk_bytes.clear();
16231        store
16232            .shard_collections_recovery_failed
16233            .store(true, Ordering::Release);
16234
16235        // While the scan still fails (an unreadable pack), nothing is written.
16236        let junk = dir.join("pack_00000000000000ff.pack");
16237        fs::write(&junk, b"not a packfile").unwrap();
16238        assert!(store.persist_shard_collections().is_err());
16239        assert!(store
16240            .shard_collections_recovery_failed
16241            .load(Ordering::Acquire));
16242        assert_eq!(fs::read(&sidecar).unwrap(), before, "no zero-byte sidecar");
16243
16244        // Once the scan can succeed, the next persist retries it and recovers.
16245        fs::remove_file(&junk).unwrap();
16246        store.persist_shard_collections().unwrap();
16247        assert!(!store
16248            .shard_collections_recovery_failed
16249            .load(Ordering::Acquire));
16250        assert_eq!(
16251            PackfileStorage::collection_disk_bytes_from_disk(&dir)
16252                .unwrap()
16253                .get(&TEST_COLLECTION),
16254            Some(&expected)
16255        );
16256    }
16257
16258    /// Deterministic version of the recovery/append race: hold recovery between
16259    /// its scan and the swap of its totals and force a writer into that window.
16260    /// The writer must be blocked by the collection mutexes; without them its
16261    /// frame would be appended after the scan and then be lost by the swap.
16262    #[test]
16263    fn a_writer_cannot_slip_into_the_recovery_scan_to_swap_window() {
16264        use std::sync::mpsc::{channel, RecvTimeoutError};
16265        use std::time::Duration;
16266
16267        let wait = Duration::from_secs(10);
16268        let dir = test_dir("sidecar_recovery_window");
16269        let store = Arc::new(PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap());
16270        store
16271            .put(
16272                &TEST_COLLECTION,
16273                &distinct_id(0),
16274                &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"seed")),
16275            )
16276            .unwrap();
16277        store.sync_all().unwrap();
16278        store.index_tables.write().collection_disk_bytes.clear();
16279        store
16280            .shard_collections_recovery_failed
16281            .store(true, Ordering::Release);
16282
16283        let (scanned_tx, scanned_rx) = channel::<()>();
16284        let (resume_tx, resume_rx) = channel::<()>();
16285        let resume_rx = parking_lot::Mutex::new(resume_rx);
16286        *store.recovery_pause_hook.lock() = Some(Arc::new(move || {
16287            scanned_tx.send(()).unwrap();
16288            resume_rx
16289                .lock()
16290                .recv_timeout(Duration::from_secs(10))
16291                .unwrap();
16292        }));
16293
16294        let recovery = {
16295            let store = Arc::clone(&store);
16296            std::thread::spawn(move || store.persist_shard_collections().unwrap())
16297        };
16298        // Recovery has scanned and is paused, still holding its locks.
16299        scanned_rx.recv_timeout(wait).unwrap();
16300
16301        let (started_tx, started_rx) = channel::<()>();
16302        let (done_tx, done_rx) = channel::<()>();
16303        let writer = {
16304            let store = Arc::clone(&store);
16305            std::thread::spawn(move || {
16306                started_tx.send(()).unwrap();
16307                store
16308                    .put(
16309                        &TEST_COLLECTION,
16310                        &distinct_id(1),
16311                        &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"written during recovery")),
16312                    )
16313                    .unwrap();
16314                done_tx.send(()).unwrap();
16315            })
16316        };
16317        // Only start the clock once the writer is running, so the timeout
16318        // measures lock blocking rather than thread scheduling.
16319        started_rx.recv_timeout(wait).unwrap();
16320        assert_eq!(
16321            done_rx.recv_timeout(Duration::from_secs(1)),
16322            Err(RecvTimeoutError::Timeout),
16323            "a writer must be blocked while recovery holds the collection locks"
16324        );
16325
16326        resume_tx.send(()).unwrap();
16327        recovery.join().unwrap();
16328        done_rx
16329            .recv_timeout(wait)
16330            .expect("writer must finish once recovery ends");
16331        writer.join().unwrap();
16332
16333        // `sync_all` defers the sidecar on a delta-only barrier; flush it
16334        // explicitly so this checks the totals rather than the deferral.
16335        store.sync_all().unwrap();
16336        // The sidecar is rebuilt from the shards' in-memory lengths, while
16337        // `physical_layout` reads the pack files. Force the writer's frame out
16338        // of any staging buffer first so the two sources cannot disagree just
16339        // because the frame was appended after the recovery thread's own
16340        // `flush_all` — the very window this test drives.
16341        store.shards.flush_all().unwrap();
16342        store.persist_shard_collections().unwrap();
16343        let expected = crate::packfile::layout::physical_layout(&dir)
16344            .unwrap()
16345            .collections[&TEST_COLLECTION]
16346            .disk_bytes;
16347        assert_eq!(
16348            PackfileStorage::collection_disk_bytes_from_disk(&dir)
16349                .unwrap()
16350                .get(&TEST_COLLECTION),
16351            Some(&expected),
16352            "the frame written around recovery must be in the persisted totals"
16353        );
16354        drop(store);
16355        fs::remove_dir_all(&dir).ok();
16356    }
16357
16358    /// A put whose insert triggers index growth takes a different code path;
16359    /// it must still account for its frame's bytes.
16360    #[test]
16361    fn puts_and_batches_that_grow_the_index_are_byte_accounted() {
16362        let dir = test_dir("growth_byte_accounting");
16363        let store = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
16364        let collection = [0x43u8; 16];
16365        for i in 0..200u8 {
16366            store
16367                .put(
16368                    &TEST_COLLECTION,
16369                    &distinct_id(i),
16370                    &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from(vec![b'x'; 64])),
16371                )
16372                .unwrap();
16373        }
16374        let batch: Vec<_> = (0..200u8)
16375            .map(|i| {
16376                (
16377                    distinct_id(i),
16378                    NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from(vec![b'y'; 64])),
16379                )
16380            })
16381            .collect();
16382        assert_eq!(store.put_many(&collection, &batch).unwrap(), 200);
16383
16384        // A batch into an EXISTING small collection is what grows its index
16385        // mid-batch (a fresh collection is pre-sized for the batch).
16386        let grown_collection = [0x44u8; 16];
16387        store
16388            .put(
16389                &grown_collection,
16390                &distinct_id(0),
16391                &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"seed")),
16392            )
16393            .unwrap();
16394        let (_, _, capacity_before) = store.collection_index_info(&grown_collection).unwrap();
16395        let batch: Vec<_> = (1..250u8)
16396            .map(|i| {
16397                (
16398                    distinct_id(i),
16399                    NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from(vec![b'z'; 64])),
16400                )
16401            })
16402            .collect();
16403        assert_eq!(store.put_many(&grown_collection, &batch).unwrap(), 249);
16404        let (_, _, capacity_after) = store.collection_index_info(&grown_collection).unwrap();
16405        assert!(
16406            capacity_after > capacity_before,
16407            "the batch must grow the index ({capacity_before} -> {capacity_after})"
16408        );
16409        store.sync_all().unwrap();
16410
16411        let physical = crate::packfile::layout::physical_layout(&dir).unwrap();
16412        let sidecar = PackfileStorage::collection_disk_bytes_from_disk(&dir).unwrap();
16413        for id in [TEST_COLLECTION, collection, grown_collection] {
16414            assert_eq!(
16415                sidecar.get(&id),
16416                Some(&physical.collections[&id].disk_bytes),
16417                "collection {id:02x?}: growth must not drop a frame's bytes"
16418            );
16419        }
16420        drop(store);
16421        fs::remove_dir_all(&dir).ok();
16422    }

16424    /// Recovery must be atomic with appends: frames written while it runs may
16425    /// not be left out of (or double counted in) the totals it publishes.
16426    #[test]
16427    fn sidecar_recovery_is_consistent_with_concurrent_appends() {
16428        let dir = test_dir("sidecar_recovery_concurrent");
16429        let store = Arc::new(PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap());
16430        store
16431            .put(
16432                &TEST_COLLECTION,
16433                &distinct_id(0),
16434                &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"seed")),
16435            )
16436            .unwrap();
16437        store.sync_all().unwrap();
16438
16439        store.index_tables.write().collection_disk_bytes.clear();
16440        store
16441            .shard_collections_recovery_failed
16442            .store(true, Ordering::Release);
16443
16444        let writer = {
16445            let store = Arc::clone(&store);
16446            std::thread::spawn(move || {
16447                for i in 1..200u8 {
16448                    store
16449                        .put(
16450                            &TEST_COLLECTION,
16451                            &distinct_id(i),
16452                            &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from(vec![b'x'; 64])),
16453                        )
16454                        .unwrap();
16455                }
16456            })
16457        };
16458        // Recover while the writer is appending.
16459        while store
16460            .shard_collections_recovery_failed
16461            .load(Ordering::Acquire)
16462        {
16463            let _ = store.persist_shard_collections();
16464        }
16465        writer.join().unwrap();
16466        // `sync_all` now defers the sidecar on a delta-only barrier, so flush
16467        // it explicitly before checking the totals recovery published.
16468        store.sync_all().unwrap();
16469        store.persist_shard_collections().unwrap();
16470
16471        let expected = crate::packfile::layout::physical_layout(&dir)
16472            .unwrap()
16473            .collections[&TEST_COLLECTION]
16474            .disk_bytes;
16475        assert_eq!(
16476            PackfileStorage::collection_disk_bytes_from_disk(&dir)
16477                .unwrap()
16478                .get(&TEST_COLLECTION),
16479            Some(&expected),
16480            "totals published by recovery must match the frames on disk"
16481        );
16482        drop(store);
16483        fs::remove_dir_all(&dir).ok();
16484    }

16486    /// A checkpoint that survives without its shard→collection sidecar must not

16489    #[test]

16532    /// A delta-only sync must not rewrite the sidecar: it records staleness and
16533    /// waits for an explicit flush. The first sync (no checkpoint base) is a
16534    /// full rewrite, so it is still an anchor.
16535    #[test]
16536    fn delta_barrier_defers_sidecar_until_an_explicit_flush() {
16537        let dir = test_dir("sidecar_deferred_delta_barrier");
16538        let store = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
16539
16540        store
16541            .put(
16542                &TEST_COLLECTION,
16543                &distinct_id(0),
16544                &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"seed")),
16545            )
16546            .unwrap();
16547        store.sync_all().unwrap();
16548        assert_eq!(
16549            store.stats().sidecar_writes,
16550            1,
16551            "the checkpoint anchor writes the sidecar"
16552        );
16553        let sidecar = PackfileStorage::shard_collections_path(&dir);
16554        let after_checkpoint = fs::read(&sidecar).unwrap();
16555
16556        store
16557            .put(
16558                &TEST_COLLECTION,
16559                &distinct_id(1),
16560                &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"more")),
16561            )
16562            .unwrap();
16563        store.sync_all().unwrap();
16564        assert_eq!(
16565            store.stats().sidecar_writes,
16566            1,
16567            "a delta-only barrier must not rewrite the sidecar"
16568        );
16569        assert!(store.shard_collections_stale.load(Ordering::Relaxed));
16570        assert_eq!(
16571            fs::read(&sidecar).unwrap(),
16572            after_checkpoint,
16573            "the on-disk sidecar is left stale, not rewritten"
16574        );
16575
16576        // An explicit flush is the checkpoint/repack/shutdown anchor.
16577        store.persist_shard_collections().unwrap();
16578        assert_eq!(store.stats().sidecar_writes, 2);
16579        assert!(!store.shard_collections_stale.load(Ordering::Relaxed));
16580        assert_eq!(
16581            PackfileStorage::collection_directory_from_disk(&dir),
16582            vec![(TEST_COLLECTION, 2)]
16583        );
16584
16585        drop(store);
16586        fs::remove_dir_all(&dir).ok();
16587    }
16588
16589    /// A sidecar left stale by a deferred delta barrier must not be trusted: a
16590    /// concurrent read-only open falls back to the slot walk. Dropping the
16591    /// writer flushes it, so a later open trusts it again.
16592    #[test]
16593    fn stale_sidecar_forces_slot_scan_and_drop_repins_it() {
16594        let dir = test_dir("sidecar_stale_then_drop");
16595        let store = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
16596        for i in 0..3u8 {
16597            store
16598                .put(
16599                    &TEST_COLLECTION,
16600                    &distinct_id(i),
16601                    &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from(vec![i])),
16602                )
16603                .unwrap();
16604        }
16605        store.sync_all().unwrap(); // checkpoint anchor: sidecar written
16606
16607        for i in 3..6u8 {
16608            store
16609                .put(
16610                    &TEST_COLLECTION,
16611                    &distinct_id(i),
16612                    &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from(vec![i])),
16613                )
16614                .unwrap();
16615        }
16616        store.sync_all().unwrap(); // delta barrier: sidecar deferred
16617
16618        let reader = PackfileStorage::open_read_only(dir.clone()).unwrap();
16619        assert_eq!(
16620            reader.open_timings().unwrap().bookkeeping_source,
16621            BookkeepingSource::SlotScan,
16622            "a stale sidecar must not be trusted"
16623        );
16624        assert_eq!(
16625            reader
16626                .collection_summaries()
16627                .into_iter()
16628                .find(|(id, _, _, _)| *id == TEST_COLLECTION)
16629                .unwrap()
16630                .1,
16631            6,
16632            "the slot walk must still see every live record"
16633        );
16634        drop(reader);
16635
16636        // Dropping the writer flushes the deferred sidecar, re-pinned to the
16637        // live pack set.
16638        drop(store);
16639        let reopened = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
16640        assert_eq!(
16641            reopened.open_timings().unwrap().bookkeeping_source,
16642            BookkeepingSource::Sidecar,
16643            "Drop must have re-pinned the sidecar to the live packs"
16644        );
16645        assert_eq!(
16646            PackfileStorage::collection_directory_from_disk(&dir),
16647            vec![(TEST_COLLECTION, 6)]
16648        );
16649        drop(reopened);
16650        fs::remove_dir_all(&dir).ok();
16651    }

16653    /// A torn (partially written) sidecar must be treated as absent: open
16654    /// rebuilds from the slot walk, and the next clean barrier regenerates it
16655    /// with exact byte totals.
16656    #[test]
16657    fn torn_sidecar_is_ignored_and_regenerated() {
16658        let dir = test_dir("sidecar_torn");
16659        {
16660            let store = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
16661            store
16662                .put(
16663                    &TEST_COLLECTION,
16664                    &distinct_id(0),
16665                    &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"x")),
16666                )
16667                .unwrap();
16668            store.sync_all().unwrap();
16669        }
16670        let sidecar = PackfileStorage::shard_collections_path(&dir);
16671        let full = fs::read(&sidecar).unwrap();
16672        assert!(full.len() > 20);
16673        fs::write(&sidecar, &full[..full.len() / 2]).unwrap();
16674
16675        let reopened = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
16676        assert_eq!(
16677            reopened.open_timings().unwrap().bookkeeping_source,
16678            BookkeepingSource::SlotScan,
16679            "a torn sidecar must not be trusted"
16680        );
16681        // The open observed a missing sidecar, so the clean barrier regenerates
16682        // it without needing any write.
16683        reopened.sync_all().unwrap();
16684        assert!(reopened.stats().sidecar_writes >= 1);
16685        let expected = crate::packfile::layout::physical_layout(&dir)
16686            .unwrap()
16687            .collections[&TEST_COLLECTION]
16688            .disk_bytes;
16689        assert_eq!(
16690            PackfileStorage::collection_disk_bytes_from_disk(&dir)
16691                .unwrap()
16692                .get(&TEST_COLLECTION),
16693            Some(&expected),
16694            "regeneration must use exact byte totals, not zeros"
16695        );
16696        drop(reopened);
16697        fs::remove_dir_all(&dir).ok();
16698    }

16700    /// The rate-limited flush must stay consistent while writers append.
16701    #[test]
16702    fn maybe_persist_shard_collections_is_consistent_under_concurrent_writes() {
16703        let dir = test_dir("sidecar_maybe_persist_concurrent");
16704        let store = Arc::new(PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap());

16709                    let mut id = [0u8; 16];
16710                    id[..4].copy_from_slice(&i.to_le_bytes());
16711                    id[9] = u8::try_from(i & 0xff).unwrap().wrapping_mul(37);
16712                    store
16713                        .put(
16714                            &TEST_COLLECTION,
16715                            &id,
16716                            &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from(vec![b'x'; 32])),
16717                        )
16718                        .unwrap();
16719                }
16720            })
16721        };
16722        while !writer.is_finished() {
16723            store.persist_shard_collections().unwrap();
16724        }
16725        writer.join().unwrap();
16726        store.sync_all().unwrap();
16727        store.persist_shard_collections().unwrap();
16728
16729        let expected = crate::packfile::layout::physical_layout(&dir)
16730            .unwrap()
16731            .collections[&TEST_COLLECTION]
16732            .disk_bytes;

16734            PackfileStorage::collection_disk_bytes_from_disk(&dir)
16735                .unwrap()
16736                .get(&TEST_COLLECTION),
16737            Some(&expected),
16738            "totals flushed under concurrent writes must match the frames on disk"
16739        );
16740        assert_eq!(
16741            PackfileStorage::collection_directory_from_disk(&dir),
16742            vec![(TEST_COLLECTION, 500)]
16743        );
16744        drop(store);
16745        fs::remove_dir_all(&dir).ok();
16746    }

16748    /// A write that is never synced is deliberately not flushed at shutdown:
16749    /// it already advances a pack past the checkpoint, so the next open cannot
16750    /// take the checkpoint fast path and never consults the sidecar. Correctness
16751    /// must hold anyway, because the full rescan rebuilds everything.
16752    #[test]
16753    fn unsynced_write_then_drop_reopens_by_full_scan_with_correct_data() {
16754        let dir = test_dir("sidecar_unsynced_drop");

16762                )
16763                .unwrap();
16764            store.sync_all().unwrap();
16765            // A later write with no sync must not mark the sidecar stale, and
16766            // `Drop` must not need to flush it.
16767            store
16768                .put(
16769                    &TEST_COLLECTION,
16770                    &distinct_id(1),
16771                    &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"unsynced")),
16772                )
16773                .unwrap();
16774            assert!(!store.is_shard_collections_stale());
16775        }

16777        let reopened = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
16778        assert_eq!(
16779            reopened.open_timings().unwrap().path,
16780            OpenPath::FullScan,
16781            "an unsynced write invalidates the checkpoint fast path"
16782        );
16783        assert_eq!(
16784            reopened
16785                .collection_summaries()
16786                .into_iter()
16787                .find(|(id, _, _, _)| *id == TEST_COLLECTION)
16788                .unwrap()
16789                .1,
16790            2,
16791            "the full rescan must still recover every record"
16792        );

16795    }

16865            .repack_collection_reachable(&TEST_COLLECTION, |_hash, _data| Vec::new())
16866            .unwrap();

16868        let repacked_physical = crate::packfile::layout::physical_layout(&dir).unwrap();
16869        let repacked_expected = repacked_physical
16870            .collections
16871            .get(&TEST_COLLECTION)

16874        assert_eq!(
16875            PackfileStorage::collection_disk_bytes_from_disk(&dir)
16876                .unwrap()
16877                .get(&TEST_COLLECTION),

16883    #[test]
16884    fn test_collection_summaries_from_disk_capacity_matches_new_collection_floor() {
16885        // A one-node collection's live index starts at
16886        // `NEW_COLLECTION_INDEX_FLOOR` (64), never `LossyIndex::new`'s own
16887        // generic 16-slot floor. The disk-only estimate (no packfiles
16888        // opened) must report the same capacity the live index actually
16889        // has, or a load-factor figure derived from it is wrong.
16890        let dir = test_dir("collection_summaries_from_disk_capacity_floor");
16891        let store = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
16892        store
16893            .put(
16894                &TEST_COLLECTION,
16895                &distinct_id(0),
16896                &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from_static(b"x")),
16897            )
16898            .unwrap();
16899        store.sync_all().unwrap();
16900
16901        let live_capacity = store
16902            .collection_index_info(&TEST_COLLECTION)
16903            .expect("collection exists")
16904            .2;
16905        assert_eq!(
16906            live_capacity, 64,
16907            "sanity check: a fresh one-node collection's live index capacity \
16908             is NEW_COLLECTION_INDEX_FLOOR"
16909        );
16910
16911        // Force `open` down its packfile-scan path rather than letting it use
16912        // the serialized checkpoint, then ensure the reconstructed index has
16913        // the same floor as the original collection.
16914        drop(store);
16915        fs::remove_file(PackfileStorage::index_checkpoint_path(&dir)).unwrap();
16916        let reopened = PackfileStorage::open(dir.clone()).unwrap();
16917        assert_eq!(
16918            reopened
16919                .collection_index_info(&TEST_COLLECTION)
16920                .expect("scanned collection exists")
16921                .2,
16922            u32::try_from(NEW_COLLECTION_INDEX_FLOOR).unwrap(),
16923            "an open-time scan keeps the new-collection index floor"
16924        );
16925
16926        let from_disk = PackfileStorage::collection_summaries_from_disk(&dir)
16927            .expect("directory sidecar was persisted by sync_all");
16928        let (_, disk_nodes, _, disk_capacity) = from_disk
16929            .into_iter()
16930            .find(|(id, _, _, _)| *id == TEST_COLLECTION)
16931            .expect("collection present in disk summary");
16932        assert_eq!(disk_nodes, 1);
16933        assert_eq!(
16934            disk_capacity, live_capacity,
16935            "disk-only capacity estimate must match the live index, not undershoot it"
16936        );
16937    }

16999    fn test_plan_collection_repack_matches_real_repack_without_mutating() {

17001        let store = PackfileStorage::open(dir).unwrap();

17008                    &NodeData::new(bytes::Bytes::from(vec![i])),
17009                )
17010                .unwrap();
17011        }
17012        // Duplicate a hash's payload under a fresh id to create something
17013        // dedup would drop... actually LossyIndex already dedups by hash
17014        // on insert, so instead exercise the "no live roots: keep
17015        // everything" path, which is what --root-less usage always hits.
17016        let plan = store

17024        // The dry run must not have mutated anything: a real repack run
17025        // right after must see the exact same collection state and produce the
17026        // exact same result.
17027        let (kept, dropped) = store
17028            .repack_collection_reachable(&TEST_COLLECTION, |_hash, _data| Vec::new())
17029            .unwrap();
